knowledge_statements.statement_title: Admissible Query Points for Exact Subgradient Access
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subgradient-existence boundary for the exact oracle interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For proper convex \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), define
\[
Q_{\mathrm{or}}=\{x\in\operatorname{dom}f:\partial f(x)\ne\varnothing\}.
\]
An exact value-subgradient oracle is queryable only on \(Q_{\mathrm{or}}\). In finite dimensions,
\[
\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f)\subseteq Q_{\mathrm{or}},
\]
so a finite convex function on all of \(\mathbb R^n\) is queryable everywhere.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact subgradient access is defined only where a subgradient exists; relative-interior points are always admissible.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper and convex in finite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.title: Admissible Query Points for Exact Subgradient Access

knowledge_statements.statement_title: An Effective-Domain Boundary Point May Have No Subgradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete boundary of exact subgradient-oracle queryability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define
\[
f(x)=\begin{cases}-\sqrt{x},&x\ge0,\\+\infty,&x<0.\end{cases}
\]
Then \(f\) is proper, closed, and convex, and \(0\in\operatorname{dom}f\), but \(\partial f(0)=\varnothing\). Hence membership in the effective domain alone does not guarantee exact subgradient access.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed convex function can be finite at a domain-boundary point while having no subgradient there.
knowledge_statements.title: An Effective-Domain Boundary Point May Have No Subgradient
Exact Value-Subgradient Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact first-order oracle for a finite-dimensional convex objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper and convex. An exact value-subgradient oracle, queried at \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\), returns \((f_x,g_x)\) satisfying \(f_x=f(x)\), \(g_x\in\partial f(x)\), and hence
\[
f(y)\ge f_x+\langle g_x,y-x\rangle\qquad\text{for every }y\in\mathbb{R}^n.
\]
Thus the returned affine function is a globally valid supporting minorant of \(f\) that is exact at the query point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The oracle returns the exact objective value and a subgradient, producing a global affine lower bound that touches the objective at the query point.

notation.meaning: convex subdifferential of f at x
oracle value and subgradient returned at x

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the oracle-interface leaf, but no evidence is supplied. Also, a proper convex function need not have a nonempty subdifferential at every point of its effective domain, so the oracle's admissible query set or a subgradient-existence hypothesis requires authoritative support.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Exact-Oracle Consistency Inequalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rejected because finite-record interpolation and inconsistency certificates have a dedicated terminal node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: f_j\ge f_i+\langle g_i,x_j-x_i\rangle\quad\forall i,j.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pairwise subgradient inequalities characterize finite exact convex-oracle interpolation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{(x_i,f_i,g_i)\}\text{ is convex-oracle realizable}\iff f_j\ge f_i+\langle g_i,x_j-x_i\rangle\ \forall i,j.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Exact-Oracle Consistency Inequalities

intermediate_metadata.reason: The local inventory is exact objective value, an exact convex subgradient, its touching global affine support, and the precise query set where such output exists. Finite-record interpolation, model consistency, supporting-cut algorithms, and differentiable-point Clarke access were excluded to their dedicated scopes.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: An Unshifted Epsilon-Subgradient Affine Function Need Not Be a Minorant
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle-level necessity of the epsilon downward shift.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f=\delta_{[0,1]}\), let \(x=0\), and let \(\varepsilon>0\). Then \(g=\varepsilon\) belongs to \(\partial_\varepsilon f(0)\), but the unshifted affine function \(a(y)=f(0)+gy=\varepsilon y\) exceeds \(f(y)=0\) for \(0<y\le1\). The shifted function \(a(y)-\varepsilon=\varepsilon y-�\varepsilon\) is a global minorant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonzero epsilon-subgradient may require the full epsilon downward shift before its affine function becomes a valid cut.
knowledge_statements.title: An Unshifted Epsilon-Subgradient Affine Function Need Not Be a Minorant
Epsilon-Subgradient Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additively inexact subgradient oracle with prescribed error \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper and convex, let \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\), and let \(\varepsilon\ge0\). An \(\varepsilon\)-subgradient oracle returns the exact value \(f(x)\) and a vector \(g_x\in\partial_\varepsilon f(x)\), where
\[
\partial_\varepsilon f(x)=\left\{g\in\mathbb{R}^n: f(y)\ge f(x)+\langle g,y-x\rangle-\varepsilon\ \text{for every }y\in\mathbb{R}^n\right\}.
\]
For \(\varepsilon=0\), this reduces to an exact value-subgradient oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The oracle returns an exact value and a vector whose affine subgradient inequality may underestimate the objective by at most epsilon.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The epsilon-subdifferential formula is standard, but the exact-value oracle convention has no source. The plain statement is also misleading: the unshifted affine function may overestimate the objective by at most epsilon; the shifted affine function is the global minorant.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fenchel-Gap Characterization of Epsilon Subgradients
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rejected because it is a convex-analysis characterization of epsilon subdifferentials, not primarily an oracle-interface statement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: g\in\partial_\varepsilon f(x)\iff f(x)+f^*(g)-\langle g,x\rangle\le\varepsilon.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Epsilon-subgradient membership is equivalent to a bounded Fenchel–Young gap.
knowledge_statements.title: Fenchel-Gap Characterization of Epsilon Subgradients

intermediate_metadata.reason: The local inventory is the epsilon-subgradient oracle contract, its exact-value convention, zero-error specialization, and the necessary downward shift for a valid affine cut. Fenchel duality, epsilon-subdifferential nesting, the consuming algorithm, and general cut-validity theory were excluded to their canonical scopes.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Monotonicity and Exact Limit of Epsilon Subdifferentials
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rejected because nesting of epsilon subdifferentials belongs to the foundational epsilon-subdifferential node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: 0\le\varepsilon_1\le\varepsilon_2\Rightarrow\partial_{\varepsilon_1}f(x)\subseteq\partial_{\varepsilon_2}f(x),\qquad \partial f(x)=\bigcap_{\varepsilon>0}\partial_\varepsilon f(x).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Epsilon-subdifferentials enlarge with epsilon and recover the exact subdifferential in the zero-error intersection.
knowledge_statements.title: Monotonicity and Exact Limit of Epsilon Subdifferentials

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Accuracy Does Not Replace Global Cut Validity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp distinction between query-point accuracy and global affine minorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(y)=0\), \(x=0\), \(\ell=0\), and \(g=1\), the affine function \(a(y)=\ell+g(y-x)=y\) has zero query-point error but exceeds \(f(y)\) for every \(y>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Perfect value agreement at the query point does not make an affine function a valid global lower cut.
knowledge_statements.title: Local Accuracy Does Not Replace Global Cut Validity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inexact Cut–Epsilon-Subgradient Equivalence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Translation between a globally valid inexact cut and epsilon-subgradient data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(a(y)=\ell+\langle g,y-x\rangle\) and set \(e=f(x)-\ell\). If \(e\ge0\), then
\[
f(y)\ge a(y)\ \forall y
\iff g\in\partial_e f(x).
\]
Consequently, a valid cut with \(e\le\delta\) has \(g\in\partial_\delta f(x)\), and \(g\in\partial_\delta f(x)\) yields the valid cut \(f(x)-\delta+\langle g,\cdot-x\rangle\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A globally valid inexact cut is exactly an epsilon-subgradient inequality whose epsilon equals its query-point gap.
knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Cut–Epsilon-Subgradient Equivalence
Inexact Cut Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle interface returning a globally valid affine cut with bounded value error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper and convex. A \(\delta\)-inexact cut oracle, queried at \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\), returns \((\ell_x,g_x,\delta_x)\) with \(0\le\delta_x\le\delta\) such that
\[
\ell_x\le f(x)\le \ell_x+\delta_x,
\qquad
f(y)\ge \ell_x+\langle g_x,y-x\rangle\quad\text{for every }y\in\mathbb{R}^n.
\]
Equivalently, the cut is a global affine minorant and its gap from \(f\) at the query point is at most \(\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The oracle returns a global affine lower cut whose value at the query point lies within the prescribed additive error of the objective.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and local topic match, but this particular inexact-cut interface and its certified value-gap convention require a cited authoritative source.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Requested Accuracy Alone Implies No Cost Law
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between caller-controlled error and computational cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A guarantee \(0\le\delta(x,\eta)\le\eta\) for requested tolerance \(\eta>0\) imposes no bound on oracle work \(C(x,\eta)\). Any estimate \(C(x,\eta)\le\Phi(\eta)\) is a separate cost-model assumption.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Requesting a smaller certified error does not itself specify the work needed to obtain it.

notation.meaning: work required by the oracle call

knowledge_statements.title: Requested Accuracy Alone Implies No Cost Law
Adjustable-Accuracy Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parameterized inexact oracle whose certified error is controlled by the caller.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper and convex. An adjustable-accuracy cut oracle accepts a query \((x,\eta)\), where \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\) and \(\eta>0\), and returns \((\ell_{x,\eta},g_{x,\eta},\delta_{x,\eta})\) satisfying
\[
0\le\delta_{x,\eta}\le\eta,
\qquad
\ell_{x,\eta}\le f(x)\le\ell_{x,\eta}+\delta_{x,\eta},
\]
\[
f(y)\ge\ell_{x,\eta}+\langle g_{x,\eta},y-x\rangle\qquad\text{for every }y\in\mathbb{R}^n.
\]
The requested tolerance may vary between calls; no monotonicity of returned cuts is implied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The caller requests a tolerance, and the oracle returns a valid affine lower cut with certified query-point error no larger than that tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\le f(x)-\ell_{x,\eta}\le\delta_{x,\eta}\le\eta\), with a globally valid affine minorant.

notation.meaning: certified error achieved by the oracle

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the leaf, but neither the adjustable-accuracy convention nor its relationship between requested and achieved error is sourced. Any intended cost-versus-accuracy requirement also remains unspecified.

children.title: Unconstrained Domains
children.top_down_role: Domain geometry without explicit feasibility restrictions.

knowledge_statements.title: Unconstrained Domains
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex minimization with no explicit feasibility restriction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An unconstrained convex optimization problem has the form
\[
\inf_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n} f(x),
\]
where \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) is proper and convex. In the strict unconstrained-domain regime, \(f\) is finite on all of \(\mathbb{R}^n\), so every point is admissible for objective-oracle queries. Extended values may instead encode implicit constraints, but then the effective feasible set is \(\operatorname{dom}f\), and the regime is not strictly full-domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The decision variable ranges over all Euclidean space; in the strict regime the objective is finite and queryable everywhere.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The explicit feasible set is \(\mathbb{R}^n\); strict full-domain access additionally requires \(\operatorname{dom}f=\mathbb{R}^n\).

notation.meaning: effective domain where f is finite

source_refs.locator: Chapter 1. Fundamentals of the Theory and Methods of Unconstrained Minimization p. 2

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Full Domain Does Not Ensure Attainment or Boundedness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundaries of full-space access without coercivity or another localization assumption.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The finite closed convex functions \(f_1(x)=e^x\) and \(f_2(x)=x\) on \(\mathbb R\) satisfy
\[
\inf f_1=0,\quad\operatorname*{argmin}f_1=\varnothing,
\qquad
\inf f_2=-\infty.
\]
Thus full-domain access alone ensures neither attainment nor a finite infimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A full-domain convex objective may have an unattained finite infimum or be unbounded below.
knowledge_statements.title: Full Domain Does Not Ensure Attainment or Boundedness

children.top_down_role: Objective regimes where coercivity supplies global localization.

knowledge_statements.title: Coercive Objective Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coercivity condition for an extended-real convex objective on Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A proper function \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) is coercive when
\[
\lim_{\lVert x\rVert\to\infty} f(x)=+\infty.
\]
Equivalently, for every \(\alpha\in\mathbb{R}\), the lower level set \(L_\alpha=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:f(x)\le\alpha\}\) is bounded. If \(f\) is also lower semicontinuous, each nonempty level set is compact; if \(f\) is proper as well, then \(f\) attains its finite global minimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coercive objective diverges along every sequence escaping to infinity; with lower semicontinuity, its bounded sublevel sets are compact and a minimum is attained.
assumptions_latex: Minimum attainment additionally assumes that \(f\) is lower semicontinuous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Coercivity is equivalent to boundedness of every lower level set; lower semicontinuity yields compactness and minimum attainment.

notation.meaning: lower level set at height alpha

source_refs.locator: Chapter 1. Fundamentals of the Theory and Methods of Unconstrained Minimization p. 2

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex Coercivity Without Closedness Need Not Give Attainment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp lower-semicontinuity boundary for minimum attainment in the extended-real convex regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) by \[f(x)=\begin{cases}x,&x>0,\\+\infty,&x\le0.\end{cases}\] Then \(f\) is proper, convex, and coercive, but it is not lower semicontinuous at \(0\), \(\inf f=0\), and \(\operatorname*{argmin}f=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proper convex coercive function can fail to attain its infimum when lower semicontinuity is omitted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{proper convex coercivity alone does not imply minimum attainment}.
review_flags: Corrects the Builder's nonconvex example so that the counterexample remains inside this convex-objective leaf.

children.title: Coercivity-Induced Localization
children.top_down_role: Localization consequences supplied by coercive objective behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Coercivity-Induced Localization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduction of an unconstrained coercive problem to a compact sublevel set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and coercive, and choose \(x_0\in\operatorname{dom}f\). Then
\[
L_0=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:f(x)\le f(x_0)\}
\]
is nonempty and compact. Every global minimizer belongs to \(L_0\), and
\[
\inf_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}f(x)=\min_{x\in L_0}f(x).
\]
Consequently, any descent method whose accepted iterates satisfy \(f(x_{k+1})\le f(x_k)\) remains inside the compact set \(L_0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite initial value localizes a coercive unconstrained problem to a compact sublevel set containing all minimizers and every monotonically accepted iterate.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and coercive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_0\) is compact, contains every minimizer, and satisfies \(\inf_{\mathbb{R}^n}f=\min_{L_0}f\).

notation.meaning: sublevel set determined by the initial point

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Compactness Does Not Imply Computational Simplicity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between compact convex geometry and an algorithmic domain-access model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Nonemptiness, compactness, and convexity of \(Q\) do not by themselves provide a projection, proximal map, linear-minimization oracle, or complexity bound for any of these primitives. Thus \(Q\) is computationally simple only relative to a declared representation and access primitive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A compact convex set is not automatically computationally simple; simplicity must name the supplied representation or oracle.
assumptions_latex: No computational representation or domain oracle for \(Q\) is assumed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Q\text{ compact and convex}\ \not\Rightarrow\ Q\text{ computationally simple}.
knowledge_statements.title: Compactness Does Not Imply Computational Simplicity
Compact Simple Domains
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compact convex feasible sets equipped with a tractable proximal subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Relative to a norm \(\lVert\cdot\rVert\), a compact simple domain is a nonempty compact convex set \(Q\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) supplied with a continuous, strongly convex prox function \(d:Q\to\mathbb{R}\) such that, for every \(g\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(z\in Q\), and \(\lambda>0\), one can compute
\[
\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in Q}\left\{\langle g,x\rangle+\lambda D_d(x,z)\right\},
\qquad
D_d(x,z)=d(x)-d(z)-\langle\nabla d(z),x-z\rangle.
\]
Simplicity is therefore relative to the chosen prox geometry and computational model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A compact simple domain is a compact convex feasible set on which the required prox-linear minimization problem can be computed tractably.
assumptions_latex: \(d\) is differentiable on the query region and strongly convex on \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed prox-linear minimization is computationally available for every admissible \(g\), \(z\), and \(\lambda\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The chosen definition is one possible prox-geometry meaning of a simple domain, but that convention is not universal and has no source. The differentiability domain needed for the displayed Bregman divergence at every z in Q must also be stated consistently.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Formula-Based Explicit Convex Constraint Access
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Declared access convention for convex inequalities, affine equalities, and an explicit base set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An explicit convex-constraint representation is \[Q=Q_0\cap\bigcap_{i=1}^m\{x:g_i(x)\le0\}\cap\{x:Ax=b\},\] where \(Q_0\) is convex, each \(g_i\) is convex on the relevant domain, and the representation declares computational access to membership in \(Q_0\), the residual \(Ax-b\), and the constraint values \(g_i(x)\) together with any subgradients required by the selected method. The intersection \(Q\) is convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Explicit access means the convex inequalities, affine equalities, base-set membership, and required constraint oracle information are supplied directly.
assumptions_latex: Each \(g_i\) is convex on the relevant domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Q\text{ is convex, and feasibility can be checked through the declared formula-based access}.
review_flags: Explicitness is intentionally defined relative to the declared computational interface.
knowledge_statements.title: Formula-Based Explicit Convex Constraint Access

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Explicit Constraint Access Need Not Provide Cheap Projection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between formula-based constraint access and stronger geometric primitives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Access to convex constraint values, subgradients, and affine residuals does not by itself provide the Euclidean projection onto \(Q\) or an exact proximal master over \(Q\); either operation may require solving an additional convex optimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Explicit formulas and constraint subgradients do not automatically supply a projection or prox oracle.
assumptions_latex: Only the declared formula-based constraint access is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{explicit constraint access}\ \not\Rightarrow\ \text{direct projection or proximal access}.
knowledge_statements.title: Explicit Constraint Access Need Not Provide Cheap Projection
Explicit Convex Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex feasible domains specified directly by inequalities, affine equalities, and a simple base set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An explicitly constrained convex problem may be represented as
\[
\min_{x\in Q} f(x),
\qquad
Q=Q_0\cap\{x:g_i(x)\le0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\cap\{x:Ax=b\},
\]
where \(Q_0\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is closed and convex, \(f\) and each \(g_i\) are proper convex functions on a neighborhood of \(Q_0\), and \(Ax=b\) is affine. The representation is explicit when membership and the values or subgradients needed to enforce these constraints are directly computable from the supplied formulas.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The feasible set is given directly by a convex base set, convex inequality formulas, and affine equalities with computable constraint information.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g_1,\ldots,g_m\) are proper and convex on the relevant domain.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation is convex and fits the leaf, but the criterion that makes the constraints computationally explicit is model-dependent and unsupported by a source.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strong Separation-Oracle Domain
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed convex domain accessed through exact membership and strict separating-hyperplane responses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex. A strong separation oracle queried at \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) either certifies \(x\in Q\) or returns \(a\ne0\) and \(\beta\) such that \[\langle a,y\rangle\le\beta<\langle a,x\rangle\qquad(\forall y\in Q).\] The returned halfspace contains all of \(Q\) and excludes the query point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strong separation query either certifies membership or returns a strict separating halfspace containing the entire domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x\in Q\quad\text{or}\quad \exists(a,\beta):\ \langle a,y\rangle\le\beta<\langle a,x\rangle\ \forall y\in Q.

notation.meaning: normal and offset of the separating hyperplane

review_flags: The mismatched polyhedral citation from the deferred seed is not retained.
knowledge_statements.title: Strong Separation-Oracle Domain

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Separation Is Distinct from Projection and Optimization Access
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between exact separation and stronger domain primitives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A separation-oracle response does not itself return \(P_Q(x)\), a minimizer of a linear functional over \(Q\), or a proximal point over \(Q\). Computational reductions among separation, membership, and optimization require an explicit quantitative model, including suitable boundedness, accuracy, and representation assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Separation is a different primitive from exact projection, linear optimization, or proximal access.
assumptions_latex: Only exact separation-oracle access is supplied.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{separation response}\ \not\equiv\ \text{projection, linear optimization, or proximal response}.
knowledge_statements.title: Separation Is Distinct from Projection and Optimization Access

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Separation Cuts Form Nested Outer Approximations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometry generated by accumulated valid separation-oracle responses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If valid oracle responses give halfspaces \(H_j=\{y:\langle a_j,y\rangle\le\beta_j\}\) satisfying \(Q\subseteq H_j\), then \[P_k=\bigcap_{j=1}^kH_j\] is closed and convex and satisfies \(Q\subseteq P_{k+1}\subseteq P_k\). A query point strictly separated by \(H_j\) is excluded from \(P_j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accumulated separating halfspaces form nested closed convex outer approximations and exclude the separated query points.
assumptions_latex: Each nonmember query is strictly separated by its returned halfspace.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Separation Cuts Form Nested Outer Approximations
Separation-Oracle Domains
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed convex domains accessed through membership and separating-hyperplane queries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Q\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex. A strong separation oracle, queried at \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), either certifies \(x\in Q\) or returns a nonzero vector \(a\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and scalar \(\beta\in\mathbb{R}\) such that
\[
\langle a,y\rangle\le\beta<\langle a,x\rangle
\qquad\text{for every }y\in Q.
\]
The returned inequality is a verifiable halfspace containing \(Q\) and excluding the query point. A domain supplied only through this interface need not have an explicit constraint representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Queries either confirm membership or return a strict separating hyperplane whose containing halfspace includes the entire convex domain but excludes the query point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The oracle certifies \(x\in Q\) or returns \((a,\beta)\) with \(\langle a,y\rangle\le\beta<\langle a,x\rangle\) for all \(y\in Q\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Interior Lipschitz Bounds Need Not Extend to the Domain Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary failure for convex local Lipschitz regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
f(x)=\begin{cases}-\sqrt{1-x^2},&x\in[-1,1],\\+\infty,&\text{otherwise}.�\end{cases}
\]
Then \(f\) is proper, closed, and convex and locally Lipschitz on \((-1,1)\), but
\[
f'(x)=\frac{x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}
\]
is unbounded as \(x\to\pm1\). Hence \(f\) is not Lipschitz on its full effective domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed convex function may be locally Lipschitz on the relative interior but not Lipschitz up to the domain boundary.
knowledge_statements.title: Interior Lipschitz Bounds Need Not Extend to the Domain Boundary

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Relative-Interior Local Lipschitz Regularity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Automatic local regularity of finite-dimensional proper convex functions away from the effective-domain boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A proper convex function \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is locally Lipschitz on \(\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f)\), relative to \(\operatorname{aff}(\operatorname{dom}f)\). Equivalently, every compact \(K\subset\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f)\) admits \(L_K<\infty\) such that
\[
|f(x)-f(y)|\le L_K\|x-y\|\quad(x,y\in K).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proper convex function is automatically locally Lipschitz on the relative interior of its effective domain.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper and convex in finite dimensions.

notation.meaning: affine hull of the effective domain

knowledge_statements.title: Relative-Interior Local Lipschitz Regularity
Lipschitz Nonsmooth Objectives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order characterization of Lipschitz continuity for finite convex objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, open, and convex, and let \(f:D\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex. If every subgradient satisfies \(\lVert g\rVert_*\le L\) for all \(x\in D\) and \(g\in\partial f(x)\), then
\[
|f(x)-f(y)|\le L\lVert x-y\rVert\qquad\text{for all }x,y\in D.
\]
Conversely, if \(f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz on \(D\), then every \(g\in\partial f(x)\) satisfies \(\lVert g\rVert_*\le L\). Nondifferentiability is permitted throughout.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite convex function on an open convex domain, L-Lipschitz continuity is equivalent to all subgradients having dual norm at most L.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz on \(D\) if and only if \(\lVert g\rVert_*\le L\) for every \(x\in D\) and \(g\in\partial f(x)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-dimensional open-domain equivalence between Lipschitz continuity and uniformly bounded convex subgradients is precise and fits the regularity leaf, but no authoritative source or locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Directional growth bound and its Lipschitz specialization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-growth inequalities expressed through the source-defined directional quantity \(v_f\) and modulus \(\omega_f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\),
\[
f(x)-f(\bar x)\le \omega_f\!\left(\bar x;v_f(\bar x;x)\right).
\]
If \(f\) is Lipschitz continuous on \(B_2(\bar x,R)\) with constant \(M\), then every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfying \(v_f(\bar x;x)\le R\) also satisfies
\[
f(x)-f(\bar x)\le M\bigl(v_f(\bar x;x)\bigr)_+.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Growth from the reference point is bounded by the directional growth modulus. Under M-Lipschitz continuity on the radius-R ball, it is bounded by M times the positive part of the directional quantity whenever that quantity is at most R.
assumptions_latex: f\text{ is Lipschitz continuous on }B_2(\bar x,R)\text{ with constant }M\quad\text{for the second inequality}
v_f(\bar x;x)\le R\quad\text{for the second inequality}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f(x)-f(\bar x)\le \omega_f(\bar x;v_f(\bar x;x)),\qquad f(x)-f(\bar x)\le M(v_f(\bar x;x))_+\ \text{under the stated Lipschitz assumptions}

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Convex Objectives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional representation of proper polyhedral convex functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A proper lower-semicontinuous convex function \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) is polyhedral exactly when its epigraph is a nonempty polyhedron. Equivalently, there exist a nonempty polyhedron \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), finitely many vectors \(a_1,\ldots,a_m\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and scalars \(b_1,\ldots,b_m\in\mathbb{R}\) such that
\[
f(x)=\max_{1\le i\le m}\{\langle a_i,x\rangle+b_i\}+\delta_P(x),
\]
where \(\delta_P(x)=0\) for \(x\in P\) and \(\delta_P(x)=+\infty\) otherwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proper closed convex function is polyhedral exactly when it is a finite maximum of affine functions over a polyhedral effective domain.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{epi}f\) is polyhedral if and only if \(f=\max_i(\langle a_i,\cdot\rangle+b_i)+\delta_P\) for finite affine data and a polyhedron \(P\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conjugacy Preserves Polyhedral Convexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional Fenchel conjugacy for proper closed polyhedral convex functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A proper lower-semicontinuous convex function \(f\) is polyhedral if and only if its Fenchel conjugate \(f^*\) is polyhedral. Moreover, \(y\in\partial f(x)\) if and only if \(x\in\partial f^*(y)\), equivalently \(f(x)+f^*(y)=\langle x,y\rangle\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Polyhedral convexity is invariant under conjugacy, with inverse primal and dual subgradient relations.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is proper, lower-semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\) is polyhedral if and only if \(f^*\) is polyhedral.
knowledge_statements.title: Conjugacy Preserves Polyhedral Convexity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polyhedral Objectives Cannot Have Positive Curvature on Open Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between polyhedral and strongly convex objective regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A finite-valued polyhedral convex function on a nonempty open convex set of positive dimension is affine on some nonempty open subset. Consequently it cannot be \(\mu\)-strongly convex on that set for any \(\mu>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Affine cells prevent finite-valued polyhedral objectives from being strongly convex on open positive-dimensional domains.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is finite-valued and polyhedral on a nonempty open convex set \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\) is not \(\mu\)-strongly convex on \(Q\) for any \(\mu>0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Objectives Cannot Have Positive Curvature on Open Sets

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polyhedral Weak-Sharp Error Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global objective error bound when the minimizer set is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) be proper closed polyhedral convex, \(X^*=\operatorname*{argmin}f\ne\varnothing\), and \(f^*=\min f\). There exists \(\alpha>0\) such that \[f(x)-f^*\ge\alpha\operatorname{dist}(x,X^*)\qquad(x\in\operatorname{dom}f).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polyhedral convex objective with a minimizer has a global linear error bound.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, closed, convex, and polyhedral.
knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Weak-Sharp Error Bound

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Subdifferential of a Polyhedral Convex Objective
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Active-piece subdifferential formula on a polyhedral effective domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(f(x)=\max_{1\le i\le m}\{\langle a_i,x\rangle+b_i\}+\delta_P(x)\) and \(I(x)=\{i:\langle a_i,x\rangle+b_i=f(x)\}\), then for \(x\in P\), \[\partial f(x)=\operatorname{conv}\{a_i:i\in I(x)\}+N_P(x).\] Hence \(x\) minimizes \(f\) exactly when \(0\in\operatorname{conv}\{a_i:i\in I(x)\}+N_P(x)\). The graph of \(\partial f\) is a finite union of polyhedral sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The subdifferential consists of convex combinations of active slopes plus the domain normal cone, yielding an explicit optimality test.
knowledge_statements.title: Subdifferential of a Polyhedral Convex Objective

knowledge_statements.title: Smooth Objectives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex objectives with Lipschitz-continuous gradients relative to a norm and its dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Q\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be convex, let \(\|\cdot\|\) have dual norm \(\|\cdot\|_*\), and let \(f\) be convex and differentiable on a neighborhood of \(Q\). The objective is \(L\)-smooth on \(Q\) when
\[\|\nabla f(x)-\nabla f(y)\|_*\le L\|x-y\|\qquad(x,y\in Q).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex differentiable objective is smooth when its gradient is Lipschitz continuous in the chosen primal and dual norms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nabla f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz from \((Q,\|\cdot\|)\) to the dual normed space.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Smoothness–Strong-Convexity Conjugacy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Full-domain Fenchel-dual characterization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a proper closed convex function \(f\) and \(L>0\), \(f\) is finite and differentiable on \(\mathbb R^n\) with \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient if and only if \(f^*\) is \(1/L\)-strongly convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Full-domain convex smoothness is dual to reciprocal strong convexity of the conjugate.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is proper, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\) is \(L\)-smooth on \(\mathbb R^n\) if and only if \(f^*\) is \(1/L\)-strongly convex.
knowledge_statements.title: Smoothness–Strong-Convexity Conjugacy

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Baillon–Haddad Cocoercivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean first-order geometry of convex smooth functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(f\) is convex and differentiable on an open convex set and \(
abla f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz with \(L>0\), then \[\langle
abla f(x)-
abla f(y),x-yangle\ge rac1L\|
abla f(x)-
abla f(y)\|_2^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The gradient of a convex L-smooth function is reciprocal-L cocoercive.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex and differentiable on an open convex Euclidean domain.
knowledge_statements.title: Baillon–Haddad Cocoercivity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Descent Lemma and Convex Smoothness Equivalence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent Euclidean first-order inequalities on an open convex domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be open and convex, and let \(f:Q\to\mathbb R\) be convex and differentiable. Then \(\nabla f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz on \(Q\) if and only if, for all \(x,y\in Q\), \[0\le f(y)-f(x)-\langle\nabla f(x),y-x\rangle\le\frac L2\|y-x\|_2^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex differentiable objective on an open domain, Lipschitz gradients are equivalent to quadratic linearization error.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is finite, convex, and differentiable on \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nabla f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz exactly when the stated Bregman-error bound holds.
knowledge_statements.title: Descent Lemma and Convex Smoothness Equivalence

children.title: Smoothness-Transition Regimes
children.top_down_role: Navigation across the boundary between weakly smooth and smooth cases.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Boundedness Is Essential for Exponent Downgrading
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of global lower-exponent embeddings on unbounded domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(x)=\frac12x^2\) on \(\mathbb R\), \(\nabla f(x)=x\) is globally Lipschitz, but for every \(0\le\alpha<1\) there is no finite \(C\) satisfying \(|x-y|\le C|x-y|^\alpha\) for all \(x,y\in\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A globally Lipschitz gradient need not obey any lower-exponent global Hölder bound on an unbounded domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nabla f\) is Lipschitz but not globally \(\alpha\)-Hölder.
knowledge_statements.title: Boundedness Is Essential for Exponent Downgrading

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Zero-Exponent Endpoint Controls Only Oscillation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical boundary of the formal exponent-zero comparison.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A bound \(\|G(x)-G(y)\|_*\le L_0\) for all distinct \(x,y\) bounds only the total oscillation of \(G\); it does not imply continuity. Thus \(\nu=0\) is a formal endpoint comparison, not Hölder continuity in the continuity-implying sense.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The zero-exponent endpoint bounds oscillation but does not imply continuity.
assumptions_latex: \(G:Q\to\mathbb R^n\) satisfies \(\|G(x)-G(y)\|_*\le L_0\) for distinct points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The bounded-oscillation condition alone does not imply continuity of \(G\).
knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Exponent Endpoint Controls Only Oscillation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nesting of Hölder-Gradient Regimes on Bounded Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison of arbitrary Hölder exponents on a bounded domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Q\) have diameter \(D<\infty\). If \(\|
abla f(x)-
abla f(y)\|_*\le L_ eta\|x-y\|^ eta\) on \(Q\), where \(0\le\alpha\le eta\le1\), then \[\|
abla f(x)-
abla f(y)\|_*\le L_ eta D^{ eta-\alpha}\|x-y\|^\alpha.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a bounded set, every higher Hölder-gradient exponent implies every lower exponent with a diameter-adjusted constant.
knowledge_statements.title: Nesting of Hölder-Gradient Regimes on Bounded Sets
Smoothness-Transition Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interpolation of Lipschitz-gradient regularity into Hölder-gradient regimes on bounded domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(Q\) has finite diameter \(D\) under \(\|\cdot\|\), and \(f\) is \(L\)-smooth on \(Q\). For every \(
u\in[0,1]\),
\[\|
abla f(x)-
abla f(y)\|_*\le L D^{1-
u}\|x-y\|^
u\qquad(x,y\in Q).\]
Thus the Lipschitz-gradient regime \(
u=1\) continuously supplies every weaker Hölder regime, including the bounded-gradient-difference endpoint \(
u=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a bounded domain, a Lipschitz gradient is Hölder continuous for every exponent from zero to one, with a diameter-adjusted constant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For each \(\nu\in[0,1]\), the gradient is Hölder continuous with constant \(L D^{1-\nu}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strong Convexity Implies Smooth Conjugacy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fenchel-dual regularity generated by Euclidean strong convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(f\) is proper, closed, and \(\mu\)-strongly convex, then \(f^*\) is finite and differentiable on \(\mathbb R^n\), \[
abla f^*(y)=\operatorname*{argmax}_{x}\{\langle y,xangle-f(x)\},\qquad \|
abla f^*(y)-
abla f^*(z)\|_2\le\mu^{-1}\|y-z\|_2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The conjugate of a closed strongly convex function is everywhere differentiable with reciprocal-modulus Lipschitz gradient.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, closed, and \(\mu\)-strongly convex on \(\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.title: Strong Convexity Implies Smooth Conjugacy

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strong Monotonicity of the Subdifferential
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order characterization for proper closed convex functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A proper closed convex function \(f\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex if and only if its convex subdifferential is \(\mu\)-strongly monotone: \[\langle g_x-g_y,x-y\rangle\ge\mu\|x-y\|_2^2\] for all \(g_x\in\partial f(x)\) and \(g_y\in\partial f(y)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong convexity is equivalent to strong monotonicity of the convex subdifferential.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, closed, and convex on \(\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex if and only if \(\partial f\) is \(\mu\)-strongly monotone.
knowledge_statements.title: Strong Monotonicity of the Subdifferential

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quadratic-Shift and Jensen Characterizations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent Euclidean formulations of strong convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a proper extended-real function \(f\) on a convex set \(Q\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and \(\mu>0\), the following are equivalent: \(f-\frac\mu2\|\cdot\|_2^2\) is convex on \(Q\); and for every \(x,y\in Q\), \(t\in[0,1]\), \[f((1-t)x+ty)\le(1-t)f(x)+tf(y)-\frac\mu2t(1-t)\|x-y\|_2^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong convexity is convexity after subtracting a quadratic, equivalently Jensen convexity with a uniform quadratic deficit.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The quadratic-shift and strong-Jensen formulations are equivalent.
knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic-Shift and Jensen Characterizations

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Existence, Uniqueness, and Quadratic Growth
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global minimization consequences in finite-dimensional Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Every proper closed \(\mu\)-strongly convex function on \(\mathbb R^n\) has a unique minimizer \(x^*\), and \[f(x)-f(x^*)\ge\frac\mu2\|x-x^*\|_2^2\qquad(x\in\operatorname{dom}f).\] Equivalently, \(0\in\partial f(x^*)\), and no other point satisfies this inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Proper closed strong convexity guarantees a unique minimizer, a zero-subgradient certificate, and global quadratic growth.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is proper, closed, and \(\mu\)-strongly convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There is a unique \(x^*\) with \(0\in\partial f(x^*)\), and the stated quadratic-growth bound holds.
knowledge_statements.title: Existence, Uniqueness, and Quadratic Growth
Strongly Convex Objectives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong convexity expressed by a uniform quadratic strengthening of every subgradient support inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Q\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be convex and let \(f:Q\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and convex. For \(\mu>0\), the objective is \(\mu\)-strongly convex relative to \(\|\cdot\|\) when, for every \(x,y\in Q\) and every \(g\in\partial f(x)\),
\[f(y)\ge f(x)+\langle g,y-x\rangle+\frac{\mu}{2}\|y-x\|^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong convexity strengthens each supporting-hyperplane inequality by a uniform positive quadratic term.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every subgradient support inequality has quadratic margin \(\frac{\mu}{2}\|y-x\|^2\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Distance bound under the stated strong-convexity gap equality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-geometry result for a strongly convex, Lipschitz-continuous function; the equality between the quadratic term and objective gap is an explicit hypothesis, not a general consequence of strong convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $f$ be $\mu$-strongly convex and $M$-Lipschitz continuous, let $x^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}f$, and define $f^*=f(x^*)$. If $\frac{\mu}{2}\lVert x_0-x^*\rVert^2=f(x_0)-f^*\le M\lVert x_0-x^*\rVert$, then $\lVert x_0-x^*\rVert\le\frac{2M}{\mu}$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the objective gap at x0 is exactly the stated strong-convexity quadratic term and is bounded by the Lipschitz estimate, then the distance from x0 to the minimizer is at most 2M divided by mu.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strong convexity in Euclidean geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order definition of strong convexity, its twice-differentiable Hessian characterization, and the quadratic-regularization construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\mu>0\), a differentiable function \(F:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex if and only if \[F(\eta)\ge F(\theta)+F'(\theta)^\top(\eta-\theta)+\frac{\mu}{2}\|\eta-�\theta\|_2^2\quad\forall\eta,\theta\in\mathbb{R}^d.\] If \(F\) is twice differentiable, this is equivalent to \(F''(\theta)\succeq\mu I\) for all \(\theta\). Moreover, if \(G\) is convex, possibly nonsmooth, then \(G(\cdot)+\frac{\mu}{2}\|\cdot\|_2^2\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong convexity strengthens the supporting-tangent inequality by a positive quadratic term. For twice-differentiable functions, every Hessian eigenvalue must be at least the strong-convexity parameter. Adding the corresponding quadratic to a convex function, including a nonsmooth one, produces a strongly convex function.
assumptions_latex: F:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}\text{ is differentiable for the displayed first-order definition}
F\text{ is twice differentiable for the Hessian equivalence}
G:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}\text{ is convex for the quadratic-regularization construction}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\text{ is }\mu\text{-strongly convex}\iff \forall\eta,\theta,\ F(\eta)\ge F(\theta)+F'(\theta)^\top(\eta-\theta)+\frac{\mu}{2}\|\eta-\theta\|_2^2;\quad F\in C^2\Rightarrow\bigl(F\text{ is }\mu\text{-strongly convex}\iff F''(\theta)\succeq\mu I\ \forall\theta\bigr);\quad G\text{ convex}\Rightarrow G+\frac{\mu}{2}\|\cdot\|_2^2\text{ is }\mu\text{-strongly convex}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex Decomposition Does Not Imply Proximability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between additive convex structure and computational access.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Properness, closedness, and convexity of \(g\) ensure that
\[
\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda g}(v)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_x\left\{g(x)+\frac{1}{2\lambda}\|x-v\|^2\right\}
\]
is mathematically well defined under standard finite-dimensional assumptions, but do not imply a closed form or a prescribed evaluation cost. Proximal access is a separate oracle assumption.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed convex term is not automatically available through an efficiently evaluable proximal mapping.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: g\text{ closed convex}\not\Rightarrow\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda g}\text{ is available at prescribed cost}.
knowledge_statements.title: Convex Decomposition Does Not Imply Proximability

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Composite Convex Subdifferential and Optimality Rule
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact first-order structure of a smooth-plus-convex additive objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F=f+g\), where \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is convex and differentiable and \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is proper, closed, and convex. Then
\[
\partial F(x)=\nabla f(x)+\partial g(x),
\]
and
\[
x^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}F\iff0\in\nabla f(x^\star)+\partial g(x^\star).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The subdifferential of a smooth-plus-convex sum is the gradient plus the nonsmooth subdifferential, yielding exact convex optimality.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is finite, convex, and differentiable on \(\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.title: Composite Convex Subdifferential and Optimality Rule
Composite Convex Objectives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive smooth-plus-proximable convex objective structure used by first-order model methods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Q\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be convex. A composite convex objective has the form
\[F(x)=f(x)+g(x),\qquad x\in Q,\]
where \(f:Q\to\mathbb{R}\) is convex and differentiable and \(g:Q\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex. In model methods, \(f\) is accessed through first-order linearizations while \(g\) is retained exactly in each local model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A composite convex objective is the sum of a differentiable convex term and a proper closed convex term retained exactly in local models.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is finite, convex, and differentiable on \(Q\).
\(g\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F=f+g\) is convex on \(Q\), with the nonsmooth term available for exact model retention.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Q\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be convex, let \(f:Q\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and convex, and let \(I\) be a finite nonempty index set. Given \(x_i\in\operatorname{dom}f\) and \(g_i\in\partial f(x_i)\) for every \(i\in I\), define, for \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\),
\[m_I(x)=\max_{i\in I}\bigl\{f(x_i)+\langle g_i,x-x_i\rangle\bigr\}.\]
Then \(m_I\) is convex and polyhedral on \(\mathbb{R}^n\), and \(m_I(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in Q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The maximum of a finite nonempty collection of subgradient cuts is a convex polyhedral function that globally underestimates the objective on its domain.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Primal–Dual Pairing Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Norm compatibility controlling affine oracle models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a finite-dimensional normed space \((E,\|\cdot\|)\) and its dual norm,
\[
|\langle g,u\rangle|\le\|g\|_*\|u\|.
\]
Thus \(\|g\|_*\le G\) implies \(|\langle g,u\rangle|\le G\|u\|\). Finiteness of each individual dual norm is automatic and is not a substantive boundedness assumption.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Oracle slopes are measured in the norm dual to the primal displacement norm; a uniform dual bound controls affine-model variation.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Pairing Compatibility

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strong Convexity Without Existence Control Is Insufficient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between uniqueness and attainment for regularized model subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(Q=(0,1)\), the function \(d(x)=x^2\) is strongly convex, but \(\inf_Qd=0\) is not attained. Strong convexity guarantees at most one minimizer; closedness, lower semicontinuity, and a level-boundedness condition are needed for existence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong convexity gives uniqueness, not attainment on a nonclosed or otherwise nonattaining domain.
knowledge_statements.title: Strong Convexity Without Existence Control Is Insufficient

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strongly Convex Prox Geometry Makes Affine Masters Well Posed
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Precise solvability consequence of compatible prox geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Q\subset E\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let \(d:Q\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, coercive, and \(\sigma\)-strongly convex, with \(\sigma>0\). Then for every \(g\in E^*\),
\[
\min_{x\in Q}\{\langle g,x\rangle+d(x)\}
\]
has a unique minimizer, provided the objective is level bounded; in particular this holds when the stated coercivity dominates the affine term.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compatible strongly convex prox geometry yields a unique affine-master solution once attainment is ensured by level boundedness.
assumptions_latex: \(d\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\sigma\)-strongly convex.
The combined affine-plus-prox objective is level bounded.
knowledge_statements.title: Strongly Convex Prox Geometry Makes Affine Masters Well Posed
Geometry–Oracle Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility of oracle covectors, primal geometry, and prox curvature in model subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be closed and convex, and equip the primal space with \(\|\cdot\|\) and the oracle space with its dual norm \(\|\cdot\|_*\). Geometry and oracle are compatible when every returned covector \(g\) has \(\|g\|_*<\infty\), and the prox function \(d:Q\to\mathbb{R}\) is differentiable and \(\sigma\)-strongly convex relative to \(\|\cdot\|\) for some \(\sigma>0\). Consequently, oracle pairings are continuous and regularized linear-model subproblems are strongly convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Oracle outputs must lie in the dual geometry, while the prox function must be strongly convex in the associated primal norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Compatibility holds exactly when oracle covectors have finite dual norm and \(d\) has strong-convexity modulus \(\sigma>0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cutting-plane algorithm for multiple kernel learning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiple-kernel-learning specialization of a cutting-plane oracle method, with an SVM-dual oracle, linear master problem, and model-gap stopping test.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(t=0\), \(\beta_0\in B\), and \(\varepsilon>0\). At iteration \(t\), choose \(\alpha_t\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{\alpha\in A}S(\alpha,\beta_t)\), set \(D(\beta_t)=S(\alpha_t,\beta_t)\) and \(D'(\beta_t)=(S_1(\alpha_t),\ldots,S_K(\alpha_t))\), increment \(t\), and form \[D_t(\beta)=\max_{i=0,\ldots,t-1}\langle D'(\beta_i),\beta\rangle.\] Choose \(\beta_t\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\beta\in B}D_t(\beta)\), and repeat until \[D(\beta_{t-1})-D_t(\beta_t)\le\varepsilon.\] The oracle subproblem is a convex quadratic program equivalent to the standard SVM dual, and the master subproblem is a linear program.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from feasible kernel weights, the method repeatedly solves the SVM-dual oracle, adds the resulting cut to a maximum-of-cuts model, minimizes that model over the kernel-weight feasible set by linear programming, and stops when the objective-model gap is at most the prescribed tolerance.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint Separating Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A subgradient of a violated convex inequality separates the infeasible query from its feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(c:Q\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex and \(C=\{x\in Q:c(x)\le0\}\). If \(y\in Q\) satisfies \(c(y)>0\) and \(s_y\in\partial c(y)\), then every \(x\in C\) obeys
\[\langle s_y,x-y\rangle\le-c(y)<0.\]
Hence the halfspace \(H_y=\{x:\langle s_y,x-y\rangle\le-c(y)\}\) contains \(C\) and excludes \(y\), providing a verifiable separation certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a violated convex constraint, any subgradient defines a halfspace containing all feasible points and excluding the query.

notation.meaning: separating halfspace generated at the query

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Boundary of Subgradient Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions under which the standard constraint cut need not be a strict global separator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The containment and exclusion conclusions require convex subgradient minorization and strict violation. If \(c(y)\le0\), the query is not excluded by the standard construction. If \(c\) is nonconvex or the supplied vector gives only local first-order information, the affine inequality need not hold for all feasible points. For example, let \(Q=\mathbb R\), \(c(x)=1-x^2\), and \(y=0\). Then \(c(y)=1>0\) and \(c'(y)=0\), but the proposed inequality \(0\le-1\) is impossible although \(C=(-\infty,-1]\cup[1,\infty)\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict violation and global convex minorization are essential; a nonconvex local derivative can fail to separate an infeasible query.
assumptions_latex: The standard cut is formed from the value and first-order information at \(y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Without strict violation and convex subgradient validity, \(C\subseteq H_y\) and \(y\notin H_y\) are not guaranteed.
knowledge_statements.title: Boundary of Subgradient Separation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Separation Margin and Query Distance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative geometry of a convex-constraint separating cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the separating-cut assumptions, suppose additionally that \(C\neq\varnothing\). Then \(s_y\neq0\), and for \[H_y=\{x:\langle s_y,x-y\rangle\le-c(y)\}\] the Euclidean distance from the rejected query to the halfspace is \[\operatorname{dist}(y,H_y)=\frac{c(y)}{\|s_y\|}>0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonempty feasible set, the cut has a nonzero normal and separates the query by violation divided by subgradient norm.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Transport of a Linearization Error Between Centers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Updates the recorded deficit of a fixed supporting cut when the reference center changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fixed supporting cut \(\ell_y(x)=f(y)+\langle g_y,x-y\rangle\), define \(e_y(c)=f(c)-\ell_y(c)\). For any \(c,z\in\operatorname{dom}f\), \[e_y(z)=e_y(c)+f(z)-f(c)-\langle g_y,z-c\rangle.\] Both errors are nonnegative when \(g_y\in\partial f(y)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The error of a fixed cut at a new center equals its old error plus the objective change minus the change predicted by the cut.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: The model deficit of a stored supporting cut measured at a designated reference point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and convex, let \(y,\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}f\), and let \(g_y\in\partial f(y)\). The linearization error of the cut generated at \(y\), measured at \(\bar x\), is
\[e_y(\bar x)=f(\bar x)-f(y)-\langle g_y,\bar x-y\rangle\ge0.\]
For every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), the same affine cut has the reference-centered representation
\[f(y)+\langle g_y,x-y\rangle=f(\bar x)+\langle g_y,x-\bar x\rangle-e_y(\bar x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linearization-error record is the nonnegative gap between a convex objective and a stored supporting cut at a chosen reference point; it also supplies the reference-centered representation of that affine cut.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Cut Validity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact global validity of an objective cut is equivalent to exact subgradient membership.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:Q\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and convex, let \(y\in\operatorname{dom}f\), and let \(g\in\mathbb{R}^n\). The anchored affine function \(\ell(x)=f(y)+\langle g,x-y\rangle\) is an exact valid cut precisely when
\[\ell(x)\le f(x)\qquad\text{for every }x\in Q.\]
Equivalently, exact cut validity holds if and only if \(g\in\partial f(y)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine cut anchored at the exact function value is globally valid exactly when its slope is an exact convex subgradient.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper and convex on convex \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\ell\le f\) on \(Q\) if and only if \(g\in\partial f(y)\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive-error validity characterized by the convex epsilon-subdifferential.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Q\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be convex, let \(f:Q\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and convex, let \(y\in\operatorname{dom}f\), let \(g\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and let \(\varepsilon\ge0\). The slope \(g\) defines an \(\varepsilon\)-valid cut at \(y\) when
\[f(x)\ge f(y)+\langle g,x-y\rangle-\varepsilon\qquad\text{for every }x\in Q.\]
Equivalently, this condition is \(g\in\partial_\varepsilon f(y)\). Thus the affine function \(x\mapsto f(y)+\langle g,x-y\rangle-\varepsilon\) is a global lower model of \(f\) on \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inexact cut with a slope in the ambient dual space is globally valid after lowering its intercept by epsilon exactly when that slope is an epsilon-subgradient.
knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Cut Validity

children.title: Cut-Validity Failure Boundaries

knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Validity Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes exactly when an affine oracle cut ceases to be a global convex minorant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and convex, let \(y\in\operatorname{dom}f\), and define \(h(x)=f(y)+\langle g,x-y\rangle-\varepsilon\), where \(\varepsilon\ge 0\). The cut is globally valid, meaning \(h(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), if and only if \(g\in\partial_{\varepsilon}f(y)\). Thus validity fails precisely when \(g\notin\partial_{\varepsilon}f(y)\): then some \(x\) satisfies \(h(x)>f(x)\), so the cut can exclude points of \(\operatorname{epi}f\). A merely local linearization or an underestimated error allowance does not establish global validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine cut is globally valid exactly when its slope is an epsilon-subgradient with a sufficient error allowance; otherwise it exceeds the objective somewhere and can remove true epigraph points.

source_refs.locator: 3.4.2 Methods of Linear Approximation p. 87

source_witnesses.locator: 3.4.2 Methods of Linear Approximation p. 87

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Underestimated Error Allowance Invalidates a Cut
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp scalar example of the error threshold for an inexact affine cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=x^2\), \(y=0\), and \(g=1\). The affine cut \[h_\varepsilon(x)=x-\varepsilon\] is globally valid exactly when \(\varepsilon\ge\tfrac14\), since \[\sup_{x\in\mathbb R}(x-x^2)=\tfrac14.\] For \(0\le\varepsilon<\tfrac14\), \(h_\varepsilon(1/2)=1/2-\varepsilon>1/4=f(1/2)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For this quadratic and inexact slope, every error allowance below one quarter makes the cut exceed the objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(h_\varepsilon\le f\) on \(\mathbb R\) if and only if \(\varepsilon\ge1/4\).
knowledge_statements.title: Underestimated Error Allowance Invalidates a Cut
Epigraph Outer Approximations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Represents a finite cutting-plane model as an outer polyhedral approximation of a convex epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and convex. Let \(I\) be a nonempty finite index set, and for every \(i\in I\), let \(y_i\in\operatorname{dom}f\) and \(g_i\in\partial f(y_i)\). Define \(h_i(x)=f(y_i)+\langle g_i,x-y_i\rangle\) and \(m_I(x)=\max_{i\in I}h_i(x)\). Then \(m_I(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), so \(\operatorname{epi}f\subseteq\operatorname{epi}m_I\). Moreover, \(\operatorname{epi}m_I=\{(x,t)\in\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}:t\ge h_i(x)\text{ for every }i\in I\}\), which is a polyhedral outer approximation of \(\operatorname{epi}f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonempty finite collection of valid affine cuts, the intersection of the corresponding upper halfspaces contains the true epigraph and equals the epigraph of the maximum-of-cuts model.

notation.meaning: supporting affine cut generated at y_i

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nested Epigraph Refinement Under Cut Addition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adding valid cuts tightens an epigraph outer approximation without excluding the true epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\subseteq J\) be nonempty finite sets of globally valid affine minorants of \(f\), with \(m_I=\max_{i\in I}h_i\) and \(m_J=\max_{j\in J}h_j\). Then \(m_I\le m_J\le f\) pointwise and \(\operatorname{epi}f\subseteq\operatorname{epi}m_J\subseteq\operatorname{epi}m_I\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding valid cuts raises the lower model and shrinks its epigraph while preserving containment of the true epigraph.
assumptions_latex: Every \(h_j\) is an affine global minorant of \(f\).
knowledge_statements.title: Nested Epigraph Refinement Under Cut Addition

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Contact at Exact Cut-Generation Points
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local exactness of the outer epigraph approximation at a retained exact subgradient cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(h_i(x)=f(y_i)+\langle g_i,x-y_i\rangle\), where \(g_i\in\partial f(y_i)\), is retained in \(m_I=\max_{j\in I}h_j\), then \(m_I(y_i)=f(y_i)\). Thus the two epigraphs have the common graph point \((y_i,f(y_i))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A retained exact subgradient cut makes the model epigraph touch the true epigraph at its generation point.
assumptions_latex: The exact cut at \(y_i\) is retained.
knowledge_statements.title: Contact at Exact Cut-Generation Points
Objective Minorant Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the finite maximum of globally valid affine cuts used to underestimate a convex objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and convex, and let \(I\) be a nonempty finite index set. An objective minorant model is \(m_I(x)=\max_{i\in I}\{a_i+\langle g_i,x\rangle\}\), where \(a_i\in\mathbb{R}\), \(g_i\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and \(a_i+\langle g_i,x\rangle\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(i\in I\). Consequently, \(m_I\) is a finite-valued polyhedral convex function satisfying \(m_I(x)\le f(x)\) everywhere. An exact subgradient cut generated at \(y_i\in\operatorname{dom}f\) has \(a_i=f(y_i)-\langle g_i,y_i\rangle\) with \(g_i\in\partial f(y_i)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An objective minorant model is the maximum of a nonempty finite collection of globally valid affine underestimators; it is finite-valued, convex, polyhedral, and never exceeds the objective.
assumptions_latex: \(a_i\in\mathbb{R}\), \(g_i\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and \(a_i+\langle g_i,x\rangle\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(i\in I\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pointwise Ordering Under Cut Addition and Deletion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basic fidelity ordering for finite objective minorant models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(I\subseteq J\) are nonempty finite families of globally valid affine minorants of \(f\), then \(m_I(x)\le m_J(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\). Deleting cuts cannot increase the model; if a deleted exact cut is the unique active cut at its generation point, deletion makes the retained model strictly smaller than \(f\) there.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding valid cuts raises a minorant; deleting cuts lowers it and loses interpolation when the removed exact cut was uniquely active.
assumptions_latex: Every indexed affine function globally minorizes \(f\).
For the strict-loss clause, the deleted exact cut is uniquely active at its generation point.
knowledge_statements.title: Pointwise Ordering Under Cut Addition and Deletion

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Active-Cut Subdifferential Formula
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact subdifferential representation of a finite affine objective minorant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m(x)=\max_{i\in I}\{a_i+\langle g_i,x\rangle\}\) and \(I(x)=\{i\in I:a_i+\langle g_i,x\rangle=m(x)\}\). Then \(\partial m(x)=\operatorname{conv}\{g_i:i\in I(x)\}\). In particular, if all active cuts have the same slope, \(m\) is differentiable at \(x\) with that gradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The subdifferential of a finite cutting-plane minorant is the convex hull of its active cut slopes.
assumptions_latex: Each cut is real-valued and affine.
knowledge_statements.title: Active-Cut Subdifferential Formula

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Affine minorant generated by an active maximizer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies the first-order affine model of a max-represented function with the affine component selected by an active maximizing parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and \(Q_d\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) be nonempty, let \(A:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be linear with adjoint \(A^*\), and let \(g:Q_d\to\mathbb R\). Define \(f(x)=\max_{u\in Q_d}\{\langle Ax,u\rangle-g(u)\}\). Suppose \(f\) is differentiable at \(\bar x\in Q\), and choose \(u(\bar x)\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{u\in Q_d}\{\langle A\bar x,u\rangle-g(u)\}\) such that \(\nabla f(\bar x)=A^*u(\bar x)\). Then, for every \(x\in Q\), \(f(\bar x)+\langle\nabla f(\bar x),x-\bar x\rangle=\langle Ax,u(\bar x)\rangle-g(u(\bar x))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a differentiability point, an active maximizing parameter whose adjoint image is the gradient generates exactly the function's first-order affine minorant.
assumptions_latex: A:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\text{ is linear with adjoint }A^*
\bar x\in Q\text{ and }f\text{ is differentiable at }\bar x
u(\bar x)\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{u\in Q_d}\{\langle A\bar x,u\rangle-g(u)\},\quad \nabla f(\bar x)=A^*u(\bar x)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall x\in Q,\qquad f(\bar x)+\langle\nabla f(\bar x),x-\bar x\rangle=\langle Ax,u(\bar x)\rangle-g(u(\bar x))

knowledge_statements.title: Feasible-Set Outer Approximations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constructs an outer approximation of a convex inequality-defined feasible set from constraint cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q\in\mathbb{N}\), let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be closed and convex, and let \(f_j:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and convex for \(j=1,\ldots,q\). Define \(C=\{x\in X:f_j(x)\le0\text{ for }j=1,\ldots,q\}\). For each \(j\), let \(I_j\) be finite and, for every \(i\in I_j\), choose \(y_{ji}\in\operatorname{dom}f_j\) and \(g_{ji}\in\partial f_j(y_{ji})\). Set \(h_{ji}(x)=f_j(y_{ji})+\langle g_{ji},x-y_{ji}\rangle\) and \(C_I=\{x\in X:h_{ji}(x)\le0\text{ for every }j\text{ and }i\in I_j\}\). Then \(C\subseteq C_I\), although points in \(C_I\) need not satisfy the original nonlinear inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replacing finitely many convex-constraint conditions by supporting cuts produces a convex outer approximation containing every feasible point, though it may also contain infeasible points.
assumptions_latex: Each \(I_j\) is finite, and \(y_{ji}\in\operatorname{dom}f_j\), \(g_{ji}\in\partial f_j(y_{ji})\) for every \(i\in I_j\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nested Feasible-Set Refinement Under Constraint-Cut Addition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotone tightening of constraint-cut outer approximations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each constraint \(j\), let \(I_j\subseteq J_j\) be finite families of globally valid affine minorants of \(f_j\), and let \(C_I,C_J\) be the corresponding cut-defined sets. Then \(C\subseteq C_J\subseteq C_I\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding valid constraint cuts shrinks the relaxation without removing any truly feasible point.
assumptions_latex: Every added affine cut globally minorizes its corresponding convex constraint function.

notation.meaning: outer approximations before and after adding cuts

knowledge_statements.title: Nested Feasible-Set Refinement Under Constraint-Cut Addition
Full-Memory Cut Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a cutting-plane model that permanently retains every valid cut generated so far.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose iteration \(k\) has generated globally valid affine cuts \(h_1,\ldots,h_k\) satisfying \(h_i(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\). The full-memory cut model is \(m_k(x)=\max_{1\le i\le k}h_i(x)\). After generating \(h_{k+1}\), it is updated by \(m_{k+1}(x)=\max\{m_k(x),h_{k+1}(x)\}\). Hence \(m_k\le m_{k+1}\le f\) pointwise: the lower model improves monotonically, while its number of explicitly stored cuts grows by one whenever a nonredundant new cut is retained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A full-memory model keeps every generated valid cut, so its maximum-of-cuts minorant increases pointwise and its stored representation can grow with every iteration.
