knowledge_statements.statement_title: Redundant-Cut Characterization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed deletion test for one stored cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m(x)=\max_{i\in I}h_i(x)\). A cut \(h_j\) can be deleted without changing this represented function exactly when \(h_j(x)\leq\max_{i\in I\setminus\{j\}}h_i(x)\) everywhere.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut is functionally redundant exactly when the other cuts dominate it everywhere.
assumptions_latex: Every \(h_i\) is affine on the common model domain.
review_flags: Deleting cuts is a representation-reduction or restricted-memory operation, whereas this leaf defines permanent retention of every generated cut.
knowledge_statements.title: Redundant-Cut Characterization

intermediate_metadata.reason: The accepted seed exhausts the locally owned full-memory definition, monotone strengthening, validity, and storage-growth boundary. The proposed redundancy-deletion condition is deferred as canonically belonging to representation reduction or restricted memory. Kelley iterations, truncation tradeoffs, multiple-cut batches, and component disaggregation were excluded as adjacent scopes.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Proximal-Master Aggregation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual-weight aggregation preserving the current proximal-master solution and value while compressing active cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m(x)=\max_{i\in I}(a_i^{\mathsf T}x+b_i)\), let \(t>0\), and let \(x^+\) minimize \(m(x)+\frac1{2t}\|x-c\|^2\). If \(A=\{i:a_i^{\mathsf T}x^++b_i=m(x^+)\}\), then there exist \(\lambda_i\geq0\), \(i\in A\), with \(\sum_{i\in A}\lambda_i=1\) and \(\sum_{i\in A}\lambda_i a_i+(x^+-c)/t=0\). For \(\bar h=\sum_{i\in A}\lambda_i(a_i^{\mathsf T}x+b_i)\), one has \(\bar h\leq m\), \(\bar h(x^+)=m(x^+)\), and \(x^+\) minimizes \(\bar h(x)+\frac1{2t}\|x-c\|^2\) with the same optimal value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An optimality-multiplier convex combination of active cuts compresses them to one valid cut while preserving the current proximal-master solution and value.
assumptions_latex: All cuts are finite-valued affine functions.

notation.meaning: cuts active at the proximal-master minimizer

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Proximal-Master Aggregation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Arbitrary Truncation Can Destroy Inter-Iteration Monotonicity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete bounded-memory example showing the effect of deleting a previously active cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=|x|\). At iteration \(k\), retain \(h_-(x)=-x\) and \(h_+(x)=x\), so \(m_k(x)=|x|\). If a memory-one rule discards \(h_-\) and retains only \(h_+\), then \(m_{k+1}(x)=x\le |x|=f(x)\), but \(m_{k+1}(-1)=-1<1=m_k(-1)\). Thus validity survives while \(m_k\le m_{k+1}\) fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the absolute-value objective, deleting one supporting cut leaves a valid one-cut model but lowers the model on a half-line.
assumptions_latex: The memory bound permits retaining only one of the two cuts.

notation.meaning: the supporting cut x maps to -x
the supporting cut x maps to x

knowledge_statements.title: Arbitrary Truncation Can Destroy Inter-Iteration Monotonicity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Validity Does Not Imply Fidelity Preservation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between the minorant invariant and pointwise or inter-iteration fidelity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_k\) be a finite nonempty family of retained affine cuts satisfying \(h\le f\), and set \(m_k=\max_{h\in C_k}h\). Then \(m_k\le f\) follows from cut validity. In contrast, \(m_{k-1}\le m_k\) requires the new representation to dominate the preceding model; arbitrary deletion need not do so. Likewise, an aggregate preserving one proximal-master solution and value need not preserve the discarded model pointwise away from that solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Valid retained cuts always produce a valid lower model, but validity alone guarantees neither monotone model growth nor full-memory fidelity.
assumptions_latex: Each retained cut is a global affine minorant of \(f\).
Each retained family is finite and nonempty.
knowledge_statements.title: Validity Does Not Imply Fidelity Preservation
Restricted-Memory Cut Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a valid minorant maintained with a uniformly bounded number of explicit or aggregate cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\ge1\) be a memory bound. At iteration \(k\), choose an index set \(I_k\) with \(|I_k|\le B\) and retain affine cuts \(h_i\le f\) for \(i\in I_k\); optionally, a discarded collection may be replaced by an aggregate affine cut \(\bar h_k\le f\). The restricted-memory model is \(m_k(x)=\max\bigl(\{h_i(x):i\in I_k\}\cup\{\bar h_k(x)\}\bigr)\), omitting the aggregate when absent. The bound \(m_k\le f\) is preserved, but pointwise monotonicity between successive models is not guaranteed unless the aggregation and retention rules impose it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A restricted-memory model stores at most a fixed number of cuts, possibly plus a valid aggregate; it remains a minorant but need not improve monotonically.
assumptions_latex: Every retained or aggregate cut is a global minorant of \(f\).

notation.meaning: retained cut indices at iteration k

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Separate Cuts Dominate Their Aggregate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fidelity comparison between retaining simultaneous cuts separately and replacing them by one convex aggregate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h_r\leq f\) for \(r\in R\), where \(R\) is finite and nonempty, and let \(\lambda_r\geq0\) with \(\sum_{r\in R}\lambda_r=1\). The aggregate cut \(\bar h=\sum_{r\in R}\lambda_rh_r\) is valid, and \(\bar h(x)\leq\max_{r\in R}h_r(x)\leq f(x)\) for every \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex aggregate of simultaneous valid cuts remains valid but is pointwise dominated by their separate maximum.
assumptions_latex: Each \(h_r\) is an affine global minorant of \(f\).
\(\lambda\) belongs to the probability simplex on \(R\).
knowledge_statements.title: Separate Cuts Dominate Their Aggregate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Batch Insertion Is Independent of Retention Policy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates multiple-cut batch insertion from subsequent full- or restricted-memory management.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_{k-1}\) be the cuts retained before oracle call \(k\), and let \(H_k=\{h_{k,r}:r\in R_k\}\) be a finite nonempty batch of valid cuts for the same objective. Multiple-cut insertion forms the pool \(C_{k-1}\cup H_k\), with every member of \(H_k\) represented separately. A subsequent retention map \(\mathcal R_k\) may retain, discard, or validly aggregate cuts. Thus \(C_k=\mathcal R_k(C_{k-1}\cup H_k)\); full memory keeps the entire pool, while restricted memory may return a smaller valid representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiple-cut describes separate insertion of a batch, not its storage lifetime; full- or restricted-memory management may be applied afterward.
assumptions_latex: Every \(h_{k,r}\) is a valid affine minorant of the same objective.
Every aggregate produced by \(\mathcal R_k\) is a valid minorant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_k=\mathcal R_k(C_{k-1}\cup H_k)\), with the members of \(H_k\) separately represented before retention.

notation.meaning: batch of cuts returned at iteration k

knowledge_statements.title: Batch Insertion Is Independent of Retention Policy
Multiple-Cut Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Represents an iteration that adds several simultaneous oracle cuts to one maximum-of-cuts model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose oracle call \(k\) returns a finite family of affine functions \(h_{k,r}\), indexed by \(r\in R_k\), each satisfying \(h_{k,r}(x)\le f(x)\) for all \(x\). Given a previous minorant \(m_{k-1}\le f\), the multiple-cut update is \(m_k(x)=\max\bigl\{m_{k-1}(x),\max_{r\in R_k}h_{k,r}(x)\bigr\}\). Therefore \(m_{k-1}\le m_k\le f\) pointwise. Unlike a single aggregate-cut update, this representation preserves each returned affine inequality separately in the master problem, subject to any later memory-management rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multiple-cut update inserts several valid oracle cuts separately into the model, preserving their individual inequalities and monotonically strengthening the minorant while retained.

notation.meaning: cuts returned by oracle call k

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Disaggregate Model Dominates Aligned Aggregate Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fidelity comparison for separate component models of a finite-sum objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f=\sum_{r=1}^R f_r\), and for a common finite nonempty index set \(I\) let \(h_{r,i}\leq f_r\). Define \(m_D(x)=\sum_{r=1}^R\max_{i\in I}h_{r,i}(x)\) and \(m_A(x)=\max_{i\in I}\sum_{r=1}^R h_{r,i}(x)\). Then \(m_A(x)\leq m_D(x)\leq f(x)\) for every \(x\). The first inequality can be strict when different components attain their maxima at different indices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Summing separate componentwise cut maxima is at least as strong as taking the maximum of aligned summed cuts and can be strictly stronger.
assumptions_latex: \(h_{r,i}(x)\leq f_r(x)\) for every component, index, and point.
knowledge_statements.title: Disaggregate Model Dominates Aligned Aggregate Cuts

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Componentwise Disaggregate Updates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle-update rule for a finite-sum disaggregate model when selected components are evaluated.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m_k=\sum_{r=1}^R m_{r,k}\), where \(m_{r,k}\le f_r\). If iteration \(k\) evaluates a nonempty set \(S_k\subseteq\{1,\ldots,R\}\) and obtains affine cuts \(h_{r,k}\le f_r\) for \(r\in S_k\), set \(m_{r,k+1}=\max\{m_{r,k},h_{r,k}\}\) for \(r\in S_k\) and \(m_{r,k+1}=m_{r,k}\) otherwise. Then \(m_k\le m_{k+1}\le f=\sum_{r=1}^R f_r\). Simultaneous updating is the case \(S_k=\{1,\ldots,R\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A partial disaggregate update strengthens only evaluated component models; simultaneous updating strengthens them all. Componentwise-valid cuts preserve the finite-sum minorant.

notation.meaning: new valid cut for component r

knowledge_statements.title: Componentwise Disaggregate Updates
Disaggregate Cut Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Models a finite-sum objective by maintaining a separate maximum-of-cuts minorant for each component.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\sum_{r=1}^{R}f_r(x)\), where every \(f_r\) is proper and convex on a common convex domain. For each component, let \(h_{r,i}\le f_r\) be valid affine cuts indexed by a finite set \(I_r\), and define \(m_r(x)=\max_{i\in I_r}h_{r,i}(x)\). The disaggregate model is \(m(x)=\sum_{r=1}^{R}m_r(x)\), and it satisfies \(m(x)\le f(x)\) throughout the common domain. Its epigraph master may introduce variables \(t_r\) with inequalities \(t_r\ge h_{r,i}(x)\) and minimize \(\sum_{r=1}^{R}t_r\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite-sum objective, a disaggregate model keeps separate cut maxima for the components and sums them, producing a valid structured minorant.

notation.meaning: cut indices retained for component r

knowledge_statements.title: Linear Cutting-Plane Masters
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Specifies the unstabilized linear master for minimizing a polyhedral cutting-plane minorant over a polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a nonempty polyhedron \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), a nonempty finite index set \(I_k\), and affine cuts \(h_i(x)=a_i+\langle g_i,x\rangle\) for \(i\in I_k\), consider the linear program \(\inf\{t:x\in X,\ t\ge h_i(x)\text{ for every }i\in I_k\}\). If it has an optimal solution, choose \((x^{k+1},t^{k+1})\) from its solution set; equivalently, \(x^{k+1}\) minimizes \(m_k(x)=\max_{i\in I_k}h_i(x)\) over \(X\), and \(t^{k+1}=m_k(x^{k+1})\). If the program is infeasible or unbounded below, report that status instead.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The linear master minimizes an epigraph variable subject to a nonempty finite collection of retained affine cuts and polyhedral constraints; it returns a next oracle point and model value only when an optimum exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\text{If an optimum exists,}\quad (x^{k+1},t^{k+1})\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X,\,t}\{t:t\ge h_i(x)\ \forall i\in I_k\}.\]

notation.meaning: maximum of the retained affine cuts
epigraph variable for the cut model

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Feasibility and Recession Boundary of the Linear Master
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes feasibility, attainment, and unboundedness for the finite-cut linear master over a nonempty polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty polyhedron and \(m(x)=\max_{i\in I}\{a_i+\langle g_i,x\rangle\}\) for a nonempty finite set \(I\). The epigraph master is feasible. It is unbounded below if and only if there exists \(d\in\operatorname{rec}X\) such that \(\max_{i\in I}\langle g_i,d\rangle<0\). Otherwise its finite infimum is attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The linear master is automatically feasible; it is unbounded exactly when a feasible recession direction strictly decreases every cut, and otherwise it attains a finite optimum.

notation.meaning: recession cone of the feasible polyhedron

knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility and Recession Boundary of the Linear Master

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quadratic-Master Optimality Inclusion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient primal optimality certificate for a finite-cut Euclidean stabilized master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A point \(x^+\in X\) minimizes \(m(x)+(\rho/2)\|x-c\|^2\) if and only if there are weights \(\lambda_i\ge0\), supported on the cuts active at \(x^+\), with \(\sum_i\lambda_i=1\), and \(v\in N_X(x^+)\) such that \(0=\sum_i\lambda_i g_i+\rho(x^+-c)+v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimality is certified by balancing an aggregate active-cut slope, the proximal displacement, and a feasible-set normal.

notation.meaning: cuts active at the candidate minimizer

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic-Master Optimality Inclusion

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Existence and Uniqueness of the Quadratically Stabilized Trial Point
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Well-posedness supplied by positive Euclidean stabilization of a finite cutting-plane model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, let \(m\) be the maximum of a nonempty finite family of real-valued affine functions, let \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), and let \(\rho>0\). Then \(m+(\rho/2)\|\cdot-c\|_2^2+\delta_X\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, coercive, and \(\rho\)-strongly convex on its domain; hence it has exactly one minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive Euclidean stabilization makes a finite cutting-plane master coercive and strongly convex, yielding one unique trial point.
assumptions_latex: \(m\) is a nonempty finite maximum of real-valued affine functions.
knowledge_statements.title: Existence and Uniqueness of the Quadratically Stabilized Trial Point

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Positive Curvature Is Essential for Uniform Master Well-Posedness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp boundary for the unconditional well-posedness supplied by quadratic stabilization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the stabilization weight is zero, a finite affine cutting-plane model need not attain a minimum or have a unique minimizer. With \(X=\mathbb R\), \(m(x)=-x\), and \(\rho=0\), the master is unbounded below; with \(m(x)=0\), every point minimizes it. Thus \(\rho>0\) is essential for an unconditional existence-and-uniqueness guarantee over arbitrary nonempty closed convex \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without positive quadratic curvature, the master may be unbounded or have infinitely many minimizers.
knowledge_statements.title: Positive Curvature Is Essential for Uniform Master Well-Posedness

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Proximal-Mapping Representation of the Stabilized Master
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identification of the quadratic cutting-plane master as a proximal mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q=m+\delta_X\), where \(m:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is a finite convex cutting-plane model and \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex. For \(\rho>0\), \[x_\rho(c):=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\left\{m(x)+\frac\rho2\|x-c\|^2\right\}=\operatorname{prox}_{q/\rho}(c).\] Consequently, \(c\mapsto x_\rho(c)\) is firmly nonexpansive and hence \(1\)-Lipschitz.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratically stabilized master is the proximal mapping of the cutting-plane model plus the feasible-set indicator, so its trial point depends firmly nonexpansively on the center.
assumptions_latex: \(m:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is finite and convex.
\(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_\rho=\operatorname{prox}_{(m+\delta_X)/\rho}\), and \(x_\rho\) is firmly nonexpansive as a function of the center.

notation.meaning: stabilized-master trial point centered at c

knowledge_statements.title: Proximal-Mapping Representation of the Stabilized Master

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Trial-Point and Stability-Center Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interface between solving the stabilized master and updating the bundle center.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Solving the master produces \[x^{k+1}=\arg\min_{x\in X}\left\{m_k(x)+\frac{\rho_k}{2}\|x-c_k\|^2\right\}.\] This does not imply \(c_{k+1}=x^{k+1}\): a separate serious/null-step rule may accept the trial point as the new center or retain \(c_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proximal master computes a trial point; center acceptance is a separate algorithmic decision.
assumptions_latex: The finite-cut stabilized master satisfies the stated well-posedness assumptions.
knowledge_statements.title: Trial-Point and Stability-Center Separation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite-Cut Epigraph Form of the Quadratically Stabilized Master
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Epigraph formulation of the finite-cut Euclidean proximal master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(m(x)=\max_{i\in I}\{a_i+\langle g_i,x\rangle\}\) for nonempty finite \(I\), then \[\min_{x\in X}\left\{m(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}\|x-c\|_2^2\right\}=\min_{x\in X,t\in\mathbb R}\left\{t+\frac{\rho}{2}\|x-c\|_2^2:t\ge a_i+\langle g_i,x\rangle\ \forall i\in I\right\}.\] The optimal \(x\)-components coincide and every optimal pair satisfies \(t=m(x)\). When \(X\) is polyhedral, the epigraph problem is a strongly convex quadratic program in its \(x\)-component.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One epigraph variable converts the finite-cut proximal master into an equivalent convex problem; it is a quadratic program when the feasible set is polyhedral.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.

notation.meaning: epigraph variable for the cutting-plane model

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Cut Epigraph Form of the Quadratically Stabilized Master
Quadratically Stabilized Masters
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Specifies a proximal cutting-plane master centered at the current stability center.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a closed convex set \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), a polyhedral minorant \(m_k\), a center \(c_k\in X\), and a parameter \(\rho_k>0\), compute \(x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\{m_k(x)+(\rho_k/2)\|x-c_k\|_2^2\}\). In epigraph form, solve \((x^{k+1},t^{k+1})\in\operatorname*{argmin}\{t+(\rho_k/2)\|x-c_k\|_2^2:x\in X,\ t\ge h_i(x)\text{ for every retained cut }i\}\). Output \(x^{k+1}\) as the trial point; the rule accepting it as a new center is external to this master.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The stabilized master adds a positive quadratic penalty around a stability center to the cutting-plane model and returns the unique trial point when a solution exists.
assumptions_latex: \(m_k\) is a proper polyhedral convex minorant on \(X\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Trust-Region Localization Does Not Ensure Uniqueness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shows that compact trust-region localization alone does not make a polyhedral master strictly convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(X=\mathbb R\), \(c=0\), \(\Delta=1\), and the one-cut model \(m(x)=0\), every \(x\in[-1,1]\) solves the trust-region master.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constant cutting-plane model over a nontrivial trust region has infinitely many minimizers.
knowledge_statements.title: Trust-Region Localization Does Not Ensure Uniqueness

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Existence of a Trust-Region Master Solution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Well-posedness of finite cutting-plane model minimization over a finite-radius norm ball.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be closed, let \(c\in X\), let \(0<\Delta<\infty\), let \(\|\cdot\|\) be any norm, and let \(m\) be a finite continuous cutting-plane model. Then \(X\cap\{x:\|x-c\|\le\Delta\}\) is nonempty and compact, so \(m\) attains its minimum there.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite-radius trust region centered at a feasible point makes the master feasible and compact, so a finite continuous cut model attains a minimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Existence of a Trust-Region Master Solution

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Trust-Region Master Normal-Cone Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient optimality condition including the feasible-region and trust-region normals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B=\{x:\|x-c\|\le\Delta\}\), let \(C=X\cap B\), and let \(m:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be convex. A feasible point \(x^+\in C\) minimizes \(m\) over \(C\) if and only if \(0\in\partial m(x^+)+N_C(x^+)\). If \(\operatorname{ri}X\cap\operatorname{ri}B\ne\varnothing\), this is equivalent to the existence of \(g\in\partial m(x^+)\), \(v\in N_X(x^+)\), and \(w\in N_B(x^+)\) such that \(g+v+w=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimality balances a model subgradient with the normal to the feasible trust region; under a relative-interior qualification, that normal separates into feasible-set and ball normals.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(m:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is finite and convex.

notation.meaning: convex normal cone to C at x

knowledge_statements.title: Trust-Region Master Normal-Cone Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Radius Monotonicity of the Trust-Region Master Value
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependence of the optimal cutting-plane model value on the trust-region radius.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\Delta>0\), define \[\theta(\Delta):=\min\{m(x):x\in X,\ \|x-c\|\le\Delta\}.\] Whenever these minima are finite and attained, \(0<\Delta_1\le\Delta_2\) implies \[\theta(\Delta_2)\le\theta(\Delta_1).\] If \(c\in X\), then \(\theta(\Delta)\le m(c)\), and the predicted model reduction \(m(c)-\theta(\Delta)\) is nonnegative and nondecreasing in \(\Delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Enlarging a trust region cannot worsen its optimal model value or decrease the predicted model reduction from a feasible center.
assumptions_latex: \(m\) is finite on the relevant feasible trust regions.

notation.meaning: optimal trust-region master value at radius Delta

knowledge_statements.title: Radius Monotonicity of the Trust-Region Master Value

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Trust-Region Master and Globalization Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interface separating the localized model solve from acceptance and radius management.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A solution \(x^{k+1}\in\arg\min\{m_k(x):x\in X,\ \|x-c_k\|\le\Delta_k\}\) is a trial point. Its acceptance as a new center and the choice of \(\Delta_{k+1}\) require a separate actual-to-predicted reduction rule; master optimality alone implies neither decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solving the trust-region master does not itself accept the trial point or determine the next radius.
assumptions_latex: The trust-region master attains its minimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Trust-Region Master and Globalization Separation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite-Cut Epigraph Form of the Trust-Region Master
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Epigraph formulation for a finite cutting-plane model over a norm trust region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(m(x)=\max_{i\in I}\{a_i+\langle g_i,x\rangle\}\) and \(B(c,\Delta)=\{x:\|x-c\|\le\Delta\}\), \[\min_{x\in X\cap B(c,\Delta)}m(x)=\min_{x,t}\{t:x\in X,\ \|x-c\|\le\Delta,\ t\ge a_i+\langle g_i,x\rangle\ \forall i\in I\}.\] The optimal \(x\)-components coincide and every optimal pair satisfies \(t=m(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The finite-cut trust-region master has an equivalent epigraph formulation with one inequality per cut and a norm-ball constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X\cap B(c,\Delta)}m(x)=\{x:(x,m(x))\text{ solves the epigraph problem}\}.\]
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Cut Epigraph Form of the Trust-Region Master
Trust-Region Masters
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Specifies cutting-plane model minimization within a norm ball around a designated center.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a closed convex set \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), a proper polyhedral model \(m_k\), a center \(c_k\in X\), a radius \(\Delta_k>0\), and a norm \(\|\cdot\|\), compute \(x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}\{m_k(x):x\in X,\ \|x-c_k\|\le\Delta_k\}\). In epigraph form, minimize \(t\) subject to \(x\in X\), \(\|x-c_k\|\le\Delta_k\), and \(t\ge h_i(x)\) for every retained cut. Output the minimizer as the trial point; acceptance and radius adjustment require a separate actual-versus-predicted reduction rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The trust-region master minimizes the cut model inside a norm ball centered at the current reference point; acceptance and radius updates are separate decisions.
assumptions_latex: \(m_k\) is proper and polyhedral on the trust region.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: KKT Certificate for a Polyhedral Level Master
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimality test for projection onto affine cut inequalities and a closed convex working set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m(x)=\max_{i\in I}(a_i+g_i^{\mathsf T}x)\), let \(L=\{x\in X:a_i+g_i^{\mathsf T}x\le\ell\ \forall i\}\ne\varnothing\), and assume a constraint qualification ensuring the normal-cone sum rule. A feasible point \(x^+\in L\) equals \(P_L(c)\) if and only if there exist \(\lambda_i\ge0\) and \(v\in N_X(x^+)\) such that \[x^+-c+\sum_{i\in I}\lambda_i g_i+v=0,\qquad \lambda_i(a_i+g_i^{\mathsf T}x^+-\ell)=0\quad\forall i.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feasibility, normal-cone stationarity, and complementary slackness certify a polyhedral level projection.
assumptions_latex: A constraint qualification permits the stated normal-cone representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^+=P_L(c)\) if and only if suitable \((\lambda,v)\) satisfy feasibility, stationarity, and complementarity.

notation.meaning: normal cone of the working set at the trial point
working-set normal in the stationarity condition

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Existence and Uniqueness of the Level Projection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Well-posedness of a level-constrained Euclidean master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, let \(m\) be closed and convex, let \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), and suppose \(L=\{x\in X:m(x)\le\ell\}\ne\varnothing\). Then \(L\) is closed and convex, and \[x^+=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in L}\frac12\|x-c\|^2\] exists and is unique. Moreover, \(x^+=c\) exactly when \(c\in L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonempty closed convex model-level set has a unique Euclidean projection of the center; the center is unchanged exactly when it already satisfies the level.

notation.meaning: Euclidean projection of c onto L

knowledge_statements.title: Existence and Uniqueness of the Level Projection
Level-Constrained Masters
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Specifies a proximal master constrained by a prescribed cutting-plane model level.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a closed convex set \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), a polyhedral minorant \(m_k\), a center \(c_k\in X\), and a level \(\ell_k\) such that \(L_k=\{x\in X:m_k(x)\le\ell_k\}\) is nonempty, compute \(x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in L_k}(1/2)\|x-c_k\|_2^2\). When \(m_k(x)=\max_{i\in I_k}h_i(x)\), the level constraint is equivalently \(h_i(x)\le\ell_k\) for every \(i\in I_k\). Output the projection as the next trial point; if \(L_k\) is empty, report level infeasibility and revise the level.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A level master projects the current center onto the set where every retained cut lies below a chosen level, reporting infeasibility when that set is empty.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Master Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: LP dual of a finite cutting-plane master over a polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\le b\}\) and \(m(x)=\max_{1\le i\le k}\{a_i+g_i^\top x\}\). If the primal master has a finite attained value and satisfies linear-programming strong duality, then
\[
\min_{x\in X,\,t\in\mathbb R}\{t:a_i+g_i^\top x\le t\ \forall i\}
=
\max_{\lambda,\mu}\left\{\sum_{i=1}^k\lambda_i a_i-b^\top\mu:\lambda\ge0,\ \mu\ge0,\ \sum_{i=1}^k\lambda_i=1,\ \sum_{i=1}^k\lambda_i g_i+A^\top\mu=0\right\}.
\]
Thus dual cut weights form a convex combination whose aggregate slope is balanced by a normal to \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The linear master equals a dual maximization over convex weights on cuts and nonnegative multipliers for the polyhedral feasible-set constraints.
assumptions_latex: The primal master has a finite attained optimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_{\mathrm P}=v_{\mathrm D}\) with the displayed primal and dual formulations.

notation.meaning: nonnegative multiplier assigned to cut i
nonnegative multiplier for the polyhedral constraints

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linear-Master Primal–Dual Optimality Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complementary-slackness certificate for the polyhedral linear cutting-plane master and its dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the notation of Dual Master Representations, let \((x,t)\) be primal feasible and \((\lambda,\mu)\) dual feasible. They are optimal with equal value if and only if \[\lambda_i\bigl(t-a_i-g_i^{\mathsf T}x\bigr)=0\quad(i=1,\ldots,k),\qquad \mu_j\bigl(b_j-A_jx\bigr)=0\quad(j=1,\ldots,p).\] Thus positive cut weights occur only on active cuts, and positive feasible-set multipliers occur only on active rows of \(Ax\le b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feasible primal and dual master points certify optimality when their cut and feasible-set multipliers satisfy complementary slackness.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Piecewise-Linear Cutting-Plane Underestimators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite cutting-plane models of convex objective and constraint functions formed from sampled subgradients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X=\{x_j\}_{j=0}^{\infty}\subseteq Q\). For \(k\ge 0\), choose \(g(x_j)\in\partial f(x_j)\) and \(\bar g(x_j)\in\partial\bar f(x_j)\) for \(0\le j\le k\), and define
\[
\hat f_k(X;x)=\max_{0\le j\le k}\left[f(x_j)+\langle g(x_j),x-x_j\rangle\right],
\]
\[
\check f_k(X;x)=\max_{0\le j\le k}\left[\bar f(x_j)+\langle\bar g(x_j),x-x_j\rangle\right].
\]
If \(f\) and \(\bar f\) are convex, then for every \(x\in Q\),
\[
\hat f_k(X;x)\le f(x),\qquad \check f_k(X;x)\le\bar f(x).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The maximum of the accumulated subgradient affine minorants defines a piecewise-linear cutting-plane model. For convex f and bar f, the respective models are global lower bounds on Q.
assumptions_latex: g(x_j)\in\partial f(x_j),\quad \bar g(x_j)\in\partial\bar f(x_j)\quad(0\le j\le k)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall x\in Q:\quad \hat f_k(X;x)\le f(x),\qquad \check f_k(X;x)\le\bar f(x).

source_refs.locator: 3.4.2 Methods of Linear Approximation p. 87

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(k\ge1\), let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), and let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper and convex. For points \(y_i\in X\cap\operatorname{dom}f\) and subgradients \(g_i\in\partial f(y_i)\), define
\[
m_k(x):=\max_{1\le i\le k}\{f(y_i)+g_i^\top(x-y_i)\}.
\]
Then \(m_k(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in X\). Consequently, if the master value is finite,
\[
L_k:=\inf_{x\in X}m_k(x)\le f^*:=\inf_{x\in X}f(x).
\]
The stored cuts and feasible-set description, together with a verifiable certificate of the master value, certify \(L_k\) as a global lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimizing globally valid supporting cuts over the original feasible set produces a certified lower bound on the true optimal value; any claimed optimizer or optimal value must itself be verifiably certified.
knowledge_statements.title: Master-Value Lower Bounds

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Upper-bound certificate supplied by the best evaluated feasible point.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 1. Fundamentals of the Theory and Methods of Unconstrained Minimization p. 2

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(k\ge1\), let \(X\neq\varnothing\), and let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\). For evaluated points \(y_1,\ldots,y_k\in X\) with finite objective values, choose
\[
i_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{1\le i\le k}f(y_i),\qquad \bar x_k:=y_{i_k},\qquad U_k:=f(\bar x_k),
\]
and define \(f^*:=\inf_{x\in X}f(x)\). Then
\[
f^*\le U_k.
\]
After evaluating another feasible point \(y_{k+1}\in X\) with finite value, update
\[
U_{k+1}:=\min\{U_k,f(y_{k+1})\}\le U_k.
\]
The incumbent point and its recorded objective evaluation form an upper-bound certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a function defined on the feasible set, the smallest finite objective value among evaluated feasible points is an upper bound on the optimum and cannot increase as points are added.
knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent Upper Bounds

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 1. Fundamentals of the Theory and Methods of Unconstrained Minimization p. 2

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Feasibility and Evaluation Requirements for Upper Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary for treating a recorded objective value as an incumbent upper bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A finite recorded value \(\widehat f(y)\) certifies an upper bound on \(f^*:=\inf_{x\in X}f(x)\) when \(y\in X\) and \(\widehat f(y)\ge f(y)\). Without feasibility or this one-sided evaluation guarantee, the claim can fail. For \(X=\{1\}\) and \(f(x)=x^2\), one has \(f^*=1\), while the infeasible point \(y=0\) has value \(0\); reporting \(\widehat f(1)=0\) likewise underestimates the feasible value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certified incumbent requires a feasible point and an exact or one-sided-overestimating objective evaluation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y\in X\) and \(\widehat f(y)\ge f(y)\) imply \(f^*\le\widehat f(y)\); absent either condition the implication is not guaranteed.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility and Evaluation Requirements for Upper Bounds

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute primal-lower-bound gap for a valid cutting-plane bound pair.

source_refs.locator: 3.4.2 Methods of Linear Approximation p. 87

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given finite bounds \(L_k\le f^*\le U_k\), define the absolute model gap by
\[
G_k^{\mathrm{abs}}:=U_k-L_k.
\]
Then
\[
G_k^{\mathrm{abs}}\ge0,\qquad 0\le U_k-f^*\le G_k^{\mathrm{abs}}.
\]
For every tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\), the condition \(G_k^{\mathrm{abs}}\le\varepsilon\) certifies that the incumbent is absolutely \(\varepsilon\)-optimal. Both bounds must concern the same objective and feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The upper bound minus a valid lower bound bounds the incumbent's absolute suboptimality and, for any nonnegative tolerance, gives an absolute stopping certificate.
knowledge_statements.title: Absolute Model Gaps

notation.meaning: relative model gap under the stated normalization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scale-normalized gap using an explicit denominator convention.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For finite bounds \(L_k\le f^*\le U_k\), define
\[
G_k^{\mathrm{rel}}:=\frac{U_k-L_k}{\max\{1,|U_k|\}}.
\]
This quantity is nonnegative and its denominator is positive. For every \(\varepsilon\ge0\),
\[
G_k^{\mathrm{rel}}\le\varepsilon
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
0\le U_k-f^*\le\varepsilon\max\{1,|U_k|\}.
\]
This is a mixed absolute-relative accuracy convention; any different denominator defines a different convention and must be stated explicitly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalizing the valid bound gap by the maximum of one and the incumbent magnitude gives a zero-safe mixed absolute-relative stopping certificate for every nonnegative tolerance.

Their absolute gaps decrease from \(101\) to \(2\), but for \[G^{\mathrm{rel}}(L,U)=\frac{U-L}{\max\{1,|U|\}}\] the normalized gaps increase from \(101/100\) to \(2\).

Lower-Bound Validity Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions under which a master value ceases to be a global lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The implication \(L_k:=\inf_{x\in X}m_k(x)\le f^*\) requires \(m_k(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in X\) and minimization over all of \(X\). It may fail if cuts are merely local, invalid, or computed inexactly without certified error corrections. It also fails for a restricted master: if \(Y_k\subsetneq X\), then \(\inf_{x\in Y_k}m_k(x)\) need not be below \(f^*\). Likewise, the raw objective value of a proximal, trust-region, or level-stabilized master is not automatically a lower bound for the original problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A master value is not a global lower bound when cuts lack global validity, the domain is restricted, or stabilization changes the minimized objective.
assumptions_latex: The claimed bound is obtained from a cutting-plane master.
At least one global-validity or full-domain requirement is absent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{x\in Y_k}m_k(x)\le f^*\) is not guaranteed when \(Y_k\subsetneq X\) or \(m_k\nleq f\) on \(X\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: The extract specifies an absolute model-gap stopping rule but provides no termination or convergence guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose $x_0\in X$ and $\varepsilon>0$. For $t=1,2,\ldots$, evaluate $f(x_{t-1})$ and a subgradient $f'(x_{t-1})$, form $f_t(x)=\max_{0\le i\le t-1}\{f(x_i)+\langle f'(x_i),x-x_i\rangle\}$, and select $x_t\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}f_t(x)$. Stop when $f(x_t)-f_t(x_t)\le\varepsilon$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Kelley's method accumulates affine subgradient minorants, minimizes their pointwise maximum over X, and stops when the objective-to-model gap at the new master solution is at most epsilon.
assumptions_latex: f'(x_i)\text{ satisfies }f(x)\ge f(x_i)+\langle f'(x_i),x-x_i\rangle\quad\forall x\in X

notation.meaning: oracle subgradient at the query point

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subgradient-oracle construction of one globally valid affine cut.

source_refs.locator: 3.4.2 Methods of Linear Approximation p. 87

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper and convex, let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), and let the current model satisfy \(m_{k-1}(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in X\). Input a query point \(y_k\in X\cap\operatorname{dom}f\) to a first-order oracle. Obtain \(f(y_k)\) and \(g_k\in\partial f(y_k)\), and form
\[
\ell_k(x):=f(y_k)+g_k^\top(x-y_k).
\]
Then \(\ell_k(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in X\), with \(\ell_k(y_k)=f(y_k)\). Update
\[
m_k(x):=\max\{m_{k-1}(x),\ell_k(x)\}.
\]
The output satisfies \(m_{k-1}(x)\le m_k(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Given a previously valid model, evaluate a convex function and a subgradient at the query point, form the affine support, and append it to obtain another globally valid underestimator.

knowledge_statements.title: Linear Master Minimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Epigraph formulation of the Kelley linear master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given cuts \(\ell_i(x)=a_i+g_i^\top x\) for \(1\le i\le k\) and a polyhedral feasible set \(X\), solve
\[
(x_{k+1},t_k)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X,\,t\in\mathbb R}\{t:\ell_i(x)\le t,\ i=1,\ldots,k\}.
\]
Equivalently, \(x_{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}m_k(x)\), where \(m_k(x)=\max_{1\le i\le k}\ell_i(x)\), and \(t_k=m_k(x_{k+1})\). Output \(x_{k+1}\) as the next oracle query and \(t_k\) as the master value, provided the master is feasible and bounded below.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve the epigraph linear program for the maximum of all stored cuts; return its minimizer as the next query and its value as the master bound.
assumptions_latex: The finite master is feasible and bounded below.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Affine-support representation and finite cutting-plane master problem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Supporting-hyperplane representation underlying Kelley linear master minimization; no convergence claim is included.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}$ be finite and convex, and let $S\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n$ be polyhedral. Then
\[
f(x)=\sup_{y\in\mathbb{R}^n}\sup_{g\in\partial f(y)}\{f(y)+g^T(x-y)\}.
\]
Consequently, minimizing $f$ over $S$ has the semi-infinite epigraph formulation
\[
\min_{x\in S,v}v\quad\text{s.t.}\quad v\ge f(y)+g^T(x-y)\quad\forall y\in\mathbb{R}^n,\ g\in\partial f(y).
\]
For sampled points $x_1,\ldots,x_k\in S$ and $g_i\in\partial f(x_i)$, retaining only their supports gives the finite master LP
\[
\min_{x\in S,v}v\quad\text{s.t.}\quad v\ge f(x_i)+g_i^T(x-x_i),\quad i=1,\ldots,k,
\]
which is a relaxation of the semi-infinite formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite convex function is the supremum of all its affine subgradient supports. Retaining supports collected at finitely many points yields Kelley’s finite linear master problem, a relaxation of the semi-infinite epigraph formulation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f(x)=\sup_{y\in\mathbb{R}^n}\sup_{g\in\partial f(y)}[f(y)+g^T(x-y)],\quad\text{and the finite-support master LP relaxes the semi-infinite epigraph formulation.}

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\neq\varnothing\), let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), and define \(f^*:=\inf_{x\in X}f(x)\). Initialize with an evaluated point \(y_1\in X\) having finite value by setting \(\bar x_1:=y_1\) and \(U_1:=f(y_1)\). After evaluating \(y_{k+1}\in X\) with finite value, update
\[
(\bar x_{k+1},U_{k+1}):=
\begin{cases}
(y_{k+1},f(y_{k+1})),&f(y_{k+1})<U_k,\\
(\bar x_k,U_k),&f(y_{k+1})\ge U_k.
\end{cases}
\]
At every iteration,
\[
U_k=f(\bar x_k)=\min_{1\le i\le k}f(y_i)\ge f^*,
\]
so \(U_k\) is a nonincreasing upper bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a function defined on the feasible set, keep the evaluated feasible point with the smallest finite objective value; its value is a nonincreasing upper bound on the explicitly defined optimum.

assumptions_latex: For every \(k\ge1\), \(m_k(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in X\), and \(v_k:=\inf_{x\in X}m_k(x)\in\mathbb R\) is certified.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), and define \(f^*:=\inf_{x\in X}f(x)\). After solving each full cutting-plane master, let
\[
v_k:=\inf_{x\in X}m_k(x)\in\mathbb R.
\]
Assume \(m_k(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in X\), so each certified value satisfies \(v_k\le f^*\). Initialize \(L_1:=v_1\), and for every \(k\ge2\) update
\[
L_k:=\max\{L_{k-1},v_k\}.
\]
Then \(L_{k-1}\le L_k\le f^*\). In the exact full-memory method, \(m_{k-1}(x)\le m_k(x)\) on \(X\), hence \(v_{k-1}\le v_k\) and \(L_k=v_k\). Output \(L_k\) with its master-value certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from the first certified master value, record the greatest certified lower bound for each subsequent iteration; exact full-memory master values are already nondecreasing.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\neq\varnothing\), let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), and define \(f^*:=\inf_{x\in X}f(x)\). Given an incumbent \(\bar x_k\in X\) and finite tracked bounds satisfying
\[
L_k\le f^*\le U_k=f(\bar x_k),

compute
\[
G_k^{\mathrm{abs}}:=U_k-L_k,
\qquad
G_k^{\mathrm{rel}}:=\frac{U_k-L_k}{\max\{1,|U_k|\}}.
\]
Record \((\bar x_k,L_k,U_k,G_k^{\mathrm{abs}},G_k^{\mathrm{rel}})\). For prescribed \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}},\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}\ge0\), an implementation may stop under its selected criterion. The absolute criterion \(G_k^{\mathrm{abs}}\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}\) certifies
\[
0\le f(\bar x_k)-f^*\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}},

and the relative criterion \(G_k^{\mathrm{rel}}\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}\) certifies
\[
0\le f(\bar x_k)-f^*\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}\max\{1,|U_k|\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Monotonicity and Limit of the Tracked Absolute Gap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequence property of the absolute gap when both component histories are monotone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let finite sequences \((L_k)\) and \((U_k)\) satisfy \(L_k\le f^*\le U_k\), \(L_{k+1}\ge L_k\), and \(U_{k+1}\le U_k\). Define \(G_k:=U_k-L_k\). Then \(0\le G_{k+1}\le G_k\), so \(G_k\to G_\infty\) for some \(G_\infty\ge0\). If \(U_k=f(\bar x_k)\) and \(G_k\to0\), then \(0\le f(\bar x_k)-f^*\le G_k\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Monotone certified upper- and lower-bound histories yield a nonincreasing absolute gap; a gap tending to zero forces incumbent objective values to the optimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\le G_{k+1}\le G_k\), \(G_k\to G_\infty\ge0\), and \(G_k\to0\Rightarrow f(\bar x_k)-f^*\to0\).

source_refs.locator: 3.4.2 Methods of Linear Approximation p. 87

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper and convex, let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and define \(f^*:=\inf_{x\in X}f(x)\). Choose \(y_1\in X\cap\operatorname{dom}f\). At iteration \(k\ge1\), evaluate \(f(y_k)\), select \(g_k\in\partial f(y_k)\), retain every cut
\[
\ell_i(x):=f(y_i)+g_i^\top(x-y_i),\qquad 1\le i\le k,
\]
and define
\[
m_k(x):=\max_{1\le i\le k}\ell_i(x).
\]
Solve
\[
y_{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}m_k(x),
\qquad
L_k:=m_k(y_{k+1}).
\]
Choose
\[
i_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{1\le i\le k}f(y_i),
\qquad
\bar x_k:=y_{i_k},
\qquad
U_k:=f(\bar x_k).
\]
For a prescribed \(\varepsilon\ge0\), stop when \(U_k-L_k\le\varepsilon\); otherwise increment \(k\). Upon termination, output \(\bar x_k\) and \((L_k,U_k)\), which satisfy
\[
0\le f(\bar x_k)-f^*\le U_k-L_k\le\varepsilon.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Retain every supporting cut, minimize their maximum globally, explicitly track the best evaluated feasible point and both bounds, and stop when their certified absolute gap meets the prescribed tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Standard Full-Memory Kelley Method

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Packing Bound for Kelley Termination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimension-dependent worst-case oracle bound obtained from separation of successive master points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Assume additionally that \(\operatorname{diam}(X)\le D\) and every returned subgradient satisfies \(\|g_k\|\le G\). If \(U_k-L_k>\varepsilon>0\), then the next master point satisfies
\[
\|y_{k+1}-y_i\|>\varepsilon/G\qquad(i=1,\ldots,k).
\]
Consequently the number of iterations having gap greater than \(\varepsilon\) is at most the \((\varepsilon/G)\)-packing number of \(X\), and in \(\mathbb R^n\) is no larger than \((1+2GD/\varepsilon)^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Before reaching an epsilon gap, exact Kelley query points are epsilon-over-G separated, yielding a finite but dimension-dependent packing bound.
assumptions_latex: Every oracle subgradient has norm at most \(G\).
Master and oracle computations are exact.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unbounded First Kelley Master
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp well-posedness failure for the unstabilized full-memory iteration on an unbounded feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\mathbb R\), \(f(x)=|x|\), \(y_1=1\), and \(g_1=1\in\partial f(1)\). Then \(m_1(x)=f(1)+g_1(x-1)=x\), so \(\inf_{x\in X}m_1(x)=-\infty\), although \(\min_{x\in X}f(x)=0\). Thus the original problem is solvable while the first Kelley master is not.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Primal–Dual Kelley Master
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Epigraph and multiplier representations of the finite full-memory master over a polyhedral feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Write \(\ell_i(x)=a_i^\top x+b_i\), \(i=1,\ldots,k\), and let \(X\) be a nonempty polyhedron. The master is the linear program
\[
L_k=\min_{x,t}\{t:x\in X,\ a_i^\top x+b_i\le t\ (i=1,\ldots,k)\}.
\]
If its optimal value is finite, then
\[
L_k=\max_{\lambda\in\Delta_k}\left\{\sum_{i=1}^k\lambda_i b_i-\sigma_X\!\left(-\sum_{i=1}^k\lambda_i a_i\right)\right\},
\qquad \Delta_k=\{\lambda\ge0:\mathbf1^\top\lambda=1\}.
\]
At a primal-dual optimum \((x_k,t_k,\lambda_k)\),
\[
0\in\sum_i\lambda_{k,i}a_i+N_X(x_k),\qquad
\lambda_{k,i}(a_i^\top x_k+b_i-t_k)=0.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Kelley master is an epigraph linear program whose simplex-weight dual and complementary slackness certify master optimality and identify active cuts.
assumptions_latex: The finite master has a finite optimal value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The primal and dual values equal \(L_k\), with the displayed stationarity and complementarity conditions.

notation.meaning: convex normal cone to X at x

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Global Bound Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic convergence of the exact full-memory iteration under compact-domain regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, compact, and convex, and let \(f\) be finite and convex on an open neighborhood of \(X\). For exact full-memory Kelley iterations,
\[
L_k\le L_{k+1}\le f^*\le U_{k+1}\le U_k,
\qquad L_k\uparrow f^*,\quad U_k\downarrow f^*.
\]
Hence \(U_k-L_k\to0\), and every accumulation point of the incumbent sequence is optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a compact feasible set, exact Kelley lower and upper bounds converge monotonically to the optimum.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is finite and convex on an open neighborhood of \(X\).
Oracle calls and master solutions are exact.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded algorithm statement for minimizing the current Kelley oracle model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a feasible set \(Q\) and oracle models \(\hat f_k(X;\cdot)\) constructed from the oracle calls, choose \(x_0\in Q\). For each \(k\ge0\), compute
\[
x_{k+1}\in\operatorname{Arg\,min}_{x\in Q}\hat f_k(X;x).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose an initial feasible point. At iteration k, select the next iterate as any minimizer over the feasible set of the current Kelley oracle model.
assumptions_latex: \hat f_k(X;\cdot)\text{ is the oracle model available at iteration }k

knowledge_statements.title: Multiple-Cut Kelley Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Kelley iteration retaining several oracle cuts generated at each trial point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be closed and convex, and let \(f\) be convex. Initialize with \(x^1\in X\). At iteration \(k\), obtain affine minorants \(\ell_{k,j}(x)=f(x^k)+\langle g_{k,j},x-x^k\rangle\leq f(x)\) for \(j=1,\ldots,r_k\). Form \(m_k(x)=\max_{1\leq i\leq k,\,1\leq j\leq r_i}\ell_{i,j}(x)\), compute \(x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}m_k(x)\), and set \(L_k=\min_{x\in X}m_k(x)\) and \(U_k=\min_{1\leq i\leq k}f(x^i)\). Stop when \(U_k-L_k\leq\varepsilon\); otherwise retain the cuts and continue.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each iteration adds several valid affine minorants, minimizes their pointwise maximum, and stops when the incumbent upper bound and model lower bound differ by at most the tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
Every displayed master problem attains a finite minimum.

notation.meaning: model lower bound and incumbent upper bound

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the Multiple-Cut Kelley Methods leaf, and the displayed cuts and bounds are internally coherent under the stated finite-attainment assumption. However, no source is cited, so the precise multiple-cut formulation and stopping certificate cannot be reviewed against an inspectable algorithm locator.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strengthening from Simultaneous Supporting Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed effect of taking several whole-objective subgradient supports at one query point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper and convex, let \(y\in\operatorname{dom}f\), and choose \(g_j\in\partial f(y)\) for \(j=1,\ldots,r\). Define \(\ell_j(x):=f(y)+\langle g_j,x-y\rangle\) and \(q(x):=\max_{1\le j\le r}\ell_j(x)\). Then \(q(x)\le f(x)\), \(q(y)=f(y)\), and \(q(x)\ge\ell_j(x)\) for every \(j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Several whole-objective subgradient supports at one point form a touching minorant stronger than each constituent support, but it is unresolved whether this construction is the intended multiple-cut Kelley variant.
knowledge_statements.title: Strengthening from Simultaneous Supporting Cuts

intermediate_metadata.reason: The topic remains deferred because its defining interpretation is materially ambiguous. The proposed simultaneous-support property is therefore deferred despite its algebraic correctness: a careful editor might place it under Supporting-Cut Generation, while established multiple-cut methods may instead use disaggregated component models. Restricted-memory deletion and proximity stabilization are excluded as sibling scopes.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Newest-Cut-Only Kelley Cycling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of arbitrary bounded-memory deletion even with exact cuts and a compact feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Minimize \(f(x)=|x|\) over \(X=[-1,1]\). Start at \(x^1=1\), impose memory limit \(M=1\), and after each query retain only the newest exact supporting cut. At \(x^k=1\), the retained cut is \(\ell_k(x)=x\), whose unique minimizer over \(X\) is \(x^{k+1}=-1\). At \(x^k=-1\), the retained cut is \(\ell_k(x)=-x\), whose unique minimizer is \(x^{k+1}=1\). Hence \(x^k=(-1)^{k+1}\), every queried value equals \(1\), and the method never approaches the unique minimizer \(x^*=0\), although every retained cut is globally valid and every restricted master is solved exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Keeping only the newest exact cut makes Kelley alternate forever between the endpoints of the absolute-value problem, so cut validity and bounded storage alone do not ensure convergence.
assumptions_latex: Memory is \(M=1\), only the newest exact supporting cut is retained, and each restricted master is solved exactly.
knowledge_statements.title: Newest-Cut-Only Kelley Cycling
Restricted-Memory Kelley Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Kelley variant limiting the number of stored affine minorants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be closed and convex, and let \(f\) be convex. Given a memory limit \(M\geq1\), maintain an index set \(I_k\) with \(|I_k|\leq M\) and valid cuts \(\ell_i\leq f\). Compute \(x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\max_{i\in I_k}\ell_i(x)\), query \(g_{k+1}\in\partial f(x^{k+1})\), and create \(\ell_{k+1}(x)=f(x^{k+1})+\langle g_{k+1},x-x^{k+1}\rangle\). Choose \(I_{k+1}\subseteq I_k\cup\{k+1\}\), retaining the new cut and at most \(M-1\) old or aggregated valid cuts. Stop under a prescribed model-gap or stationarity test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method solves a Kelley master model while retaining only a bounded number of valid new, old, or aggregated cuts.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
Every retained or aggregated cut is a global affine minorant of \(f\).
Each restricted master problem has a selected minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|I_k|\leq M\) for every \(k\), while \(m_k(x)=\max_{i\in I_k}\ell_i(x)\leq f(x)\) on \(X\).

notation.meaning: indices of cuts retained at iteration k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the restricted-memory leaf, and the stated memory and minorization invariants are plausible. An authoritative source is required to distinguish a recognized restricted-memory Kelley method from an arbitrary cut-deletion scheme and to specify admissible aggregation and retention policies; such policies are essential for any convergence interpretation.

children.title: Proximity-Controlled Cutting-Plane Methods
children.top_down_role: Transition from unstabilized Kelley models to bundle stabilization.

knowledge_statements.title: Proximity-Controlled Cutting-Plane Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratically stabilized cutting-plane step bridging Kelley and bundle methods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m_k\leq f\) be a cutting-plane model on a closed convex set \(X\), let \(z^k\in X\) be a center, and choose \(t_k>0\). Compute \(x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\{m_k(x)+(2t_k)^{-1}\|x-z^k\|^2\}\), evaluate \(f(x^{k+1})\), and append a subgradient cut there. For a parameter \(\eta\in(0,1)\), declare a serious step and set \(z^{k+1}=x^{k+1}\) when \(f(z^k)-f(x^{k+1})\geq\eta\bigl(f(z^k)-m_k(x^{k+1})\bigr)\); otherwise take a null step with \(z^{k+1}=z^k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proximal term keeps model minimizers near a center, while a serious-step test decides whether the center moves or only the model improves.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(f\) is proper convex and every generated cut globally minorizes \(f\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The trial point minimizes a stabilized model, and the center update is determined by the displayed serious-step inequality.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role and proximal serious/null-step structure fit this transition leaf. The exact serious-step formula requires source verification, particularly whether the model must be exact at the center, whether the predicted decrease is required to be positive, and how the proximal parameter is updated.

knowledge_statements.title: Compact-Domain Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Full-memory Kelley convergence on a compact feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, compact, and convex, and let \(f\) be finite and convex on an open neighborhood of \(X\). In the full-memory Kelley method, choose \(g_i\in\partial f(x^i)\), define \(m_k(x)=\max_{1\leq i\leq k}\{f(x^i)+\langle g_i,x-x^i\rangle\}\), and take \(x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}m_k(x)\). With \(L_k=\min_{x\in X}m_k(x)\) and \(U_k=\min_{1\leq i\leq k}f(x^i)\), one has \(L_k\uparrow f^*\), \(U_k\downarrow f^*\), and every cluster point of incumbent solutions is optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a compact convex domain, full-memory Kelley lower and upper bounds converge to the optimum, and incumbent cluster points are optimal.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, compact, and convex.
\(f\) is finite and convex on an open neighborhood of \(X\).
Exact subgradients and exact full-memory master minimizers are used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_k\uparrow f^*=\min_{x\in X}f(x)\), \(U_k\downarrow f^*\), and every incumbent cluster point lies in \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}f(x)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem role matches Compact-Domain Convergence, and the hypotheses are consistent with a standard full-memory Kelley convergence regime. No inspectable theorem source is supplied, and the phrase "incumbent solutions" does not formally define the selected incumbent sequence whose cluster points are asserted to be optimal.

children.title: Bounded-Iterate Convergence
children.top_down_role: Convergence results conditioned on bounded iterate sequences.

knowledge_statements.title: Bounded-Iterate Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Full-memory Kelley convergence when its trial sequence is bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be closed and convex, and let \(f\) be finite and convex on an open neighborhood of \(X\). Apply the exact full-memory Kelley method and suppose its trial sequence \(\{x^k\}\) is bounded. If \(f^*=\inf_{x\in X}f(x)\) is finite and attained, then the Kelley bounds satisfy \(L_k\uparrow f^*\) and \(U_k\downarrow f^*\). Every cluster point of \(\{x^k\}\) along which \(f(x^k)-L_{k-1}\to0\) is optimal; in particular, every cluster point of incumbent solutions belongs to \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If exact full-memory Kelley trial points remain bounded and an optimum exists, its model and incumbent bounds converge, and incumbent cluster points are optimal.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is closed and convex, and \(f\) is finite convex on a neighborhood of \(X\).
The Kelley trial sequence is bounded and all master problems are solved exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_k\uparrow f^*\), \(U_k\downarrow f^*\), and every incumbent cluster point is optimal.

notation.meaning: full-memory model lower bound and incumbent value

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem role fits the bounded-iterate convergence leaf. The exact implication from bounded Kelley trials to vanishing bound gap, including the regularity needed for the generated subgradients, must be checked against an authoritative theorem. The selected incumbent points also need an explicit definition in the sourced version.

children.title: Coercive-Objective Convergence
children.top_down_role: Convergence results where coercivity supplies bounded localization.

knowledge_statements.title: Coercive-Objective Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coercivity converts a level safeguard into bounded-iterate Kelley convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be closed and convex, and let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) be lower semicontinuous, convex, and coercive on \(X\), meaning \(f(x)\to+\infty\) whenever \(x\in X\) and \(\|x\|\to\infty\). Consider an exact full-memory Kelley scheme whose accepted trial points satisfy the level safeguard \(f(x^k)\leq f(x^1)\). Then \(\{x^k\}\) is bounded, \(f\) attains its minimum on \(X\), and the bounded-iterate Kelley convergence conclusions apply: the lower and incumbent upper bounds converge to \(f^*=\min_{x\in X}f(x)\), and incumbent cluster points are optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a coercive convex objective, a fixed-level safeguard bounds Kelley trials; consequently the standard bounded-iterate convergence conclusions hold.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(f\) is lower semicontinuous, convex, and coercive on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x^k\}\) is bounded, \(L_k\to f^*\), \(U_k\to f^*\), and incumbent cluster points minimize \(f\) on \(X\).

notation.meaning: Kelley lower and incumbent upper bounds

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem role fits the coercive-objective convergence leaf, and coercivity plus the displayed level safeguard does imply bounded trials and attainment in finite dimensions. A source is still required for the claimed Kelley convergence transfer and for a precise algorithmic account of how all Kelley trial points satisfy the safeguard.

children.title: Unbounded-Sequence Failure Boundary
children.top_down_role: Failure boundary arising when neither boundedness nor coercive localization is available.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Coercivity Controls Only Value-Bounded Sequences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact boundary on what objective coercivity can imply about Kelley trial sequences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be coercive. Every sequence \((x^k)\) satisfying \(\sup_k f(x^k)<+\infty\) is bounded. Conversely, if \((x^k)\) is unbounded, it has a subsequence \((x^{k_j})\) with \(\|x^{k_j}\|\to\infty\) and hence \(f(x^{k_j})\to+�\infty\). Therefore coercivity bounds Kelley trial points only when the method also supplies a uniform upper bound on their true objective values; minimizing affine lower models alone supplies no such bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coercivity bounds sequences whose true objective values are bounded, but it does not by itself bound arbitrary minimizers of Kelley lower models.
assumptions_latex: The sequence consists of feasible points in \(\operatorname{dom}f\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_k f(x^k)<+\infty\Rightarrow (x^k)\text{ is bounded}\); an unbounded sequence has a subsequence along which \(f\to+\infty\).

notation.meaning: a sequence of Kelley trial or accepted points

knowledge_statements.title: Coercivity Controls Only Value-Bounded Sequences
Unbounded-Sequence Failure Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundedness cannot be dropped merely because the objective is coercive.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(X=\mathbb R\), let \(f(x)=\sqrt{1+x^2}\), which is smooth, convex, coercive, and uniquely minimized at \(0\). Starting Kelley at any \(x^1>0\) yields the first cut \(\ell_1(x)=f(x^1)+f'(x^1)(x-x^1)\), where \(f'(x^1)>0\). Hence \(\inf_{x\in\mathbb R}\ell_1(x)=-\infty\), so the first master problem has no minimizer. Thus coercivity of the true objective neither bounds the affine model nor guarantees that an unstabilized Kelley trial sequence is well defined; a bounded domain, trust region, proximal term, or comparable safeguard is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coercive convex objective can have an unbounded first Kelley master problem, so coercivity alone does not ensure a bounded or even well-defined trial sequence.
assumptions_latex: The unstabilized Kelley master contains only cuts generated so far.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{x\in X}\ell_1(x)=-\infty\), although \(f\) is coercive and has a unique minimizer.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary role is correct, and the displayed derivative makes the first affine master unbounded below as claimed. The record has no evidence reference or explicit standard-field rationale, so the constructed example and the broader safeguard conclusion require an inspectable source or registered rationale.

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Finite-Termination Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite termination when an oracle exposes finitely many affine pieces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty compact polyhedron and \(f(x)=\max_{1\leq j\leq q}\{a_j^\top x+b_j\}\). Suppose the Kelley oracle at every trial point returns an active affine piece, and the full-memory master retains each distinct returned piece. If \(U_k-L_k>0\), then the oracle must return a piece absent from the current model; otherwise the trial point would certify optimality. Consequently at most \(q\) distinct pieces can be added, and after finitely many iterations the method obtains \(U_k=L_k=f^*\) and an exact minimizer. With tolerance \(\varepsilon\geq0\), termination occurs once \(U_k-L_k\leq\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite max of affine functions, retaining every active piece returned by the oracle yields exact termination after finitely many distinct pieces are exposed.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is the maximum of \(q<\infty\) affine functions.
The oracle returns an active affine piece and full memory retains every distinct piece.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The method terminates exactly after adding at most \(q\) distinct pieces, with \(U_k=L_k=f^*\).

notation.meaning: master lower bound and incumbent upper bound

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem role fits the finite-termination leaf, and finite exposure of active affine pieces is a plausible termination mechanism. A source is needed to verify the exact oracle and indexing convention under which a positive gap forces a previously absent piece and to support the stated at-most-q distinct-piece bound.

knowledge_statements.title: Kelley Bound-Convergence Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotonicity and convergence of full-memory Kelley bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the full-memory Kelley model \(m_k\), define \(L_k=\inf_{x\in X}m_k(x)\) and \(U_k=\min_{1\leq i\leq k}f(x^i)\). Because \(m_k\leq m_{k+1}\leq f\), one has \(L_k\leq L_{k+1}\leq f^*\leq U_{k+1}\leq U_k\). If, additionally, the trial sequence lies in a compact subset on which the generated subgradients are bounded and every master infimum is attained, then \(U_k-L_k\to0\). Therefore both monotone sequences converge to \(f^*=\inf_{x\in X}f(x)\), and \(U_k-L_k\) is a valid a posteriori optimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Full-memory Kelley lower bounds rise and incumbent upper bounds fall; under bounded-trial regularity, their gap vanishes and both converge to the optimum.
assumptions_latex: Every stored cut is a global minorant and no cut is discarded.
For gap convergence, trials are compactly contained, subgradients are bounded there, and masters attain their infima.

notation.meaning: model lower and incumbent upper bounds

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The monotonic bound inequalities are a property, but the asserted vanishing gap and convergence to the optimum are theorem-level conclusions within this convergence-regime leaf. An authoritative source is required to verify that compact containment, bounded generated subgradients, and master attainment are sufficient in the precise Kelley formulation used here and to settle the most appropriate terminal content kind.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Max-Absolute-Quadratic Kelley Test Problem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete convex problem used as an adverse instance in the analysis of Kelley's cutting-plane method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define $f:\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}$ and $Q\subset\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ by
\[
f(y,x)=\max\{|y|,\|x\|^2\},\qquad Q=\{(y,x):y^2+\|x\|^2\le 1\}.
\]
The associated optimization problem is
\[
\min\{f(y,x):(y,x)\in Q\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The objective is the maximum of the absolute value of the scalar coordinate and the squared Euclidean norm of the vector coordinate, minimized over the Euclidean unit ball.

source_evidence.locator: Nonsmooth Convex Optimization / Methods with Complete Data / Kelley's Method / Definition 3.66

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unique Optimum of the Max-Absolute-Quadratic Test Problem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimal solution and value of the concrete problem used in Kelley instability analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For
\[
f(y,x)=\max\{|y|,\|x\|^2\},\qquad Q=\{(y,x):y^2+\|x\|^2\le1\},
\]
the problem $\min\{f(y,x):(y,x)\in Q\}$ has the unique optimal solution $(y^*,x^*)=(0,0)$ and optimal value $f^*=0$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On the Euclidean unit ball, the maximum of the absolute scalar coordinate and the squared norm of the vector coordinate has the origin as its unique minimizer, with value zero.
