knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polyhedral Master Recession Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact recession-direction test for unboundedness of a finite affine Kelley master over a polyhedral feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty polyhedron and \(m(x)=\max_{1\le i\le q}\{a_i^\top x+b_i\}\). Then \(\inf_{x\in X}m(x)=-\infty\) if and only if there exists \(d\in\operatorname{rec}X\) such that \(a_i^\top d<0\) for every \(i=1,\ldots,q\), equivalently \(m^\infty(d)=\max_i a_i^\top d<0\). Such a direction certifies that the Kelley master has no finite lower bound or minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polyhedral Kelley master is unbounded below exactly when a feasible recession direction strictly decreases every retained affine cut.
assumptions_latex: The master is the maximum of finitely many affine cuts.

notation.meaning: recession cone of the feasible polyhedron
recession function of the polyhedral master

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Master Recession Certificate
Unbounded Master Problems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine Kelley models may be unbounded on unbounded feasible sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\mathbb R\), \(f(x)=|x|\), and initialize at \(x^1=1\). The unique subgradient is \(g_1=1\), so the first Kelley cut is \(\ell_1(x)=1+(x-1)=x\). The master value is therefore \(\inf_{x\in\mathbb R}\ell_1(x)=-\infty\), and no model minimizer exists, although \(f\) is proper, closed, convex, coercive, and has the unique minimizer \(0\). Thus an unstabilized Kelley iteration need not be well defined on an unbounded domain unless existing cuts make the master level-bounded or an explicit bounding mechanism is imposed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even for the coercive objective absolute value, one initial tangent produces an unbounded Kelley master problem on the real line.
assumptions_latex: The master problem uses no trust region, proximal term, or artificial bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{x\in X}\ell_1(x)=-\infty\), so the first Kelley trial point is undefined.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary role exactly fits Unbounded Master Problems, and the absolute-value calculation is internally correct. Because the record supplies neither a citation nor explicit standard-field rationale, the example and its general boundary statement remain unsupported candidate knowledge.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonunique Master-Argmin Oscillation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact master-minimizer selections need not converge when stopping is disabled and no tie-breaking rule is imposed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=[-1,1]\) and \(f(x)\equiv0\). Every exact oracle call returns \(g_k=0\), so every cut and every full-memory model satisfy \(\ell_k(x)=m_k(x)=0\) on \(X\). Hence \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}m_k(x)=X\) and \(L_k=U_k=f^*=0\) for every \(k\). If iterations are continued despite this exact stopping certificate and no tie-breaking rule is imposed, the admissible exact selections \(x^{k+1}=(-1)^k\) oscillate forever.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a Kelley implementation ignores an already-zero gap and uses arbitrary exact master minimizers, nonunique minimizers can produce a permanently oscillating trial sequence.
assumptions_latex: Iteration continues despite \(U_k-L_k=0\), and no convergent tie-breaking rule is imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_k=U_k=f^*=0\) for all \(k\), while the admissible selection \(x^{k+1}=(-1)^k\) does not converge.

notation.meaning: full-memory Kelley model after k oracle calls
master lower bound and incumbent upper bound

knowledge_statements.title: Nonunique Master-Argmin Oscillation
Model-Minimizer Oscillation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Kelley model minimization need not produce descent trial points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=[-1,1]\) and \(f(x)=|x|\). Starting at \(x^1=1\), the first cut is \(\ell_1(x)=x\), whose unique minimizer over \(X\) is \(x^2=-1\). Hence the trial point jumps between opposite endpoints while \(f(x^2)=f(x^1)=1\), so no objective decrease occurs. The cut generated at \(-1\) is \(\ell_2(x)=-x\), after which the model becomes \(m_2(x)=\max\{x,-x\}=|x|\) and selects \(0\). This example exhibits large model-minimizer motion and nonmonotone trial behavior even on a compact domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For absolute value on an interval, the first Kelley step jumps between opposite endpoints without decreasing the objective, illustrating unstable model-minimizer motion.
assumptions_latex: Each full-memory master problem is minimized exactly.

notation.meaning: model after the two endpoint cuts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample role fits the leaf, and the two endpoint cuts are calculated correctly. The example demonstrates one endpoint-to-endpoint jump without descent, followed immediately by selection of zero; it does not by itself establish persistent oscillation. A source is required to support the intended local sense of "oscillation" or to justify this one-step instability example as the terminal statement.

knowledge_statements.title: Quantitative-Rate Limitations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle lower bound limiting quantitative guarantees for unstabilized Kelley schemes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In the local first-order oracle model, consider minimizing an \(L\)-Lipschitz convex function over the Euclidean ball \(X=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:\|x\|_2\leq R\}\). There is a universal constant \(c>0\) such that, for every deterministic method using fewer than \(c\min\{d,(LR/\varepsilon)^2\}\) oracle calls, some admissible function has returned points whose best objective error exceeds \(\varepsilon\). Since Kelley cutting-plane methods use only function values and subgradients, they are subject to this lower bound absent additional structure. Monotone model bounds alone therefore cannot imply a dimension-free rate better than order \((LR/\varepsilon)^2\) in this class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: General Lipschitz nonsmooth convex problems impose a first-order oracle lower bound, so Kelley models alone cannot guarantee a uniformly faster dimension-free rate.
assumptions_latex: The algorithm is deterministic and accesses \(f\) only through a local value-subgradient oracle.
The feasible region is a radius-\(R\) Euclidean ball in \(\mathbb R^d\).
The objective is convex and \(L\)-Lipschitz on the ball.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The worst-case oracle complexity is \(\Omega\!\left(\min\{d,(LR/\varepsilon)^2\}\right)\) for producing an \(\varepsilon\)-optimal point.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A complexity-bound role is appropriate for Quantitative-Rate Limitations, but the exact lower bound, its min-with-d dimension dependence, the local-oracle model, and the quantification over returned points require a precise theorem citation. The transfer from a general deterministic first-order lower bound to the stated Kelley limitation also needs explicit source support.

knowledge_statements.title: Full-Memory Growth
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unbounded master-model growth in the full-memory Kelley method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex, and suppose an oracle returns \((f(x_j),g_j)\) with \(g_j\in\partial f(x_j)\) at iteration \(j\). The full-memory Kelley model is \[m_k(x)=\max_{0\le j\le k}\{f(x_j)+\langle g_j,x-x_j\rangle\}.\] If no cut is deleted or aggregated, the master problem at iteration \(k\) contains \(k+1\) stored affine cuts, counting repeated oracle calls separately. Consequently, its storage and constraint count grow at least linearly with the iteration count; bounded-memory complexity cannot be asserted without a retention, deletion, or aggregation rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Keeping every oracle cut makes the Kelley master’s storage and constraint count grow linearly with the number of iterations.
assumptions_latex: Each oracle call supplies a valid subgradient cut.
No cut is deleted or aggregated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m_k\) stores \(k+1\) cuts, so master size is unbounded as \(k\to\infty\).

notation.meaning: Kelley cutting-plane model after iteration k
oracle subgradient at the j-th query point

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bundle-model underestimation and feasible-set affine lower bound
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At every iteration \(k\) of the primal bundle method, \(\varphi_k(y)\le f(y)\) for all \(y\in\mathbb R^n\). Moreover, for every \(y\in C\), \[f(y)\ge f(x_k)+\langle\widehat s_k+\widehat p_k,y-x_k\rangle-\varepsilon_k,\] where \[\varepsilon_k:=\widehat e_k-t_k\langle\widehat p_k,\widehat s_k+\widehat p_k\rangle=f(x_k)-\varphi_k(y_{k+1})-t_k\|\widehat s_k+\widehat p_k\|^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At every iteration, the primal bundle model globally underestimates the objective. The aggregate subgradient and master normal vector also provide an explicit affine lower bound for the objective over the feasible set.
assumptions_latex: \varphi_k,\ y_{k+1},\ \widehat s_k,\ \widehat p_k,\ \widehat e_k\text{ are generated by Algorithm 3.1.4}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \varphi_k(y)\le f(y)\quad\forall y\in\mathbb R^n,\qquad f(y)\ge f(x_k)+\langle\widehat s_k+\widehat p_k,y-x_k\rangle-\varepsilon_k\quad\forall y\in C.

conclusion.target: global objective underestimation and an affine lower bound on the feasible set

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite optimal termination of the polyhedral proximal bundle method
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be polyhedral and let \(f(x)=\max_{i\in I}\{a_i^{\prime}x+b_i\}\), where \(I\) is finite. Assume \(\arg\min_{x\in X}f(x)\ne\varnothing\) and that every subgradient used to add a cutting plane belongs to \(\{a_i:i\in I\}\). Then the proximal bundle method terminates after finitely many iterations with an optimal solution.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Raw Bundle
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complete point-value-subgradient information accumulated from oracle calls before selection or compression.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If the oracle has been called at points \(y_i\in\mathbb R^n\), \(i=1,\ldots,L\), with \(f_i:=f(y_i)\) and \(s_i\in\partial f(y_i)\), then the raw bundle is
\[
\mathcal B_{\mathrm{raw}}:=\{(y_i,f_i,s_i):i=1,\ldots,L\}.
\]
Because \(L\) grows with the number of oracle calls and need not admit an a priori uniform bound, practical storage requires selection of retained triples and/or compression of their information.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The raw bundle contains every sampled point, its function value, and a subgradient obtained there. Its size can grow without a uniform bound, so an implementation must select records or compress their information.

children.title: Bundle Point Records
children.top_down_role: Stored locations represented in the bundle information system.

knowledge_statements.title: Bundle Point Records
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Point-side entries in a finite bundle information system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A bundle point record is a tuple \(p_i=(i,x_i,\tau_i)\), where \(i\) is a unique identifier, \(x_i\in\operatorname{dom}f\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is an oracle query point, and \(\tau_i\) is optional iteration or provenance metadata. A finite bundle point table is \(P=\{p_i:i\in I_P\}\), with distinct identifiers. Numerical oracle values and subgradients are not components of \(p_i\); they belong to oracle evaluation records associated with its identifier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bundle point record stores a uniquely identified oracle query point and optional provenance, separately from its oracle output.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P=\{(i,x_i,\tau_i):i\in I_P\}\) is the finite point-side bundle table.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the leaf, but separating point data from oracle outputs and including identifier/provenance fields is a specific information-system convention requiring a cited source.

children.title: Oracle Evaluation Records
children.top_down_role: Stored oracle outputs associated with evaluated locations.

knowledge_statements.title: Oracle Evaluation Records
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle-output entries used to construct valid bundle cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a convex function \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\), an exact oracle evaluation record associated with point identifier \(i\) is \(r_i=(i,v_i,g_i)\), where \(v_i=f(x_i)\in\mathbb{R}\) and \(g_i\in\partial f(x_i)\). Its affine cut is \(\ell_i(x)=v_i+\langle g_i,x-x_i\rangle\), which satisfies \(\ell_i(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\). A record is valid only when its identifier resolves to the point at which both oracle quantities were computed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact oracle record stores a function value and subgradient at an identified point, thereby determining a global affine minorant.

notation.meaning: affine cutting plane determined by the record

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact-oracle record and induced affine minorant are mathematically coherent and fit the leaf, but no supporting source is cited.

children.title: Point–Record Association
children.top_down_role: Structural links between bundle locations and their oracle records.

knowledge_statements.title: Point–Record Association
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Referential and mathematical consistency between query points and oracle outputs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{(i,x_i,\tau_i):i\in I_P\}\) be a point table and \(R=\{(j,v_j,g_j):j\in I_R\}\) an exact oracle-record table. A point–record association is consistent precisely when \(I_R\subseteq I_P\), every \(j\in I_R\) resolves to exactly one point \(x_j\), and \[v_j=f(x_j),\qquad g_j\in\partial f(x_j).\] Under this condition, reconstructing the cut from the associated entries gives \(v_j+\langle g_j,x-x_j\rangle\le f(x)\) for all \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Association is consistent when each oracle record uniquely resolves to the point where its stored value and subgradient were evaluated.
assumptions_latex: The oracle records are intended to be exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Consistency is equivalent to unique identifier resolution together with \(v_j=f(x_j)\) and \(g_j\in\partial f(x_j)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition is internally coherent, but its precise identifier-based consistency convention lacks an inspectable source.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Recentering Formula for Linearization Errors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact update of a stored cut's linearization error when the stability center changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an exact stored cut \((x_i,f(x_i),g_i)\) with \(g_i\in\partial f(x_i)\), define \(\alpha_i(z)=f(z)-f(x_i)-\langle g_i,z-x_i\rangle\). For any new center \(z'\in\operatorname{dom}f\), \[\alpha_i(z')=\alpha_i(z)+f(z')-f(z)-\langle g_i,z'-z\rangle.\] Both \(\alpha_i(z)\) and \(\alpha_i(z')\) are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stored exact cut can be recentered by adding the objective change and subtracting the cut's predicted change.
knowledge_statements.title: Recentering Formula for Linearization Errors

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Zero Linearization Error and Cut Contact
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterization of when an exact stored cut supports the objective at the current center.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the exact convex-cut assumptions, \[\alpha_i(z)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad f(z)=f(x_i)+\langle g_i,z-x_i\rangle\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad g_i\in\partial f(z).\] Thus zero linearization error means that the stored affine cut touches \(f\) at the center and its slope is also a center subgradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact stored cut has zero center error exactly when it touches the objective there, equivalently when its slope is also a center subgradient.
knowledge_statements.title: Zero Linearization Error and Cut Contact
Bundle Linearization Errors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Center-relative error attached to an exact bundle cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper and convex, let \(z\in\operatorname{dom}f\) be the current stability center, and let \((x_i,f(x_i),g_i)\) satisfy \(g_i\in\partial f(x_i)\). The bundle linearization error of cut \(i\) at \(z\) is \[\alpha_i(z)=f(z)-f(x_i)-\langle g_i,z-x_i\rangle.\] The subgradient inequality gives \(\alpha_i(z)\ge0\), and the same cut has the center-relative form \(f(z)+\langle g_i,x-z\rangle-\alpha_i(z)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bundle linearization error is the nonnegative gap between the center value and a stored cut evaluated at the center.

notation.meaning: linearization error of cut i at the center
stored subgradient at the bundle point

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The center-relative linearization-error definition and nonnegativity claim are correct for exact convex cuts, but no bundle-method citation is supplied.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bundle Linearization Error and Subgradient-Error Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition of linearization error at the current iterate and the resulting compressed actual-bundle representation, before accounting for aggregation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f\) be convex and let \(s_i\in\partial f(y_i)\). The linearization error of the sampling record at \(x_k\) is
\[
e_i^k:=f(x_k)-\bigl[f(y_i)+\langle s_i,x_k-y_i\rangle\bigr]\ge 0.
\]
Then \(s_i\in\partial_{e_i^k}f(x_k)\). Neglecting the aggregation qualification, the actual bundle can therefore be stored as
\[
\{(s_i,e_i^k):i=1,\ldots,k\},
\]
without retaining the sampling points \(y_i\). When \(L=k\), this uses \(k(n+1)\) scalar entries instead of \(k(2n+1)\) for the raw triples, at the cost of discarding information.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The linearization error is the gap between the current function value and the affine subgradient minorant generated at a sampled point. Convexity makes it nonnegative and makes the sampled subgradient an approximate subgradient at the current iterate. Storing subgradient-error pairs removes the sampling points and reduces memory, but loses information; aggregation requires an additional qualification.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Transport Identity for Bundle Linearization Errors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact algebraic update of the linearization error of a fixed sampling record between two iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For iterates \(x_k,x_{k'}\) and a fixed sampling record \((y_i,s_i)\), define
\[
e_i^j:=f(x_j)-\bigl[f(y_i)+\langle s_i,x_j-y_i\rangle\bigr].
\]
Then
\[
e_i^{k'}=e_i^k+f(x_{k'})-\bigl[f(x_k)+\langle s_i,x_{k'}-x_k\rangle\bigr].
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The linearization error of a fixed sampling record at a new iterate equals its old error plus the difference between the new function value and the affine prediction from the old iterate using the stored subgradient.

children.title: Active Cuts
children.top_down_role: Cuts currently active in the master representation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polyhedral Activity Regions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Points at which an individual retained cut is active.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a retained affine cut \(\ell_i\) in \(m=\max_{j\in I}\ell_j\), its activity region is \[R_i=\{x:i\in A(x)\}=\bigcap_{j\in I}\{x:\ell_i(x)\geq\ell_j(x)\}.\] Hence \(R_i\) is a closed convex polyhedron, possibly empty; a tie places the point in every corresponding activity region.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut's activity region is the possibly empty polyhedron where it dominates every retained cut.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R_i=\bigcap_{j\in I}\{x:\ell_i(x)\geq\ell_j(x)\}\text{ is a closed convex polyhedron}.
knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Activity Regions

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Active-Cut Subdifferential Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order representation of a finite maximum using the cuts active at the evaluation point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m(x)=\max_{i\in I}\{a_i+\langle g_i,x\rangle\}\) for finite nonempty \(I\), and let \(A(y)=\{i:\ell_i(y)=m(y)\}\). Then \(A(y)\neq\varnothing\) and \[\partial m(y)=\operatorname{conv}\{g_i:i\in A(y)\}.\] Slopes of inactive cuts therefore do not contribute to \(\partial m(y)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The active set is nonempty, and the model subdifferential is the convex hull of the active-cut slopes.

notation.meaning: convex subdifferential of the model at y

knowledge_statements.title: Active-Cut Subdifferential Representation
Active Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cuts attaining the bundle model at a specified master point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\) be a finite nonempty index set, let \(\ell_i:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be affine for every \(i\in I\), and define \(m(x)=\max_{i\in I}\ell_i(x)\). For a specified point \(y\in\mathbb{R}^n\), the active-cut set is \[A(y)=\{i\in I:\ell_i(y)=m(y)\}.\] Thus a retained cut is active at \(y\) exactly when it attains the bundle model value there.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A retained cut is active at a specified point exactly when it attains the cutting-plane model's maximum at that point.

notation.meaning: maximum of the retained affine cuts
retained affine cut indexed by i

children.title: Retained Inactive Cuts
children.top_down_role: Inactive cuts preserved for later model use.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pointwise-Safe but Not Globally-Safe Deletion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local consequence and global limitation of deleting currently inactive cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(J_0\subseteq J(y)\), assume \(I\setminus J_0\neq\varnothing\), and define \(\widehat m(x)=\max_{i\in I\setminus J_0}\ell_i(x)\). Then \[\widehat m(y)=m(y),\qquad A_{\widehat m}(y)=A_m(y),\qquad \partial\widehat m(y)=\partial m(y).\] Unless every deleted cut is dominated by \(\widehat m\) on the region of interest, however, \(\widehat m(x)<m(x)\) can hold elsewhere. Present inactivity therefore certifies deletion safety only at the current point, not global model equivalence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deleting currently inactive cuts preserves the model value and subdifferential at the current point but may weaken the model elsewhere.
assumptions_latex: Every cut in \(J_0\) has strictly positive slack at \(y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat m(y)=m(y),\quad\partial\widehat m(y)=\partial m(y),\quad\text{but generally }\widehat m\not\equiv m.
knowledge_statements.title: Pointwise-Safe but Not Globally-Safe Deletion

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Persistence of Strict Inactivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Neighborhood stability of an inactive cut having positive model slack.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m(x)=\max_{j\in I}\ell_j(x)\), and suppose \(s_i(y)=m(y)-\ell_i(y)>0\). Then there is a neighborhood \(U\) of \(y\) such that \(i\notin A(x)\) for every \(x\in U\). If \(\ell_j(x)=a_j+\langle g_j,x\rangle\) and \(L_i=\max_{j\in I}\|g_j-g_i\|>0\), then \(\|x-y\|<s_i(y)/L_i\) implies \(i\notin A(x)\). If \(L_i=0\), the cut is inactive everywhere.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive slack makes inactivity stable locally, with a radius controlled by slack and relative cut slopes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists U\ni y\ \forall x\in U:\ i\notin A(x).

notation.meaning: positive slack of cut i at y

knowledge_statements.title: Local Persistence of Strict Inactivity
Retained Inactive Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stored cuts not attaining the current bundle model value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\) be the retained cut set, let \(m(x)=\max_{i\in I}\ell_i(x)\), and fix the current master point \(y\). The retained inactive-cut set is \[J(y)=\{i\in I:\ell_i(y)<m(y)\}=I\setminus A(y).\] Its members remain available for subsequent models despite having positive slack \(s_i(y)=m(y)-\ell_i(y)>0\) at the current point. Inactivity is point-dependent: a cut in \(J(y)\) may become active after the master point or model changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A retained inactive cut stays in memory but lies strictly below the current model value at the current master point.

notation.meaning: model slack of cut i at y

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The point-dependent definition of retained inactive cuts is coherent and fits the leaf, but it depends on the unsourced active-cut definition and supplies no citation of its own.

children.title: Cut-Status Transitions
children.top_down_role: Transitions among active, inactive, and discarded cut states.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Status Changes Along a Moving Master Point
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transition geometry for a fixed finite cut family along a line segment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a finite retained family \(\{\ell_i\}_{i\in I}\) and let \(y(t)=(1-t)y_0+ty_1\), \(0\leq t\leq1\). If \(A(y(t))\) changes at \(t_*\), then at least two retained cuts tie actively there: \(\ell_i(y(t_*))=\ell_j(y(t_*))=m(y(t_*))\) for some \(i\ne j\). Each nonidentically-zero difference \(\ell_i(y(t))-\ell_j(y(t))\) has at most one zero, so the active set is constant on the open intervals determined by these finitely many crossing parameters. Cuts whose differences vanish identically remain tied throughout the segment and do not create additional transition parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Along a segment, activity can change only at an active tie, and a fixed finite affine family has only finitely many transition parameters.
assumptions_latex: The retained family is fixed along the segment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A(y(t))\text{ changes only at active ties and has finitely many transition parameters}.
knowledge_statements.title: Status Changes Along a Moving Master Point
Cut-Status Transitions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Status update induced by cut deletion, insertion, and activity at a new master point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a finite retained set \(I_k\), affine cuts \(\ell_i\) for \(i\in I_k\), a deletion set \(D_k\subseteq I_k\), a new valid cut with index \(q_k\notin I_k\setminus D_k\), and a point \(y_{k+1}\in\mathbb{R}^n\), set \[I_{k+1}=(I_k\setminus D_k)\cup\{q_k\}.\] Define \[m_{k+1}(y_{k+1})=\max_{i\in I_{k+1}}\ell_i(y_{k+1}),\qquad A_{k+1}=\{i\in I_{k+1}:\ell_i(y_{k+1})=m_{k+1}(y_{k+1})\},\] and \[J_{k+1}=I_{k+1}\setminus A_{k+1}.\] A surviving cut may therefore change between active and inactive status when the retained set or evaluation point changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After deleting selected cuts and inserting a new valid cut, recompute the model maximum at the new master point and classify every retained cut as active or inactive.
assumptions_latex: Every \(i\in I_k\cup\{q_k\}\) indexes a valid affine cut \(\ell_i\).
\(y_{k+1}\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and the finite maximum is evaluated exactly.

children.title: Aggregate Subgradients
children.top_down_role: Compressed subgradient information retained by bundle models.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Aggregate Slopes as Epsilon-Subgradients
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise subdifferential meaning of a consistently aggregated bundle slope at the stability center.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z\in\operatorname{dom}f\), and suppose \[\bar\ell(x)=f(z)+\langle\bar g,x-z\rangle-\bar\alpha\le f(x)\quad\text{for all }x,\] where \(\bar\alpha\ge0\). Then \(\bar g\in\partial_{\bar\alpha}f(z)\). In particular, \(\bar\alpha=0\) implies \(\bar g\in\partial f(z)\), and \(\bar g=0\) in that case certifies that \(z\) minimizes \(f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid aggregate slope is an epsilon-subgradient at the center, with epsilon equal to its aggregate linearization error.
knowledge_statements.title: Aggregate Slopes as Epsilon-Subgradients
Aggregate Subgradients
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex aggregation of slopes from center-relative bundle cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\) be a finite nonempty index set and let the retained center-relative cuts have slopes \(g_i\in\mathbb{R}^n\) for \(i\in I\). Given weights \(\lambda_i\ge 0\) satisfying \(\sum_{i\in I}\lambda_i=1\), the aggregate subgradient associated with these weights is \[\bar g=\sum_{i\in I}\lambda_i g_i.\] The term denotes the aggregate bundle slope; without additional hypotheses, it does not assert that \(\bar g\in\partial f(z)\) at the stability center \(z\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An aggregate subgradient is the convex combination of retained cut slopes generated by nonnegative weights summing to one; it need not be a subgradient at the stability center.

notation.meaning: convex aggregation weight for cut i

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex-combination and minorant properties of the aggregate linearization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: For the aggregate linearization defined by the cited aggregate-subgradient construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\widetilde f^k\) be the aggregate linearization defined by (2.27) from the linearizations (2.29). Then \(\widetilde f^k\) is a convex combination of those linearizations and
\[f(x)\geq \widetilde f^k(x)\qquad\text{for all }x.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The constructed aggregate linearization is a convex combination of the component linearizations and is a global lower bound for the objective.
assumptions_latex: \widetilde f^k\text{ is the aggregate linearization defined by (2.27) from the linearizations (2.29)}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widetilde f^k\text{ is their convex combination and }(\forall x)\;f(x)\geq\widetilde f^k(x).

children.title: Aggregate Supporting Planes
children.top_down_role: Compressed affine model information retained in the master problem.

knowledge_statements.title: Aggregate Supporting Planes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine global minorant obtained by convexly combining center-relative bundle planes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper and convex, let \(z\in\operatorname{dom}f\), and let \(\ell_i(x)=f(z)+\langle g_i,x-z\rangle-\alpha_i\) satisfy \(\ell_i(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(i\) in a finite nonempty set \(I\). For weights \(\lambda_i\ge0\) with \(\sum_{i\in I}\lambda_i=1\), define \[\bar g=\sum_{i\in I}\lambda_i g_i,\qquad \bar\alpha=\sum_{i\in I}\lambda_i\alpha_i.\] The aggregate plane is \[\bar\ell(x)=\sum_{i\in I}\lambda_i\ell_i(x)=f(z)+\langle\bar g,x-z\rangle-\bar\alpha,\] and it satisfies \(\bar\ell(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex combination of valid center-relative bundle planes is another affine global minorant whose slope and linearization error are the corresponding weighted averages.
assumptions_latex: For every \(i\in I\), \(\ell_i(x)=f(z)+\langle g_i,x-z\rangle-\alpha_i\le f(x)\) for all \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\).

children.title: Aggregation Consistency
children.top_down_role: Consistency requirements linking aggregate vectors to aggregate planes.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Mismatched Aggregation Weights Break Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of the center-relative identity when slopes, errors, and planes use incompatible weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z=0\), \(f(z)=0\), \(\ell_1(x)=x\), and \(\ell_2(x)=-x-1\), with \((g_1,\alpha_1)=(1,0)\) and \((g_2,\alpha_2)=(-1,1)\). If \(\bar g=g_1=1\), \(\bar\alpha=\alpha_2=1\), and \(\bar\ell=\ell_1\), then \[f(z)+\bar g x-\bar\alpha=x-1\ne x=\bar\ell(x).\] Thus separate convex-hull membership of the stored components is insufficient; one common weight vector is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Using incompatible weights for the aggregate slope, error, and plane can destroy their affine identity.
assumptions_latex: The slope, error, and plane are assembled with incompatible convex weights.
knowledge_statements.title: Mismatched Aggregation Weights Break Consistency
Aggregation Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility of aggregate slopes, errors, and affine planes under common convex weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\) be finite and nonempty, and let \(\ell_i(x)=f(z)+\langle g_i,x-z\rangle-\alpha_i\) be center-relative affine planes using a common center \(z\). An aggregate triple \((\bar g,\bar\alpha,\bar\ell)\) is consistent with these planes when there is one weight vector \(\lambda\) satisfying \(\lambda_i\ge0\) and \(\sum_{i\in I}\lambda_i=1\) such that \[\bar g=\sum_{i\in I}\lambda_i g_i,\qquad \bar\alpha=\sum_{i\in I}\lambda_i\alpha_i,\qquad \bar\ell=\sum_{i\in I}\lambda_i\ell_i.\] These equalities imply the affine identity \[\bar\ell(x)=f(z)+\langle\bar g,x-z\rangle-\bar\alpha\quad\text{for every }x\in\mathbb{R}^n.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Aggregation is consistent when one common convex weight vector generates the aggregate slope, error, and plane, preserving their center-relative affine identity.
assumptions_latex: All component planes use the same center \(z\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Consistency holds when a single convex weight vector generates \(\bar g\), \(\bar\alpha\), and \(\bar\ell\), in which case \(\bar\ell(x)=f(z)+\langle\bar g,x-z\rangle-\bar\alpha\).

children.title: Stability Centers
children.top_down_role: Persistent reference locations used by stabilized bundle architectures.

knowledge_statements.title: Stability Centers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accepted reference points about which stabilized bundle master problems are regularized.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In a stabilized bundle method for minimizing a proper convex function \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) over a nonempty closed convex set \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), a stability center is a feasible accepted point \(z_k\in C\cap\operatorname{dom}f\), with known value \(f(z_k)\), about which the next master problem is stabilized. For example, given a convex bundle model \(m_k\) and \(t_k>0\), a proximal trial point may be chosen from \[y_{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}\left\{m_k(x)+\frac{1}{2t_k}\lVert x-z_k\rVert^2\right\}.\] The point \(y_{k+1}\) has the trial role and becomes a new stability center only if the method's acceptance test accepts it; otherwise the current center is retained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stability center is the accepted feasible reference point around which the bundle master problem is regularized; a generated trial point becomes the next center only upon acceptance.
assumptions_latex: \(m_k\) is a convex bundle model and \(t_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stabilization term is centered at \(z_k\), and a generated \(y_{k+1}\) assumes the stability-center role only after acceptance.

notation.meaning: trial point generated by the stabilized master problem

children.title: Trial Points
children.top_down_role: Candidate evaluation locations produced by stabilized master problems.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Proximal Trial-Point Optimality Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order characterization and uniqueness of an unconstrained proximal bundle trial point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(m_k:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, and convex, let \(x_k^c\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and let \(t_k>0\). The problem
\[
\min_x\left\{m_k(x)+\frac{1}{2t_k}\|x-x_k^c\|^2\right\}
\]
has a unique minimizer \(y_k\). A point \(y\) equals \(y_k\) if and only if
\[
0\in\partial m_k(y)+\frac{1}{t_k}(y-x_k^c),
\]
equivalently, there exists \(g_k^a\in\partial m_k(y)\) such that \(g_k^a=(x_k^c-y)/t_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proximal bundle trial point is unique and is certified exactly by cancellation of a model subgradient with the scaled displacement from the center.
assumptions_latex: \(m_k\) is proper, closed, and convex on \(\mathbb{R}^n\).

notation.meaning: model subgradient balancing the proximal displacement

knowledge_statements.title: Proximal Trial-Point Optimality Certificate

assumptions_latex: \(m_k\leq f\) is a finite convex bundle model and \(x_k^c\in\operatorname{dom}f\).
\(t_k>0\), and the stabilized model subproblem has a minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y_k\) is the point at which the objective oracle is queried and acceptance is tested.
review_flags: No supplied locator directly covers convex bundle trial points; authoritative source required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proximal trial point for a finite-dimensional convex bundle method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given the center \(x_k^c\), model \(m_k\), and parameter \(t_k>0\), a trial point is any solution
\[
y_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\left\{m_k(x)+\frac{1}{2t_k}\lVert x-x_k^c\rVert^2\right\}.
\]
After computing \(y_k\), the method evaluates an objective oracle at \(y_k\). The resulting value and subgradient information are used to compare actual decrease with model-predicted decrease and to construct the next bundle model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A trial point minimizes the stabilized bundle model around the current center, then supplies the oracle information used for acceptance and model refinement.
knowledge_statements.title: Trial Points

children.title: Center–Trial Role Separation
children.top_down_role: Distinct informational and computational roles of centers and trial points.

assumptions_latex: At iteration \(k\), the algorithm stores a center \(x_k^c\) and computes a trial point \(y_k\).
An acceptance test classifies the iteration as serious or null.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The center changes only after acceptance, whereas every trial point may contribute oracle information to the model.

notation.meaning: candidate generated by the stabilized subproblem

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports the center-trial architecture; authoritative source required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational separation of accepted iterates from evaluated candidates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Center-trial role separation requires that \(x_k^c\) represent the last accepted iterate and that \(y_k\) represent only the current candidate. If iteration \(k\) is serious, set \(x_{k+1}^c=y_k\); if it is null, set \(x_{k+1}^c=x_k^c\). In either case, oracle information obtained at \(y_k\) may be incorporated into \(m_{k+1}\). Thus evaluation of a candidate does not by itself authorize replacement of the center.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The center is the last accepted iterate; the trial point is merely a candidate. A null step preserves the center but may still improve the model.
knowledge_statements.title: Center–Trial Role Separation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle fits the center–trial separation leaf and is internally coherent, but its serious/null update architecture lacks cited evidence.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Schematic Serious–Null Step in a Bundle Trust-Region Method
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Acceptance and model-refinement branching after solving the current bundle trust-region subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given iterates \(\{z^i\}_{i=1}^k\), trial points \(\{y^i\}_{i=1}^k\), and regularization parameter \(t_k\), compute an optimal solution \(d^k\) of (6.7) and set \(y^{k+1}=z^k+d^k\). If \(\mathcal F(y^{k+1})\) is sufficiently smaller than \(\mathcal F(z^k)\), either enlarge \(t_k\) and resolve (6.7), or take the serious step \(z^{k+1}=y^{k+1}\). Otherwise, either reduce \(t_k\) and resolve (6.7), or take the null step \(z^{k+1}=z^k\) and compute \(v(y^{k+1})\in\partial\mathcal F(y^{k+1})\) to improve the model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve the bundle trust-region subproblem and test its trial point. Sufficient decrease allows a serious step; insufficient decrease allows a null step that retains the incumbent and adds subgradient information. In either case, the regularization parameter may instead be adjusted and the subproblem solved again.
assumptions_latex: \{z^i\}_{i=1}^k\text{ and }\{y^i\}_{i=1}^k\text{ are the available iterate and trial-point sequences}
t_k\text{ is the current regularization parameter}
d^k\text{ is an optimal solution of subproblem (6.7)}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: z^{k+1}=y^{k+1}\text{ after a serious step, or }z^{k+1}=z^k\text{ with }v(y^{k+1})\in\partial\mathcal F(y^{k+1})\text{ after a null step, unless }t_k\text{ is adjusted and (6.7) is resolved}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Descent and Null Steps in a Stabilized Bundle Method
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Terminology under Algorithm 1.2.2, classified by whether the stability center is replaced by the trial point or retained.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under Algorithm 1.2.2, changing the stability center is called a descent step, while retaining it is called a null step. If \(K\subset\mathbb N\) denotes the descent iterations, then \[k\in K\iff x_{k+1}=y_{k+1},\qquad k\notin K\iff x_{k+1}=x_k.\] On a null step, the bundle method enriches the piecewise-affine model \(\varphi_k\); in contrast, a line search changes its norming or step-control parameter without changing the model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A descent step replaces the stability center by the trial point, whereas a null step retains the current center. The descent-index set therefore consists exactly of the accepted-center iterations. After a null step, a bundle method enriches its piecewise-affine model, unlike a line search, which changes its step control without changing the model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: k\in K\iff x_{k+1}=y_{k+1},\qquad k\notin K\iff x_{k+1}=x_k

source_witnesses.locator: Acceleration of the Cutting-Plane Algorithm: Primal Forms of Bundle Methods / XV.1. Accelerating the Cutting-Plane Algorithm / Definition 1.2.4

assumptions_latex: \(m_k\leq f\), \(m_k(x_k^c)=f(x_k^c)\), and \(y_k\) is a trial point.
review_flags: No supplied locator directly covers serious-step acceptance in bundle methods; authoritative source required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard actual-versus-predicted reduction test with an exact objective oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the predicted and actual decreases by
\[
\Delta_k=f(x_k^c)-m_k(y_k),\qquad A_k=f(x_k^c)-f(y_k).
\]
For a fixed \(\eta\in(0,1)\), iteration \(k\) is a serious step precisely when
\[
A_k\geq\eta\Delta_k.
\]
On a serious step the accepted center is updated by \(x_{k+1}^c=y_k\). The inequality ensures that a fixed fraction of the decrease predicted by the model is realized by the true objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A trial point is accepted when its actual objective decrease is at least a fixed fraction of the model-predicted decrease.
knowledge_statements.title: Serious-Step Acceptance

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits Serious-Step Acceptance and the stated implication is correct under its hypotheses, but predicted-decrease conventions vary and no source fixes this version.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Full-Retention Null-Step Monotonicity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotonic strengthening of the regularized master value when a null step retains the complete previous model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix a center \(x^c\) and parameter \(t>0\). Suppose a null-step update sets \(m_{k+1}=\max\{m_k,\ell_k\}\), where \(m_k\) and \(\ell_k\) are proper convex minorants of \(f\). Define
\[
q_j^*=\inf_x\left\{m_j(x)+\frac{1}{2t}\|x-x^c\|^2\right\},\qquad D_j=f(x^c)-q_j^*.
\]
Then \(m_{k+1}\ge m_k\), so \(q_{k+1}^*\ge q_k^*\) and \(D_{k+1}\le D_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a fixed center and proximal parameter, retaining the complete old model and adding a null-step cut raises the regularized master value and decreases its model gap.
assumptions_latex: The center \(x^c\) and parameter \(t>0\) remain fixed.

notation.meaning: regularized model gap at the fixed center

review_flags: The comparison requires full retention and a fixed center and stabilization parameter; cut deletion or parameter changes invalidate it.
knowledge_statements.title: Full-Retention Null-Step Monotonicity

assumptions_latex: The serious-step test fails at \(y_k\), and \(x_{k+1}^c=x_k^c\).
An exact oracle returns \(f(y_k)\) and \(g_k\in\partial f(y_k)\).
The next model may retain selected old cutting planes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The refined model remains a convex minorant of \(f\) and is exact at \(y_k\).

notation.meaning: new supporting plane at the rejected trial point

review_flags: No supplied locator directly covers null-step bundle refinement; authoritative source required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-oracle cutting-plane refinement after a rejected trial point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
After rejection of \(y_k\), keep the center fixed and form the supporting plane
\[
\ell_k(x)=f(y_k)+\langle g_k,x-y_k\rangle,
\qquad g_k\in\partial f(y_k).
\]
Choose a retained model \(\widehat m_k\leq f\) from the existing bundle and update
\[
m_{k+1}(x)=\max\{\widehat m_k(x),\ell_k(x)\}.
\]
Then recompute a stabilized trial point from \(m_{k+1}\). The null iteration terminates without changing the center, while the added plane records the discrepancy exposed at \(y_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After rejection, keep the center, add the oracle supporting plane at the trial point, and solve the strengthened stabilized model again.
knowledge_statements.title: Null-Step Model Refinement

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits Null-Step Model Refinement, and the max update is exact at the trial point under the stated minorant assumptions. A source is still required for this particular retention and refinement rule.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Loss of Control as Stabilization Vanishes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional example showing escape of proximal trials when the parameter diverges.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(m(x)=x\) on \(\mathbb{R}\) and fix \(c\in\mathbb{R}\). For every \(t>0\),
\[
y_t=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb{R}}\left\{x+\frac{(x-c)^2}{2t}\right\}=c-t.
\]
Hence, if \(t_k\to+\infty\), then \(|y_{t_k}-c|=t_k\to+\infty\), while the unstabilized master satisfies \(\inf_x m(x)=-\infty\). Positivity of each finite parameter guarantees a well-defined individual proximal trial but does not prevent escape when stabilization vanishes along the sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an affine model, trial points equal the center minus the proximal parameter, so diverging parameters make the trials escape and expose the unbounded unstabilized master.
assumptions_latex: The center \(c\) is fixed and \(t_k>0\) with \(t_k\to+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.title: Loss of Control as Stabilization Vanishes

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Monotone Response to the Proximal Parameter
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparative statics of exact proximal trials for a fixed convex model and center.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(m:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, and convex, fix \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and define
\[
y_t=\operatorname*{argmin}_x\left\{m(x)+\frac{1}{2t}\|x-c\|^2\right\},\qquad t>0.
\]
For \(0<s<t\),
\[
\|y_s-c\|\le \|y_t-c\|,
\qquad m(y_s)\ge m(y_t).
\]
Thus increasing \(t\) weakens stabilization: exact trial displacement cannot decrease and the attained unregularized model value cannot increase.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a fixed convex model and center, a larger proximal parameter produces a no-smaller trial displacement and a no-higher model value.
assumptions_latex: The model and center are fixed while \(0<s<t\).

notation.meaning: exact trial point for proximal parameter t

review_flags: The comparison requires the same model and center at both parameter values.
knowledge_statements.title: Monotone Response to the Proximal Parameter

assumptions_latex: Each trial subproblem uses a parameter \(t_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The controlled sequence satisfies \(t_k\in[t_{\min},t_{\max}]\), preserving a strongly convex proximal subproblem.
review_flags: Bundle methods use differing parameter conventions and update policies; a source is needed to fix the intended variant.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safeguarded multiplicative control; detailed increase and decrease rules are method-dependent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A safeguarded stabilization-parameter controller chooses
\[
t_{k+1}=\min\{t_{\max},\max\{t_{\min},\gamma_k t_k\}\},
\qquad \gamma_k>0.
\]
The factor \(\gamma_k\) may depend only on information available after the serious-null decision, such as the ratio of actual to predicted decrease. The controller is admissible when it keeps \(t_{k+1}>0\) and within the prescribed bounds. Under the convention \(\lVert x-x_k^c\rVert^2/(2t_k)\), smaller \(t_k\) imposes stronger stabilization and larger \(t_k\) permits a more distant trial.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proximal parameter is adjusted from observed model performance and safeguarded inside a positive bounded interval; smaller values impose stronger stabilization.
knowledge_statements.title: Stabilization-Parameter Control

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits stabilization-parameter control, but the multiplicative policy and admissibility requirements are method-dependent and unsupported by a citation.

The oracle has returned a value and subgradient record at \(y_k\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ephemeral algorithmic data associated with the current candidate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The trial-point state at iteration \(k\) is the tuple
\[
T_k=(y_k,m_k(y_k),\mathcal O_k^y,\Delta_k),
\]
where \(y_k\) solves the stabilized model subproblem, \(\mathcal O_k^y\) contains the oracle value and subgradient data obtained at \(y_k\), and \(\Delta_k\) is the predicted decrease. This state supports the serious-null decision and model refinement. It is not an accepted iterate state unless the acceptance condition is satisfied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Trial-point state stores the current candidate, its model value, oracle response, and predicted decrease for acceptance and refinement.

children.title: Center State

assumptions_latex: The method has an accepted point \(x_k^c\in\operatorname{dom}f\).
The bundle model and stabilization data are based at \(x_k^c\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistent data attached to the last accepted iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The center state at iteration \(k\) is the persistent tuple
\[
C_k=(x_k^c,f(x_k^c),\mathcal B_k,t_k),
\]
where \(x_k^c\) is the last accepted point, \(f(x_k^c)\) is its objective value, \(\mathcal B_k\) is the bundle information referenced to that center, and \(t_k>0\) is the current stabilization parameter. A null step may modify \(\mathcal B_k\) and \(t_k\) but leaves \(x_k^c\) and \(f(x_k^c)\) unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Center state stores the last accepted point, its value, center-referenced bundle data, and stabilization parameter, persisting across null steps.

children.title: State-Separation Invariants
children.top_down_role: Bookkeeping boundaries that keep trial information distinct from center information.

assumptions_latex: Every iteration is classified as exactly one serious or null step.
Oracle information is attached to the point where it was evaluated.
Center replacement is performed only by the acceptance rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The center always denotes an accepted point, while the current trial remains distinguishable until acceptance.
review_flags: No supplied locator states these implementation-level invariants; authoritative source required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency invariants for maintaining separate accepted and candidate states.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(s_k=1\) denote a serious step and \(s_k=0\) a null step. State separation requires
\[
x_{k+1}^c=\begin{cases}y_k,&s_k=1,\\x_k^c,&s_k=0,\end{cases}
\]
while the oracle record generated at \(y_k\) remains labeled by \(y_k\). Before acceptance, updating \(T_k\) must not overwrite \(x_k^c\) or \(f(x_k^c)\). On a null step, model and parameter components may change, but the accepted-point components of \(C_k\) remain invariant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A serious step transfers the trial point into center state; a null step preserves the accepted point while allowing model and parameter updates.
knowledge_statements.title: State-Separation Invariants

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind and statement fit State-Separation Invariants, but these implementation-level invariants have no cited source or locator.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Center Gap Implies Epsilon-Subgradient Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order consequence of a globally valid lower model with finite center gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m\leq f\) be proper convex functions, let \(c\in\operatorname{dom}f\cap\operatorname{dom}m\), and set \(e_c=f(c)-m(c)\). Then \[\partial m(c)\subseteq\partial_{e_c}f(c).\] In particular, center exactness \(e_c=0\) implies \(\partial m(c)\subseteq\partial f(c)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid lower model with center gap e has only e-subgradients of the objective at the center; exact agreement gives genuine subgradients.

notation.meaning: epsilon-subdifferential of f at the center

knowledge_statements.title: Center Gap Implies Epsilon-Subgradient Consistency

assumptions_latex: \(m_k\) is a convex bundle model and \(x_k^c\in\operatorname{dom}f\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At the center, the model has neither value error nor a positive modeling gap.
review_flags: No supplied locator directly covers center-exact bundle models; authoritative source required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact lower-model accuracy at the current stability center.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The bundle model is center-accurate at \(x_k^c\) when
\[
m_k(x)\leq f(x)\quad\text{for all }x\in\mathbb{R}^n,
\qquad m_k(x_k^c)=f(x_k^c).
\]
Equivalently, the center modeling error \(e_k^c=f(x_k^c)-m_k(x_k^c)\) is zero while the global lower-model error is nonnegative. For a maximum of exact supporting planes, center accuracy is ensured by retaining a plane generated at \(x_k^c\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A center-accurate bundle model globally underestimates the objective and agrees with it exactly at the current stability center.
knowledge_statements.title: Center-Based Model Accuracy

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition correctly expresses exact lower-model accuracy at the center and fits the leaf, but no source supports the terminology and bundle-model claim.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Active-Weight Exactness at an Aggregation Point
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accuracy preserved by weights supported on cuts active at a specified point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m(x)=\max_{i\in I}\ell_i(x)\), choose \(y\), and let \(\lambda\) lie in the simplex with \(\lambda_i>0\Rightarrow i\in A(y)\). For \(\bar\ell=\sum_i\lambda_i\ell_i\), \[\bar\ell(y)=m(y),\qquad \bar\ell(x)\leq m(x)\quad\forall x.\] If additionally \(m(y)=f(y)\), then \(\bar\ell(y)=f(y)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Aggregating cuts active at a point preserves the model value there and inherits objective exactness when the model is exact.
assumptions_latex: Positive weights occur only on cuts active at \(y\).

notation.meaning: cuts active at the aggregation point

knowledge_statements.title: Active-Weight Exactness at an Aggregation Point

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Aggregate Plane as an Epsilon-Subgradient Plane
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order accuracy interpretation of an aggregate lower plane at a center.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\bar\ell(x)=\bar\ell(c)+\langle\bar g,x-c\rangle\leq f(x)\) and define \(\bar e=f(c)-\bar\ell(c)\geq0\). Then \[f(x)\geq f(c)+\langle\bar g,x-c\rangle-\bar e\quad\forall x,\] so \(\bar g\in\partial_{\bar e}f(c)\). If \(\bar\ell=\sum_i\lambda_i\ell_i\), then \(\bar g=\sum_i\lambda_i g_i\) and \(\bar e=\sum_i\lambda_i e_i^c\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An aggregate lower plane with center gap e has an aggregate slope that is an e-subgradient at the center.
assumptions_latex: \(\bar\ell\) is a finite affine global minorant of \(f\).
knowledge_statements.title: Aggregate Plane as an Epsilon-Subgradient Plane

assumptions_latex: The bundle contains affine minorants \(\ell_i(x)=a_i+\langle g_i,x\rangle\leq f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The aggregate plane is a globally valid affine minorant and its center error is the weighted average of the constituent errors.
review_flags: No supplied locator directly covers aggregate-plane accuracy in bundle methods; authoritative source required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accuracy inherited by a convex aggregation of valid cutting planes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the aggregate plane by
\[
\bar\ell(x)=\sum_i\lambda_i\ell_i(x),
\qquad \lambda_i\geq0,
\qquad \sum_i\lambda_i=1.
\]
Then \(\bar\ell(x)\leq f(x)\) for every \(x\). At the center \(x_k^c\), if \(e_i^c=f(x_k^c)-\ell_i(x_k^c)\), its error satisfies
\[
f(x_k^c)-\bar\ell(x_k^c)=\sum_i\lambda_i e_i^c.
\]
Consequently, if every positively weighted plane has center error at most \(\varepsilon_k\), the aggregate plane has center error at most \(\varepsilon_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex combination of valid cutting planes remains a valid lower plane, and its center error is the same convex combination of their errors.
knowledge_statements.title: Aggregate-Plane Accuracy

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property and formulas for convex aggregation are mathematically consistent and fit Aggregate-Plane Accuracy, but the record contains no cited evidence.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Asymmetric Value-Error Correction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic correction for an epsilon-subgradient oracle with asymmetric value-error bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(-\delta_i^-\leq\widetilde f_i-f(z_i)\leq\delta_i^+\) and \(g_i\in\partial_{\varepsilon_i}f(z_i)\), where \(\delta_i^-,\delta_i^+,\varepsilon_i\geq0\). Define \[\ell_i(x)=\widetilde f_i-\delta_i^+-\varepsilon_i+\langle g_i,x-z_i\rangle.\] Then \(\ell_i(x)\leq f(x)\) for all \(x\), and \[0\leq f(z_i)-\ell_i(z_i)\leq\delta_i^-+\delta_i^++\varepsilon_i.\] For symmetric uncertainty \(\delta_i^- =\delta_i^+=\delta_i\), the bound is \(2\delta_i+\varepsilon_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subtracting the upper value-error bound and epsilon tolerance gives a valid cut; its query gap is bounded by the full value-uncertainty width plus epsilon.
knowledge_statements.title: Asymmetric Value-Error Correction

assumptions_latex: At query \(z_i\), an oracle returns \((\widetilde f_i,g_i,\varepsilon_i)\) with \(g_i\in\partial_{\varepsilon_i}f(z_i)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each corrected plane underestimates \(f\), with explicit accuracy loss \(\varepsilon_i+\delta_i\).
review_flags: Inexact-oracle conventions vary; a source is required to confirm the intended error model and correction.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic value-error and epsilon-subgradient model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The oracle data are model-accurate when the corrected affine function
\[
\ell_i^{\mathrm{in}}(x)=\widetilde f_i-\delta_i+\langle g_i,x-z_i\rangle-\varepsilon_i
\]
satisfies \(\ell_i^{\mathrm{in}}(x)\leq f(x)\) for every \(x\). This follows from \(g_i\in\partial_{\varepsilon_i}f(z_i)\) and \(\widetilde f_i-\delta_i\leq f(z_i)\). At the query point,
\[
0\leq f(z_i)-\ell_i^{\mathrm{in}}(z_i)\leq 2\delta_i+\varepsilon_i.
\]
Thus convergence claims requiring asymptotic exactness must control the accumulated oracle tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Correcting an inexact value and epsilon-subgradient yields a valid lower plane whose query-point error is explicitly bounded by the oracle tolerances.
knowledge_statements.title: Inexact-Oracle Model Accuracy

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The corrected-plane calculation gives query-point error at most \(2\delta_i+\varepsilon_i\), whereas conclusion_latex claims accuracy loss \(\varepsilon_i+\delta_i\). The intended inexact-oracle convention and correct bound require a source before revision can be fixed reliably.

assumptions_latex: Use the biased model \(m(x)=|x|-\epsilon\) at center \(x^c=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A persistent center gap can create positive predicted decrease with zero actual decrease, invalidating model-based stationarity.
review_flags: No supplied locator covers this illustrative failure construction; source or reviewer validation required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete failure caused by persistent loss of center exactness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For any \(t>0\), the stabilized subproblem
\[
\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}}\left\{|x|-\epsilon+\frac{x^2}{2t}\right\}
\]
has trial point \(y=0\). Nevertheless, the model predicts decrease
\[
f(x^c)-m(y)=\epsilon>0,
\]
whereas the actual decrease is \(f(x^c)-f(y)=0\). Hence every serious-step test with a positive acceptance fraction rejects the trial, and the uncorrected model gap persists. This example shows that global minorization alone does not replace center exactness or a vanishing error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a persistently downward-shifted model of the absolute-value function, predicted decrease stays positive although the trial point and true objective do not improve.
knowledge_statements.title: Model-Accuracy Failure Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the leaf and the example is algebraically coherent, but the construction and its claimed methodological implication lack cited support.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Zero Aggregate Norm Alone Does Not Certify Stationarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of an untagged aggregate formed from subgradients at different points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=|x|\), with \(g_1=1\in\partial f(1)\) and \(g_2=-1\in\partial f(-1)\). Equal weights give \(\bar g=(g_1+g_2)/2=0\). Nevertheless, at the current point \(x=2\), \[0\notin\partial f(2)=\{1\},\] so \(x=2\) is nonstationary despite \(\|\bar g\|=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cancellation among subgradients stored at different points can make their aggregate zero at a nonstationary current iterate.
knowledge_statements.title: Zero Aggregate Norm Alone Does Not Certify Stationarity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Error-Tagged Aggregate Is an Epsilon-Subgradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correct stationarity interpretation of subgradients aggregated from different oracle points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g_i\in\partial f(x_i)\) and \(\ell_i(z)=f(x_i)+\langle g_i,z-x_i\rangle\). For \(\lambda_i\ge0\) with \(\sum_i\lambda_i=1\), set \[\bar g=\sum_i\lambda_i g_i,\qquad \bar\ell=\sum_i\lambda_i\ell_i.\] At a reference point \(x\), define \(\varepsilon(x)=f(x)-\bar\ell(x)\ge0\). Then \[\bar g\in\partial_{\varepsilon(x)}f(x),\] equivalently \[f(z)\ge f(x)+\langle\bar g,z-x\rangle-\varepsilon(x)\quad\text{for all }z.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An aggregate of subgradients from different points is an epsilon-subgradient at the reference point when its aggregate linearization error is retained.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is finite and convex.

notation.meaning: convex epsilon-subdifferential of f at x

knowledge_statements.title: Error-Tagged Aggregate Is an Epsilon-Subgradient
Basic Aggregate Subgradient Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional unconstrained convex minimization with aggregated cutting-plane information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex. At iteration \(k\), retain subgradients \(g_i\in\partial f(x_i)\) and choose weights \(\lambda_i^k\ge 0\) satisfying \(\sum_i\lambda_i^k=1\). Form the aggregate subgradient \(\bar g_k=\sum_i\lambda_i^k g_i\), choose a prescribed stepsize \(t_k>0\), and set \(x_{k+1}=x_k-t_k\bar g_k\). Evaluate \(f(x_{k+1})\), obtain \(g_{k+1}\in\partial f(x_{k+1})\), and update the weights or retained cuts. Stop when a declared test such as \(\|\bar g_k\|\le\varepsilon\) holds; otherwise output the last iterate after the iteration limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Aggregate stored subgradients by convex weights, step opposite the aggregate, add a new oracle subgradient, and stop when the aggregate is sufficiently small.
assumptions_latex: A subgradient oracle is available at every queried point.
\(t_k>0\) and the aggregation weights are specified.

notation.meaning: stored subgradient at a queried point

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits, but a convex combination of subgradients taken at different points is not generally a subgradient at the current iterate, so its norm alone is not a stationarity certificate. A bundle-method source must specify the aggregation and stopping logic.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Active-Plane Equalities and Conditional Projection Characterization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iteration identities for Algorithm 5.1, including projection conclusions under positive linear dependence of the selected subgradients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At iteration \(k\) of Algorithm 5.1,
\[f_j^k+\langle g^j,d^k\rangle\le u^k\quad(j\in J^k),\qquad f_j^k+\langle g^j,d^k\rangle=u^k\quad(j\in\widehat J^k),\]
\[\widehat f_s^k(x^k+d^k)=\widehat f_r^k(x^k+d^k)=u^k,\qquad v_s^k(d^k)=v^k=u^k-f(x^k).\]
If additionally
\[0\in\operatorname{conv}\{g^j:j\in\widehat J^k\},\]
then
\[y^{k+1}=\operatorname{Pr}_{X_s^k}x^k=\operatorname{Pr}_{X_r^k}x^k,\qquad d^k=\operatorname{Pr}_{D^k}0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At an iteration of Algorithm 5.1, every current plane value in the search direction is at most the common value u^k, and every plane selected with a positive multiplier attains that value. The two models agree at the trial point, and the predicted-value identities hold. If zero lies in the convex hull of the selected subgradients, the next point and direction have the stated Euclidean projection representations.
assumptions_latex: k\text{ is an iteration of Algorithm 5.1}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{gathered}f_j^k+\langle g^j,d^k\rangle\le u^k\ (j\in J^k),\quad f_j^k+\langle g^j,d^k\rangle=u^k\ (j\in\widehat J^k),\\ \widehat f_s^k(x^k+d^k)=\widehat f_r^k(x^k+d^k)=u^k,\quad v_s^k(d^k)=v^k=u^k-f(x^k),\\ 0\in\operatorname{conv}\{g^j:j\in\widehat J^k\}\Rightarrow y^{k+1}=\operatorname{Pr}_{X_s^k}x^k=\operatorname{Pr}_{X_r^k}x^k,\quad d^k=\operatorname{Pr}_{D^k}0.\end{gathered}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Simplex-Constrained Representation of the Aggregate Subproblem Value
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algorithm-specific equivalent formulation of the subproblem at iteration \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At iteration \(k\ge 1\) of Algorithm 3.1, \(w^k\) is the optimal value of
\[\min_{\lambda}\ \frac12\left\|\sum_{j\in J^k}\lambda_jy^j+\lambda_pp^{k-1}\right\|^2+\sum_{j\in J^k}\lambda_j\lambda_j^k+\lambda_p\alpha_p^k\]
subject to
\[\lambda_j\ge0\ (j\in J^k),\qquad \lambda_p\ge0,\qquad \sum_{j\in J^k}\lambda_j+\lambda_p=1.\]
This optimization problem is equivalent to subproblem (3.1).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At every iteration, the aggregate subproblem value is the optimum of the displayed simplex-constrained quadratic problem, which is equivalent to subproblem (3.1).
assumptions_latex: \text{The quantities are those defined at iteration }k\text{ of Algorithm 3.1}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Minimum-Norm Hull Selection Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimality conditions for selecting the least-norm vector from a finite represented subgradient hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=\operatorname{conv}\{g_1,\ldots,g_r\}\ne\varnothing\) and let \(s=P_C(0)\). Then \[\langle s,g_i-s\rangle\ge0\quad(i=1,\ldots,r),\] equivalently \(\langle s,g-s\rangle\ge0\) for every \(g\in C\). Moreover, \(s=0\) if and only if \(0\in C\). If every \(g_i\in\partial f(x)\), then \(s=0\) certifies \(0\in\partial f(x)\), hence global optimality of \(x\) for proper convex \(f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection inequalities certify the minimum-norm hull selection, and a zero selection certifies convex optimality when all represented vectors are current subgradients.
assumptions_latex: For the optimality conclusion, \(f\) is proper convex and \(g_i\in\partial f(x)\) for all \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s=P_C(0)\iff \langle s,g-s\rangle\ge0\ \forall g\in C\), and \(s=0\Rightarrow0\in\partial f(x)\) under the same-point subgradient assumption.

notation.meaning: Euclidean projection of the origin onto C

knowledge_statements.statement_title: An Incomplete Selection Need Not Give Descent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of selecting a direction from only part of the current subdifferential.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\max\{x,-2x\}\). At \(x=0\), \(\partial f(0)=[-2,1]\). If the represented set contains only \(g=1\), its minimum-norm hull selection is \(s=1\), but for \(d=-s=-1\), \[f'(0;d)=\max\{d,-2d\}=2>0.\] Thus the negative minimum-norm vector of an incomplete represented subset of \(\partial f(x)\) need not be a descent direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Selecting from only part of the current subdifferential can produce an ascent direction.
assumptions_latex: The represented subgradient set at zero is \(\{1\}\).
knowledge_statements.title: An Incomplete Selection Need Not Give Descent
Subgradient-Selection Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimum-norm selection from subgradients represented by the active bundle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_k\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and available subgradients \(g_{k,1},\ldots,g_{k,r}\in\partial f(x_k)\), solve \[\lambda^k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\lambda\ge0,\,\mathbf{1}^{\mathsf T}\lambda=1}\left\|\sum_{i=1}^r\lambda_i g_{k,i}\right\|^2.\] Set \(s_k=\sum_i\lambda_i^k g_{k,i}\). If \(\|s_k\|\le\varepsilon\), return \(x_k\); otherwise choose \(t_k>0\), set \(x_{k+1}=x_k-t_ks_k\), and refresh the available subgradients. The selected vector is the Euclidean minimum-norm element of the convex hull of the represented subgradients.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select the minimum-norm convex combination of represented subgradients, stop when it is small, and otherwise step in its negative direction.
assumptions_latex: The represented subgradient set is nonempty and finite.

notation.meaning: represented subgradient at the current point

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The minimum-norm convex-hull selection is mathematically valid under the stated same-point assumptions, but it may not represent the intended aggregate-subgradient precursor, whose stored cuts commonly originate at different points. The exact variant requires a source.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonnegative Directional Derivative Gives No Armijo Guarantee
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of guaranteed Armijo acceptance without a strict directional-descent certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(u)=|u|\), \(x=0\), and \(d=1\), one has \(f'(0;1)=1\). Hence, for every \(t>0\) and \(\sigma\in(0,1)\), \[f(x+td)=t>\sigma t=f(x)+\sigma t f'(x;d).\] Thus a nonnegative directional derivative does not guarantee acceptance of any positive trial length.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without strict directional descent, a convex polyhedral objective can reject every positive Armijo trial.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonnegative Directional Derivative Gives No Armijo Guarantee

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Termination of Directional-Derivative Armijo Backtracking
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Well-posedness of the line search after an aggregate procedure supplies a strict descent direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex and finite on a neighborhood of \(x\), and suppose \(f'(x;d)<0\). For every \(\sigma\in(0,1)\), there exists \(\bar t>0\) such that \[f(x+td)\le f(x)+\sigma t f'(x;d)\qquad(0<t\le\bar t).\] Consequently, geometric backtracking with \(t_j=\alpha_0\beta^j\), \(\alpha_0>0\), and \(\beta\in(0,1)\), accepts after finitely many reductions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strict directional-descent certificate guarantees finite termination of nonsmooth Armijo backtracking.

notation.meaning: one-sided directional derivative at x along d

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Termination of Directional-Derivative Armijo Backtracking
Line-Search Aggregate Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Aggregate directions coupled with a sufficient-decrease line search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At \(x_k\), construct an aggregate vector \(s_k\) from retained cutting-plane information and select a direction \(d_k\) satisfying \(f'(x_k;d_k)<0\), commonly by refining the aggregate until this condition holds. Given \(\alpha_0>0\), \(\beta\in(0,1)\), and \(\sigma\in(0,1)\), choose the first \(j\ge0\) for which \[f(x_k+\beta^j\alpha_0d_k)\le f(x_k)+\sigma\beta^j\alpha_0 f'(x_k;d_k).\] Set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\beta^j\alpha_0d_k\), query a subgradient there, and update the aggregate. Stop upon the prescribed stationarity or iteration test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Refine the aggregate to obtain a strict descent direction, then use backtracking to enforce nonsmooth Armijo decrease before updating the bundle.

notation.meaning: aggregate vector formed from retained cuts

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: nonsmooth Armijo search along a certified descent direction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Armijo calculation is coherent once a strict descent direction exists, but the defining aggregate refinement procedure is unspecified and no cited source establishes this as the intended line-search aggregate method.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Rejected trial point implies a strict slope-linearization inequality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Line-search lemma for aggregate subgradient methods in unconstrained convex minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) be convex. Suppose \(y=x^k+t d^k\), where \(t\in(0,1]\), and \(f(y)>f(x^k)+mtv^k\). Let \(g=g_f(y)\in\partial f(y)\) and define \(\alpha=f(x^k)-\bigl(f(y)+\langle g,x^k-y\rangle\bigr)\). Then \(-\alpha+\langle g,d^k\rangle>mv^k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex objective, if a trial point along the search direction violates the sufficient-decrease test, then its subgradient and linearization error satisfy the stated strict slope inequality.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polyhedrality Alone Does Not Imply Finite Termination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating polyhedral objective structure from algorithm-specific finite termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=|x|\) and \(x_0>0\). The valid subgradient iteration \[x_{k+1}=x_k-t_kg_k,\qquad g_k=1\in\partial f(x_k),\qquad t_k=\frac{x_k}{2},\] satisfies \(x_{k+1}=x_k/2>0\) for every finite \(k\). Thus \(x_k\to0\), the unique minimizer, but no iterate is optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subgradient iteration can converge geometrically on a polyhedral objective without reaching its minimizer in finitely many steps.
knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedrality Alone Does Not Imply Finite Termination
Polyhedral Finite-Convergence Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite termination induced by a polyhedral error bound and uniform successful-step decrease.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be proper polyhedral convex, let \(f^*=\min f\), and let \(S=\operatorname*{argmin}f\ne\varnothing\). On any bounded level set containing the iterates there exists \(\kappa>0\) such that \[f(x)-f^*\ge\kappa\operatorname{dist}(x,S).\] Consequently, consider an aggregate method whose nonoptimal successful iterates satisfy \(f(x_{k+1})\le f(x_k)-\delta\) for some fixed \(\delta>0\), and whose unsuccessful model refinements identify a new face from a finite polyhedral model. It can perform at most \(\lceil(f(x_0)-f^*)/\delta\rceil\) successful steps and only finitely many distinct face refinements before certifying optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Polyhedral error bounds, uniform objective decrease, and finitely many model faces yield finite termination and an explicit bound on successful steps.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper polyhedral convex with nonempty minimizer set.
All iterates remain in a bounded level set.
Successful steps decrease \(f\) by at least \(\delta>0\), and refinements expose previously unidentified faces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_{\mathrm{succ}}\le\left\lceil\dfrac{f(x_0)-f^*}{\delta}\right\rceil\), and the total number of model refinements is finite.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: polyhedral error bound plus finite-face argument

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content belongs in a finite-convergence container, but the claimed total finite termination depends on an algorithm-specific guarantee that every unsuccessful refinement exposes a previously unidentified member of a finite face family. That guarantee and the successful-step count need direct support.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Termination of the Polyhedral Proximal Bundle Method
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite termination under finite polyhedral cutting data and cuts selected from the represented affine slopes.

Assume \arg\min_{x\in X}f(x)\ne\varnothing and that every subgradient used to add a cutting plane is one of the vectors a_i, i\in I. Then the bundle method terminates after finitely many iterations with an optimal solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a polyhedral feasible set and a finite maximum-of-affine objective with a nonempty solution set, the proximal bundle method terminates finitely at an optimum when every added cut uses one of the represented affine slopes.
assumptions_latex: g_k\in\{a_i:i\in I\}\text{ for every subgradient added to the model}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists K<\infty\text{ such that the bundle method terminates with }x_K\in\arg\min_{x\in X}f(x)
