knowledge_statements.statement_title: Basic Proximal Bundle Method with Serious and Null Steps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cutting-plane master problem with a proximal center updated by a sufficient-progress test.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let F_k(x)=\max_{0\le i\le k}\{f(x_i)+(x-x_i)^{\prime}g_i\}, where g_i\in\partial f(x_i), and let p_k(x)=\frac{1}{2c_k}\|x-y_k\|^2, where c_k>0 and y_k\in\{x_i:i\le k\}. Compute x_{k+1}\in\arg\min_{x\in X}\{F_k(x)+p_k(x)\}. For fixed \beta\in(0,1), define \delta_k=f(y_k)-F_k(x_{k+1})-p_k(x_{k+1}) and set y_{k+1}=x_{k+1} if f(y_k)-f(x_{k+1})\ge\beta\delta_k; otherwise set y_{k+1}=y_k. Initialize y_0=x_0. The former case is a serious step and the latter a null step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method minimizes a cutting-plane model plus a quadratic term centered at a past iterate. The center moves to the trial point when actual decrease meets the sufficient-progress test; otherwise it remains fixed, producing a null step.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Quadratic Bundle Master
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean proximal master problem for a finite cutting-plane model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\bar x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(t>0\), and let the bundle cuts be \(\ell_i(\bar x+d)=\beta_i+g_i^{\mathsf T}d\), where \(\ell_i\le f\). With \(m(\bar x+d)=\max_{1\le i\le r}\ell_i(\bar x+d)\), the primal proximal bundle master is \[\min_{d\in\mathbb{R}^n,\,r_0\in\mathbb{R}}\;r_0+\frac{1}{2t}\|d\|^2\quad\text{subject to}\quad \beta_i+g_i^{\mathsf T}d\le r_0\quad(i=1,\ldots,r).\] Its unique displacement \(d^*\) defines the trial point \(x^+=\bar x+d^*\); the epigraph variable satisfies \(r_0^*=m(x^+)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The primal bundle master minimizes the cutting-plane epigraph value plus a quadratic proximal penalty, producing a unique trial displacement.
assumptions_latex: The bundle contains finitely many affine minorants \(\ell_i\le f\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^+=\bar x+d^*\), where \((d^*,r_0^*)\) solves the displayed strongly convex quadratic program and \(r_0^*=m(x^+)\).

notation.meaning: maximum of the stored affine cuts

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Contact-preserving replacement in a quadratic bundle master
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded invariance result for replacing the master model while retaining its aggregate contact plane.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mu>0\), let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be closed and convex, and suppose \(y_+\in C\), \(\widehat s\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(\widehat p\in N_C(y_+)\) satisfy \[y_+=x-\frac1\mu(\widehat s+\widehat p).\] Define \[\bar f^{\mathrm a}(y):=f(x)-\widehat e+\langle\widehat s,y-x\rangle.\] If \(\psi:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) satisfies \(\psi(y)\ge\bar f^{\mathrm a}(y)\) for every \(y\in\mathbb R^n\), with equality at \(y_+\), then \[y_+\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in C}\left\{\psi(y)+\frac\mu2\|y-x\|^2\right\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any extended-real model that dominates the aggregate affine plane and contacts it at the trial point preserves that point as a minimizer of the quadratically stabilized constrained problem.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unique solution and aggregate plane for the primal quadratic bundle master
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded characterization of a quadratically stabilized convex bundle master and its aggregate affine minorant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\varphi:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be convex, let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, let \(\mu>0\), and suppose \(\varphi(x)\le f(x)\). Then \[\min_{y\in C}\left\{\varphi(y)+\frac{\mu}{2}\|y-x\|^2\right\}\] has a unique solution \(y_+\). There exist \(\widehat s\in\partial\varphi(y_+)\) and \(\widehat p\in N_C(y_+)\) such that \[y_+=x-\frac1\mu(\widehat s+\widehat p).\] Moreover, for every \(y\in\mathbb R^n\), \[\varphi(y)\ge f(x)+\langle\widehat s,y-x\rangle-\widehat e,\qquad \widehat e:=f(x)-\varphi(y_+)-\frac1\mu\langle\widehat s,\widehat s+\widehat p\rangle\ge0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The constrained quadratic stabilization of a finite convex model has a unique solution. Its optimality condition combines a model subgradient and a normal-cone vector, and the resulting aggregate plane globally minorizes the model with nonnegative error.
assumptions_latex: C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\text{ is nonempty, closed, and convex}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists!\,y_+\in C:\ y_+=x-\mu^{-1}(\widehat s+\widehat p),\quad \varphi(y)\ge f(x)+\langle\widehat s,y-x\rangle-\widehat e\ \forall y\in\mathbb R^n,\quad \widehat e\ge0.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Small-parameter form of the primal bundle direction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact small-parameter characterization of the aggregate direction produced by the primal quadratic bundle master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume that \(e_i=0\) for some \(i\in\{1,\ldots,\ell\}\). Then there exists \(\underline t>0\) such that, for every \(t\in(0,\underline t]\), \(\widehat s(t)\) is generated by a solution of \[\min_{\substack{\alpha\in\Delta_\ell\\ \sum_{i=1}^{\ell}\alpha_i e_i=0}}\frac12\left\|\sum_{i=1}^{\ell}\alpha_i s_i\right\|^2.\] Equivalently, for each such \(t\), there is a minimizing \(\alpha(t)\) with \(\widehat s(t)=\sum_{i=1}^{\ell}\alpha_i(t)s_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If at least one bundle error is zero, then below a positive parameter threshold the primal bundle direction is a minimum-norm convex aggregate of the stored subgradients subject to zero aggregate error.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual Optimizer and Aggregate Uniqueness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniqueness and complementarity structure of the unconstrained Euclidean simplex dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Lambda^*\) solve \[\max_{\lambda\ge0,\;\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}\lambda=1}\left\{\beta^{\mathsf T}\lambda-\frac t2\|G\lambda\|^2\right\},\qquad t>0.\] The multiplier vector need not be unique, but \(G\lambda\) is identical for every \(\lambda\in\Lambda^*\). Hence the aggregate subgradient \(\bar g^*=G\lambda\) and displacement \(d^*=-t\bar g^*\) are unique. Moreover, \(\lambda_i^*>0\) implies \(\beta_i+g_i^{\mathsf T}d^*=\max_j(\beta_j+g_j^{\mathsf T}d^*)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimal dual weights may be nonunique, but all produce the same aggregate subgradient and primal step; positive weights occur only on active cuts.
assumptions_latex: The bundle contains finitely many affine cuts.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual Optimizer and Aggregate Uniqueness
Dual Proximal Bundle Master
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simplex quadratic dual of the primal proximal bundle master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the primal master with cuts \(\beta_i+g_i^{\mathsf T}d\) and parameter \(t>0\), Lagrange multipliers \(\lambda_i\ge0\) for the cutting-plane constraints satisfy \(\sum_i\lambda_i=1\). Strong quadratic-programming duality gives \[\min_d\left\{\max_i(\beta_i+g_i^{\mathsf T}d)+\frac{1}{2t}\|d\|^2\right\}=\max_{\lambda\ge0,\,\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}\lambda=1}\left\{\sum_i\lambda_i\beta_i-\frac{t}{2}\left\|\sum_i\lambda_i g_i\right\|^2\right\}.\] If \(\lambda^*\) is dual optimal, then \(\bar g^*=\sum_i\lambda_i^*g_i\) is the aggregate subgradient and the primal displacement is \(d^*=-t\bar g^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The master dual maximizes aggregate cut height minus a quadratic aggregate-subgradient penalty over the simplex, with displacement equal to minus the scaled aggregate.
assumptions_latex: The primal master has finitely many affine cuts.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d^*=-t\sum_i\lambda_i^*g_i\), and the displayed primal and dual optimal values coincide.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Lagrange dual of the quadratic epigraph master

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Directional-derivative bound for a dual bundle direction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Applies to the aggregate direction and any multiplier supplied by the referenced dual bundle construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the minimal value in the defining error problem is zero, so e_j=0 for some j\le\ell, and suppose that for some solution \alpha of the master problem the corresponding coefficient satisfies \alpha_j>0. Then every multiplier \mu described by the dual construction satisfies \[f'(x;-\widehat s_\varepsilon)\ge-\|\widehat s_\varepsilon\|^2-\mu\varepsilon.\] If all extreme points of \partial f(x) occur among the \ell bundle elements, equality holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When a zero-error bundle element receives positive weight in some master solution, the true directional derivative along the negative aggregate vector has the stated lower bound. The bound is exact if the bundle contains every extreme point of the current subdifferential.
assumptions_latex: \mu\ \text{is a multiplier described by the referenced dual construction}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f'(x;-\widehat s_\varepsilon)\ge-\|\widehat s_\varepsilon\|^2-\mu\varepsilon,\quad\text{with equality if all extreme points of }\partial f(x)\text{ occur in the bundle}

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Proximal-Point Interpretation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bundle trial point as an epsilon-inexact proximal point of the true objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m\le f\) be a convex cutting-plane model and let \[x^+\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\left\{m(x)+\frac{1}{2t}\|x-\bar x\|^2\right\},\qquad t>0.\] Define \(\varepsilon=f(x^+)-m(x^+)\ge0\). Model optimality gives \(v=(\bar x-x^+)/t\in\partial m(x^+)\). Because \(m\le f\), the same vector satisfies \(v\in\partial_{\varepsilon}f(x^+)\). Thus the bundle trial point obeys the inexact proximal inclusion \[0\in\partial_{\varepsilon}f(x^+)+\frac{1}{t}(x^+-\bar x).\] When \(\varepsilon=0\), this is the exact proximal-point optimality condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The model minimizer is an epsilon-inexact proximal point of the true function, with epsilon equal to the model gap at the trial point.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(m\) are proper convex functions with \(m\le f\).
The displayed model-proximal problem has a minimizer.

notation.meaning: model gap at the trial point

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: epsilon-subgradient consequence of a global model minorant

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform Strong Convexity of Fixed-Parameter Masters
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural consequence of using one positive proximal parameter at every iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m_k:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper closed convex and fix \(t>0\). Then \[\Phi_k(x)=m_k(x)+\frac1{2t}\|x-\bar x_k\|_2^2\] is proper, closed, coercive, and \(1/t\)-strongly convex. It therefore has a unique minimizer \(x_k^+\), characterized by \[0\in\partial m_k(x_k^+)+t^{-1}(x_k^+-\bar x_k).\] The strong-convexity modulus is the same at every iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed positive proximal parameter gives all convex bundle masters the same strong-convexity modulus and a unique trial point.
assumptions_latex: m_k\text{ is proper, closed, and convex}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Phi_k\text{ is }1/t\text{-strongly convex and has a unique minimizer}.
knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Strong Convexity of Fixed-Parameter Masters

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fixed-Parameter Model-Decrease Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iteration-uniform displacement bound for convex fixed-parameter masters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix \(t>0\). For each iteration let \(m_k\) be proper, closed, and convex with \(m_k(\bar x_k)<+\infty\), and let
\[x_k^+=\operatorname*{argmin}_x\left\{m_k(x)+\frac1{2t}\|x-\bar x_k\|^2\right\}.\]
Then
\[m_k(\bar x_k)-m_k(x_k^+)\ge\frac1{2t}\|x_k^+-\bar x_k\|^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every fixed-parameter master has the same displacement-based lower bound on predicted model decrease.
assumptions_latex: m_k\text{ is proper, closed, and convex}.
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Parameter Model-Decrease Certificate
Fixed Proximal Parameters
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proximal bundle iteration using one constant stabilization parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose a proximal center \(\bar x_0\), a bundle model \(m_0\le f\), and a constant \(t>0\). At iteration \(k\), compute \[x_k^+\in\operatorname*{argmin}_x\left\{m_k(x)+\frac{1}{2t}\|x-\bar x_k\|^2\right\}.\] Let \(\Delta_k=f(\bar x_k)-m_k(x_k^+)\). For a fixed \(\eta\in(0,1)\), declare a serious step and set \(\bar x_{k+1}=x_k^+\) when \(f(\bar x_k)-f(x_k^+)\ge\eta\Delta_k\); otherwise set \(\bar x_{k+1}=\bar x_k\). Add a cut at \(x_k^+\), retain \(t\) unchanged, and stop when \(\Delta_k\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve every bundle master with the same proximal parameter, moving the center only when actual decrease captures a fixed fraction of predicted decrease.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper closed convex and the bundle models satisfy \(m_k\le f\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(t_k=t\) for every iteration, while the center update is determined by the displayed serious-step test.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: canonical fixed-parameter serious/null-step bundle scheme

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits, but predicted-decrease definitions, serious-step tests, and stopping tests vary across proximal bundle schemes. A bundle-specific source is needed to confirm this exact fixed-parameter variant.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Proximal Parameters
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ratio-based adaptation of proximal stabilization after trial-point evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), solve the proximal bundle master with \(t_k>0\), obtaining \(x_k^+\) and predicted decrease \(\Delta_k=f(\bar x_k)-m_k(x_k^+)>0\). Define the agreement ratio \[\rho_k=\frac{f(\bar x_k)-f(x_k^+)}{\Delta_k}.\] Choose constants \(0<\eta_1<\eta_2<1\), \(0<\gamma_-<1<\gamma_+\). After applying the prescribed serious-step test, update \(t_{k+1}=\gamma_-t_k\) if \(\rho_k<\eta_1\), set \(t_{k+1}=t_k\) if \(\eta_1\le\rho_k\le\eta_2\), and set \(t_{k+1}=\gamma_+t_k\) if \(\rho_k>\eta_2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compare actual and predicted decrease, strengthen stabilization after poor agreement, preserve it after moderate agreement, and relax it after good agreement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(t_{k+1}\in\{\gamma_-t_k,t_k,\gamma_+t_k\}\) is selected by the agreement ratio \(\rho_k\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Failure Modes Excluded by Two-Sided Parameter Safeguards
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separate roles of positive lower and finite upper bounds on the proximal parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the affine model \(m(x)=g^{\mathsf T}x\) centered at \(c\), the master minimizer is \(x_t^+=c-tg\). Thus \(t_k\downarrow0\) makes \(\|x_{t_k}^+-c\|=t_k\|g\|\downarrow0\) while the curvature \(1/t_k\) diverges. Conversely, for \(m(x)=-x\) centered at zero, the minimizer is \(x_t^+=t\) and the optimal value is \(-t/2\); hence \(t_k\to\infty\) removes uniform curvature and sends the trial points and master values to infinity and minus infinity, respectively. Bounds \(0<t_{\min}\le t_k\le t_{\max}<\infty\) exclude both regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive lower bound prevents arbitrarily severe stabilization and vanishing affine-model steps, while a finite upper bound prevents loss of uniform curvature and unbounded affine-model trials.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: t_k\downarrow0\Rightarrow x_{t_k}^+\to c,\qquad t_k\to\infty\Rightarrow\text{uniform master curvature is lost}.
knowledge_statements.title: Failure Modes Excluded by Two-Sided Parameter Safeguards
Proximal-Parameter Safeguards
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform bounds preventing vanishing or unbounded proximal parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\widehat t_{k+1}>0\) be any parameter proposed by an adaptive bundle rule. Given constants \(0<t_{\min}\le t_{\max}<+\infty\), the safeguarded update is \[t_{k+1}=\min\{t_{\max},\max\{t_{\min},\widehat t_{k+1}\}\}.\] Equivalently, every accepted parameter must satisfy \(t_{\min}\le t_k\le t_{\max}\). For the master penalty \(\|x-\bar x_k\|^2/(2t_k)\), these bounds keep the quadratic coefficient between \(1/(2t_{\max})\) and \(1/(2t_{\min})\), excluding both loss of stabilization and arbitrarily severe stabilization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Project each proposed proximal parameter onto a fixed positive interval, thereby bounding the strength of quadratic stabilization above and below.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: interval projection safeguard for proximal parameters

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pointwise Definiteness Does Not Give Uniform Metric Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes well-posed individual masters from uniform control of the metric sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The conditions \(H_k\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\) make each convex quadratic master strongly convex, but do not imply iteration-independent norm equivalence. For \(H_k=k^{-1}I\), every \(H_k\) is positive definite while \(\lambda_{\min}(H_k)\downarrow0\). Hence pointwise positive definiteness cannot replace bounds \(\mu I\preceq H_k\preceq LI\) in results requiring uniform metric control.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Individual masters may be well posed while their metrics degenerate across iterations; uniform spectral bounds are an additional assumption.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: H_k\succ0\ \forall k\not\Rightarrow\exists\mu,L>0:\ \mu I\preceq H_k\preceq LI\ \forall k.

notation.meaning: smallest eigenvalue of the current metric

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Euclidean Coordinate Form of a Variable-Metric Master
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-master coordinate representation and optimality condition for variable-metric proximal stabilization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\), \(t>0\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), and let \(m\) be proper closed convex. Under \(z=H^{1/2}(x-c)\), \[\min_x\left\{m(x)+\frac1{2t}(x-c)^{\mathsf T}H(x-c)\right\}=\min_z\left\{m(c+H^{-1/2}z)+\frac1{2t}\|z\|_2^2\right\}.\] The master has a unique minimizer \(x^+\), characterized by \(0\in\partial m(x^+)+t^{-1}H(x^+-c)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A square-root change of variables converts a positive-definite variable-metric master into a Euclidean proximal master and yields its exact optimality condition.
assumptions_latex: m\text{ is proper, closed, and convex}

notation.meaning: positive-definite square root of the metric

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Variable-Metric Predicted-Decrease Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Master-decrease certificate in the current metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(m\) be proper, closed, and convex, let \(H\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\), \(t>0\), and suppose \(m(c)<+\infty\). If
\[x^+=\operatorname*{argmin}_x\left\{m(x)+\frac1{2t}\|x-c\|_H^2\right\},\]
then
\[m(c)-m(x^+)\ge \frac1{2t}\|x^+-c\|_H^2\ge0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A variable-metric master lowers the unstabilized model by at least half the squared metric displacement divided by the proximal parameter.
assumptions_latex: m\text{ is proper, closed, and convex}.
knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Metric Predicted-Decrease Bound
Variable-Metric Proximal Bundle Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bundle stabilization in an iteration-dependent positive-definite metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), choose a symmetric positive-definite matrix \(H_k\) and solve \[x_k^+\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\left\{m_k(x)+\frac{1}{2t_k}(x-\bar x_k)^{\mathsf T}H_k(x-\bar x_k)\right\}.\] Apply the usual serious/null-step test, update the cutting-plane model, and update \(H_k\) only through a rule preserving \(\mu I\preceq H_k\preceq LI\) for fixed \(0<\mu\le L<+\infty\). If \(\bar g_k\) is the aggregate subgradient given by the master dual, the trial displacement satisfies \(x_k^+-\bar x_k=-t_kH_k^{-1}\bar g_k\). Stop under the chosen model-gap test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replace Euclidean stabilization by a uniformly positive-definite changing metric; the trial displacement is the inverse-metric-scaled negative aggregate subgradient.
assumptions_latex: Each model \(m_k\) is a convex minorant of \(f\).
\(t_k>0\) and \(\mu I\preceq H_k\preceq LI\) for fixed positive \(\mu,L\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_k^+-\bar x_k=-t_kH_k^{-1}\bar g_k\), with a uniquely defined trial point.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: uniformly bounded variable-metric proximal master

A bundle-specific source is required.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Master-Preserving Aggregate Cut
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact aggregation of current proximal-master active information before bounded-memory deletion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m(x)=\max_i\ell_i(x)\), and let \((x^+,\lambda^*)\) be primal-dual optimal for the Euclidean proximal master, where \(\lambda_i^*\ge0\), \(\sum_i\lambda_i^*=1\), and positive weights are supported on cuts active at \(x^+\). Define \(\ell_{\mathrm{agg}}=\sum_i\lambda_i^*\ell_i\). Then \[\ell_{\mathrm{agg}}\le f,\qquad \ell_{\mathrm{agg}}(x^+)=m(x^+),\qquad \nabla\ell_{\mathrm{agg}}=\sum_i\lambda_i^*g_i.\] Retaining this aggregate preserves the solved master's value and proximal first-order condition at \(x^+\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The optimal dual aggregate is a valid minorant preserving the current master's value and stationarity at its trial point.
assumptions_latex: Every affine cut \ell_i globally minorizes f.
\lambda^*\text{ is an optimal simplex multiplier for the current proximal master}.
Positive multipliers are supported on cuts active at x^+.
review_flags: This establishes aggregation of the complete optimal multiplier information; a deletion-only aggregation policy requires separately defined normalized weights and guarantees.
knowledge_statements.title: Master-Preserving Aggregate Cut
Limited-Memory Proximal Bundle Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounded bundle storage with an aggregate cut preserving discarded information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a memory limit \(M\ge2\). After solving the proximal master, let active cut multipliers be \(\lambda_i\ge0\) with \(\sum_i\lambda_i=1\), and replace cuts selected for deletion by their aggregate \[\ell_{\mathrm{agg}}(x)=\sum_i\lambda_i\ell_i(x).\] Because every \(\ell_i\le f\), the aggregate also satisfies \(\ell_{\mathrm{agg}}\le f\). Retain this aggregate cut, the newest oracle cut, and at most \(M-2\) selected individual cuts; define the next model as their pointwise maximum. Solve the next proximal master with that model, apply the serious/null-step rule, and repeat until the model-gap stopping test holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Keep a bounded number of cuts while replacing discarded active information by one convexly aggregated cut that remains a valid global minorant.
assumptions_latex: Every stored affine cut \(\ell_i\) globally minorizes the convex objective \(f\).
The aggregation weights are nonnegative and sum to one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\ell_{\mathrm{agg}}\le f\), and the next bundle contains at most \(M\) cuts.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: bounded cut storage using a dual aggregate cut

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A convex aggregate of valid cuts remains a valid minorant and the memory count is correct. However, it is unclear whether the multipliers aggregate all active cuts or only deleted cuts; those alternatives have different information-preservation properties and require a precise limited-memory bundle source.

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Proximal Bundle Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex variant with inexact cutting planes and approximate proximal subproblem solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be proper, closed, and convex. At sampled points \(y_i\), obtain \((\tilde f_i,g_i,\varepsilon_i)\) satisfying \(f(z)\ge \tilde f_i+\langle g_i,z-y_i\rangle-\varepsilon_i\) for every \(z\). Form \(m_k(z)=\max_{i\in I_k}\{\tilde f_i+\langle g_i,z-y_i\rangle-\varepsilon_i\}\). Given center \(x_k\) and \(t_k>0\), compute \(y_{k+1}\) whose proximal objective is within \(\delta_k\ge0\) of \(\inf_z\{m_k(z)+\|z-x_k\|^2/(2t_k)\}\). Accept \(y_{k+1}\) as the next center only when its verified objective decrease exceeds a prescribed fraction of the error-adjusted predicted decrease; otherwise retain \(x_k\) and add the new inexact cut. Stop when the error-adjusted predicted decrease is below tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Build error-valid affine cuts, approximately solve the stabilized bundle model, and accept a serious step only when verified decrease sufficiently matches error-adjusted prediction.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, closed, and convex on \(\mathbb{R}^n\).
Every oracle response satisfies the displayed global inexact-cut inequality.
\(t_k>0\), and subproblem errors \(\delta_k\) are controlled by the chosen stopping rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y_{k+1}\) is either accepted as a serious-step center or supplies a new cut for a null step.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm content kind fits the method leaf, and the variables and finite-dimensional convex scope are explicit. However, the oracle-error model, approximate proximal-subproblem criterion, error-adjusted predicted decrease, acceptance test, and stopping rule are convention-dependent and have no cited source. Their exact mathematical compatibility cannot be confirmed from the record alone.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Center Exactness and Predicted-Decrease Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonnegativity certificate for the standard composite bundle prediction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the current model is exact at the center, \(m_k(x_k)=f(x_k)\), and \(y_{k+1}\) minimizes the composite proximal master, then \[\Delta_k:=F(x_k)-\bigl(m_k(y_{k+1})+h(y_{k+1})\bigr)\ge \frac{1}{2t_k}\|y_{k+1}-x_k\|^2\ge0.\] Thus a nonzero trial displacement gives strictly positive predicted decrease.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Retaining center exactness makes the composite predicted decrease nonnegative and bounds it below by the proximal quadratic.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Composite Master Optimality System
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order characterization of the exact-term composite proximal bundle subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m_k=\max_{i\in I_k}\ell_i\), let \(h\) be proper closed convex, and let \(y_{k+1}\) minimize \[m_k(z)+h(z)+\frac{1}{2t_k}\|z-x_k\|^2,\qquad t_k>0.\] Then there are active-cut weights \(\lambda_i\ge0\), \(\sum_i\lambda_i=1\), and \(q_{k+1}\in\partial h(y_{k+1})\) such that \[0=\sum_i\lambda_i g_i+q_{k+1}+\frac1{t_k}(y_{k+1}-x_k).\] Conversely, this relation with active-cut simplex weights characterizes the unique minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Composite-master optimality balances an aggregate bundle subgradient, a subgradient of the exact term, and the proximal displacement.
assumptions_latex: m_k\text{ is a finite maximum of affine functions with slopes }g_i.
h\text{ is proper, closed, and convex}.
t_k>0\text{ and the master is proper}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fenchel–Simplex Dual of the Composite Proximal Master
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual representation of one exact-term composite bundle master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Write \(m(z)=\max_{i\in I}\{a_i+\langle g_i,z\rangle\}\), let \(\psi(z)=h(z)+\|z-x^c\|^2/(2t)\), and assume \(h\) is proper, closed, and convex and \(t>0\). Then
\[\inf_z\{m(z)+\psi(z)\}=\max_{\lambda\in\Delta_I}\left\{\sum_{i\in I}\lambda_i a_i-\psi^*\!\left(-\sum_{i\in I}\lambda_i g_i\right)\right\}.\]
At a primal-dual optimum \((z^*,\lambda^*)\), every positive \(\lambda_i^*\) indexes a cut active at \(z^*\), and \(-\sum_i\lambda_i^*g_i\in\partial\psi(z^*)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The composite master has a simplex dual coupling the aggregate bundle slope to the conjugate of the exact term and proximal quadratic.
assumptions_latex: h\text{ is proper, closed, and convex}.
knowledge_statements.title: Fenchel–Simplex Dual of the Composite Proximal Master
Composite Proximal Bundle Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex sum with one oracle-accessible term and one proximable closed convex term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=f+h\), where \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is convex and queried through values and subgradients, while \(h:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, convex, and handled exactly. From cuts \(f(y_i)+\langle g_i,z-y_i\rangle\), with \(g_i\in\partial f(y_i)\), form \(m_k(z)\) as their maximum. Given center \(x_k\in\operatorname{dom}h\) and \(t_k>0\), compute \(y_{k+1}\in\arg\min_z\{m_k(z)+h(z)+\|z-x_k\|^2/(2t_k)\}\). Compare \(F(x_k)-F(y_{k+1})\) with \(F(x_k)-[m_k(y_{k+1})+h(y_{k+1})]\); accept a serious step when the former is at least a fixed fraction of the latter, and otherwise keep the center and append a cut of \(f\) at \(y_{k+1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Model only the oracle term, retain the simple convex term exactly, solve a stabilized composite subproblem, and use actual-versus-predicted decrease for serious steps.

\(h\) is proper, closed, convex, and its stabilized subproblem is solvable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The trial point minimizes the composite bundle-proximal model and is processed by the stated serious/null-step test.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Optimality Certificate on a Euclidean Bundle Region
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order certificate for minimizing a convex bundle model over a Euclidean ball.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper closed convex, \(c\in\operatorname{dom}m\), and \(\Delta>0\). A feasible point \(y\) minimizes \(m\) over \(B_2(c,\Delta)\) if and only if there exist \(g\in\partial m(y)\) and \(\lambda\ge0\) such that \[g+\lambda(y-c)=0,\qquad \lambda(\|y-c\|_2-\Delta)=0.\] Thus an interior minimizer satisfies \(0\in\partial m(y)\), whereas a nonstationary minimizer lies on the boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Euclidean-region trial is optimal exactly when a model subgradient is balanced by a nonnegative radial normal with complementary boundary activity.
assumptions_latex: m\text{ is proper, closed, and convex}
knowledge_statements.title: Optimality Certificate on a Euclidean Bundle Region
Polyhedral Bundle Regions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Trust region defined by finitely many linear inequalities around the bundle center.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_k\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(A_k\in\mathbb{R}^{q\times n}\), and \(b_k\in\mathbb{R}^q_+\). A polyhedral bundle region is \[\mathcal R_k^{P}=\{x_k+d:A_kd\le b_k\}.\] It is a trust region when the displacement set \(\{d:A_kd\le b_k\}\) is bounded and contains \(0\) in its interior. The box region \(\|d\|_\infty\le\Delta_k\) is the special case obtained by stacking \(I\) and \(-I\) with right-hand side \(\Delta_k\mathbf 1\). With a polyhedral bundle model, minimizing the model over this region admits an epigraph linear-programming formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polyhedral bundle region constrains displacement by finitely many linear inequalities; boundedness and interior containment of zero make it a genuine local trust region.
assumptions_latex: \(\{d:A_kd\le b_k\}\) is bounded and contains \(0\) in its interior.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal R_k^{P}\) is a bounded polyhedral neighborhood of \(x_k\).

knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Metric Bundle Regions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ellipsoidal trust region induced by an iteration-dependent positive-definite metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_k\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(\Delta_k>0\), and let \(H_k\in\mathbb{S}_{++}^n\). The variable-metric bundle region is \[\mathcal R_k^{H}=\{x_k+d:d^{\mathsf T}H_kd\le\Delta_k^2\}.\] Equivalently, \(\mathcal R_k^{H}=\{x_k+d:\|d\|_{H_k}\le\Delta_k\}\), where \(\|d\|_{H_k}=\sqrt{d^{\mathsf T}H_kd}\). It is a closed, bounded, convex ellipsoid. If uniform constants \(0<\mu\le L<\infty\) satisfy \(\mu I\preceq H_k\preceq LI\), its geometry remains uniformly equivalent to Euclidean geometry across iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A variable-metric bundle region is an ellipsoid defined by a positive-definite iteration-dependent matrix; uniform spectral bounds prevent degenerating geometry.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal R_k^{H}\) is an ellipsoidal neighborhood of \(x_k\), uniformly nondegenerate under the stated spectral bounds.

notation.meaning: metric norm induced by the matrix

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric failure when metric eigenvalues approach zero or infinity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With fixed \(\Delta>0\), the metrics \(H_k=k^{-2}I\) produce Euclidean balls of radius \(k\Delta\), whereas \(H_k=k^2I\) produces balls of radius \(\Delta/k\). Thus pointwise positive definiteness makes each region an ellipsoid but does not prevent unbounded expansion or collapse across iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Iterationwise positive definiteness does not prevent metric regions from expanding indefinitely or collapsing in Euclidean geometry.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Euclidean Sandwich for Variable-Metric Regions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp Euclidean inclusions implied by uniform spectral bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(0<\mu\le L\), \(\mu I\preceq H_k\preceq LI\), and \(\mathcal R_k^H=\{x_k+d:d^{\mathsf T}H_kd\le\Delta_k^2\}\), then \[B_2\!\left(x_k,\frac{\Delta_k}{\sqrt L}\right)\subseteq\mathcal R_k^H\subseteq B_2\!\left(x_k,\frac{\Delta_k}{\sqrt\mu}\right).\] The constants are attained in eigendirections associated with eigenvalues \(L\) and \(\mu\), when present.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform eigenvalue bounds sandwich every metric ellipsoid between Euclidean balls with explicit sharp radii.

Bundle Model Agreement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Actual-to-predicted decrease ratio for a trust-region bundle trial point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m_k\) be a bundle model satisfying \(m_k(x_k)=f(x_k)\), and let \(y_k\) be a trial point. Define the predicted decrease \(p_k=f(x_k)-m_k(y_k)\) and actual decrease \(a_k=f(x_k)-f(y_k)\). When \(p_k>0\), the bundle model-agreement ratio is \[\rho_k=\frac{a_k}{p_k}.\] For a prescribed \(\eta\in(0,1)\), model agreement sufficient for a serious step is the predicate \(\rho_k\ge\eta\), equivalently \(f(y_k)\le f(x_k)-\eta p_k\). If \(p_k\le0\), the ratio is not used as an acceptance certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Agreement is the ratio of actual objective decrease to bundle-model predicted decrease; a trial is acceptable when this ratio exceeds a fixed threshold.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Range and Exactness of the Agreement Ratio
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consequences of global lower-model validity at a trial point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m_k\le f\), \(m_k(x_k)=f(x_k)\), \(p_k=f(x_k)-m_k(y_k)>0\), \(a_k=f(x_k)-f(y_k)\), and \(\rho_k=a_k/p_k\). Then \(a_k\le p_k\), so \(\rho_k\le1\), with \(\rho_k=1\) if and only if \(m_k(y_k)=f(y_k)\). No universal finite lower bound exists across convex bundle instances: for \(f_K(x)=\max\{-x,Kx\}\), \(m(x)=-x\), \(x_k=0\), and \(y_k=1\), one has \(p_k=1\) and \(\rho_k=-K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid lower model makes agreement at most one, with equality exactly at trial-point model exactness, but agreement can be arbitrarily negative across convex instances.
knowledge_statements.title: Range and Exactness of the Agreement Ratio
Bundle Radius Management
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Threshold-based trust-region radius update using bundle model agreement and boundary activity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(0<\eta_1<\eta_2<1\), \(0<\gamma_-<1<\gamma_+\), and bounds \(0<\Delta_{\min}\le\Delta_{\max}\). After computing a trial displacement \(d_k\) and agreement ratio \(\rho_k\), update \[\Delta_{k+1}=\begin{cases}\max\{\Delta_{\min},\gamma_-\Delta_k\},&\rho_k<\eta_1,\\ \min\{\Delta_{\max},\gamma_+\Delta_k\},&\rho_k\ge\eta_2\text{ and }\|d_k\|\ge\theta\Delta_k,\\ \Delta_k,&\text{otherwise},\end{cases}\] where \(\theta\in(0,1]\). Reject the trial when \(\rho_k<\eta_1\); accept it when \(\rho_k\ge\eta_1\). The clipping bounds apply at every iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Shrink the radius after poor agreement, enlarge it after strong agreement near the boundary, otherwise retain it, and always enforce positive finite bounds.
assumptions_latex: The agreement ratio is evaluated only for positive predicted decrease.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Delta_{k+1}\in[\Delta_{\min},\Delta_{\max}]\), with contraction, expansion, or retention determined by model agreement.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Well-Defined Bundle Trial Acceptance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary well-posedness checks before applying a serious-step acceptance test.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let p_k=f(x_k)-m_k(y_k). The actual-to-predicted acceptance ratio may be evaluated only when y_k is an admissible trial, f(y_k) is available and finite, and p_k>0. For a fixed \eta\in(0,1), a serious step requires f(x_k)-f(y_k)\ge \eta p_k. If any prerequisite fails or the inequality fails, y_k is not accepted as the new center; handling of the bundle, radius, or stopping test is delegated to the specified algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluate agreement only for an admissible, finitely evaluated trial with positive predicted decrease. Accept it only after sufficient actual decrease; otherwise do not move the center.
assumptions_latex: Admissibility includes every feasibility requirement of the underlying problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}=y_k\) is permitted only if \(y_k\) is admissible, \(f(y_k)\in\mathbb R\), \(p_k>0\), and \(f(x_k)-f(y_k)\ge\eta p_k\).
knowledge_statements.title: Well-Defined Bundle Trial Acceptance
Trust-Region Safeguards
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Well-posedness and acceptance safeguards for bundle trust-region iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A safeguarded bundle trust-region iteration enforces \(0<\Delta_{\min}\le\Delta_k\le\Delta_{\max}<\infty\), requires a feasible trial point, and accepts a serious step only if the predicted decrease \(p_k\) is positive and the actual decrease satisfies \(f(x_k)-f(y_k)\ge\eta p_k\) for some \(\eta\in(0,1)\). If the trial evaluation is unavailable, nonfinite, infeasible, or fails this inequality, the center remains \(x_{k+1}=x_k\), the valid new cutting-plane information is retained when available, and the radius is not enlarged. Termination based on prediction is permitted only when the model and oracle error tolerances are also satisfied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Keep radii bounded, accept only feasible finite trials with positive prediction and sufficient decrease, retain the center after failure, and include oracle errors in termination.
assumptions_latex: Accepted cuts are valid lower estimators of the convex objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted trial has certified sufficient decrease; every failed trial preserves the current center and cannot enlarge the radius.

knowledge_statements.title: Bundle Trust Methods with Line Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bundle trust-region direction followed by backtracking along the trial displacement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m_k\) be a convex bundle model exact at the center \(x_k\). Compute \(d_k\in\arg\min_{\|d\|\le\Delta_k}m_k(x_k+d)\) and set \(p_k=f(x_k)-m_k(x_k+d_k)\). If \(p_k\le0\), stop according to the model tolerance. Otherwise choose \(\sigma,\beta\in(0,1)\) and select the first \(t_k\in\{1,\beta,\beta^2,\ldots\}\) satisfying \(f(x_k+t_kd_k)\le f(x_k)-\sigma t_kp_k\). Set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+t_kd_k\), add a value-subgradient cut at this point, and update the trust radius from model agreement. If no admissible step above a prescribed minimum is found, retain \(x_k\), add available trial cuts, and reduce the radius.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compute a bundle trust-region direction, backtrack along it until scaled predicted decrease is realized, then update the bundle and radius.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex and has a value-subgradient oracle.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An accepted line-search trial satisfies \(f(x_{k+1})\le f(x_k)-\sigma t_kp_k\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct trial acceptance by model agreement, without searching along the trial segment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a center \(x_k\), bundle model \(m_k\), region \(\mathcal R_k\), and threshold \(\eta\in(0,1)\), compute \(y_k\in\arg\min_{y\in\mathcal R_k}m_k(y)\) and \(p_k=f(x_k)-m_k(y_k)\). If \(p_k\) is below tolerance, stop. Otherwise evaluate \(f(y_k)\), form \(\rho_k=[f(x_k)-f(y_k)]/p_k\), and set \(x_{k+1}=y_k\) when \(\rho_k\ge\eta\), or \(x_{k+1}=x_k\) otherwise. In both cases add a valid cut at \(y_k\); update the region radius using \(\rho_k\). No intermediate point \(x_k+t(y_k-x_k)\) is evaluated solely to choose a step length.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve one trust-region bundle subproblem and accept or reject its trial directly from model agreement, without a line search along the segment.

The trial subproblem has a solution and \(p_k>0\) when agreement is evaluated.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex, let \(I_k\) be a finite nonempty index set, and let \(a_i\in\mathbb{R}\) and \(g_i\in\mathbb{R}^n\) for every \(i\in I_k\). Suppose the bundle model is \(m_k(x_k+d)=\max_{i\in I_k}\{a_i+\langle g_i,d\rangle\}\). Given \(A_k\in\mathbb{R}^{q\times n}\) and \(b_k\in\mathbb{R}^q\), assume the displacement region \(\{d\in\mathbb{R}^n:A_kd\le b_k\}\) is nonempty and bounded. Compute \((d_k,r_k)\) by the linear program \[\min_{d\in\mathbb{R}^n,\ r\in\mathbb{R}} r\quad\text{subject to}\quad a_i+\langle g_i,d\rangle\le r\ \text{for every }i\in I_k,\qquad A_kd\le b_k.\] Set \(y_k=x_k+d_k\) and define \(p_k=f(x_k)-r_k\). If \(p_k\) is below the stopping tolerance, terminate. Otherwise evaluate \(f(y_k)\) and a subgradient at \(y_k\), append the resulting valid cut, and accept \(y_k\) when \(f(x_k)-f(y_k)\) is at least a prescribed fraction of \(p_k>0\); if this test fails, retain \(x_k\). Update the polyhedral region according to the selected trust-region policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Express the finite cutting-plane model and polyhedral trust region by linear inequalities, solve the resulting epigraph linear program, and apply the serious/null-step test only when the predicted decrease is positive.

knowledge_statements.title: Single Aggregate-Plane Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bundle compression retaining one aggregate plane plus the newly generated oracle plane.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), let the stored aggregate plane be \(\bar\ell_k(x)=\bar a_k+\langle\bar g_k,x\rangle\), with \(\bar\ell_k\le f\), and obtain a new oracle plane \(\ell_k\le f\). Solve the stabilized model subproblem using \(m_k(x)=\max\{\bar\ell_k(x),\ell_k(x)\}\). Let \(\lambda_k\in[0,1]\) be an optimal multiplier assigned to \(\bar\ell_k\) in the epigraph formulation, and define \[\bar\ell_{k+1}=\lambda_k\bar\ell_k+(1-\lambda_k)\ell_k.\] Discard the two constituent planes after storing \(\bar\ell_{k+1}\), generate the next oracle plane at the trial point, and use the usual serious/null-step acceptance rule. Stop when the stabilized model prediction is within tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compress the active model information into one convexly aggregated affine lower plane, retain it, and combine it with the next oracle plane.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex, and every constituent affine plane globally underestimates \(f\).
\(\lambda_k\in[0,1]\) is obtained from the stabilized subproblem multipliers.
The stabilized subproblem has an optimal solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar\ell_{k+1}\le f\), so the single stored aggregate remains a valid affine lower estimator.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm content kind fits the aggregate-plane method leaf, and a convex combination of valid affine lower estimators is again valid. However, the identification of \(\lambda_k\) with a particular epigraph multiplier, the ordering of aggregation and new-cut generation, and the claim that only one aggregate plus the new plane is retained depend on the precise stabilized subproblem formulation. No source is supplied for those conventions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dominance over the Single-Aggregate Model
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural effect of retaining valid recent cuts in addition to one aggregate plane.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(a_k\le f\) be an aggregate affine minorant and let \(c_i\le f\) be retained recent affine cuts for \(i\in R_k\). Define
\[m_k^{\mathrm{agg}}(x):=a_k(x),\qquad m_k^{\mathrm{ar}}(x):=\max\{a_k(x),\max_{i\in R_k}c_i(x)\}.\]
Then
\[m_k^{\mathrm{agg}}(x)\le m_k^{\mathrm{ar}}(x)\le f(x)\quad\text{for every }x.\]
For every center \(x_k\) and \(t_k>0\),
\[\inf_x\left\{m_k^{\mathrm{agg}}(x)+\frac{\|x-x_k\|^2}{2t_k}\right\}\le\inf_x\left\{m_k^{\mathrm{ar}}(x)+\frac{\|x-x_k\|^2}{2t_k}\right\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding valid recent cuts produces a tighter valid model and a no-smaller proximal-master lower bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Dominance over the Single-Aggregate Model
Aggregate-Plus-Recent-Cut Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restricted-memory convex bundle model retaining one aggregate plane and selected recent oracle cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex. At iteration \(k\), retain an aggregate affine minorant \(a_k\leq f\) and recent cuts \(c_i(x)=f(y_i)+\langle g_i,x-y_i\rangle\), where \(g_i\in\partial f(y_i)\) and \(i\in R_k\). Form \(m_k(x)=\max\{a_k(x),\max_{i\in R_k}c_i(x)\}\), compute the stabilized trial point \(y_{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_x\{m_k(x)+(2t_k)^{-1}\|x-x_k\|^2\}\), and query \(f(y_{k+1})\) and a subgradient there. After the serious/null-step test, update the center and replace discarded active planes by a convex aggregate supporting \(m_k\) at \(y_{k+1}\). Output a center satisfying the prescribed model-gap tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maintain one aggregate minorant plus recent subgradient cuts, minimize their stabilized maximum, query a new cut, and aggregate discarded active information until the model gap is small.
assumptions_latex: \(t_k>0\), and every stored plane globally minorizes \(f\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m_k\leq f\), while the bundle memory is bounded by \(1+|R_k|\).
review_flags: Specialized aggregation update and serious/null-step convention require an authoritative bundle-method source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the leaf, but the aggregation update, serious/null-step convention, and claimed tolerance output depend on a specific bundle-method variant and have no cited source.

knowledge_statements.title: Aggregation with Subgradient Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Aggregation rule selecting a valid subgradient from active cutting planes at the stabilized trial point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(m_k(x)=\max_{i\in I_k}\{\alpha_i+\langle g_i,x\rangle\}\) and let \(y_{k+1}\) solve a stabilized model subproblem. Define the active set \(A_k=\{i:m_k(y_{k+1})=\alpha_i+\langle g_i,y_{k+1}\rangle\}\). Select coefficients \(\lambda_i\geq0\) with \(\sum_{i\in A_k}\lambda_i=1\), preferably the subproblem multiplier vector, and set \(\bar g_k=\sum_{i\in A_k}\lambda_i g_i\) and \(a_{k+1}(x)=m_k(y_{k+1})+\langle\bar g_k,x-y_{k+1}\rangle\). Then retain \(a_{k+1}\), together with any designated recent cuts, for the next model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose a convex combination of active cut slopes, use it as a model subgradient, and store its supporting plane as the aggregate cut.
assumptions_latex: \(I_k\) is finite and every plane in \(m_k\) minorizes the convex objective.
\(y_{k+1}\) is a finite solution of the stabilized model subproblem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar g_k\in\partial m_k(y_{k+1})\) and \(a_{k+1}(x)\leq m_k(x)\leq f(x)\) for every \(x\).
review_flags: Exact multiplier-based selection rule needs a bundle-method source locator.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role and active-slope aggregation statement are appropriate, but the preferred multiplier selection and its place in the bundle update require an inspectable bundle-method source.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Directional-Fidelity Characterization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact condition under which one aggregate active-plane slope preserves every first-order direction of a polyhedral model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(m(x)=\max_{i\in I}\{\alpha_i+\langle g_i,x\rangle\}\), and let \(I(y)\) be its active set at \(y\). Choose \(\lambda_i\ge0\) on \(I(y)\) with \(\sum_i\lambda_i=1\), set \(\bar g=\sum_i\lambda_i g_i\), and define \(a(x)=m(y)+\langle\bar g,x-y\rangle\). Then
\[m'(y;d)=\max_{i\in I(y)}\langle g_i,d\rangle,\qquad a'(y;d)=\langle\bar g,d\rangle.\]
Equality for every direction \(d\) holds if and only if \(g_i=\bar g\) for every \(i\in I(y)\). Thus genuine active-slope diversity forces directional information loss.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A single aggregate plane preserves every directional derivative exactly when all active cut slopes coincide.
assumptions_latex: \(m\) is a finite maximum of affine functions.
\(\bar g\) is a convex combination of slopes active at \(y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a'(y;\cdot)=m'(y;\cdot)\) in every direction if and only if \(g_i=\bar g\) for every \(i\in I(y)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Directional-Fidelity Characterization
Aggregation Information-Loss Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies when one aggregate plane preserves only local first-order model information and loses other bundle geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m(x)=\max_{i\in I}c_i(x)\), choose \(y\), and aggregate active cuts into \(a(x)=m(y)+\langle\bar g,x-y\rangle\) with \(\bar g\in\partial m(y)\). The aggregate preserves the value and selected subgradient at \(y\), but generally \(a(x)<m(x)\) away from \(y\). For example, for \(m(x)=|x|=\max\{x,-x\}\), \(y=0\), and equal weights, \(a(x)=0\); hence all directional growth is lost although \(a(0)=m(0)\). Equality \(a=m\) globally can hold only when the retained aggregate affine function itself represents the relevant model over the localization region.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A single aggregate plane preserves one model value and subgradient but can discard directional growth; aggregating the two cuts of absolute value at zero yields the zero plane.
assumptions_latex: \(m\) is a finite maximum of affine minorants.
\(\bar g\) is a convex combination of slopes active at \(y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Local first-order consistency at \(y\) does not imply global preservation of the polyhedral model.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Level-Method Update and Stopping Rule
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basic level-method iteration using the current bound gap and projection onto the level localization set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Choose \(x_0\in Q\), \(\epsilon>0\), and \(\alpha\in(0,1)\). At iteration \(k\geq0\), compute \(\widehat f_k^*\) and \(f_k^*\). If
\[
f_k^*-\widehat f_k^*\leq\epsilon,
\]
stop. Otherwise set
\[
x_{k+1}=\pi_{\mathcal L_k(\alpha)}(x_k).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose an initial point, an accuracy, and a level coefficient. Stop when the current upper–lower bound gap is at most the accuracy; otherwise project the current iterate onto the level set.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Level Method Iteration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection-based level method using a model minimum, an incumbent record value, and a prescribed gap tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given $Q\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n$, $x_0\in Q$, $\epsilon>0$, and $\alpha\in(0,1)$, for $k=0,1,2,\ldots$ compute $\hat f_k^*=\min_{x\in Q}\hat f_k(X;x)$ and $f_k^*=\min_{0\le i\le k}f(x_i)$. Stop if $f_k^*-\hat f_k^*\le\epsilon$. Otherwise set $\ell_k(\alpha)=(1-\alpha)\hat f_k^*+\alpha f_k^*$, form $\mathcal L_k(\alpha)=\{x\in Q:\hat f_k(X;x)\le\ell_k(\alpha)\}$, and update $x_{k+1}=\pi_{\mathcal L_k(\alpha)}(x_k)$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each iteration, minimize the current model and compute the best objective value observed so far. Stop when their gap is at most the requested accuracy. Otherwise interpolate between them to choose a level, form the associated model sublevel set, and project the current iterate onto that set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f_k^*-\hat f_k^*\le\epsilon\ \Longrightarrow\ \operatorname{stop};\qquad f_k^*-\hat f_k^*>\epsilon\ \Longrightarrow\ x_{k+1}=\pi_{\mathcal L_k(\alpha)}(x_k).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Iteration bound and stopping guarantee for the Level Method
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case complexity on a bounded domain for a Lipschitz convex objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $Q\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be nonempty and bounded with $\operatorname{diam}(Q)=D$, and let $f:Q\to\mathbb{R}$ be convex and $M_f$-Lipschitz with respect to the norm defining $D$. Assume the optimal value $f^*=\min_{x\in Q}f(x)$ is defined. For $\epsilon>0$ and $\alpha\in(0,1)$, the Level Method applied to $\min_{x\in Q}f(x)$ terminates after at most $\left\lfloor\frac{M_f^2D^2}{\epsilon^2\alpha(1-\alpha)^2(2-\alpha)}\right\rfloor+1$ iterations. If it terminates at iteration $k$ by its stopping criterion, then its best trial value satisfies $f_k^*-f^*\le\epsilon$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a nonempty bounded domain of diameter D, the Level Method for an M_f-Lipschitz convex objective terminates within the stated O(M_f²D²/ε²) iteration bound. Termination by its stopping test certifies that the best trial value is within ε of the optimum.
assumptions_latex: f:Q\to\mathbb{R}\text{ is convex and }M_f\text{-Lipschitz with respect to the norm defining }D
f_k^*\text{ is the best objective value among trial points through iteration }k

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Complete componentwise model for a finite-maximum constraint
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded definition used in the constrained level-method construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\bar f(x)=\max_{1\le i\le m}f_i(x)\). Given \(x_0,\ldots,x_k\in Q\) and subgradients \(g_i(x_j)\in\partial f_i(x_j)\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\) and \(j=0,\ldots,k\), define
\[
\hat f_k(X;x)=\max_{0\le j\le k}\max_{1\le i\le m}\left[f_i(x_j)+\langle g_i(x_j),x-x_j\rangle\right].
\]

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Optimally parameterized Level-Method complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iteration complexity for the specified level parameter, measured using the initial distance to a chosen minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $Q$ be a nonempty closed convex subset of a Euclidean space, let $f:Q\to\mathbb{R}$ be convex, and suppose $\|g\|\le M_f$ for every $x\in Q$ and $g\in\partial f(x)$. Initialize the Level Method at $x^0\in Q$ and use $\alpha=\alpha^*=\frac{1}{2+\sqrt2}$. Let $x^*\in\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{x\in Q}f(x)$, set $f^*=f(x^*)$, and define $D=\|x^0-x^*\|$. Then, for every $\epsilon>0$, the number of iterations required to produce $x^N\in Q$ with $f(x^N)-f^*\le\epsilon$ satisfies $N\le\frac{4M_f^2D^2}{\epsilon^2}$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex objective with uniformly bounded subgradients, the Level Method using α*=1/(2+√2) reaches ε objective accuracy in at most 4M_f²D²/ε² iterations, where D is the initial distance to a chosen minimizer.
assumptions_latex: Q\text{ is a nonempty closed convex subset of a Euclidean space}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linear and Quadratic Subproblem Representations of the Level Method
knowledge_statements.scope_note: LP and QP realizations of the model-minimization and Euclidean projection steps for a polyhedral cutting-plane model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume $Q$ is a polytope and $\hat f_k(X;x)=\max_{0\le i\le k}\{f(x_i)+\langle g(x_i),x-x_i\rangle\}$. Then $\hat f_k^*$ is the optimal value of $\min_{x,t}t$ subject to $f(x_i)+\langle g(x_i),x-x_i\rangle\le t$ for $i=0,\ldots,k$ and $x\in Q$. Moreover, $x_{k+1}=\pi_{\mathcal L_k(\alpha)}(x_k)$ is obtained by minimizing $\|x-x_k\|^2$ subject to $f(x_i)+\langle g(x_i),x-x_i\rangle\le\ell_k(\alpha)$ for $i=0,\ldots,k$ and $x\in Q$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When Q is a polytope and the model is the maximum of accumulated affine cuts, minimizing the model has an epigraph linear-program representation. Projecting onto the level set has a convex quadratic-program representation requiring every accumulated cut to lie below the current level.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \hat f_k^*=\min_{x\in Q,\,t}\{t:f(x_i)+\langle g(x_i),x-x_i\rangle\le t,\ i=0,\ldots,k\},\quad x_{k+1}\in\arg\min_{x\in Q}\{\|x-x_k\|^2:f(x_i)+\langle g(x_i),x-x_i\rangle\le\ell_k(\alpha),\ i=0,\ldots,k\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Model Minimum, Record Value, Level Value, Level Set, and Gap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Core quantities used by a level method for a model constructed from the iterates through index k.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $Q\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n$ and let $\hat f_k(X;\cdot):Q\to\mathbb{R}$ be a model constructed from $x_0,\ldots,x_k\in Q$. Define $\hat f_k^*=\min_{x\in Q}\hat f_k(X;x)$ and $f_k^*=\min_{0\le i\le k}f(x_i)$. For $\alpha\in(0,1)$, define $\ell_k(\alpha)=(1-\alpha)\hat f_k^*+\alpha f_k^*$ and $\mathcal L_k(\alpha)=\{x\in Q:\hat f_k(X;x)\le\ell_k(\alpha)\}$. The model-value interval and gap are $\Delta_k=[\hat f_k^*,f_k^*]$ and $\delta_k=f_k^*-\hat f_k^*$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The minimal model value is the minimum of the current model over Q, and the record value is the best objective value among the iterates through k. A coefficient strictly between zero and one interpolates between them to form the level value. The corresponding level set consists of points whose model value does not exceed that level. Their interval and difference are denoted by Delta_k and delta_k.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \hat f_k^*=\min_{x\in Q}\hat f_k(X;x),\quad f_k^*=\min_{0\le i\le k}f(x_i),\quad \ell_k(\alpha)=(1-\alpha)\hat f_k^*+\alpha f_k^*,\quad \mathcal L_k(\alpha)=\{x\in Q:\hat f_k(X;x)\le\ell_k(\alpha)\},\quad \Delta_k=[\hat f_k^*,f_k^*],\quad \delta_k=f_k^*-\hat f_k^*.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nested Model-Record Intervals and Monotone Gaps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotonicity invariant for pointwise nondecreasing global lower models and incumbent record values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $Q$ be nonempty, let $(x_i)_{i\ge0}\subseteq Q$, and let $f:Q\to\mathbb{R}$. Suppose that for every $k\ge0$ and $x\in Q$, $\hat f_k(X;x)\le f(x)$ and $\hat f_{k+1}(X;x)\ge\hat f_k(X;x)$. Define $\hat f_k^*=\min_{x\in Q}\hat f_k(X;x)$ and $f_k^*=\min_{0\le i\le k}f(x_i)$. Then, for every $k\ge0$, $\hat f_k^*\le\hat f_{k+1}^*\le f_{k+1}^*\le f_k^*$. Consequently, with $\Delta_k=[\hat f_k^*,f_k^*]$ and $\delta_k=f_k^*-\hat f_k^*$, one has $\Delta_{k+1}\subseteq\Delta_k$ and $\delta_{k+1}\le\delta_k$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If each model globally underestimates the objective and the models increase pointwise with the iteration index, then their minimum values are nondecreasing while the best observed objective values are nonincreasing. The resulting model-record intervals are nested and their gaps are nonincreasing.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lower bound on a Level-Method step
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric separation forced by the cutting-plane level condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}$ be convex and suppose $\|g\|\le M_f$ for every $x\in\mathbb{R}^n$ and $g\in\partial f(x)$, where $M_f>0$. Then $\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|\ge (1-\alpha)\delta_k/M_f$.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Nonemptiness Threshold for Model Sublevels
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Attainment boundary for nonemptiness of a model sublevel within its working region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\neq\varnothing\), let \(m:Q\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), and set \(\alpha=\inf_{x\in Q}m(x)\in\mathbb R\). For \(L(\ell)=\{x\in Q:m(x)\leq\ell\}\), \(L(\ell)=\varnothing\) if \(\ell<\alpha\), while \(L(\ell)\neq\varnothing\) if \(\ell>\alpha\). At \(\ell=\alpha\), the set is nonempty exactly when \(m\) attains its infimum on \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A model sublevel is empty below the model infimum, nonempty above it, and nonempty at the infimum exactly when the infimum is attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\ell<\alpha\Rightarrow L(\ell)=\varnothing\), \(\ell>\alpha\Rightarrow L(\ell)\neq\varnothing\), and \(L(\alpha)\neq\varnothing\) exactly when \(m\) attains \(\alpha\).

notation.meaning: model infimum over the working region
model sublevel within the working region

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Nonemptiness Threshold for Model Sublevels
Projection-Center Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean projection characterization for choosing a prox-center from a nonempty convex localization set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L_k\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let \(x_k\in\mathbb{R}^n\). The projection center \(x_{k+1}=P_{L_k}(x_k)\) is the unique minimizer of \(\tfrac12\|x-x_k\|^2\) over \(L_k\). It is characterized by \[\langle x_k-x_{k+1},z-x_{k+1}\rangle\leq0\quad\text{for every }z\in L_k.\] Consequently, \(\|x_{k+1}-z\|^2\leq\|x_k-z\|^2-\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|^2\) for every \(z\in L_k\), so projection toward the localization set yields a quantified decrease in squared distance to each retained point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection onto a closed convex localization set is unique, satisfies the normal-cone inequality, and decreases squared distance to every point in that set.
assumptions_latex: \(L_k\) is nonempty, closed, and convex in Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}=P_{L_k}(x_k)\) is unique and satisfies the displayed variational and distance inequalities.

notation.meaning: Euclidean projection onto the localization set

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Level-Method Step-Length Lower Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower bound on the displacement produced by a level-method projection update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the sequence \(\{x_k\}\) generated by the level method,
\[
\lVert x_{k+1}-x_k\rVert\geq\frac{(1-\alpha)\delta_k}{M_f}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each generated level-method update has displacement at least one minus alpha times the current gap divided by M sub f.
assumptions_latex: \{x_k\}\text{ is generated by the level method}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Level-width decrease bound under retained width
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elementary inequality controlling the change between two members of the Level-Method width sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $Q$ be bounded with $\operatorname{diam}(Q)\le D$, let $\{\delta_k\}_{k\ge 0}$ be a sequence of nonnegative real numbers, and let $\alpha\in[0,1]$. If integers $p\ge k$ satisfy $\delta_p\ge(1-\alpha)\delta_k$, then $\delta_k-\delta_p\le\alpha\delta_k$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a later nonnegative level width retains at least a (1−α) fraction of the width at iteration k, its decrease from that width is at most an α fraction. The source also assumes that the problem set is bounded with diameter at most D, although that assumption is not needed for this inequality.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cumulative halfspace localization set and centered localization radius
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines cumulative localization geometry from vector observations. The quantities v_i use the previously defined function v_f from Definition 3.36; that dependency is essential and is not redefined by this extract.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), \(g:Q\to\mathbb R^n\), and \(\{x_i\}_{i=0}^{\infty}\subseteq Q\). For \(k\ge0\), define \[S_k:=\{x\in Q:\langle g(x_i),x_i-x\rangle\ge0\text{ for every }i=0,\ldots,k\}.\] Fix \(x^*\in Q\), and, using the previously defined quantity \(v_f\), set \(v_i:=v_f(x^*;x_i)\ge0\) and \(v_k^*:=\min_{0\le i\le k}v_i\). Then, equivalently, \[v_k^*=\max\{r\ge0:B_2(x^*,r)\subseteq S_k\}=\max\{r\ge0:\langle g(x_i),x_i-x\rangle\ge0\text{ for }i=0,\ldots,k\text{ and all }x\in B_2(x^*,r)\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The localization set is the intersection, within Q, of all halfspaces generated through iteration k. The smallest previously defined localization measure equals the largest radius of a Euclidean ball centered at the reference point that is contained in this cumulative localization set.

knowledge_statements.title: Nested Localization Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Update regime that preserves every valid cut by intersecting successive model sublevels with the preceding localization set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q_0\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex. For each \(k\), let \(H_k\) be a closed convex set containing the target solution set \(X^*\), and define \(Q_{k+1}=Q_k\cap H_k\). Then \(Q_{k+1}\subseteq Q_k\) and \(X^*\subseteq Q_k\) for every \(k\), provided \(X^*\subseteq Q_0\). When \(H_k=\{x:m_k(x)\leq\ell_k\}\), validity requires \(m_k(x^*)\leq\ell_k\) for every \(x^*\in X^*\). Thus nesting accumulates localization information without excluding a solution, but an invalid level cut can make a later set empty or remove all minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Intersecting each localization set with a valid new convex cut produces nested sets that retain all solutions; one invalid cut can destroy this guarantee.
assumptions_latex: Each \(H_k\) is closed, convex, and contains \(X^*\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nested localization sets generated by cutting vectors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines cumulative halfspace localization from a sequence of points in a convex set and associated vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be convex, let $X=\{x_i\}_{i=0}^\infty\subset Q$, and associate $g(x_k)\in\mathbb R^n$ with every $k\ge0$. Define $S_0(X)=Q$ and, for every $k\ge0$, $S_{k+1}(X)=\{x\in S_k(X):\langle g(x_k),x_k-x\rangle\ge0\}$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from Q, each successive localization set retains exactly those points in the current set lying in the halfspace selected by the vector associated with the current sequence point.

children.title: Reset Localization Sets
children.top_down_role: Localization geometries reconstructed at phase or progress resets.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Reset Localization Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic reconstruction of a localization set after discarding accumulated within-phase constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be a closed convex base region, let \(\mathcal J\) index the closed convex localization constraints retained at a reset, and define
\[
Q^+=X\cap\bigcap_{j\in\mathcal J}H_j.
\]
If the target solution set satisfies \(X^*\subseteq X\) and \(X^*\subseteq H_j\) for every \(j\in\mathcal J\), then \(X^*\subseteq Q^+\), so the rebuilt set is nonempty whenever \(X^*\ne\varnothing\). Because discarded constraints need not contain \(Q^+\), generally \(Q^+\nsubseteq Q\) for the pre-reset set \(Q\). If any retained constraint excludes a minimizer, the reset no longer certifies solution retention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reset rebuilds localization from the base region and selected retained constraints; valid retained constraints preserve every solution, but the rebuilt set generally breaks nesting.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and every retained \(H_j\) are closed and convex.

notation.meaning: indices of constraints retained at reset

review_flags: The choice of retained cuts and new center is deliberately left to the complete level algorithm using this geometry.
knowledge_statements.title: Reset Localization Geometry
Reset Localization Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonmonotone localization update that discards accumulated geometry while retaining currently certified cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a base feasible region \(X\), a current lower model \(m_k\), a level \(\ell_k\), and a reset index \(r\), define the post-reset localization set by \[Q_{k+1}=X\cap\{x:m_k^{\mathrm{keep}}(x)\leq\ell_k\},\] where \(m_k^{\mathrm{keep}}\) is formed only from cuts explicitly retained at the reset. Discard all older localization constraints not represented in \(m_k^{\mathrm{keep}}\), choose a new center by projecting a reference point onto \(Q_{k+1}\), and continue only if this set is nonempty. If every retained cut is a lower bound for \(f\) and \(f(x^*)\leq\ell_k\), then every minimizer \(x^*\) remains in the reset set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reset rebuilds localization from the base feasible set and selected valid cuts, discarding old geometry while preserving minimizers whenever the chosen level remains valid.
assumptions_latex: The selected level satisfies \(f(x^*)\leq\ell_k\) for each retained minimizer \(x^*\).

notation.meaning: model made from cuts retained after reset

review_flags: The precise reset construction and retained-cut policy require a level-method source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the reset leaf, but the retained-cut policy, projection reference, and reset construction are method-dependent and have no source. The unused reset index also indicates that the intended variant is not fully specified.

children.title: Localization-Reset Triggers
children.top_down_role: Structural conditions separating continued nesting from localization reset.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Certified Bound Triggers for Localization Reset
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Method-independent sufficient events for ending a level-localization phase and rebuilding its working set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(L\le f^*\le U\), choose \(\ell\in(L,U)\), let \(W\subseteq X\) contain the solution set \(X^*\), and let \(m\le f\) on \(W\). Two certified phase-completion events are:
\[
W\cap\{x:m(x)\le\ell\}=\varnothing,
\qquad\text{or}\qquad
U^+\le U-\eta(U-L)
\]
for a prescribed \(\eta\in(0,1)\), where \(U^+\) is an attained incumbent value. In the first case \(f^*\ge\ell\), so \(L\) may be replaced by \(\ell\); in the second, \(U\) may be replaced by \(U^+\). Either certified bound update may terminate the current phase and trigger reconstruction. The empty-set implication can fail if \(W\) excludes all minimizers or \(m\) is not a valid lower model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A localization phase may reset after certified model-level infeasibility raises the lower bound or after a prescribed incumbent improvement lowers the upper bound; invalid models or working sets destroy the first certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(U^+\) is the objective value of a feasible evaluated point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Model-level emptiness certifies \(f^*\ge\ell\), while the incumbent test certifies \(f^*\le U^+\); either bound update is a valid reset trigger.
review_flags: Radius, travel-distance, and method-specific restart tests are intentionally excluded.
knowledge_statements.title: Certified Bound Triggers for Localization Reset
Localization-Reset Triggers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Verifiable events under which a level method terminates a localization phase and rebuilds its working set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a phase have bounds \(L<U\), level \(\ell\in(L,U)\), localization set \(Q_k\), and reference center \(x^c\). A reset trigger is satisfied when at least one certified event occurs: \[Q_k\cap\{x:m_k(x)\leq\ell\}=\varnothing,\qquad U_k\leq\ell,\qquad L_k\geq\ell,\qquad\text{or}\qquad \|x_k-x^c\|>R,\] where the last event is an explicitly imposed radius safeguard. The first event certifies that the model lower bound exceeds the level on \(Q_k\); the next two certify passage of an upper or lower phase threshold. On a trigger, update the corresponding bound before rebuilding the localization set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reset when the level set becomes empty, an upper or lower phase threshold is crossed, or an imposed localization-radius safeguard is violated.
assumptions_latex: \(m_k\) is a valid convex lower model on \(Q_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any displayed event is a checkable condition for terminating the current localization phase.
review_flags: Reset triggers vary across level-method variants; an authoritative algorithm specification is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the leaf, but these triggers combine conventions from potentially different level-method variants. In addition, emptiness of the displayed sublevel set does not by itself certify a strict lower-bound increase without an attainment or equivalent assumption.

knowledge_statements.title: Upper-Lower Bound Intervals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimal-value enclosure supplied by a feasible incumbent and a valid global lower model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(f^*=\inf_{x\in X}f(x)\). Let \(\hat x_k\in X\) be feasible and set \(U_k=f(\hat x_k)\). Let \(m_k\leq f\) on \(X\) and define \(L_k=\inf_{x\in X}m_k(x)\), assuming this value is finite. Then \[L_k\leq f^*\leq U_k.\] Hence \([L_k,U_k]\) is a verifiable enclosure of the optimal value and \(G_k=U_k-L_k\) is an absolute optimality-gap certificate. If \(G_k\leq\varepsilon\), the incumbent is \(\varepsilon\)-optimal: \(f(\hat x_k)-f^*\leq\varepsilon\). Monotone bookkeeping may use the running bounds \(\max_{j\leq k}L_j\) and \(\min_{j\leq k}U_j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible objective value is an upper bound and the infimum of a global lower model is a lower bound; their difference certifies incumbent suboptimality.
assumptions_latex: \(\hat x_k\in X\) and \(m_k(x)\leq f(x)\) for every \(x\in X\).
review_flags: A method-specific source locator should be added during certification.
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Endpoint Levels Lose Uniform Two-Sided Progress
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp boundary for uniformly interior level interpolation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For certified bounds \(L<U\) and \(\ell=(1-\theta)L+\theta U\), a constant \(c>0\) can satisfy both \(\ell-L\geq c(U-L)\) and \(U-\ell\geq c(U-L)\) uniformly over the admissible choices exactly when those choices obey \(c\leq\theta\leq1-c\). Thus endpoint choices, or fractions approaching either endpoint, destroy a uniform two-sided progress margin.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform two-sided distance from the interval endpoints is equivalent to keeping the interpolation fraction uniformly away from zero and one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Uniform inequalities \(\ell-L\geq c(U-L)\) and \(U-\ell\geq c(U-L)\) hold for some \(c>0\) exactly when \(\theta\) is uniformly bounded away from \(0\) and \(1\).
knowledge_statements.title: Endpoint Levels Lose Uniform Two-Sided Progress
Level-Selection Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Admissible fixed-fraction and adaptive choices of a target level inside a certified value interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given certified bounds \(L_k<U_k\), select \(\theta_k\in[\underline\theta,\overline\theta]\subset(0,1)\) and define \[\ell_k=(1-\theta_k)L_k+\theta_k U_k.\] Then \(L_k<\ell_k<U_k\), with \(\ell_k-L_k=\theta_k(U_k-L_k)\) and \(U_k-\ell_k=(1-\theta_k)(U_k-L_k)\). A fixed-fraction regime takes constant \(\theta_k\); an adaptive regime may vary it using past phase outcomes while keeping the stated uniform bounds. These bounds prevent levels from approaching either endpoint arbitrarily closely and preserve a uniform fractional opportunity to improve either certified bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose each level as a uniformly interior convex combination of the lower and upper bounds; the fraction may be fixed or adapt to phase outcomes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_k<\ell_k<U_k\), and both distances to the interval endpoints are fixed fractions of its width.
review_flags: Specific adaptive policies require separate sources.
