assumptions_latex: \(L\leq f^*\leq U\), \(G=U-L\), and all updated bounds remain certified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G_p\leq\rho^pG_0\) with \(\rho=\max\{\overline\theta,1-\underline\theta\}<1\), and \(G_p\leq\varepsilon\) after at most \(\max\{0,\lceil\log(G_0/\varepsilon)/\log(1/\rho)\rceil\}\) completed phases.
review_flags: The contraction follows directly from the stated phase-update conditions; method-specific evidence remains pending.
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric contraction obtained when each completed phase raises the lower bound or lowers the upper bound past its interior level.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a phase begin with certified bounds \(L<U\), gap \(G=U-L\), and level \(\ell=L+\theta G\), where \(\theta\in[\underline\theta,\overline\theta]\subset(0,1)\). Suppose the phase ends with either a certified lower-bound update \(L^+\geq\ell\), while \(U^+\leq U\), or an upper-bound update \(U^+\leq\ell\), while \(L^+\geq L\). Then \[G^+=U^+-L^+\leq\rho G,\qquad \rho=\max\{\overline\theta,1-\underline\theta\}<1.\] Therefore, for an initial gap \(G_0>0\), after \(p\) completed phases, \(G_p\leq\rho^pG_0\). For every tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\), the number of completed phases sufficient to obtain \(G_p\leq\varepsilon\) is at most \[\max\left\{0,\left\lceil\frac{\log(G_0/\varepsilon)}{\log(1/\rho)}\right\rceil\right\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If every phase moves one certified bound past an interior level, the bound gap contracts geometrically. For a positive tolerance, the stated nonnegative logarithmic phase bound suffices, including the case in which the initial gap already meets the tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Phase-Based Gap Reduction
Euclidean Prox-Level Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Level method using Euclidean projection onto the current model-sublevel localization set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be closed and convex, and let \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex. Initialize a feasible incumbent \(\hat x_0\), a certified lower bound \(L_0\), and a center \(x_0\in X\). At iteration \(k\), choose \(\ell_k\in(L_k,U_k)\), where \(U_k=f(\hat x_k)\), construct a convex lower model \(m_k\leq f\), and set \(Q_k=X\cap\{x:m_k(x)\leq\ell_k\}\). If \(Q_k=\varnothing\), raise the lower bound above the level; otherwise compute \(x_{k+1}=P_{Q_k}(x_k)\), query \(f(x_{k+1})\) and a subgradient, and update the incumbent and model. Stop when \(U_k-L_k\leq\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose an interior level, project the current center onto its model sublevel, query a new cut, update bounds and incumbent, and stop at the certified gap tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, and \(f\) is convex on \(X\).
Every model \(m_k\) is a valid convex lower bound for \(f\).
The projection subproblem is solved whenever \(Q_k\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output incumbent \(\hat x_k\) satisfies \(f(\hat x_k)-f^*\leq\varepsilon\) whenever the stopping test holds.

notation.meaning: Euclidean projection onto the localization set

review_flags: A dedicated prox-level algorithm source is required to certify the bound-update and phase conventions.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the leaf, but the phase and bound-update conventions need a dedicated prox-level source. In particular, an empty model sublevel does not alone justify raising the certified lower bound strictly above the level without an attainment or equivalent assumption.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bregman Projection Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variational and three-point certificates for the non-Euclidean prox-center.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the preceding assumptions, \(x^+\in Q\) is the Bregman projection of \(z\) onto \(Q\) if and only if \[\langle\nabla\omega(x^+)-\nabla\omega(z),x-x^+\rangle\ge0\qquad(\forall x\in Q).\] Equivalently, it satisfies the generalized Pythagorean inequality \[D_\omega(x,z)\ge D_\omega(x,x^+)+D_\omega(x^+,z)\qquad(\forall x\in Q).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feasibility plus the Bregman variational inequality exactly certifies the prox-center and yields the generalized Pythagorean inequality.
assumptions_latex: \(\omega\) is differentiable and strongly convex on the relevant open convex region.
knowledge_statements.title: Bregman Projection Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strongly Convex Bregman Projection Is Well Posed
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence and uniqueness of the non-Euclidean prox-center on a closed convex model-level set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\subset\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, let \(z\in\Omega\), and let \(\omega\) be differentiable and \(\mu\)-strongly convex on an open convex set \(\Omega\supseteq Q\cup\{z\}\). Then \[D_\omega(x,z)\ge \frac{\mu}{2}\|x-z\|^2\quad(x\in Q),\] so \(D_\omega(\cdot,z)\) is coercive on \(Q\) and has a unique minimizer there.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong convexity makes the Bregman objective coercive and strictly convex, so every nonempty closed convex localization set has a unique Bregman prox-center.
assumptions_latex: \(\omega\) is differentiable and \(\mu\)-strongly convex on an open convex region containing \(Q\cup\{z\}\).
review_flags: Corrects the Builder's false assertion that strong convexity alone may fail to give attainment on a closed unbounded set.
knowledge_statements.title: Strongly Convex Bregman Projection Is Well Posed
Non-Euclidean Prox-Level Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bregman prox-level scheme for finite-dimensional convex minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be closed and convex, let \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex, and let \(\omega\) be differentiable and strongly convex on \(X\). Given bounds \(L_k\leq f^*\leq U_k\), choose \(\ell_k\in(L_k,U_k)\) and a convex cutting-plane model \(m_k\leq f\). Initialize \(x_0\in X\). At iteration \(k\), form \(Q_k=\{x\in X:m_k(x)\leq\ell_k\}\). If \(Q_k=\varnothing\), replace \(L_k\) by \(\ell_k\); otherwise set \[x_{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in Q_k}D_\omega(x,x_k),\qquad D_\omega(x,y)=\omega(x)-\omega(y)-\langle\nabla\omega(y),x-y\rangle.\] Update \(U_{k+1}\) using the best evaluated objective value, and stop when \(U_k-L_k\leq\varepsilon\), returning the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A prox-level method projects onto the current model level set using Bregman divergence, updates objective bounds, and returns the incumbent when their gap meets the tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is finite and convex on \(X\), and every model satisfies \(m_k\leq f\).
\(\omega\) is differentiable and strongly convex on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U_k-L_k\leq\varepsilon\) certifies \(f(\bar x_k)-f^*\leq\varepsilon\) for the returned incumbent \(\bar x_k\).

notation.meaning: Bregman divergence generated by the prox function
current convex lower model of the objective
valid lower and upper objective bounds

review_flags: Exact non-Euclidean prox-level variant and convergence hypotheses require an authoritative method-specific source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the leaf, but no citation supports this particular Bregman prox-level update, bound-update convention, or the hypotheses needed for well-defined prox subproblems. A method-specific authoritative source with a precise locator is required.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: A Memory Cap Is Not an Information-Preservation Rule
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundary separating bounded storage from a convergent restricted-memory prox-level method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For retained-cut models \(m_k=\max_{i\in I_k}h_i\), the condition \(|I_k|\le M\) alone does not ensure \(m_{k+1}\ge m_k\), preservation of a cut active at the preceding master point, or nesting of the associated model-level sets. Deleting a cut can lower the model and enlarge its level set. Hence bounded storage alone does not specify a convergence-preserving restricted-memory method.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Arbitrary deletion can lower the model and erase active localization information; a memory limit alone is not a convergence rule.
assumptions_latex: Each \(h_i\) is a valid affine minorant.
Cuts may otherwise be deleted without a retention or aggregation invariant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |I_k|\le M\ \not\Rightarrow\ m_{k+1}\ge m_k\text{ or preservation of model-level information}.

notation.meaning: indices of cuts retained at iteration \(k\)

knowledge_statements.title: A Memory Cap Is Not an Information-Preservation Rule
Restricted-Memory Prox-Level Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Prox-level scheme retaining a uniformly bounded bundle of cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be closed and convex and let \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex. Fix a memory limit \(M\geq1\), tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\), and prox function \(d\). At iteration \(k\), retain an index set \(I_k\) with \(|I_k|\leq M\) and cuts \(h_i(x)=f(x_i)+\langle g_i,x-x_i\rangle\), where \(g_i\in\partial f(x_i)\). Define \(m_k(x)=\max_{i\in I_k}h_i(x)\), choose \(\ell_k\in(L_k,U_k)\), and form \(Q_k=\{x\in X:m_k(x)\leq\ell_k\}\). If \(Q_k=\varnothing\), set \(L_{k+1}=\ell_k\); otherwise compute \(x_{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in Q_k}d(x)\), evaluate a new cut, and discard cuts while preserving \(|I_{k+1}|\leq M\). Stop when \(U_k-L_k\leq\varepsilon\).

knowledge_statements.title: Composite Prox-Level Methods

At queried points construct affine minorants \(a_{j,k}\leq\phi_j\) and define the composite lower model \(m_k(x)=\Psi(\max_{i\leq k}a_{1,i}(x),\ldots,\max_{i\leq k}a_{p,i}(x))\). Given valid bounds \(L_k\leq F^*\leq U_k\), choose \(\ell_k\in(L_k,U_k)\). If \(Q_k=\{x\in X:m_k(x)\leq\ell_k\}\) is empty, raise \(L_k\) to \(\ell_k\); otherwise compute a prox center in \(Q_k\), evaluate all required components there, and update \(U_k\). Stop when \(U_k-L_k\leq\varepsilon\).

knowledge_statements.title: Classical Bundle-Level Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical cutting-plane level method with Euclidean prox centers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be compact and convex and let \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex. Initialize an incumbent \(\bar x_0\in X\), a valid lower bound \(L_0\), and a center \(c_0\in X\). At iteration \(k\), define \(m_k(x)=\max_{i\leq k}\{f(x_i)+\langle g_i,x-x_i\rangle\}\), where \(g_i\in\partial f(x_i)\), set \(U_k=f(\bar x_k)\), and choose \(\ell_k=L_k+\theta(U_k-L_k)\) with \(0<\theta<1\). If \(Q_k=\{x\in X:m_k(x)\leq\ell_k\}\) is empty, set \(L_{k+1}=\ell_k\); otherwise choose \(x_{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in Q_k}\frac12\|x-c_k\|^2\), query \(f(x_{k+1})\), and update the incumbent. Stop when \(U_k-L_k\leq\varepsilon\).

knowledge_statements.title: Accelerated Bundle-Level Method
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accelerated level scheme using lower, middle, and upper iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be compact and convex, let \(f\) be convex, and choose weights \(\alpha_k\in(0,1]\). Maintain a lower point \(x_k^l\), prox center \(x_k\), and incumbent \(x_k^u\). Set \(x_k^l=(1-\alpha_k)x_{k-1}^u+\alpha_kx_{k-1}\), query \(f(x_k^l)\) and \(g_k\in\partial f(x_k^l)\), and add the cut \(h_k(x)=f(x_k^l)+\langle g_k,x-x_k^l\rangle\). For a phase level \(\ell\), update the localization set by intersecting retained cuts \(h_i(x)\leq\ell\), then compute \(x_k\) as its prox minimizer. Form \(\widetilde x_k^u=(1-\alpha_k)x_{k-1}^u+\alpha_kx_k\) and retain the better of \(\widetilde x_k^u\) and \(x_{k-1}^u\). End the phase when infeasibility or the prescribed upper-gap reduction occurs.

knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Smoothing Level Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Level scheme adapting smoothing without prior smoothness parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be compact and convex and suppose \(f(x)=\widehat f(x)+\max_{y\in Y}\{\langle Ax,y\rangle-\phi(y)\}\), where \(Y\) is compact and convex. Choose a strongly convex function \(v\\) on \(Y\) and define \(f_\mu(x)=\widehat f(x)+\max_{y\in Y}\{\langle Ax,y\rangle-\phi(y)-\mu v(y)\}\). During each level phase, select \(\mu>0\) from the current objective gap, build lower models and upper estimates using \(f_\mu\), and generate accelerated level iterates over the current localization set. Decrease \(\mu\) only when the phase gap decreases, and stop when the valid nonsmoothed bounds satisfy \(U-L\leq\varepsilon\). Return the best point evaluated for \(f\).

knowledge_statements.title: Level-Gap Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal optimality certificate from valid level-method bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f^*=\inf_{x\in X}f(x)\). Suppose a level method has an incumbent \(\bar x\in X\), an upper bound \(U=f(\bar x)\), and a lower bound \(L\) satisfying \(L\leq f^*\leq U\). knowledge_statements.statement_title: Certified Phase-Ending Alternatives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Checkable lower- and upper-progress events that terminate a level-method phase.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a phase starts with certified bounds \(L_s\leq f^*\leq U_s\), gap \(\Delta_s=U_s-L_s\), and target \(\ell_s=L_s+\theta\Delta_s\), where \(0<\theta<1\). The phase may end by either of two certificates. First, certified emptiness of a global lower-model sublevel at \(\ell_s\) yields the valid non-strict update \(L_{s+1}=\ell_s\), giving \(U_s-L_{s+1}=(1-\theta)\Delta_s\). Second, a feasible incumbent with value \(U_{s+1}\) satisfying \(U_{s+1}-L_s\leq q\Delta_s\), where \(0<q<1\), gives the corresponding upper-progress certificate. Keeping the opposite bound unchanged or improving it further, either event implies \[\Delta_{s+1}\leq\max\{1-\theta,q\}\Delta_s.\] No strict inequality \(f^*>\ell_s\) is needed in the infeasibility branch.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A phase ends after certified localization infeasibility raises the lower bound non-strictly to the target, or after a feasible incumbent passes the prescribed upper-progress test; either event certifies gap contraction.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonuniform Contraction Need Not Be Geometric
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of geometric phasewise convergence when contraction factors approach one.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Delta_s=\Delta_0/(s+1)\) for \(s\geq0\), where \(\Delta_0>0\). Then \(\Delta_{s+1}=\rho_s\Delta_s\) with \(\rho_s=(s+1)/(s+2)\in(0,1)\), but \(\rho_s\uparrow1\). Although \(\Delta_s\to0\), there are no constants \(C>0\) and \(\rho\in(0,1)\) such that \(\Delta_s\leq C\rho^s\) for every \(s\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strict contraction in every phase need not yield geometric convergence when the contraction factors are not uniformly bounded below one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Delta_{s+1}<\Delta_s\) and \(\Delta_s\to0\), but the convergence is not geometric.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonuniform Contraction Need Not Be Geometric

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Variable Phase-Contraction Product Criterion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonuniform extension of phasewise contraction using products of phase factors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let valid phase gaps satisfy \(\Delta_{s+1}\leq\rho_s\Delta_s\) with \(0<\rho_s\leq1\). Then \(\Delta_s\leq\Delta_0\prod_{j=0}^{s-1}\rho_j\). Consequently, \(\Delta_s\to0\) whenever \(\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}-\log\rho_j=\infty\). If there are \(\gamma>0\) and \(s_0\) such that \(\sum_{j=0}^{s-1}-\log\rho_j\geq\gamma s\) for every \(s\geq s_0\), then \(\Delta_s\leq\Delta_0e^{-\gamma s}\) for every \(s\geq s_0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Variable phase contractions accumulate multiplicatively; divergent total log contraction gives convergence, and linear accumulated log contraction gives a geometric rate.
knowledge_statements.title: Variable Phase-Contraction Product Criterion

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inexact Phase-Contraction Recursion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Perturbed phasewise gap contraction with additive phase errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let nonnegative valid gaps satisfy \(\Delta_{s+1}\leq\rho\Delta_s+\eta_s\) for a fixed \(\rho\in(0,1)\) and \(\eta_s\geq0\). Then \[\Delta_s\leq\rho^s\Delta_0+\sum_{j=0}^{s-1}\rho^{s-1-j}\eta_j.\] Consequently, \(\eta_s\to0\) implies \(\Delta_s\to0\). If \(\eta_s\leq Cq^s\) for \(q\in(0,1)\), then \(\Delta_s=O(\max\{\rho,q\}^s)\) when \(q\neq\rho\), and \(\Delta_s=O(s\rho^s)\) when \(q=\rho\). If \(\eta_s\leq\bar\eta\), then \(\limsup_s\Delta_s\leq\bar\eta/(1-\rho)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Additive phase errors are geometrically filtered: vanishing errors preserve convergence, geometric errors yield a geometric-type rate, and persistent errors create an error floor.

notation.meaning: additive contraction error in phase s

Phasewise Gap-Contraction Theory
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric convergence from uniform contraction of phase gaps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((L_s,U_s)\) be valid phase-bound pairs for a minimization problem, so \(L_s\leq f^*\leq U_s\), and define \(\Delta_s=U_s-L_s\). Suppose there exists \(\rho\in(0,1)\) such that every completed phase satisfies \(\Delta_{s+1}\leq\rho\Delta_s\). Then, for every integer \(s\geq0\), \[\Delta_s\leq\rho^s\Delta_0.\] Hence any phase incumbent \(x_s^u\) satisfying \(f(x_s^u)=U_s\) obeys \(0\leq f(x_s^u)-f^*\leq\rho^s\Delta_0\). In particular, \(s\geq\left\lceil\log(\Delta_0/\varepsilon)/\log(1/\rho)\right\rceil\) completed phases suffice for absolute objective error at most \(\varepsilon\), when \(0<\varepsilon<\Delta_0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform contraction of the valid bound gap in every phase gives geometric objective convergence and a logarithmic bound on the number of phases.
assumptions_latex: \(L_s\leq f^*\leq U_s\) for every completed phase.
Each \(U_s\) is attained by a feasible phase incumbent.

notation.meaning: valid objective gap after phase s
phase incumbent attaining the upper bound

knowledge_statements.title: Prox-Center Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convergence of exact prox-centers for nested convex localization sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be closed and convex, let \(L_1\supseteq L_2\supseteq\cdots\) be nonempty closed convex subsets of \(Q\), and suppose \(L_\infty:=\bigcap_{k\ge1}L_k\neq\varnothing\). Let \(d:Q\to\mathbb{R}\) be continuous, coercive, and strongly convex. For each \(k\), define \(x_k=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in L_k}d(x)\), and define \(x_\infty=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in L_\infty}d(x)\). Then the minimizers are unique and \(x_k\to x_\infty\). In particular, if \(L_\infty\) equals the solution set of the convex problem, every prox-center limit is optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact prox-centers of nested, nonempty closed convex localization sets converge to the unique prox-minimizer over their intersection, which is optimal when that intersection is the solution set.
assumptions_latex: \(L_k\) are nonempty, closed, convex, and nested, with \(L_\infty\neq\varnothing\).
\(d\) is continuous, coercive, and strongly convex on \(Q\).

notation.meaning: exact prox-center of the kth localization set

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Empty Intersection Can Make Prox-Centers Diverge
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of nested-set prox-center convergence when the limiting intersection is empty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(k\geq1\), let \(L_k=[k,\infty)\subset\mathbb R\) and \(d(x)=x^2\). Each \(L_k\) is nonempty, closed, convex, and nested, and \(d\) is continuous, coercive, and strongly convex. Nevertheless, \(\bigcap_{k\geq1}L_k=\varnothing\), while \(x_k=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in L_k}d(x)=k\to+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested nonempty closed convex sets can have diverging prox-centers when their infinite intersection is empty.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Deterministic First-Order Oracle Convention
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle and accuracy conventions for comparing local Lipschitz-nonsmooth upper and lower complexity bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For convex minimization over \(Q\), a deterministic first-order oracle queried at \(x\in Q\) returns \((f(x),g)\) with \(g\in\partial f(x)\). An algorithm is \(\varepsilon\)-accurate when it returns \(\hat x\in Q\) satisfying \(f(\hat x)-\inf_Q f\le\varepsilon\). Worst-case oracle complexity is the supremum, over the stated function class and admissible oracle responses, of the number of queries required for this guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonsmooth oracle complexity counts worst-case deterministic value-subgradient queries needed to produce epsilon objective accuracy.
assumptions_latex: \(f:Q\to\mathbb R\) is convex and finite at queried points.
The oracle may return any valid subgradient at a queried point.

assumptions_latex: The lower bound uses successively independent hidden directions.

Nonsmooth Lipschitz Complexity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Geometric volume-ratio objective-gap bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This is a method-specific guarantee using the associated nonsmooth minimization construction; the quantities \(i(k)\), \(f_{i(k)}^*\), \(f^*\), \(Q\), and the relevant iterates or localization sets retain their context-defined meanings. The guarantee applies only when \(i(k)>0\).

For every applicable \(k\) satisfying \(i(k)>0\), \[f_{i(k)}^*-f^*\leq MR\left(1-\frac{1}{(n+1)^2}\right)^{k/2}\left[\frac{\operatorname{vol}_n B_2(x_0,R)}{\operatorname{vol}_n Q}\right]^{1/n}.\]

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bounded Subgradients Do Not Imply the Interior Hölder Model
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating the interior Hölder class from Lipschitz nonsmoothness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(0<\rho<1\), uniform boundedness of subgradients does not imply the normalized Hölder upper model. The function \(f(x)=|x|\) has bounded subgradients, but at \(x=0\) no single \(g_0\in[-1,1]\) and finite \(C\) satisfy \(|y|\le g_0y+C|y|^{1+\rho}\) for all sufficiently small positive and negative \(y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Absolute value shows that bounded subgradients alone do not imply an interior Hölder upper model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sup_{g\in\partial f(x)}\|g\|<\infty\not\Rightarrow f\text{ satisfies the selected-subgradient Hölder upper model}.
knowledge_statements.title: Bounded Subgradients Do Not Imply the Interior Hölder Model

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Normalized Weakly Smooth Convex Model Class
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interior Hölder class used by weakly smooth level-method complexity statements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(0<\rho<1\), a convex function belongs to the normalized \((M_\rho,\rho)\) upper-model class on \(Q\) if, at every \(x\in Q\), a first-order oracle returns \(g_x\in\partial f(x)\) such that for every \(y\in Q\), \[0\le f(y)-f(x)-\langle g_x,y-x\rangle\le\frac{M_\rho}{1+\rho}\|y-x\|^{1+\rho}.\] The returned selection appearing in the upper model is part of the class convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The interior weakly smooth class bounds the selected first-order linearization error by a normalized one-plus-rho power.
knowledge_statements.title: Normalized Weakly Smooth Convex Model Class

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Interior-Hölder Deterministic Oracle Lower Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matching Euclidean minimax lower order for each fixed interior exponent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every fixed \(0<\rho<1\), deterministic first-order minimization in Euclidean space over the normalized \((M_\rho,\rho)\) convex class has, in sufficiently large dimension, worst-case complexity \[\Omega_\rho\!\left[\left(\frac{M_\rho R^{1+\rho}}{\varepsilon}\right)^{2/(1+3\rho)}\right].\] The oracle selection, radius, and objective-error conventions must match those of the upper theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For each fixed interior exponent and sufficient Euclidean dimension, the weakly smooth level-method order is minimax sharp.
assumptions_latex: The method is deterministic and uses the stated first-order oracle.
The dimension accommodates the lower-bound construction.
knowledge_statements.title: Interior-Hölder Deterministic Oracle Lower Bound

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Interior-Hölder Level-Method Upper Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounded-radius upper order for the normalized weakly smooth convex class.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(0<\rho<1\). Under the normalized \((M_\rho,\rho)\) upper model and an initial minimizer-distance bound \(R\), an accelerated prox-level method returns \(\hat x\) with \(f(\hat x)-f^*\le\varepsilon\) in \[O\!\left[\left(\frac{M_\rho R^{1+\rho}}{\varepsilon}\right)^{2/(1+3\rho)}\right]\] first-order oracle calls.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an interior Hölder exponent, accelerated level complexity has exponent two over one plus three rho.
assumptions_latex: The Normalized Weakly Smooth Convex Model Class assumptions hold.
A minimizer lies within distance \(R\) of the initial prox-center.
Fixed compatible prox geometry is used.

assumptions_latex: \(0<\rho<1\) and the displayed Hölder upper model holds on \(Q\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Smooth First-Order Oracle Comparison Class

A deterministic smooth first-order oracle returns \((f(x),\nabla f(x))\), and complexity counts queries required to return \(\hat x\) satisfying \(f(\hat x)-f^*\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Smooth upper and lower bounds are comparable when they share the norm, smooth class, initial radius, value-gradient oracle, and objective-error criterion.

The oracle returns exact function values and gradients.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dimension Qualification in Smooth Oracle Lower Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary on matching an accelerated upper rate with a zero-chain lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Smooth first-order lower constructions based on a zero chain or successive hidden directions require ambient dimension growing with the number of iterations covered. Hence a lower order \(\Omega(\sqrt{LR^2/\varepsilon})\) established by such a construction must retain a sufficient-dimension premise and does not alone imply the same asymptotic statement in arbitrary fixed dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero-chain smooth lower bound requires dimension proportional to its query horizon.
assumptions_latex: The construction reveals at most one new independent coordinate per oracle query.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: n\ge cN\text{ is a premise of an }N\text{-step zero-chain construction}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Endpoint-Compatible Hölder Upper-Model Convention
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One normalization for comparing the nonsmooth, interior-Hölder, and smooth complexity expressions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(0\le\rho\le1\), fix an oracle selection \(g_x\in\partial f(x)\) satisfying, for all \(x,y\in Q\), \[0\le f(y)-f(x)-\langle g_x,y-x\rangle\le \frac{M_\rho}{1+\rho}\|y-x\|^{1+\rho}.\] At \(\rho=0\) this is the linearization-error model with constant \(M_0\); at \(\rho=1\) it is the standard quadratic upper model with coefficient \(M_1/2\). The endpoint constants belong to this normalization and must not be identified with constants from differently normalized classes without conversion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A single normalized linearization-error model covers all exponents, while its endpoint constants must be converted before comparison with differently defined Lipschitz constants.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex and the oracle returns the displayed subgradient selection.

notation.meaning: upper-model constant in the displayed normalization

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Algebraic Endpoints of the Hölder Complexity Expression
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Endpoint evaluation of the proposed unified exponent law, without independently asserting its algorithmic validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the expression \[\Phi_\rho(\varepsilon)=\left(\frac{M_\rho R^{1+\rho}}{\varepsilon}\right)^{\!2/(1+3\rho)},\] direct endpoint evaluation gives \(\Phi_0(\varepsilon)=M_0^2R^2/\varepsilon^2\) and \(\Phi_1(\varepsilon)=\sqrt{M_1R^2/\varepsilon}\). Thus, under the endpoint-compatible model convention, the proposed exponent family algebraically interpolates between nonsmooth and smooth scaling; establishing it as an oracle bound still requires a separate theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The unified Hölder expression reduces algebraically to the epsilon-to-minus-two and epsilon-to-minus-one-half endpoint scalings.
assumptions_latex: The endpoint constants use the stated common normalization.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume the normalized Hölder upper model with \(\rho\in[0,1]\) and constant \(M_\rho\), and suppose a minimizer lies within distance \(R\) of the initial prox-center. A universal accelerated prox-level method attains objective error at most \(\varepsilon\) in \[N_\rho(\varepsilon)=O\!\left[\left(\frac{M_\rho R^{1+\rho}}{\varepsilon}\right)^{2/(1+3\rho)}\right]\] oracle calls. The hidden constant may depend on fixed prox geometry and level parameters but not on \(\varepsilon\), \(M_\rho\), or \(R\).

Smoothness-Transition Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuous interpolation of the universal level rate between nonsmooth and smooth endpoints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(0\le\rho\le1\), suppose the convex objective satisfies the Hölder upper model with constant \(M_\rho\), and a minimizer is within distance \(R\) of the initial prox-center. The universal level-method bound \(N_\rho(\varepsilon)=O((M_\rho R^{1+\rho}/\varepsilon)^{2/(1+3\rho)})\) varies continuously in \(\rho\). At \(\rho=0\) it gives \(O(M_0^2R^2/\varepsilon^2)\); at \(\rho=1\), with \(M_1=L\), it gives \(O(\sqrt{LR^2/\varepsilon})\). Thus one exponent family connects the nonsmooth and smooth oracle regimes.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strong Convexity Converts Objective Gap to Radius
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural inequality enabling geometric restart of bounded-radius level guarantees.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(f\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex on a convex set and \(x^*\) minimizes \(f\), then every feasible \(x\) satisfies \(f(x)-f^*\ge(\mu/2)\|x-x^*\|^2\). Consequently, a certified gap \(f(x)-f^*\le\Delta\) implies \(\|x-x^*\|\le\sqrt{2\Delta/\mu}\), so geometrically decreasing gap bounds yield geometrically shrinking localization radii.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong convexity turns a certified objective gap into a distance bound, enabling restarted localization.
knowledge_statements.title: Strong Convexity Converts Objective Gap to Radius

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Abstract Geometric-Restart Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Phase schedule converting a bounded-radius objective-gap routine into a restarted routine under strong convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) be \(\mu\)-strongly convex with minimizer \(x^*\). Suppose \(\mathcal P(x,R,\delta)\) returns \(x^+\) satisfying \(f(x^+)-f^*\leq\delta\) whenever \(\|x-x^*\|\leq R\). Given a certified gap \(f(x_0)-f^*\leq\Delta_0\), define \(\Delta_s=2^{-s}\Delta_0\) and \(R_s=\sqrt{2\Delta_s/\mu}\), and set \(x_{s+1}=\mathcal P(x_s,R_s,\Delta_{s+1})\). Then every phase satisfies its radius premise and \(f(x_s)-f^*\leq\Delta_s\). Thus \(\lceil\log_2(\Delta_0/\varepsilon)\rceil\) phases suffice for objective error at most \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under strong convexity, halve the certified target gap each phase and convert the current gap into a valid radius for the next bounded-radius call.
assumptions_latex: The phase routine attains target gap \(\delta\) whenever its center lies within its supplied radius of a minimizer.

notation.meaning: certified target objective gap for phase s

knowledge_statements.title: Abstract Geometric-Restart Interface

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Restart Radii Require Certified Objective Gaps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information boundary for converting strong convexity into a valid phase radius.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) be \(\mu\)-strongly convex with minimizer \(x^*\). The radius implication is valid from a certified gap: \[f(x)-f^*\leq\Delta\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \lVert x-x^*\rVert\leq\sqrt{2\Delta/\mu}.\] A raw upper value \(U\geq f(x)\), without a valid lower bound on \(f^*\), supplies no shift-invariant radius bound. Thus an objective-based restart rule must use a certified gap such as \(U-L\) with \(L\leq f^*\), or an independently certified distance bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong convexity yields a restart radius from a certified objective gap, not from an unnormalized objective value or upper bound alone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f(x)-f^*\leq\Delta\Longrightarrow\lVert x-x^*\rVert\leq\sqrt{2\Delta/\mu},\quad U\geq f(x)\text{ alone gives no such bound}.
knowledge_statements.title: Restart Radii Require Certified Objective Gaps

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Restarted Hölder Level-Method Upper Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Total oracle complexity obtained by geometric restart under strong convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) be \(\mu\)-strongly convex, let \(f(x_0)-f^*\le\Delta_0\) be certified, and suppose the normalized Hölder upper model holds with exponent \(\rho\). Geometric restart of a bounded-radius accelerated level routine gives, for \(0\le\rho<1\), \[N(\varepsilon)=O\!\left(\log\frac{\Delta_0}{\varepsilon}+\left(\frac{M_\rho^2}{\mu^{1+\rho}\varepsilon^{1-\rho}}\right)^{1/(1+3\rho)}\right).\] For \(\rho=1\), with \(M_1=L\), \[N(\varepsilon)=O\!\left(\sqrt{\frac L\mu}\log\frac{\Delta_0}{\varepsilon}\right).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Geometric restart converts bounded-radius Hölder rates into strongly convex rates; the smooth endpoint has accelerated condition-number dependence times a logarithm.
assumptions_latex: The initial objective gap \(\Delta_0\) is certified.
The normalized Hölder model and bounded-radius phase guarantee hold.
knowledge_statements.title: Restarted Hölder Level-Method Upper Bounds

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strongly Convex Hölder Oracle Lower Orders
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regime-wise Euclidean lower orders corresponding to restarted upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under matching Euclidean deterministic first-order conventions and sufficient dimension, \(\mu\)-strongly convex normalized Hölder classes require, for each fixed \(0\le\rho<1\), \[\Omega_\rho\!\left(\frac{M_\rho^2}{\mu^{1+\rho}\varepsilon^{1-\rho}}\right)^{1/(1+3\rho)}\] queries in the nontrivial accuracy range. For smooth instances with condition number \(\kappa=L/\mu\) bounded away from one, the corresponding lower order is \[\Omega\!\left(\sqrt\kappa\log\frac{\Delta_0}{\varepsilon}\right),\] subject to the usual compatible initial-gap, accuracy, and dimension premises.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The accuracy-dependent restarted Hölder orders are minimax sharp; away from the unit-condition-number degeneracy, the smooth endpoint has the accelerated logarithmic lower order.
assumptions_latex: The method is deterministic and first-order.
The geometry is Euclidean and upper and lower comparisons use the same class and accuracy conventions.
The dimension accommodates the lower-bound query horizon.
For the smooth formula, \(L/\mu\) is bounded above one and the initial-gap and accuracy range is nontrivial.

notation.meaning: smooth condition number L divided by mu

knowledge_statements.title: Strongly Convex Hölder Oracle Lower Orders
Strongly Convex Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restarted level-method bounds under strong convexity and Hölder smoothness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) be \(\mu\)-strongly convex and satisfy the Hölder upper model of exponent \(0\le\rho\le1\) with constant \(M_\rho\). A geometric-restart level method reducing the objective gap from \(\Delta_0\) to \(\varepsilon\) uses, for \(0\le\rho<1\), \(O((M_\rho^2/(\mu^{1+\rho}\varepsilon^{1-\rho}))^{1/(1+3\rho)})\) first-order oracle calls, with initialization-dependent additive terms. For \(\rho=1\), it uses \(O(\sqrt{L/\mu}\log(\Delta_0/\varepsilon))\) gradient calls. These bounds use strong convexity to convert each gap into a shrinking distance radius.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Geometric restart improves Hölder level-method complexity under strong convexity; in the smooth case it yields the accelerated square-root condition-number factor times a logarithm.
assumptions_latex: The Hölder upper model holds with exponent \(\rho\) and constant \(M_\rho\).
Restart phases reduce the certified objective gap geometrically.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound role fits, but the exact restarted Hölder rate, its additive initialization terms, and the smooth endpoint require a source before the claim can be relied upon.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Adaptivity Alone Does Not Establish Uniform Order Optimality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical boundary separating parameter-free operation from uniform oracle optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A method that does not receive \(\rho\) or \(M_\rho\) as input is parameter-free, but that fact alone does not imply uniform order optimality. Uniform order optimality additionally requires, for every fixed admissible \(\rho\), an upper oracle bound of the regime-optimal order and a matching lower bound for the same oracle model, accuracy criterion, and problem class. Thus neither parameter-freeness alone nor a family of upper bounds alone certifies uniform optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Parameter-free operation is only adaptivity; uniform optimality also requires regime-by-regime optimal upper orders and matching lower bounds.
assumptions_latex: The oracle model, accuracy criterion, and problem class are fixed when upper and lower bounds are compared.

notation.meaning: Hölder smoothness exponent indexing the regimes

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptivity Alone Does Not Establish Uniform Order Optimality

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform Regime-Wise Oracle Order Optimality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantified definition separating one parameter-free method from regime-dependent optimality constants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a common oracle model, norm, radius convention, and objective-error criterion, and let \(\mathcal F_\rho(M_\rho,R)\) be the normalized convex Hölder class for \(\rho\in[0,1]\). A single algorithm \(\mathcal A\) is uniformly order-optimal across these regimes if it receives neither \(\rho\) nor \(M_\rho\) as input and, for every fixed \(\rho\), there are constants \(0<c_\rho\le C_\rho<\infty\), independent of \(\varepsilon\), \(M_\rho\), \(R\), and the individual instance, such that \[c_\rho\Phi_\rho(\varepsilon)\le \inf_{\mathcal B}\sup_{f\in\mathcal F_\rho(M_\rho,R)}N_{\mathcal B,f}(\varepsilon)\le \sup_{f\in\mathcal F_\rho(M_\rho,R)}N_{\mathcal A,f}(\varepsilon)\le C_\rho\Phi_\rho(\varepsilon),\] subject to the dimension premises of the lower bound. The constants may depend on \(\rho\) and fixed prox geometry; uniformity does not require one numerical constant for every regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One parameter-free algorithm is uniformly order-optimal when, for each fixed smoothness exponent, its worst-case order matches that regime's minimax lower order with constants independent of accuracy and the individual instance.
assumptions_latex: The oracle model, norm, radius convention, and accuracy criterion are fixed across upper and lower comparisons.

notation.meaning: one parameter-free algorithm used in every regime
target minimax oracle order for exponent rho
order equivalence allowing constants depending on rho and fixed geometry

knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Regime-Wise Oracle Order Optimality

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Parameter-Free Universal Prox-Level Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algorithmic interface through which one level method adapts to normalized Hölder regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A universal prox-level scheme can use only value and first-order oracle outputs, cutting-plane lower bounds, prox-localized trial points, and fixed update rules independent of \(\rho\) and \(M_\rho\). Its stopping and phase decisions use computable upper-minus-lower gaps. Consequently, the same update rule is well defined on every normalized Hölder class without receiving its exponent or constant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One prox-level update rule can operate from oracle data and certified gaps without being given the Hölder exponent or constant.
assumptions_latex: A compatible prox setup and first-order oracle are available.
The method maintains valid cutting-plane lower bounds.
Its fixed update parameters do not depend on \(\rho\) or \(M_\rho\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal A\text{ receives neither }\rho\text{ nor }M_\rho\text{ as input}.\]
knowledge_statements.title: Parameter-Free Universal Prox-Level Interface

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform Regime-Wise Optimality of Universal Level Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parameter-free upper orders and regime-matched Euclidean minimax lower orders.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: There exists a parameter-free universal accelerated prox-level method \(\mathcal A\) such that, for every fixed \(\rho\in[0,1]\) and every objective in the normalized Hölder class with a minimizer within radius \(R\), \[\sup_f N_{\mathcal A,f}(\varepsilon)=O_\rho\!\left[\left(\frac{M_\rho R^{1+\rho}}{\varepsilon}\right)^{2/(1+3\rho)}\right].\] Under matching Euclidean oracle, class, radius, accuracy, and sufficient-dimension conventions, the deterministic minimax lower order is the corresponding \(\Omega_\rho\) expression. Hence \(\mathcal A\) is regime-wise order-optimal although constants may depend on \(\rho\) and fixed prox geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A single level method, without knowing smoothness parameters, matches the minimax oracle order separately in every Hölder regime.
assumptions_latex: The normalized Hölder classes share one oracle, radius, and objective-accuracy convention.
Euclidean lower-bound geometry and the dimension premise are retained for each fixed regime.
knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Regime-Wise Optimality of Universal Level Methods
Uniform Optimality Across Smoothness Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parameter-free attainment of optimal Hölder-regime oracle orders.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the class of convex objectives satisfying, for some unknown \(\rho\in[0,1]\) and \(M_\rho<\infty\), the Hölder upper model on a closed convex domain, with a minimizer within distance \(R\) of the initial prox-center. A universal level method is uniformly order-optimal if it does not receive \(\rho\) or \(M_\rho\) as input yet, for every admissible pair, guarantees \(N(\varepsilon)=O((M_\rho R^{1+\rho}/\varepsilon)^{2/(1+3\rho)})\). Uniform optimality means this order matches the corresponding black-box lower bound separately for every \(\rho\), not that one constant is identical across all regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A universal level method is uniformly optimal when, without knowing smoothness parameters, it attains the optimal Hölder oracle order for every exponent from zero to one.
assumptions_latex: The objective obeys a Hölder upper model for some unknown \(\rho\in[0,1]\).
The method receives neither \(\rho\) nor \(M_\rho\) as input.
A minimizer lies within distance \(R\) of the initial prox-center.

notation.meaning: oracle complexity of the universal method

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits the leaf, but uniform order optimality combines a parameter-free algorithmic guarantee with regime-specific lower bounds, neither of which is cited.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lower Bounds Retain Their Class and Oracle Hypotheses
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical validity test for transferring an oracle-complexity lower bound to a restricted problem class.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal C\) be a problem class and suppose a lower bound \(T(\varepsilon)\ge \Phi(\varepsilon)\) is established by hard instances in \(\mathcal C\) under specified oracle, dimension, domain, and parameter assumptions. For a subclass \(\mathcal S\subseteq\mathcal C\), the same lower bound follows only if admissible hard instances satisfying those assumptions remain in \(\mathcal S\). In particular, an algorithm solving every instance in \(\mathcal S\) in \(o(\Phi(\varepsilon))\) oracle calls refutes the transferred universal lower bound on \(\mathcal S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restricting a problem class can remove the hard instances supporting a complexity lower bound; a faster uniform upper bound on the subclass disproves the transferred bound.
assumptions_latex: The original lower bound is quantified over a specified problem and oracle class.
The proposed claim restricts that class or changes one of its defining hypotheses.

notation.meaning: original problem class and proposed subclass

knowledge_statements.title: Lower Bounds Retain Their Class and Oracle Hypotheses

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Known-Curvature Quadratics Defeat Transferred Nonsmooth Lower Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete exact-oracle subclass showing that lower-bound hard instances must survive a class restriction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(L>0\), \(x_0\in\mathbb R^d\), and \(R\ge0\). For \(\|x_0-a\|\le R\), let \(f_a(x)=\tfrac L2\|x-a\|^2\). An exact first-order oracle at \(x_0\) returns \(\nabla f_a(x_0)=L(x_0-a)\), so \(a=x_0-L^{-1}\nabla f_a(x_0)\) and the exact minimizer is recovered after one call. Hence no worst-case lower bound diverging as \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\), including \(\Omega(\varepsilon^{-2})\), holds uniformly on this subclass.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One gradient call solves the known-curvature quadratic subclass exactly, so a nonsmooth-order lower bound cannot be transferred to it.
assumptions_latex: \(L>0\) is known and the oracle returns an exact gradient.
The restricted class consists of the displayed quadratics with \(\|x_0-a\|\le R\).
knowledge_statements.title: Known-Curvature Quadratics Defeat Transferred Nonsmooth Lower Bounds
Invalid Lower-Bound Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower bounds cannot be transferred to strictly easier oracle classes without preserving their hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A lower bound proved for the class of all \(M\)-Lipschitz convex functions does not automatically apply to a smoother subclass. Indeed, on convex \(L\)-smooth objectives with initial solution distance at most \(R\), accelerated first-order methods achieve \(O(\!\sqrt{LR^2/\varepsilon}\!)\) oracle calls. Consequently, an asserted universal lower bound \(\Omega(M^2R^2/\varepsilon^2)\) for that smooth subclass is invalid whenever its parameters make this order asymptotically larger than the smooth upper bound. Dimension restrictions, oracle information, domain geometry, and smoothness assumptions of the original lower-bound construction must all remain satisfied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonsmooth ε⁻² lower bound cannot be applied unchanged to smooth objectives, because accelerated smooth optimization has an ε⁻¹/² upper bound.
assumptions_latex: The disputed lower bound was established only for a larger nonsmooth Lipschitz class.
The restricted subclass admits the displayed accelerated smooth upper bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Omega(M^2R^2/\varepsilon^2)\) is not a valid general lower bound for the \(L\)-smooth subclass.

notation.meaning: Lipschitz constant used by the nonsmooth class
gradient Lipschitz constant of the smooth subclass

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role is appropriate and the logical warning is sound, but the quantitative comparison depends on uncited smooth upper bounds and nonsmooth lower-bound hypotheses.

knowledge_statements.title: Prematurely Empty Localization Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An underestimated level can make a valid cutting-plane localization set empty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=|x|\) on \(Q=\mathbb{R}\), so \(f^*=0\). The supporting cuts obtained at \(x=1\) and \(x=-1\) are respectively \(h_1(x)=x\) and \(h_2(x)=-x\). Their bundle model is \(m(x)=\max\{h_1(x),h_2(x)\}=|x|\). For any chosen level \(\ell<0\), the localization set \(L(\ell)=\{x\in Q:m(x)\le\ell\}\) is empty, although the original optimization problem has the minimizer \(x^*=0\). Thus nonemptiness is guaranteed by a level satisfying \(\ell\ge f^*\), but can fail when a purported lower bound places the level below \(f^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For f(x)=|x|, two exact supporting cuts give model |x|; every negative level produces an empty localization set despite the original problem having a minimizer.
assumptions_latex: The bundle contains cuts generated at \(1\) and \(-1\).

notation.meaning: maximum of the stored affine cuts

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Safe Cut Deletion Preserves Target Containment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal correctness condition for limited-memory localization in an expensive-projection regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L\) be a localization set formed from valid lower-model cuts at a level for which a target point \(x^*\) is certified to belong to \(L\). Deleting cuts produces a relaxed set \(\widetilde L\supseteq L\), and therefore \(x^*\in\widetilde L\). Cut deletion preserves target containment, although it can weaken geometric progress and need not preserve the original iteration-complexity proof.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dropping cuts enlarges the localization set and preserves a previously certified target, but may destroy the progress estimate.
assumptions_latex: Every retained inequality is a valid lower-model cut.
The target point is certified to belong to the original localization set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L\subseteq\widetilde L,\qquad x^*\in L\Longrightarrow x^*\in\widetilde L.

notation.meaning: relaxed localization set after cut deletion

knowledge_statements.title: Safe Cut Deletion Preserves Target Containment

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Redundant Cuts Separate Oracle Count from Projection Description Size
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representation-level example showing why oracle iterations do not determine prox-center input size.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the localization region be the fixed halfspace \(H=\{x:a^\top x\le b\}\). After \(k\) iterations, represent it by \(k\) identical valid cuts \(a^\top x\le b\). The feasible set and its exact projection are unchanged, but the explicit inequality description has \(k\) rows. Thus oracle iterations can increase projection-description size even when localization geometry is unchanged; an oracle-count theorem alone bounds neither the work of an implementation processing every row nor any machine-model runtime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeated identical cuts leave the localization geometry unchanged while growing its explicit projection model.
assumptions_latex: The projection implementation receives the explicit accumulated inequality description.

notation.meaning: localization set as explicitly represented after k retained cuts

knowledge_statements.title: Redundant Cuts Separate Oracle Count from Projection Description Size

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Oracle Count Excludes Prox-Center Work
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cost-accounting boundary independent of any particular projection solver or empirical runtime claim.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If iteration \(k\) uses oracle work \(C_{\mathrm{orc},k}\), prox-center work \(P_k\), and bookkeeping work \(B_k\), then an implementation-level accounting is \[T_N=\sum_{k=1}^N\bigl(C_{\mathrm{orc},k}+P_k+B_k\bigr).\] A theorem bounding only \(N\) controls neither \(\sum_kP_k\) nor \(T_N\). In particular, whenever \(\sum_kP_k\) asymptotically dominates the other terms, the oracle-call order is not an end-to-end runtime order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Oracle complexity does not bound runtime unless prox-center and maintenance costs are also controlled.
assumptions_latex: Each iteration's computational work is partitioned into oracle, prox-center, and bookkeeping components.
All costs are measured in one specified computation model.

notation.meaning: cost of the kth prox-center computation
localization-maintenance and bookkeeping cost at iteration k
total implementation cost through N iterations

knowledge_statements.title: Oracle Count Excludes Prox-Center Work

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform Cut Budgets Bound Projection Description Size
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limited-memory representation bound without a progress or runtime claim.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If each localization projection retains at most \(q\) cuts in addition to \(r\) fixed inequalities, then its explicit description has at most \(r+q\) rows at every iteration. This bounds retained-cut input size, but not conditioning or solver complexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniform cut budget prevents growth of the explicit projection model but does not itself bound runtime.
assumptions_latex: At most \(q\) cutting-plane inequalities are retained per iteration.
The feasible region contributes \(r\) fixed inequalities.

notation.meaning: explicit localization description at iteration k

knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Cut Budgets Bound Projection Description Size

knowledge_statements.statement_title: A Uniform Cut Budget Does Not Control Projection Conditioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp limitation of retained-row bounds in expensive projection regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\varepsilon>0\), let \(A_\varepsilon=\begin{bmatrix}1&0\\1&\varepsilon\end{bmatrix}\) and \(L_\varepsilon=\{x:A_\varepsilon x\le0\}\). Every description has only two rows, but \(\kappa(A_\varepsilon A_\varepsilon^\top)\to\infty\) as \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\). Thus a uniform cut budget does not provide a uniform conditioning or numerical-work bound for projection subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two nearly parallel retained cuts give a fixed-size projection model whose constraint Gram matrix becomes arbitrarily ill-conditioned.
assumptions_latex: Conditioning is measured by the spectral condition number of the displayed constraint Gram matrix.
knowledge_statements.title: A Uniform Cut Budget Does Not Control Projection Conditioning
Expensive Projection Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle complexity ceases to predict runtime when localization projections are costly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a level method makes \(N\) first-order oracle calls, each costing at most \(C_{\mathrm{orc}}\), and computes one exact prox-center per iteration, with projection costs \(P_1,\ldots,P_N\). Its total computational cost satisfies \(T\ge\sum_{k=1}^N P_k\) and is modeled by \(T=O(NC_{\mathrm{orc}}+\sum_{k=1}^N P_k)\), excluding bookkeeping. Therefore an oracle bound for \(N\) is not a runtime bound when \(\sum_kP_k\) dominates \(NC_{\mathrm{orc}}\). This regime occurs, for example, when each localization polyhedron accumulates cuts and exact projection requires solving a growing quadratic program.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A favorable oracle count does not imply favorable runtime when every prox-center requires an increasingly expensive projection onto the accumulated localization model.
assumptions_latex: Each iteration uses one oracle call and one exact prox-center computation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{k=1}^N P_k\gg NC_{\mathrm{orc}}\) implies that projection work, not oracle complexity, controls runtime.

notation.meaning: cost of one first-order oracle call
cost of the kth projection or prox-center computation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polyhedral Projection Primal–Dual Gap Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic certificate for a polyhedral projection subproblem, whose canonical home is the projection-subproblem interface rather than this runtime-failure leaf.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let L=\{x:Ax\le b\}\ne\varnothing and p=\arg\min_{x\in L}\tfrac12\|x-z\|_2^2. For primal-feasible y\in L and dual-feasible \lambda\ge0, define \Delta(y,\lambda)=\tfrac12\|y-z\|_2^2+\tfrac12\|A^\top\lambda\|_2^2-\lambda^\top(Az-b). Then \Delta(y,\lambda)\ge\tfrac12\|y-p\|_2^2.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible point and nonnegative multiplier give a valid projection-QP gap, but this generic result belongs under the projection-subproblem interface.

notation.meaning: exact Euclidean projection of z onto L

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Projection Primal–Dual Gap Certificate

knowledge_statements.title: Level-Parameter Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extreme interpolation parameters degrade progress or robustness of level localization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathrm{lb}<\mathrm{ub}\) be valid current bounds and select \(\ell_\beta=(1-\beta)\mathrm{lb}+\beta\mathrm{ub}\) with \(0<\beta<1\). Then \(\ell_\beta-\mathrm{lb}=\beta(\mathrm{ub}-\mathrm{lb})\) and \(\mathrm{ub}-\ell_\beta=(1-\beta)(\mathrm{ub}-\mathrm{lb})\). As \(\beta\uparrow1\), the level approaches the incumbent upper bound, so the localization constraint weakens and certified gap reduction can vanish. As \(\beta\downarrow0\), the level approaches the lower bound, making localization aggressive and sensitive to lower-bound or model errors; an invalid underestimated bound may make the set empty. Convergence guarantees therefore require \(\beta\) bounded away from both endpoints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choosing the level too near the upper bound weakens progress; choosing it too near the lower bound makes localization fragile and potentially empty under bound errors.

notation.meaning: current lower and upper objective bounds

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The interpolation identities are correct, but the categorical assertion that convergence guarantees require the parameter to remain uniformly away from both endpoints is method-dependent and needs a specific convergence or contraction source.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Feasible Proximal-Master Stationarity Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact optimality test for a feasible bundle trial subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonempty closed convex \(X\), proper closed convex \(m_k\), and \(t_k>0\), \(y_k\) minimizes \[m_k(x)+\frac{1}{2t_k}\lVert x-\bar x_k\rVert^2\quad\text{over }X\] if and only if \[0\in\partial m_k(y_k)+\frac{y_k-\bar x_k}{t_k}+N_X(y_k),\] subject to the standard sum qualification. The minimizer is unique whenever it exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible trial solves the proximal master when its model subgradient, proximal displacement, and feasible-set normal balance.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is nonempty, closed, and convex; \(\bar x_k\in X\); and \(t_k>0\).
The subdifferential sum qualification holds and the master attains its minimum.

notation.meaning: Convex normal cone to the feasible set.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Feasible-Oracle Access Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Initialization and oracle-access limitation of methods whose trials remain feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If every trial master is solved over \(X\) and every serious center is selected from its trial points, then \(\bar x_0\in X\) implies \(y_k,\bar x_k\in X\) for all \(k\). This architecture does not itself produce an initial feasible point from an infeasible center and does not query the objective outside \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feasible bundle methods preserve known feasibility but require an external feasible-start, projection, or restoration mechanism when no feasible center is available.
assumptions_latex: All trial masters are solved over \(X\), and serious centers are chosen from feasible trial points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x_0\in X\Rightarrow y_k,\bar x_k\in X\) for all \(k\); infeasible initialization requires another mechanism.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasible-Oracle Access Boundary
Feasible Bundle Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A proximal bundle scheme whose trial and serious iterates remain feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a nonempty closed convex set \(X\), a convex objective \(f\), a feasible center \(\bar x_0\in X\), and \(t_k>0\), store cuts \(f(x_i)+\langle g_i,x-x_i\rangle\) with feasible \(x_i\in X\) and \(g_i\in\partial f(x_i)\). Set \(m_k(x)=\max_{i\in I_k}\{f(x_i)+\langle g_i,x-x_i\rangle\}\) and compute \(y_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\{m_k(x)+\lVert x-\bar x_k\rVert^2/(2t_k)\}\). Evaluate \(f(y_k)\). If a prescribed serious-step decrease test holds, set \(\bar x_{k+1}=y_k\); otherwise set \(\bar x_{k+1}=\bar x_k\) and add the new cut. Stop on a certified model gap and output \(\bar x_k\in X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method minimizes a proximal cutting-plane model over the feasible set, accepts sufficiently improving feasible trials, and otherwise adds a cut while retaining the feasible center.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, and \(\bar x_0\in X\).
\(f\) is proper convex and subgradients are available at feasible trial points.
Each proximal model subproblem has a minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y_k\in X\) and \(\bar x_k\in X\) for every \(k\), so the reported serious center is feasible.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits and feasibility follows from solving every trial subproblem over X, but no authoritative constrained-bundle source is supplied, and the serious-step and stopping tests are left unspecified.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Penalized Proximal-Master Predicted-Decrease Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact solve and stationarity certificate for a fixed-penalty bundle master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y_k\) minimize \[M_{\rho_k,k}(y)+\frac{1}{2t_k}\lVert y-x_k\rVert^2.\] Then \[\Delta_k:=M_{\rho_k,k}(x_k)-M_{\rho_k,k}(y_k)-\frac{1}{2t_k}\lVert y_k-x_k\rVert^2\geq0.\] Moreover, \(\Delta_k=0\) if and only if \(y_k=x_k\), equivalently \(0\in\partial M_{\rho_k,k}(x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The master predicted decrease is nonnegative, and it vanishes exactly when the center is stationary for the current penalized bundle model.
assumptions_latex: \(M_{\rho_k,k}\) is proper closed convex, \(t_k>0\), and the master minimizer exists.
knowledge_statements.title: Penalized Proximal-Master Predicted-Decrease Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Penalized Bundle Model Is a Global Minorant
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity of the positive-part model used by a penalty bundle master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(m_f^k\leq f\), \(m_{c_j}^k\leq c_j\), and \(\rho\geq0\), then \[M_{\rho,k}(x):=m_f^k(x)+\rho\sum_j[m_{c_j}^k(x)]_+\leq f(x)+\rho\sum_j[c_j(x)]_+=P_\rho(x)\] for every \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The positive-part combination of objective and constraint minorants is a global minorant of the exact penalized objective.
assumptions_latex: All component models are global minorants and \(\rho\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Penalized Bundle Model Is a Global Minorant

assumptions_latex: \(f,c_1,\ldots,c_m:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) are finite convex functions with available value-subgradient oracles.
The proximal parameter satisfies \(t_k>0\), and the penalty parameter satisfies \(\rho_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The method returns a point with small predicted penalized decrease and small modeled constraint violation, or continues after updating the bundle or \(\rho_k\).

notation.meaning: Polyhedral bundle models of the objective and constraints.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard convex exact-penalty bundle master problem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex inequality constraints with an exact positive-part penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given center \(x_k\), form cutting-plane minorants \(m_f^k\leq f\) and \(m_{c_j}^k\leq c_j\). Compute \[y_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in\mathbb{R}^n}\left\{m_f^k(y)+\rho_k\sum_{j=1}^m[m_{c_j}^k(y)]_++\frac{1}{2t_k}\lVert y-x_k\rVert^2\right\}.\] Evaluate the required oracles at \(y_k\) and append their supporting cuts. Accept \(y_k\) as a serious step when actual penalized decrease is a prescribed positive fraction of predicted decrease; otherwise retain \(x_k\) and take a null step. Increase \(\rho_k\) when the modeled violation fails the chosen feasibility-progress test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A penalty bundle method minimizes stabilized cutting-plane models of the objective and positive constraint violations, accepting serious steps and increasing the penalty when feasibility progress is inadequate.
knowledge_statements.title: Penalty Bundle Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the method leaf, and the penalized master is mathematically plausible. No cited source supports the serious-step, feasibility-progress, penalty-update, or stopping rules, which are stated only generically.
