children.title: Objective Models
children.top_down_role: Bundle representations maintained for the optimization objective.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Active-Cut Subdifferential Formula
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order structure of a polyhedral objective bundle model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m_f^k(x)=\max_{i\in I_k}\{a_i+\langle g_i,x\rangle\}\) and \(A_k(x):=\{i:a_i+\langle g_i,x\rangle=m_f^k(x)\}\). Then \[\partial m_f^k(x)=\operatorname{conv}\{g_i:i\in A_k(x)\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The objective model's subdifferential is the convex hull of the slopes of its active cuts.
knowledge_statements.title: Active-Cut Subdifferential Formula

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Objective-Model Monotonicity Under Cut Updates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise effect of adding or deleting objective cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Adding globally valid cuts without deleting old ones yields \(m_f^{k+1}\geq m_f^k\) pointwise while preserving \(m_f^{k+1}\leq f\). Deleting cuts yields a model no larger than the corresponding undeleted model and may destroy interpolation at a sampled point whose necessary active cut is removed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cut addition tightens an objective lower model monotonically; cut deletion weakens it and may lose sampled-point interpolation.
assumptions_latex: Every added or retained affine cut globally minorizes \(f\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m_f^k\leq m_f^{k+1}\leq f\) under pure cut addition; deletion weakens the model relative to the full bundle.
knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Model Monotonicity Under Cut Updates

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The model is convex, polyhedral, and globally satisfies \(m_f^k(x)\leq f(x)\) for every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: supporting-hyperplane bundle model for a convex objective
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polyhedral lower models built from objective oracle information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite bundle index set \(I_k\), the objective model associated with \(\mathcal B_f^k\) is \[m_f^k(x):=\max_{i\in I_k}\{f(z_i)+\langle g_i,x-z_i\rangle\},\qquad x\in\mathbb{R}^n.\] Each affine function is a global minorant by the subgradient inequality. An aggregate cut may replace several stored cuts provided its affine function remains a global minorant of \(f\). The model is exact at a stored point \(z_i\) whenever its corresponding cut is active there.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An objective bundle model is the maximum of stored supporting affine functions, hence a convex polyhedral global lower bound on the objective.
knowledge_statements.title: Objective Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and global-minorant claim are standard and internally consistent, but the record supplies no source or inspectable locator for the bundle-model and aggregate-cut assertions.

children.title: Constraint Models
children.top_down_role: Bundle representations maintained for explicit convex constraints.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Monotonic Tightening Under Constraint-Cut Addition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of enriching constraint bundles without deleting cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If iteration \(k+1\) retains every constraint cut from iteration \(k\), then \[m_{c_j}^{k+1}(x)\geq m_{c_j}^{k}(x)\quad\forall x,j,\qquad C_{k+1}\subseteq C_k.\] Since every model remains a minorant, the true feasible set \(C\) satisfies \(C\subseteq C_{k+1}\subseteq C_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Retaining old cuts raises the constraint models and shrinks their outer feasible approximations while preserving containment of the true feasible set.
assumptions_latex: No stored constraint cut is deleted, and every new cut is a global minorant.
knowledge_statements.title: Monotonic Tightening Under Constraint-Cut Addition

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Aggregate Constraint-Violation Lower Model
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar lower model assembled from the separate constraint models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(V(x):=\max\{0,c_1(x),\ldots,c_m(x)\}\), define \[V_k(x):=\max\{0,m_{c_1}^k(x),\ldots,m_{c_m}^k(x)\}.\] If every \(m_{c_j}^k\leq c_j\), then \(V_k\) is convex polyhedral and \(0\leq V_k(x)\leq V(x)\) for every \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The maximum of zero and the separate constraint models is a convex polyhedral lower model of maximum constraint violation.
assumptions_latex: Each \(m_{c_j}^k\) is a finite convex polyhedral minorant of \(c_j\).
knowledge_statements.title: Aggregate Constraint-Violation Lower Model

assumptions_latex: For every stored constraint pair, \(h_{ji}\in\partial c_j(z_{ji})\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(j\), the model satisfies \(m_{c_j}^k(x)\leq c_j(x)\) on \(\mathbb{R}^n\), so \(m_{c_j}^k(x)>0\) certifies violation of the true constraint.

notation.meaning: Model of constraint function indexed by j.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: componentwise supporting-hyperplane models of convex constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separate polyhedral lower models for convex inequality functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the inequality \(c_j(x)\leq0\), let \(I_j^k\) index stored oracle triples \((z_{ji},c_j(z_{ji}),h_{ji})\). Its constraint model is \[m_{c_j}^k(x):=\max_{i\in I_j^k}\{c_j(z_{ji})+\langle h_{ji},x-z_{ji}\rangle\}.\] The modeled feasible set is \(C_k:=\{x:m_{c_j}^k(x)\leq0\text{ for all }j\}\). Because every cut minorizes its constraint, the true feasible set is contained in \(C_k\); thus modeled feasibility alone does not certify true feasibility, whereas positive modeled violation certifies true violation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each convex constraint is modeled by its stored supporting cuts. The modeled feasible set outer-approximates the true feasible set, while positive modeled violation proves true violation.
knowledge_statements.title: Constraint Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition correctly gives componentwise cutting-plane minorants and an outer approximation of the feasible set. It nevertheless has no cited evidence or specific locator.

children.title: Objective–Constraint Model Coupling
children.top_down_role: Interfaces coordinating separate objective and constraint representations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hard-Coupled Master KKT Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimality certificate exposing the interaction of objective and constraint models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under a convex constraint qualification, a feasible \(y_k\) solves the hard-coupled master if and only if there exist \(s_f\in\partial m_f^k(y_k)\), \(s_j\in\partial m_{c_j}^k(y_k)\), and \(\lambda_j\geq0\) such that \[s_f+\sum_{j=1}^m\lambda_js_j+\frac{y_k-x_k}{t_k}=0,\qquad \lambda_jm_{c_j}^k(y_k)=0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Objective and constraint model subgradients, nonnegative multipliers, and proximal displacement give a KKT certificate for the hard-coupled master.
assumptions_latex: The hard master is feasible and a Slater or relative-interior constraint qualification holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Primal feasibility, dual nonnegativity, stationarity, and complementary slackness characterize its unique trial point.
knowledge_statements.title: Hard-Coupled Master KKT Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hard Modeled-Feasibility Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coupling through modeled inequalities rather than a violation penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(m_f^k\), \(m_{c_j}^k\), center \(x_k\), and \(t_k>0\), the hard-coupled master is \[\min_x\left\{m_f^k(x)+\frac{1}{2t_k}\lVert x-x_k\rVert^2:m_{c_j}^k(x)\leq0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\right\}.\] If its feasible set is nonempty and the minimum is attained, its trial point is unique. Because the constraint models are minorants, modeled feasibility need not imply true feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hard coupling minimizes the objective model over the modeled feasible set; stabilization gives a unique trial, but modeled feasibility may be false feasibility.
assumptions_latex: The models are proper closed convex, \(t_k>0\), and the hard master has a feasible minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The hard-coupled master has a unique trial point, which need not satisfy the true constraints.
knowledge_statements.title: Hard Modeled-Feasibility Coupling

assumptions_latex: The objective and constraint models are finite convex polyhedral minorants.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The coupled master simultaneously trades objective improvement against modeled feasibility while retaining a unique trial point when the Euclidean proximal term is used.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: stabilized penalty coupling of objective and constraint bundle models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Penalty-form coupling of separate objective and constraint models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A stabilized objective-constraint coupling is represented by the master problem \[\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\left\{m_f^k(x)+\rho_k\sum_{j=1}^m[m_{c_j}^k(x)]_++\frac{1}{2t_k}\lVert x-x_k\rVert^2\right\}.\] Equivalently, introduce variables \(v_j\geq0\) and impose \(v_j\geq m_{c_j}^k(x)\), then minimize \(m_f^k(x)+\rho_k\sum_jv_j+(2t_k)^{-1}\lVert x-x_k\rVert^2\). This formulation preserves separate cut bundles while coupling their predictions through common trial-point and violation variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The master problem couples the objective model and separate constraint models through positive-part violation penalties and a proximal stabilization term.
knowledge_statements.title: Objective–Constraint Model Coupling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Representation is the appropriate kind, and the epigraph reformulation and uniqueness claim are mathematically plausible under the stated finite polyhedral models and Euclidean proximal term. No source or locator supports this particular coupling.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Phase-I Feasibility and Infeasibility Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Meaning of exact or globally certified Phase-I values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If Phase I produces \(x\) with \(V(x)=0\), then \(x\) is feasible and may initialize Phase II. If it certifies \(v^*:=\inf_xV(x)>0\), then the original constraint system is infeasible. A positive current value, without a matching global lower certificate, proves neither infeasibility nor Phase-I optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zero Phase-I violation certifies feasibility, while a certified positive global infimum proves infeasibility; an ordinary positive iterate proves neither.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V(x)=0\Rightarrow x\) is feasible, and \(\inf_xV(x)>0\Rightarrow\) the constraint system is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.title: Phase-I Feasibility and Infeasibility Certificates

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Tolerance Transition Does Not Certify Exact Feasibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between approximate Phase-I termination and feasible Phase-II initialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feas}}>0\), \(V(x)\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feas}}\) guarantees only \(c_j(x)\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feas}}\) for every \(j\); it does not imply \(c_j(x)\leq0\). A Phase II requiring an exactly feasible center must therefore use \(V(x)=0\), an independent restoration step, or a method permitting infeasible centers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive feasibility tolerance gives approximate rather than exact feasibility and cannot alone initialize a strictly feasible Phase II.
knowledge_statements.title: Tolerance Transition Does Not Certify Exact Feasibility

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Phase-I Violation Function and Subdifferential
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical convex objective used during feasibility restoration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For finite convex inequalities \(c_j(x)\leq0\), define \[V(x)=\max\{0,c_1(x),\ldots,c_m(x)\}.\] Then \(V\) is finite convex, \(V(x)\geq0\), and \(V(x)=0\) if and only if \(x\) is feasible. If \(V(x)>0\) and \(A(x)=\{j:c_j(x)=V(x)\}\), then \[\partial V(x)=\operatorname{conv}\bigcup_{j\in A(x)}\partial c_j(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Phase I minimizes maximum constraint violation; its zeros are feasible points and its subgradients come from maximally violated constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V^{-1}(0)=\{x:c_j(x)\leq0\ \forall j\}\), with the stated active-constraint subdifferential when \(V(x)>0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Phase-I Violation Function and Subdifferential

assumptions_latex: \(f,c_1,\ldots,c_m\) are finite convex functions with value-subgradient oracles.
The original constraint system has at least one feasible point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Phase I either reaches the prescribed feasibility tolerance before Phase II begins or reports failure under the algorithm's stopping safeguards; Phase II then targets the constrained objective.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-stage convex bundle scheme separating feasibility restoration from objective optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize a stability center \(x_0\). In Phase I, apply a stabilized bundle method to \(V\), using cuts obtained from active violated constraints, until \(V(x_k)\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feas}}\). Initialize Phase II at that center, retain valid accumulated objective and constraint cuts, and solve stabilized masters based on \(m_f^k\) together with the modeled inequalities \(m_{c_j}^k(x)\leq0\) or an exact-penalty coupling. In either phase, accept a trial point only when its actual merit improvement meets the serious-step test; otherwise perform a null step and enrich the relevant models.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Phase I uses bundle steps to reduce maximum constraint violation; after reaching feasibility tolerance, Phase II switches to stabilized constrained objective minimization.
knowledge_statements.title: Phase I-Phase II Bundle Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the leaf, but the precise two-phase procedure, retention of cuts, merit tests, safeguards, and transition conditions require an authoritative bundle-method source. None is cited.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Phase I–phase II bundle method with subgradient selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algorithm 7.5 direction construction, primal-dual interpretation, phase-II specialization, and inherited convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Algorithm 7.5 replaces the direction-finding step of Algorithm 7.1 by solving the dual subproblem (7.20), forming the scaled aggregate quantities, setting d^k=-p^k, and computing v^k by (7.21). Equivalently, (d^k,v^k) solves the primal quadratic cutting-plane subproblem (7.22), whose constraints are\quad f_j^k-f(x^k)-F(x^k)_++\langle g_f^j,d\rangle\leq v\quad(j\in J_f^k),\qquad F_j^k-F(x^k)_++\langle g_F^j,d\rangle\leq v\quad(j\in J_F^k). During phase II, Algorithm 7.5 reduces to Algorithm 5.1. The modified line searches described for Algorithm 7.1 may also be used, and the resulting methods satisfy the convergence alternatives stated in Theorem 7.4.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Algorithm 7.5 is the subgradient-selection variant of the phase I–phase II bundle method. It computes its direction through the dual aggregation problem, equivalently through the associated primal quadratic cutting-plane problem. Once feasibility is reached it becomes Algorithm 5.1, and the stated line-search variants retain the convergence alternatives of Theorem 7.4.
assumptions_latex: \text{The cuts, active index sets, scaled multipliers, and linearization errors are defined as in Algorithm 7.5.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (d^k,v^k)\text{ solves the primal direction subproblem (7.22) and corresponds to the dual construction (7.20)},\qquad F(x^k)\leq0\Rightarrow\text{phase-II reduction to Algorithm 5.1},\qquad\text{Theorem 7.4 applies to the stated variants.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Approximate-subgradient certificates for Algorithm 7.1
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iteration-specific epsilon-subdifferential inclusions for stored cuts and aggregate vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration k of Algorithm 7.1, relation (4.4) holds and, for j=1,\ldots,k,\quad g_f^j\in\partial_{\alpha_{f,j}^k+F(x^k)_+}H(x^k;x^k),\qquad g_F^j\in\partial_{\alpha_{F,j}^k}H(x^k;x^k). Moreover,\quad p_f^{k-1}\in\partial_{\alpha_{f,p}^k+F(x^k)_+}H(x^k;x^k),\quad p_F^{k-1}\in\partial_{\alpha_{F,p}^k}H(x^k;x^k),\quad p_f^k\in\partial_{\widetilde\alpha_{f,p}^k+F(x^k)_+}H(x^k;x^k),\quad p_F^k\in\partial_{\widetilde\alpha_{F,p}^k}H(x^k;x^k),\quad p^k\in\partial_{\widetilde\alpha_p^k}H(x^k;x^k),\qquad\widetilde\alpha_p^k\geq0.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each iteration, the stored objective and constraint subgradients and the old and current aggregate vectors are approximate subgradients of H at the current point. Objective-cut errors include the current positive constraint violation, and the final aggregate error is nonnegative.
assumptions_latex: \text{The cuts, aggregates, linearization errors, and function H are those defined for Algorithm 7.1.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Global convergence alternatives for Algorithm 7.1
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Infinite-run convergence in the indefinitely infeasible and eventually feasible cases, including the stated line-search variants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose Algorithm 7.1 generates an infinite sequence \{x^k\}. If F(x^k)>0 for every k, then every accumulation point of \{x^k\} solves problem (1.1). If F(x^{k_0})\leq0 for some k_0\geq1, then F(x^k)\leq0 for every k\geq k_0 and\quad f(x^k)\downarrow\inf\{f(x):F(x)\leq0\}. Hence \{x^k\} is a minimizing sequence for (1.1); if (1.1) has a solution, then the entire sequence converges to a solution. The same conclusions hold when Algorithm 7.1 uses either modified line-search rule (7.17) or (7.18).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an infinite run, if every iterate remains infeasible, every accumulation point is a solution. If the method reaches feasibility, feasibility persists and the objective values decrease to the constrained infimum; when a solution exists, the full sequence converges to one. The theorem also remains valid for either stated modified line search.
assumptions_latex: \{x^k\}\text{ is an infinite sequence generated by Algorithm 7.1.}
\text{When a modified line search is used, it is the rule specified by (7.17) or (7.18).}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{cases}F(x^k)>0\ \forall k\Rightarrow\text{every accumulation point solves (1.1)},\\F(x^{k_0})\leq0\Rightarrow F(x^k)\leq0\ \forall k\geq k_0\text{ and }f(x^k)\downarrow\inf_{F(x)\leq0}f(x),\end{cases}\quad\text{with solvability in the second case implying }x^k\to x^*\text{ solving (1.1).}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Algorithm 7.1 phase I–phase II bundle procedure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direction finding, stopping test, and transition to the feasible phase of the constrained convex bundle method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration k, Algorithm 7.1 solves the dual direction-finding subproblem (7.6), forms the aggregate vector p^k, sets d^k=-p^k, and computes v^k and w^k by (7.7a) and (7.7b). It terminates if w^k\leq\varepsilon_S. Equivalently, (d^k,v^k) solves the primal direction-finding subproblem (7.1). If F(x^k)\leq0 at some iteration k, then F(x^\ell)\leq0 for every \ell\geq k, and from iteration k onward Algorithm 7.1 coincides with Algorithm 3.1. Consequently, phase II inherits the convergence results established for Algorithm 3.1.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Algorithm 7.1 obtains its direction from a dual bundle subproblem, equivalently from the corresponding primal direction problem, and applies the stopping test based on w^k. Once a feasible iterate is reached, all later iterates remain feasible and the method becomes Algorithm 3.1, so only an indefinitely long infeasible phase requires separate convergence analysis.
assumptions_latex: \text{All bundle quantities and subproblems are defined as in Algorithm 7.1.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: w^k\leq\varepsilon_S\Rightarrow\text{termination},\qquad F(x^k)\leq0\Rightarrow\left(F(x^\ell)\leq0\ \forall\ell\geq k\right)\text{ and phase-II equivalence to Algorithm 3.1.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Optimality System for the Stabilized Exact-Component Model
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient certificate for the proximal trial point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(t_k>0\), the full-domain finite convex problem \[\min_x\ s(x)+m_r^k(x)+\frac1{2t_k}\|x-x_k\|_2^2\] has a unique minimizer \(y_k\). It is characterized by weights \(\lambda_i\ge0\) on \(A_k(y_k)\), \(\sum_i\lambda_i=1\), satisfying \[0=\nabla s(y_k)+\sum_{i\in A_k(y_k)}\lambda_iq_i+t_k^{-1}(y_k-x_k).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The stabilized exact-component model has a unique trial point certified by active-cut weights.
assumptions_latex: \(s:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is differentiable and convex.
\(m_r^k\) is a finite maximum of affine functions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed active-cut stationarity system is necessary and sufficient for the unique minimizer.
knowledge_statements.title: Optimality System for the Stabilized Exact-Component Model

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Retention Does Not Cure Nonconvex Curvature
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of the convex structured-model guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The inequality \(s+m_r^k\le s+r\) follows from \(m_r^k\le r\) without assuming convexity of \(s\). However, if \(s\) is nonconvex, the exact-component model and its stabilized master may be nonconvex, so convex stationarity is no longer sufficient for global optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Keeping a nonconvex smooth component exact preserves minorization but can destroy convexity and global stationarity certificates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Minorization survives arbitrary \(s\), but convexity and convex optimality guarantees need not.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Retention Does Not Cure Nonconvex Curvature

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convexity and Subdifferential of the Exact-Component Model
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order structure when the smooth convex component is retained exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M_k=s+m_r^k\), where \(s\) is differentiable convex and \(m_r^k(x)=\max_{i\in I_k}\{\alpha_i+\langle q_i,x\rangle\}\le r(x)\). Then \(M_k\) is convex, \(M_k\le s+r\), and \[\partial M_k(x)=\nabla s(x)+\operatorname{conv}\{q_i:i\in A_k(x)\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The exact smooth term shifts the active-cut subdifferential by its gradient while preserving convexity and lower validity.
assumptions_latex: \(s:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is differentiable and convex.
knowledge_statements.title: Convexity and Subdifferential of the Exact-Component Model

assumptions_latex: \(F=s+r\) on \(\mathbb{R}^n\), where \(s\) is differentiable convex and \(r\) is finite convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The structured model satisfies \(M_k(x)\leq F(x)\) for all \(x\), while representing the smooth component without linearization error.

notation.meaning: Bundle model of the nonsmooth component.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: structured bundle model retaining a smooth convex component exactly
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composite convex objectives whose smooth term is retained exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[m_r^k(x):=\max_{i\in I_k}\{r(z_i)+\langle q_i,x-z_i\rangle\},\qquad M_k(x):=s(x)+m_r^k(x).\] The model uses the exact value \(s(x)\) at every candidate point and approximates only \(r\) by supporting cuts. Consequently \(M_k\leq F\). A stabilized trial point may be computed by minimizing \(M_k(x)+(2t_k)^{-1}\lVert x-x_k\rVert^2\), with \(t_k>0\), and oracle information for \(r\) at the trial point is then added to the bundle.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a smooth-plus-nonsmooth convex objective, retain the smooth component exactly and approximate only the nonsmooth component by supporting cuts.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Smooth-Component Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation correctly retains the smooth convex component and minorizes only the nonsmooth component. No authoritative composite-bundle source or locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Composite Proximal-Master Optimality Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order certificate for the stabilized master retaining the prox-friendly component exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(t_k>0\), \(y_k\) minimizes \[m_f^k(x)+g(x)+\frac{1}{2t_k}\lVert x-x_k\rVert^2\] if and only if there exist \(s_k\in\partial m_f^k(y_k)\) and \(q_k\in\partial g(y_k)\) such that \[s_k+q_k+\frac{y_k-x_k}{t_k}=0.\] The minimizer is unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The exact-component master is solved when model and component subgradients balance the proximal displacement; quadratic stabilization makes the trial point unique.
assumptions_latex: \(m_f^k\) and \(g\) are proper closed convex, their relative interiors satisfy the subdifferential sum qualification, and the master attains its minimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Composite Proximal-Master Optimality Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact-Component Model Error Identity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Approximation error and domain preservation when the prox-friendly component is retained exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=f+g\) and \(M_k=m_f^k+g\), where \(m_f^k\leq f\). For every \(x\in\operatorname{dom}g\), \[F(x)-M_k(x)=f(x)-m_f^k(x)\geq0.\] If \(m_f^k\) is finite-valued, then \(\operatorname{dom}M_k=\operatorname{dom}g\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: All model error comes from the approximated component, while retaining the prox-friendly component exactly preserves its domain.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex, \(g\) is proper closed convex, and \(m_f^k\) is a finite-valued convex minorant of \(f\).
knowledge_statements.title: Exact-Component Model Error Identity

assumptions_latex: \(F=f+g\), where \(f\) is finite convex with a value-subgradient oracle and \(g\) is proper closed convex.
The proximal subproblem involving \(g\) and the chosen stabilization can be solved to the required accuracy.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The model satisfies \(M_k\leq F\) and preserves the full geometry of the prox-friendly component \(g\).

notation.meaning: Polyhedral minorant of the oracle component.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: composite bundle model retaining a proximable term exactly
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composite models retaining a proximable convex component exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A prox-friendly component model of \(F\) is \[M_k(x):=m_f^k(x)+g(x),\qquad m_f^k(x):=\max_{i	ext{ in }I_k}\{f(z_i)+\langle p_i,x-z_i\rangle\},\] where \(p_i\in\partial f(z_i)\). The trial point solves \[x_{k+1}^{\mathrm{trial}}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_x\left\{M_k(x)+\frac{1}{2t_k}\lVert x-x_k\rVert^2\right\}.\] The term \(g\) is not cut or linearized; its domain, nonsmoothness, and readily computable proximal structure remain present in the master problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A prox-friendly model replaces the oracle component by bundle cuts while retaining the proximable convex component exactly in the stabilized master problem.
knowledge_statements.title: Prox-Friendly Component Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the model leaf and the lower-model relation is mathematically consistent for an extended-valued proper closed convex prox-friendly term. The claimed structured master formulation lacks cited support and a locator.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uncertified Inner Solutions Do Not Give Contact Guarantees
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between lower validity and certified model accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any \(u_z\in U\), the component \(\Phi(\cdot,u_z)\) remains below \(F\), but without a certified bound on \(F(z)-\Phi(z,u_z)\) there is no finite contact-error guarantee at \(z\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any feasible scenario is a valid lower component, but only a certified inner solution controls contact accuracy.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Lower validity holds, while contact accuracy is unquantified without an inner-gap certificate.
knowledge_statements.title: Uncertified Inner Solutions Do Not Give Contact Guarantees

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convexity and Monotone Scenario Enrichment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural properties of restricted supremum models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If every \(x\mapsto\Phi(x,u)\) is convex, each finite restricted model \(M_k(x)=\max_{u\in U_k}\Phi(x,u)\) is convex. If \(U_k\subseteq U_{k+1}\subset U\), then \[M_k(x)\le M_{k+1}(x)\le F(x)\quad\text{for all }x.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restricted max models are convex and increase monotonically while remaining below the full supremum.
assumptions_latex: \(U_k\subseteq U_{k+1}\subset U\) are finite and nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_k\) and \(M_{k+1}\) are convex and \(M_k\le M_{k+1}\le F\).
knowledge_statements.title: Convexity and Monotone Scenario Enrichment

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Active-Scenario Subdifferential
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-maximum calculus for retained convex scenarios.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(U_k\) is finite and every retained component \(\Phi(\cdot,u)\) is finite and convex near \(x\). With \(A_k(x)=\{u\in U_k:\Phi(x,u)=M_k(x)\}\), \[\partial M_k(x)=\operatorname{conv}\bigcup_{u\in A_k(x)}\partial_x\Phi(x,u).\] If the active components are differentiable, this becomes the convex hull of their gradients.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The subdifferential of a finite restricted max is generated by active scenario subgradients.
assumptions_latex: Every retained component is finite and convex on a neighborhood of \(x\).
knowledge_statements.title: Active-Scenario Subdifferential

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Certified Exact and Inexact Scenario Enrichment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restricted-supremum guarantee with a precise approximate-maximizer certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(x)=\sup_{u\in U}\Phi(x,u)\) and \(M_k(x)=\max_{u\in U_k}\Phi(x,u)\) for finite \(U_k\subset U\). Then \(M_k\le F\). If \(u_z\in U\) satisfies \(F(z)-\Phi(z,u_z)\le\varepsilon_z\) and is added to \(U_k\), the enlarged model satisfies \[M_{k+1}(x)\le F(x),\qquad 0\le F(z)-M_{k+1}(z)\le\varepsilon_z.\] Exact contact is the case \(\varepsilon_z=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certified epsilon-maximizer preserves global minorization and gives epsilon-exact contact at the oracle point.
knowledge_statements.title: Certified Exact and Inexact Scenario Enrichment

assumptions_latex: \(U\) is nonempty and \(F(x)=\sup_{u\in U}\Phi(x,u)\) is finite.
For each \(u\in U\), the function \(x\mapsto\Phi(x,u)\) is convex.
The oracle returns a maximizing or certified approximately maximizing parameter.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For exact maximizers and exact component evaluations, \(M_k(x)\leq F(x)\) globally and \(M_k(z_i)=F(z_i)\) at every retained oracle point.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: restricted-max model for convex supremum structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex objectives represented as pointwise suprema of convex component functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite retained set \(U_k\), define the structured lower model \[M_k(x):=\max_{u\in U_k}\Phi(x,u).\] Since \(U_k\subset U\), this model minorizes \(F\). At an oracle point \(z_i\), obtain \(u_i\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{u\in U}\Phi(z_i,u)\) and add \(u_i\) to \(U_k\); then the enlarged model is exact at \(z_i\). If evaluating \(\Phi(\cdot,u_i)\) exactly is impractical, a supporting affine minorant of that convex component may be stored instead, but its validity must be preserved globally.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a supremum-structured convex objective, retain selected maximizing parameters and model the objective by the maximum over their component functions or valid cuts.
knowledge_statements.title: Max-Structure Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The restricted-maximum representation is plausible, but the assumptions allow a certified approximate maximizer while the construction and exactness conclusion require an exact maximizer. A source is needed to specify the approximation certificate and corresponding inexact model guarantees.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Oracle Failure Without Maximizer Attainment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Attainment boundary for exact inner-maximization oracle access.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U=(0,1)\) and \(\Phi(x,u)=ux\). For every \(x>0\), \[F(x)=\sup_{u\in(0,1)}ux=x,\qquad \operatorname*{argmax}_{u\in U}\Phi(x,u)=\varnothing.\] Thus a finite convex supremum need not admit the maximizing response required by the exact oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite convex supremum may fail to attain its inner maximum, so the exact saddle-oracle response need not exist.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Oracle Failure Without Maximizer Attainment

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inexact Saddle Oracle Produces an Epsilon-Cut
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cut validity when inner maximization is solved approximately.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(x)=\sup_{u\in U}\Phi(x,u)\), with \(\Phi(\cdot,u)\) convex. If \(F(z)-\Phi(z,u_z)\leq\varepsilon_z\) and \(g_z\in\partial_x\Phi(z,u_z)\), then \[F(x)\geq F(z)+\langle g_z,x-z\rangle-\varepsilon_z\quad\text{for all }x.\] Hence \(g_z\in\partial_{\varepsilon_z}F(z)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An approximate inner maximizer yields an epsilon-subgradient and a globally valid cut shifted down by the maximization error.
assumptions_latex: \(F(z)<+\infty\), \(\varepsilon_z\geq0\), and \(\Phi(\cdot,u_z)\) is convex and subdifferentiable at \(z\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g_z\in\partial_{\varepsilon_z}F(z)\), and the shifted affine function globally minorizes \(F\).
knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Saddle Oracle Produces an Epsilon-Cut

assumptions_latex: \(U\) is nonempty and \(F(x)=\sup_{u\in U}\Phi(x,u)\) is finite and convex.
For each \(u\), the map \(x\mapsto\Phi(x,u)\) is convex and subdifferentiable.
At a query point, the oracle returns an exact maximizer and an associated partial subgradient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each oracle response produces a verifiable affine global minorant of \(F\), and the maximum of accumulated responses is a valid bundle model.

notation.meaning: Affine cut returned at query z.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Danskin-type saddle oracle supporting cut
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact maximization oracles for convex-concave saddle representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At a query \(z\), choose \(u_z\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{u\in U}\Phi(z,u)\) and \(g_z\in\partial_x\Phi(z,u_z)\). The oracle returns \(F(z)=\Phi(z,u_z)\) and \(g_z\), generating \[
ell_z(x):=F(z)+\langle g_z,x-z\rangle.\] By the convexity of \(\Phi(\cdot,u_z)\), \(\ell_z(x)\leq\Phi(x,u_z)\leq F(x)\). Thus responses at query points \(z_i\) define the bundle model \(M_k(x):=\max_i\ell_{z_i}(x)\), which can be used in a stabilized master problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A saddle-point oracle maximizes the inner variable and returns a partial subgradient, yielding an affine global lower cut for the outer convex objective.
knowledge_statements.title: Saddle-Point Oracle Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The affine-minorant calculation is valid under the stated exact-maximizer assumptions, and representation is a reasonable kind. However, the scope calls this a convex-concave saddle representation without introducing concavity, topology, or maximizer-existence conditions; no source resolves the intended saddle-oracle setting.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Simplex Saddle Problem and Its Primal–Dual Marginal Forms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A finite-dimensional bilinear saddle model over two standard simplices and its nonsmooth marginal functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\). If \(a_j\) and \(\hat a_i\) are respectively the rows and columns of \(A\), consider
\[
\min_{x\in\Delta_n}\max_{u\in\Delta_m}\left\{\langle Ax,u\rangle+\langle c,x\rangle+\langle b,u\rangle\right\}.
\]
The associated marginal functions are
\[
f(x):=\langle c,x\rangle+\max_{1\le j\le m}\left\{\langle a_j,x\rangle+b^{(j)}\right\},\qquad x\in\Delta_n,
\]
and
\[
\phi(u):=\langle b,u\rangle+\min_{1\le i\le n}\left\{\langle\hat a_i,u\rangle+c^{(i)}\right\},\qquad u\in\Delta_m.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maximizing the bilinear-affine saddle function over the second simplex yields a maximum of affine functions of x, while minimizing it over the first simplex yields a minimum of affine functions of u.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f(x)=\langle c,x\rangle+\max_{1\le j\le m}\{\langle a_j,x\rangle+b^{(j)}\},\qquad \phi(u)=\langle b,u\rangle+\min_{1\le i\le n}\{\langle\hat a_i,u\rangle+c^{(i)}\}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual of the Unconstrained Disaggregate Proximal Master
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Product-of-simplices dual representation for a finite disaggregate proximal bundle master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Write \(h_{ji}(x)=a_{ji}+\langle g_{ji},x\rangle\) and let \(t>0\). The unconstrained master \(\min_x\{\sum_{j=1}^p\max_{i\in I_j}h_{ji}(x)+\frac{1}{2t}\|x-c\|^2\}\) has dual \(\max_{\lambda_j\in\Delta_{I_j}}\{\sum_{j,i}\lambda_{ji}(a_{ji}+\langle g_{ji},c\rangle)-\frac{t}{2}\|\sum_{j,i}\lambda_{ji}g_{ji}\|^2\}\). If \(\lambda^*\) is dual optimal, the unique primal trial point is \(x^*=c-t\sum_{j,i}\lambda^*_{ji}g_{ji}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The disaggregate proximal master has one simplex of cut weights per component, and their aggregate subgradient determines the unique primal trial point.
assumptions_latex: Every component has finitely many affine cuts.
The master is unconstrained in finite-dimensional Euclidean space.

notation.meaning: probability simplex over component j's cuts
dual weight of cut i in component j

knowledge_statements.title: Dual of the Unconstrained Disaggregate Proximal Master

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cartesian-Product Aggregate-Cut Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact representation of a summed disaggregate polyhedral model as an aggregate cutting-plane model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For finite component models \(m_j(x)=\max_{i\in I_j}h_{ji}(x)\), \(\sum_{j=1}^pm_j(x)=\max_{(i_1,\ldots,i_p)\in I_1\times\cdots\times I_p}\sum_{j=1}^ph_{j i_j}(x)\). Thus disaggregation stores the same aggregate model without explicitly enumerating up to \(\prod_j|I_j|\) combined cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sum of component maxima equals a maximum over Cartesian-product combinations of component cuts, so disaggregation stores the aggregate model compactly.
knowledge_statements.title: Cartesian-Product Aggregate-Cut Representation

assumptions_latex: \(F(x)=\sum_{j=1}^p f_j(x)\), with every \(f_j\) finite and convex.
For each component, stored pairs satisfy \(g_{ji}\in\partial f_j(z_{ji})\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The summed disaggregate model satisfies \(M_k(x)\leq F(x)\) and preserves component identities for independent updating and aggregation.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: disaggregate bundle model for a finite convex sum
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-sum convex objectives with separately maintained component bundles.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain \(m_j^k(x):=\max_{i\in I_j^k}\{f_j(z_{ji})+\langle g_{ji},x-z_{ji}\rangle\}\) separately for every component. Given center \(x_k\), compute \[y_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x}\left\{\sum_{j=1}^p m_j^k(x)+\frac{1}{2t_k}\lVert x-x_k\rVert^2\right\}.\] Query selected or all component oracles at \(y_k\), add their cuts only to the corresponding bundles, and use the total actual and predicted decreases in the serious-step test. On a null step, retain \(x_k\) while enriching at least one component model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A disaggregate bundle method maintains one lower model per summand and minimizes their stabilized sum, allowing each component bundle to be updated independently.
knowledge_statements.title: Disaggregate Bundle Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is the correct kind, and the summed component model is a valid lower model. If only selected components are queried at a trial point, the record does not specify how total actual decrease is certified; an authoritative disaggregate-bundle source is required.

assumptions_latex: \(F=\sum_{j=1}^p f_j\), where each component has a value-subgradient oracle.
Every stored or aggregated component cut remains a global minorant of its own component.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At every iteration, each component model remains valid and their sum is a global lower model of \(F\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: component-indexed oracle and bundle management protocol
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity-preserving management of separate component bundles and oracle calls.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), select \(S_k\). For each \(j\in S_k\), query \(f_j\) at the trial point and insert the resulting supporting cut into \(\mathcal B_j^{k+1}\). For \(j\notin S_k\), set \(\mathcal B_j^{k+1}\) to retained valid cuts from \(\mathcal B_j^k\). Cuts may be deleted or aggregated only if each resulting component model still minorizes \(f_j\). Trial-point prediction uses \(M_k=\sum_j m_j^k\); acceptance uses values of every component required to certify the chosen actual-reduction test. Stop only when the prescribed model-gap or stationarity test is evaluable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Oracle calls, cuts, deletion, and aggregation are managed by component while preserving every component lower bound and the validity of the summed model.
knowledge_statements.title: Componentwise Oracle Management

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The componentwise management protocol preserves lower-model validity, but its selection, aggregation, acceptance-certification, and stopping requirements are not tied to a cited algorithm or theorem. No source locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Partial Evaluation Cannot Certify Total Actual Reduction by Itself
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information boundary for acceptance tests under partial component evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(x)=\sum_{j=1}^p f_j(x)\), let \(c\) be the current center, and suppose that at a trial point \(y\) exact values \(f_j(y)\) are obtained only for \(j\in S\subsetneq\{1,\ldots,p\}\). Without exact cached values at \(y\) or certified bounds on \(f_j(y)\) for \(j\notin S\), these observations do not determine \(F(y)\) or \(F(c)-F(y)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Selected component evaluations do not determine the total trial value or exact actual reduction unless missing components are otherwise certified.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is a strict subset of the component indices.
No exact values or certified trial-point bounds are available for unqueried components.

notation.meaning: components evaluated at the trial point

knowledge_statements.title: Partial Evaluation Cannot Certify Total Actual Reduction by Itself

intermediate_metadata.reason: This leaf owns scheduling, refreshing, retaining, and certifying component-indexed oracle information. Its generic seed remains underspecified. The proposed partial-evaluation impossibility claim is deferred as primarily owned by the Partial Component Evaluation sibling; disaggregate master structure and bound composition are likewise excluded sibling scopes.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unobserved Components Cannot Certify Serious-Step Decrease
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information boundary for trial acceptance after evaluating only a strict subset of finite-sum components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\sum_{j=1}^p f_j\), with current center \(x\) and trial point \(z\). If only \(S\subsetneq\{1,\ldots,p\}\) is evaluated at \(z\), and some \(j\notin S\) has no certified upper bound on \(f_j(z)-f_j(x)\), then the observed data do not determine the sign of \(F(z)-F(x)\). Convex affine choices for an unobserved component can preserve all observed data while reversing that sign. Thus actual-decrease certification requires evaluating, or obtaining valid upper-change bounds for, every otherwise-uncontrolled component.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partial component values cannot certify aggregate decrease when an unevaluated component has no upper bound on its change.
assumptions_latex: At least one unevaluated component has no certified upper bound on its change from \(x\) to \(z\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sign of \(F(z)-F(x)\) is not identifiable from the partial evaluation data.

notation.meaning: Components evaluated at the trial point.

knowledge_statements.title: Unobserved Components Cannot Certify Serious-Step Decrease

assumptions_latex: \(F=\sum_{j=1}^p f_j\), with finite convex components and valid component models.
There exists \(B\geq1\) such that every component is evaluated at least once in any \(B\) consecutive iterations.
A serious step is accepted only after its required full objective value is certified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: All component models remain global minorants; bounded-delay refresh prevents any component from remaining permanently unevaluated.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: bounded-delay partial component evaluation with valid stale lower models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Partial finite-sum oracle evaluation with bounded refresh delays.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), choose a nonempty subset \(S_k\subseteq\{1,\ldots,p\}\), evaluate only \(f_j\) for \(j\in S_k\) at the trial point, and append the corresponding supporting cuts. For \(j\notin S_k\), reuse the previous valid model \(m_j^k\). Form the next master model by summing the updated and retained component models. Enforce \(\bigcup_{r=k}^{k+B-1}S_r=\{1,\ldots,p\}\) for every \(k\). Before declaring a serious step or termination, evaluate any missing components needed to certify actual decrease, feasibility, or the stated stopping condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluate only selected summands per iteration, retain valid stale models for the others, refresh every component within a bounded delay, and certify accepted progress fully.
knowledge_statements.title: Partial Component Evaluation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the leaf, and bounded refresh indeed prevents permanent omission while retained cuts remain valid. The bounded-delay policy and full-certification requirements have no cited source, and no convergence claim should be inferred without one.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Component Bound and Gap Composition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composition of certified component intervals into a certified interval for a finite sum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(F(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x)\) and, at a fixed \(x\), certified numbers \(L_i,U_i\) satisfy \(L_i\le f_i(x)\le U_i\). Then \(L:=\sum_iL_i\) and \(U:=\sum_iU_i\) satisfy \(L\le F(x)\le U\), with \(U-L=\sum_i(U_i-L_i)\). Thus \(U_i-L_i\le\delta_i\) implies \(U-L\le\sum_i\delta_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certified component intervals add to a certified interval for the sum, and their gap budgets add exactly.

notation.meaning: certified lower and upper values for component i at the same point

knowledge_statements.title: Component Bound and Gap Composition

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Coupling Can Make Summed Component Minima Strictly Loose
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp failure of exact bound composition when components share a decision variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(X=\mathbb R\), let \(f_1(x)=(x-1)^2\) and \(f_2(x)=(x+1)^2\). Then \(\inf_X f_1+\inf_X f_2=0\), whereas \(\inf_{x\in X}(f_1(x)+f_2(x))=2\). Thus the sum of independent component minima is a valid lower bound for a shared-variable sum but need not be exact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Shared variables can make the sum of component minima strictly smaller than the minimum of the summed objective.
assumptions_latex: Both components are minimized over the same scalar decision variable.
knowledge_statements.title: Coupling Can Make Summed Component Minima Strictly Loose

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Separation over Product Domains
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp condition under which component optimum bounds compose without coupling loss.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\prod_{i=1}^mX_i\) and \(F(x_1,\ldots,x_m)=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)\). Whenever the extended-real sum is well defined, \(\inf_{x\in X}F(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m\inf_{x_i\in X_i}f_i(x_i)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a product feasible set and independently parameterized summands, minimization separates exactly into component minima.
assumptions_latex: The extended-real sum contains no indeterminate form.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Separation over Product Domains
Decomposition Bound Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Aggregate lower-bound interface for a finite sum of proper convex component functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x)\) on a convex set \(X\), where each \(f_i:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and convex. Suppose the component interface supplies models \(m_i^k:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) satisfying \(m_i^k(x)\le f_i(x)\) for every \(x\in X\). Then the aggregate model
\[
m^k(x):=\sum_{i=1}^m m_i^k(x)
\]
satisfies \(m^k(x)\le f(x)\) on \(X\). Consequently, for any regularizer \(R_k:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\),
\[
\inf_{x\in X}\{m^k(x)+R_k(x)\}\le \inf_{x\in X}\{f(x)+R_k(x)\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Summing valid component lower models produces a valid model of the decomposed objective and a lower bound for every identically regularized subproblem.
assumptions_latex: \(f=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i\), with each \(f_i\) proper and convex on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m^k:=\sum_i m_i^k\le f\), and the corresponding regularized model value is a lower bound.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Persistent-Width Stopping Floor
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limitation of stopping rules based on a fixed-accuracy oracle bracket.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose every attainable certified bracket at a candidate point satisfies \(L(x)\le f(x)\le U(x)\) and \(U(x)-L(x)\ge\omega>0\). Then a stopping rule requiring bracket width at most \(\tau<\omega\) cannot fire. Thus fixed oracle accuracy cannot support arbitrarily small width-based certificates unless additional or more accurate information becomes available.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A persistent positive bracket width imposes a nonzero floor on width-based stopping certificates.
assumptions_latex: Every attainable certified bracket has width at least \(\omega>0\).

notation.meaning: Persistent lower bound on attainable bracket width.

knowledge_statements.title: Persistent-Width Stopping Floor
Fixed-Accuracy Oracle Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bundle model construction with a constant absolute oracle tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x^0\in X\), a fixed tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\), and proximal parameters \(t_k>0\), query at \(y^k\in X\) an oracle returning \((\widehat f_k,g_k)\) such that
\[
f(x)\ge \widehat f_k+\langle g_k,x-y^k\rangle-\varepsilon\quad(x\in X),
\qquad |\widehat f_k-f(y^k)|\le\varepsilon.
\]
Append the resulting affine cut to the bundle model \(m_k\), compute
\[
z^k\in\mathop{\rm argmin}_{x\in X}\left\{m_k(x)+\frac{1}{2t_k}\|x-x^k\|^2\right\},
\]
and accept or reject \(z^k\) using the method's inexact descent test. Stop when the model gap is at most a prescribed tolerance exceeding the oracle-induced uncertainty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed-accuracy bundle method uses the same oracle tolerance at every query and terminates only at a tolerance compatible with that persistent uncertainty.
assumptions_latex: The oracle satisfies the displayed global inexact-cut and value-error inequalities with fixed \(\varepsilon\).
Each proximal subproblem has a minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iterates and bundle cuts are generated with constant oracle accuracy \(\varepsilon\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the leaf, but no inspectable source supports this particular combination of oracle inequalities, descent test, and stopping rule. The phrases "method's inexact descent test" and "tolerance exceeding the oracle-induced uncertainty" do not specify a reproducible fixed-accuracy bundle variant, and the required uncertainty threshold depends on the oracle convention.

knowledge_statements.title: Vanishing-Error Oracle Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inexact bundle iteration whose requested oracle errors converge to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Choose \(x^0\in X\), positive proximal parameters \(t_k\), and tolerances \(\varepsilon_k\downarrow0\). At query point \(y^k\), obtain \((\widehat f_k,g_k)\) satisfying
\[
f(x)\ge \widehat f_k+\langle g_k,x-y^k\rangle-\varepsilon_k\quad(x\in X),
\qquad |\widehat f_k-f(y^k)|\le\varepsilon_k.
\]
Insert this cut into \(m_k\), solve
\[
z^k\in\mathop{\rm argmin}_{x\in X}\left\{m_k(x)+\frac{1}{2t_k}\|x-x^k\|^2\right\},
\]
and apply a serious/null-step test accounting for \(\varepsilon_k\). Continue while the certified model gap exceeds the requested optimization tolerance; otherwise output the current serious iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method progressively requests more accurate oracle answers, using error-aware cuts and descent tests until the model gap meets the optimization tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, closed, and convex on the nonempty closed convex set \(X\).
The displayed oracle inequalities hold at every query.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The bundle sequence is generated with asymptotically exact oracle information.

notation.meaning: oracle error requested at iteration k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm content kind and vanishing-error theme fit the leaf, but the stated procedure does not define the error-aware serious/null-step test or certified gap. Whether merely requiring epsilon_k to converge to zero is adequate depends on the bundle variant and convergence target. An authoritative algorithm statement with its accuracy schedule and decision rules is required.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Vanishing Oracle Error Alone Does Not Ensure Optimization Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic projected-subgradient example proposed as a boundary for an underspecified bundle regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=[0,1]\), \(f(x)=x\), and \(x^{k+1}=P_X(x^k-\alpha_k)\), where \(x^0=1\), \(\alpha_k>0\), and \(\sum_k\alpha_k=c<1\). Although the oracle is exact, so \(\varepsilon_k=0\to0\), the iterates converge to \(1-c>0\) instead of the minimizer \(0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact-oracle projected-subgradient method can fail when its total movement is finite.
knowledge_statements.title: Vanishing Oracle Error Alone Does Not Ensure Optimization Convergence

intermediate_metadata.reason: This leaf owns exogenously vanishing oracle error within bundle methods. Its algorithm, stopping certificate, sufficient schedule, convergence theorem, and bundle-specific failure boundary remain underspecified, so the topic is deferred. The Builder's generic projected-subgradient counterexample is deferred to general stepsize theory. Fixed and feedback-adaptive accuracy regimes remain in sibling leaves.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Termination of a Relative Accuracy-Refinement Loop
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Policy-independent inner refinement condition for a fixed positive predicted decrease.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(\eta\in(0,1)\) and \(\Delta\ge0\). If refinements produce certified widths \(w_r\ge0\) with \(w_r\to0\), then \(\Delta>0\) implies that some finite \(r_*\) satisfies \(w_{r_*}\le\eta\Delta\). If \(\Delta=0\), the same relative test requires \(w_r=0\) and need not terminate when widths approach zero only asymptotically.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Vanishing uncertainty eventually satisfies a relative test for positive predicted decrease, but not necessarily when predicted decrease is zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Delta>0\Rightarrow(\exists r_*<\infty)\;w_{r_*}\le\eta\Delta\); this implication can fail for \(\Delta=0\).

notation.meaning: Predicted decrease held fixed during refinement.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Termination of a Relative Accuracy-Refinement Loop
Adaptive-Accuracy Oracle Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bundle iteration that tightens oracle accuracy only when current uncertainty obstructs a decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(x^0\in X\) and an oracle tolerance \(\varepsilon_0>0\). At iteration \(k\), form an inexact bundle cut with error \(\varepsilon_k\), compute a proximal trial point \(z^k\), and derive a predicted decrease \(\Delta_k\ge0\). Fix \(\eta\in(0,1)\). If the available upper and lower oracle information cannot determine whether the serious-step inequality holds because its uncertainty width \(w_k\) satisfies \(w_k>\eta\Delta_k\), replace \(\varepsilon_k\) by a smaller tolerance and reevaluate the required oracle data. Otherwise perform the certified serious or null step and retain or relax accuracy according to the update policy. Output a serious iterate when its certified model gap, including \(w_k\), is within tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Oracle accuracy is tightened when uncertainty is too large relative to predicted progress; otherwise the algorithm accepts a certified serious or null step.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, closed, and convex on a nonempty closed convex set \(X\).
Oracle lower and upper information has a computable uncertainty width \(w_k\).
Repeated refinement can make \(w_k\) arbitrarily small.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted step decision has uncertainty \(w_k\le\eta\Delta_k\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the adaptive-accuracy leaf, but the uncertainty width, refinement mechanism, reevaluation scope, and retain-or-relax policy are not mathematically defined. Consequently the claimed invariant for every accepted decision is policy-dependent and cannot be validated without a specific sourced adaptive bundle algorithm.

children.title: Lower Oracle Models
children.top_down_role: Oracle-derived representations supplying lower information.

knowledge_statements.title: Lower Oracle Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global affine minorant supplied by an inexact convex oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be convex, let \(y\in\mathop{\rm dom}f\), and let an oracle return \((\widehat f_y,g_y,\varepsilon_y)\) with \(\varepsilon_y\ge0\). The associated lower oracle model is
\[
\ell_y(x):=\widehat f_y+\langle g_y,x-y\rangle-\varepsilon_y.
\]
It is valid precisely when
\[
\ell_y(x)\le f(x)\qquad\text{for every }x\in X.
\]
Equivalently, \(g_y\) is an \(\varepsilon_y\)-subgradient relative to the reported value under the convention encoded by the displayed inequality. The maximum of finitely many valid lower oracle models is again a global lower model of \(f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lower oracle model is an affine function, adjusted for oracle error, that globally underestimates the convex objective.

notation.meaning: lower affine oracle model at y

children.title: Upper Oracle Models
children.top_down_role: Oracle-derived representations supplying upper information.

knowledge_statements.title: Upper Oracle Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certified majorizing information used to assess objective values or trial-point descent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), and let \(Y\subseteq X\) be the set on which an oracle certifies upper information. An upper oracle model is a function \(u_y:Y\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), associated with a query \(y\in Y\), satisfying
\[
f(x)
\le u_y(x)
\qquad(x\in Y).
\]
For a value oracle returning \(\widehat f_y\) with certified error \(\delta_y\ge0\), the pointwise upper model at the query is
\[
u_y(y):=\widehat f_y+\delta_y,
\qquad f(y)\le u_y(y).
\]
Unless additional smoothness or structural information is supplied, this pointwise certificate need not define a finite global majorant away from \(y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An upper oracle model certifiably majorizes the objective on its stated validity set; a noisy value oracle ordinarily gives only a pointwise upper bound.
assumptions_latex: \(Y\subseteq X\) is the declared validity set.
The oracle provides a certified upper-error allowance \(\delta_y\ge0\).

notation.meaning: upper oracle model associated with y
validity set of the upper model

children.title: Oracle-Model Bracketing
children.top_down_role: Structural relation between lower and upper oracle representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Oracle-Model Bracketing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise certificate combining valid lower and upper oracle models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(L_k:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be a valid lower model of \(f\), and let \(U_k:Y_k\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be a valid upper model on \(Y_k\subseteq X\). For every \(x\in Y_k\),
\[
L_k(x)\le f(x)\le U_k(x).
\]
The computable width
\[
w_k(x):=U_k(x)-L_k(x)
\]
is therefore a certificate of model uncertainty wherever both bounds are finite. In particular, if \(w_k(x)\le\tau\), then both one-sided errors satisfy
\[
0\le f(x)-L_k(x)\le\tau,
\qquad 0\le U_k(x)-f(x)\le\tau.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Valid lower and upper models bracket the objective; their computable width certifies both one-sided model errors at the evaluation point.
assumptions_latex: Both bounds are finite at the certified point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_k(x)\le f(x)\le U_k(x)\), with both errors bounded by \(w_k(x)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Boundedness and Null-Step Direction Recursion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Technical local boundedness and recursion estimates supporting convergence analysis of Algorithm 3.1.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\bar x\in\mathbb R^N\), \(\bar a>0\), and \(B=\{y\in\mathbb R^N:\lVert y-\bar x\rVert\leq\bar a\}\). There exists a constant \(C\), independent of \(k\), such that \[\max\{\lVert p^k\rVert,\lVert g^{k+1}\rVert,1\}\leq C\quad\text{whenever }x^k\in B.\] Moreover, if \(k>1\), \(x^k\in B\), \(t_L^{k-1}=0\), and \(e^k=e^{k-1}\), then \[\frac12\lVert p^k\rVert^2\leq\phi_C\!\left(\frac12\lVert p^{k-1}\rVert^2\right),\qquad \phi_C(t)=t-\frac{(1-m_R)^2t^2}{8C^2},\quad m_R\in(0,1).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a fixed closed ball, the bundle directions and new subgradients are uniformly bounded. Under the stated null-step and unchanged-error conditions, consecutive direction norms satisfy the given scalar recursion.
assumptions_latex: \bar x\in\mathbb R^N,\quad \bar a>0,\quad B=\{y\in\mathbb R^N:\lVert y-\bar x\rVert\leq\bar a\}.
k>1,\quad t_L^{k-1}=0,\quad e^k=e^{k-1}\text{ for the recursive estimate}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists C\text{ independent of }k:\ \max\{\lVert p^k\rVert,\lVert g^{k+1}\rVert,1\}\leq C;\quad \frac12\lVert p^k\rVert^2\leq\phi_C\!\left(\frac12\lVert p^{k-1}\rVert^2\right).

knowledge_statements.title: Serious-Step Convergence Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional convergence result when a bundle method accepts infinitely many serious steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, and convex with nonempty solution set \(X^*\). Consider a proximal bundle method with exact lower cuts, bounded positive proximal parameters, and serious-step parameter \(\gamma\in(0,1)\). Let \(x^k\) denote its stability centers. If infinitely many serious steps occur and every accepted trial point realizes at least \(\gamma\) times its predicted model decrease, then
\[
f(x^k)\downarrow f^*.
\]
If the serious-iterate sequence is bounded, every cluster point belongs to \(X^*\). If, additionally, \(f\) has a unique minimizer \(x^*\), then the serious iterates converge to \(x^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With infinitely many sufficiently decreasing serious steps, objective values reach the optimum; bounded serious iterates have optimal cluster points and converge under uniqueness.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, closed, and convex with \(X^*\ne\varnothing\).
The proximal parameters remain bounded above and away from zero, and lower cuts are exact.
Infinitely many serious steps satisfy the fixed fractional-decrease test.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x^k)\to f^*\); bounded cluster points are in \(X^*\), with full convergence under uniqueness.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem role fits the convergence-regime leaf, but the generic method description is insufficient to validate convergence to the optimum. Exact lower cuts, bounded proximal parameters, and a fractional acceptance test do not by themselves specify model management, trial-point construction, predicted decrease, or safeguards needed by a particular bundle theorem. A source with the exact theorem and hypotheses is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Infinite Null-Step Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional stationarity result when a stability center is followed by infinitely many null steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, and convex. Fix a stability center \(\bar x\) in an exact proximal bundle method, and suppose all subsequent iterations are null steps. Assume the proximal parameter satisfies \(0<\underline t\le t_k\le\overline t<\infty\), every trial-point cut is retained or aggregated without losing its value and subgradient information, and the proximal subproblems are solved exactly. Then the predicted decreases converge to zero. Moreover,
\[
0\in\partial f(\bar x),
\]
so \(\bar x\) minimizes \(f\). Thus an infinite null-step tail cannot persist at a nonoptimal stability center under these model-consistency conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If exact, model-consistent null steps continue forever at one center, predicted decrease vanishes and that center must minimize the convex objective.
assumptions_latex: The oracle and proximal subproblem solutions are exact.
The stability center \(\bar x\) is fixed throughout an infinite null-step tail.
Proximal parameters are uniformly positive and bounded, and essential cuts are retained or exactly aggregated.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem content kind matches the leaf, but the asserted null-step alternative is highly dependent on the bundle update and aggregation rules. The phrase "without losing its value and subgradient information" is not a formal model-consistency condition, so it is not possible to determine whether predicted decrease must vanish or stationarity follows. A specific convergence theorem is required.

If \(t_k\le t_{k-1}\) for all \(k>k_0\) and \(\sum_{k>k_0}t_k^2/t_{k-1}=+\infty\), then \(x_{k_0}\) minimizes \(f\) on \(C\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Failure Without Lower Semicontinuity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimal-value convergence need not make a cluster point optimal when closedness is removed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(f:\mathbb R\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) by \[f(x)=\begin{cases}+\infty,&x<0,\\1,&x=0,\\x,&x>0.\end{cases}\] This function is proper and convex but not lower semicontinuous at zero. It has \(f^*=0\), while \(x^k=1/k\) satisfies \(x^k\to0\) and \(f(x^k)\to f^*\), yet \(f(0)=1>f^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex but nonclosed objective, asymptotically optimal values can accompany convergence to a nonoptimal point.
assumptions_latex: The closedness or lower-semicontinuity assumption is omitted.
knowledge_statements.title: Failure Without Lower Semicontinuity
Cluster-Point Optimality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimality of accumulation points produced by a convergent convex bundle regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, and convex, and let \((x^k)\subset\mathop{\rm dom}f\) be stability centers generated by a convergent exact-oracle bundle method. Suppose
\[
f(x^k)\to f^*:=\inf_x f(x)>-\infty.
\]
If a subsequence satisfies \(x^{k_j}\to\bar x\), then lower semicontinuity gives
\[
f(\bar x)\le\liminf_{j\to\infty}f(x^{k_j})=f^*.
\]
Since \(f^*\le f(\bar x)\), equality holds and
\[
\bar x\in\mathop{\rm argmin}_x f(x).
\]
Hence every finite cluster point of the stability-center sequence is optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Whenever bundle stability-center values converge to the finite optimum, lower semicontinuity makes every finite cluster point a minimizer.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, closed, and convex with finite infimum \(f^*\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Optimal Cluster Points Do Not Imply Full Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of full-sequence convergence without uniqueness or an anti-oscillation condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f=\delta_{[0,1]}\), and define \(x^{2j}=0\) and \(x^{2j+1}=1\). Then \((x^k)\) is bounded, \(f(x^k)=f^*=0\), and every cluster point is optimal, but \((x^k)\) does not converge.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sequence can oscillate between two minimizers even though every cluster point is optimal.
assumptions_latex: The solution set contains more than one point.
No quasi-Fejér or other anti-oscillation condition is imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every cluster point belongs to \(X^*=[0,1]\), but \((x^k)\) does not converge.
knowledge_statements.title: Optimal Cluster Points Do Not Imply Full Convergence

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unique Optimal Cluster Point Upgrade
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Topology-based full-sequence convergence under boundedness and uniqueness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((x^k)\subset\mathbb R^n\) be bounded. If every cluster point of \((x^k)\) belongs to the singleton solution set \(X^*=\{x^*\}\), then \(x^k\to x^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded sequence converges when its only possible cluster point is the unique solution.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strong-Convexity Full-Sequence Upgrade
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative upgrade from objective-value convergence to convergence of all stability centers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) be \(\mu\)-strongly convex with \(\mu>0\), and let \(x^*\) be its minimizer. If \(f(x^k)\to f(x^*)\), then \[\|x^k-x^*\|^2\le \frac{2}{\mu}\bigl(f(x^k)-f(x^*)\bigr)\to0,\] and hence \(x^k\to x^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a strongly convex objective, convergence of objective values forces convergence of the entire center sequence to the unique minimizer.
knowledge_statements.title: Strong-Convexity Full-Sequence Upgrade
Full-Sequence Convergence Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions upgrading optimal cluster points to convergence of the complete stability-center sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((x^k)\subset\mathbb R^n\) be the stability-center sequence of a convergent convex bundle method, and suppose every cluster point lies in the nonempty solution set \(X^*\). Assume \((x^k)\) is quasi-Fejér with respect to \(X^*\): for every \(x^*\in X^*\),
\[
\|x^{k+1}-x^*\|^2\le\|x^k-x^*\|^2+e_k,
\qquad e_k\ge0,
\qquad \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}e_k<\infty.
\]
If \((x^k)\) has at least one cluster point, then the entire sequence converges to some \(\bar x\in X^*\). In particular, boundedness plus the displayed inequality and cluster-point optimality yield full-sequence convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Summable quasi-Fejér errors and optimality of all cluster points upgrade subsequential convergence to convergence of the entire bundle-center sequence.
assumptions_latex: \(X^*\) is nonempty and every cluster point of \((x^k)\) belongs to \(X^*\).
The displayed quasi-Fejér inequality holds with \(\sum_k e_k<\infty\).
The sequence has at least one cluster point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists \(\bar x\in X^*\) such that \(x^k\to\bar x\).

knowledge_statements.title: Exact-Oracle Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Baseline convergence guarantee for a finite-dimensional proximal bundle method with exact convex oracle information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, and convex with nonempty minimizer set \(X^*\). Consider a proximal bundle method whose oracle returns exact values and subgradients, whose cutting-plane model retains the current exactness cut, whose proximal subproblems are solved exactly, and whose serious-step test requires a fixed fraction of predicted decrease. If the proximal parameters remain in a compact subinterval of \((0,+\infty)\), then either the method terminates at \(x^k\) with \(0\in\partial f(x^k)\), or
\[
f(x^k)\to f^*:=\min_x f(x).
\]
Every cluster point of the stability centers lies in \(X^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under exact oracle information and standard proximal-bundle safeguards, termination certifies optimality; otherwise center values reach the optimum and cluster points are minimizers.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, closed, and convex with \(X^*\ne\varnothing\).
Oracle calls and proximal subproblem solutions are exact, and the current exactness cut is retained.
Proximal parameters are uniformly positive and bounded, with a fixed fractional serious-step test.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Either finite termination occurs at a minimizer, or \(f(x^k)\to f^*\) and every cluster point belongs to \(X^*\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem role fits exact-oracle convergence, but the claimed global alternative cannot be checked from the generic safeguards alone. A proximal bundle theorem normally fixes the model update, predicted-decrease definition, serious/null-step rules, stopping test, and aggregation requirements. Because no source identifies a variant for which exactly these hypotheses imply all stated conclusions, authoritative theorem-level evidence is required.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strongly Convex Distance Convergence under Vanishing Errors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative iterate convergence obtained from the vanishing-error certificate under strong convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose
\[0\le f(x_k)-f^*\le \eta_k+c\sup_{j\ge k}\varepsilon_j,\]
and \(f\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex on the closed convex feasible set \(C\), with \(\mu>0\). If \(x^*\) is its unique minimizer, then
\[\|x_k-x^*\|\le\sqrt{\frac{2}{\mu}\left(\eta_k+c\sup_{j\ge k}\varepsilon_j\right)}.\]
Consequently, \(\eta_k\to0\) and \(\varepsilon_k\to0\) imply \(x_k\to x^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong convexity converts the vanishing objective certificate into an explicit distance bound and full-sequence convergence.
assumptions_latex: The certified objective bound holds with \(\eta_k,\varepsilon_k\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Strongly Convex Distance Convergence under Vanishing Errors

assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a nonempty closed convex set, and \(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, with \(f^*:=\inf_{x\in C}f(x)\in\mathbb{R}\).
The bundle method produces \(x_k\in C\), \(\eta_k\ge 0\), \(\varepsilon_k\ge 0\), and \(c\ge 0\) satisfying \(0\le f(x_k)-f^*\le \eta_k+c\sup_{j\ge k}\varepsilon_j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x_k)\to f^*\), and every cluster point of \((x_k)\) is optimal.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sharpness of the Persistent-Error Floor
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elementary convex instance attaining the stated generic certified-error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix \(c>0\) and \(\bar\varepsilon>0\). Let \(C=[0,\infty)\), \(f(x)=x\), \(f^*=0\), and set \(x_k=c\bar\varepsilon\), \(\eta_k=0\), and \(\varepsilon_k=\bar\varepsilon\) for every \(k\). Then
\[f(x_k)-f^*=c\bar\varepsilon=\eta_k+c\sup_{j\ge k}\varepsilon_j\]
for every \(k\). Thus the constant in the certified inequality cannot be improved from that inequality alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linear convex objective and constant incumbents attain the persistent-error floor exactly.
knowledge_statements.title: Sharpness of the Persistent-Error Floor

assumptions_latex: \(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) is proper, closed, and convex, with \(f^*:=\inf_{x\in C}f(x)\in\mathbb{R}\).
The incumbents satisfy \(0\le f(x_k)-f^*\le \eta_k+c\sup_{j\ge k}\varepsilon_j\), where \(c>0\), \(\eta_k\ge0\), and \(\eta_k\to0\).
The real, nonnegative oracle-error sequence satisfies \(\limsup_{k\to\infty}\varepsilon_k=\bar\varepsilon>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\limsup_{k\to\infty}(f(x_k)-f^*)\le c\bar\varepsilon\); this bound alone does not imply \(f(x_k)\to f^*\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \[0\le f(x_k)-f^*\le \eta_k+c\sup_{j\ge k}\varepsilon_j,\] where \(c>0\), \(\eta_k\to0\), and \(\limsup_{k\to\infty}\varepsilon_k=\bar\varepsilon>0\). Then \[\limsup_{k\to\infty}\bigl(f(x_k)-f^*\bigr)\le c\bar\varepsilon.\] This guarantee alone does not imply \(f(x_k)\to f^*\).
