knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sharp Relative-Forcing Threshold
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact boundary of the relative oracle-accuracy rule for the stated contractive recurrence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(\eta_{k+1}\le q\eta_k+c\varepsilon_k\), where \(0<q<1\), \(c>0\), and \(\varepsilon_k\le\theta\eta_k\). Write \(\rho=q+c\theta\). If \(\theta=(1-q)/c\), the constant sequences \(\eta_k=1\) and \(\varepsilon_k=\theta\) satisfy the inequalities and do not converge to zero. If \(\theta>(1-q)/c\), the permitted sequences \(\eta_k=\rho^k\eta_0\) and \(\varepsilon_k=\theta\eta_k\) grow. Hence \(\theta<(1-q)/c\) is sharp for uniform contraction under these assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At the forcing threshold the recurrence may stagnate, and above it the permitted sequences may grow.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Uniform contraction follows from these assumptions precisely in the regime \(q+c\theta<1\).
knowledge_statements.title: Sharp Relative-Forcing Threshold

assumptions_latex: Nonnegative sequences \((\eta_k)\) and \((\varepsilon_k)\) satisfy \(\eta_{k+1}\le q\eta_k+c\varepsilon_k\), where \(0<q<1\) and \(c>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: With \(\rho:=q+c\theta<1\), \(\eta_k\le\rho^k\eta_0\) and \(\varepsilon_k\le\theta\rho^k\eta_0\), so both sequences converge to zero.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: relative forcing rule for an inexact contractive recurrence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient relative oracle-accuracy rule for a contractive bundle-certificate recurrence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let nonnegative sequences \((\eta_k)\) and \((\varepsilon_k)\) satisfy \[\eta_{k+1}\le q\eta_k+c\varepsilon_k,\qquad 0<q<1,\quad c>0.\] If \(\varepsilon_k\le\theta\eta_k\) with \(0\le\theta<(1-q)/c\), then, for \(\rho:=q+c\theta<1\), \[\eta_k\le\rho^k\eta_0,\qquad \varepsilon_k\le\theta\rho^k\eta_0.\] Consequently, \(\eta_k\to0\) and \(\varepsilon_k\to0\) geometrically.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relative oracle-tolerance rule is sufficient for geometric convergence when the resulting recurrence factor is strictly below one.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Call accounting for deterministic bundle iterations with at most one oracle evaluation per classified trial.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If initialization uses one oracle call, the method classifies \(N_s\) serious trials and \(N_n\) null trials, and each classified trial uses at most one new oracle call, then \[N_{\mathrm{orc}}\le1+N_s+N_n.\] Equality holds when initialization and every classified trial use exactly one oracle call and no additional oracle calls occur.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With at most one oracle call per classified trial, total calls are bounded by one initial call plus the serious- and null-step counts.
knowledge_statements.title: Oracle-Call Complexity

children.title: Serious-Step Complexity
children.top_down_role: Complexity contributions associated with accepted center progress.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform Progress Is Necessary for a Finite Serious-Step Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of serious-step counting from a finite initial objective gap alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any \(\Delta_0>0\), the sequence \(v_j=v^*+\Delta_0 2^{-j}\) is strictly decreasing, bounded below by \(v^*\), and satisfies \(v_0-v^*=\Delta_0\), yet it has infinitely many decreases. Thus a finite initial gap and monotonicity alone do not imply a finite serious-step count.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite initial gap permits infinitely many progressively smaller accepted decreases, so a quantitative progress condition is essential.
assumptions_latex: Only strict objective decrease and the lower bound \(v^*\) are imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A finite bound on the number of serious steps does not follow without a quantitative per-step progress condition.

notation.meaning: objective value after the j-th accepted step

knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Progress Is Necessary for a Finite Serious-Step Bound

assumptions_latex: At every serious step taken before an \(\epsilon\)-certificate is obtained, \(f(x_j)-f(x_{j+1})\ge\sigma\epsilon\), where \(\sigma>0\) and \(\epsilon>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The number \(N_s\) of such serious steps satisfies \(N_s\le\left\lfloor\Delta_0/(\sigma\epsilon)\right\rfloor\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: telescoping decrease bound conditional on uniform accepted progress
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional serious-step count obtained from uniform accepted decrease before termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose every serious step taken before an \(\epsilon\)-certificate is obtained satisfies \[f(x_j)-f(x_{j+1})\ge\sigma\epsilon,\qquad \sigma>0,\quad\epsilon>0,\] and suppose \(f(x_0)-f^*\le\Delta_0<+\infty\). Then the number \(N_s\) of such serious steps satisfies \[N_s\le\left\lfloor\frac{\Delta_0}{\sigma\epsilon}\right\rfloor.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform objective decrease at each nonterminal serious step yields a bound on the number of serious steps before the target certificate is reached.
knowledge_statements.title: Serious-Step Complexity

children.title: Null-Step Complexity
children.top_down_role: Complexity contributions associated with model-refinement iterations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Total Null-Step Bound Across Fixed-Center Phases
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Aggregation of a uniform per-phase geometric-refinement bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an execution has \(N_s\) serious steps and at most \(N_s+1\) fixed-center phases. In every phase, the model defect starts at no more than \(\bar D\), contracts after each null step by a common factor \(\rho\in(0,1)\), and the phase terminates when the defect is at most \(\delta\in(0,\bar D)\). Then \[N_n\le (N_s+1)\left\lceil\frac{\log(\bar D/\delta)}{\log(1/\rho)}\right\rceil.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniform logarithmic null-step bound per fixed-center phase yields a total bound multiplied by at most one plus the serious-step count.
assumptions_latex: There are \(N_s\) serious steps and at most \(N_s+1\) fixed-center phases.
Every phase starts with defect at most \(\bar D\), contracts it by \(\rho\in(0,1)\) per null step, and ends at \(\delta\in(0,\bar D)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Total Null-Step Bound Across Fixed-Center Phases

assumptions_latex: During one fixed-center phase, a nonnegative model defect \(D_\ell\) satisfies \(D_{\ell+1}\le\rho D_\ell\) after every null step, where \(0<\rho<1\).
\(D_0\le\bar D\), and the phase terminates once \(D_\ell\le\delta\), where \(0<\delta<\bar D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At most \(\left\lceil\log(\bar D/\delta)/\log(1/\rho)\right\rceil\) null steps are needed in the phase.

notation.meaning: Model defect after l null steps at the current center

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: geometric contraction count within a fixed-center refinement phase
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional per-phase null-step count under geometric model-defect contraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: During a fixed-center phase, suppose \(D_\ell\ge0\) satisfies \[D_{\ell+1}\le\rho D_\ell,\qquad 0<\rho<1,\] with \(D_0\le\bar D\), and suppose the phase terminates when \(D_\ell\le\delta\), where \(0<\delta<\bar D\). Then the phase requires at most \[\left\lceil\frac{\log(\bar D/\delta)}{\log(1/\rho)}\right\rceil\] null steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Geometric contraction of a model defect at a fixed center gives a logarithmic bound on the null steps needed to reach the termination threshold.
knowledge_statements.title: Null-Step Complexity

children.title: Step-Type Complexity Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Comparative balance between progress iterations and refinement iterations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: A Per-Phase Refinement Bound Is Necessary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of the phase-decomposition estimate combining serious and null steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A finite serious-step count \(N_s\) alone does not imply a finite null-step or total-work bound: an execution can have \(N_s=0\) and a single fixed-center phase containing arbitrarily many or infinitely many null steps. Therefore \(N_n\le (N_s+1)B_n(\epsilon)\) requires a finite uniform null-step bound \(B_n(\epsilon)\) for every fixed-center phase.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Serious-step control does not control refinement work unless each fixed-center phase has a finite uniform null-step bound.
assumptions_latex: No finite uniform null-step bound per fixed-center phase is assumed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No finite bound on \(N_n\), oracle calls, or master solves follows from \(N_s\) alone.

notation.meaning: uniform null-step bound per fixed-center phase

knowledge_statements.title: A Per-Phase Refinement Bound Is Necessary

assumptions_latex: An execution has \(N_s\) serious steps, creating at most \(N_s+1\) fixed-center phases.
Each fixed-center phase contains at most \(B_n(\epsilon)\) null steps.
Initialization uses one oracle call, and every classified serious or null trial uses at most one new oracle call and one master solve.

notation.meaning: Maximum null steps per fixed-center phase

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: phase decomposition of serious and null bundle steps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combines accepted-step and fixed-center refinement counts into total work under explicit initialization conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an execution has \(N_s\) serious steps and therefore at most \(N_s+1\) fixed-center phases, each containing at most \(B_n(\epsilon)\) null steps. Then \[N_n\le(N_s+1)B_n(\epsilon).\] If initialization uses one oracle call and every classified trial uses at most one new oracle call and one master solve, then \[N_{\mathrm{orc}}\le1+N_s+(N_s+1)B_n(\epsilon)\] and \[N_{\mathrm{mst}}\le N_s+(N_s+1)B_n(\epsilon).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The serious-step count controls the number of fixed-center phases, while the per-phase null-step bound controls refinement work within those phases.
knowledge_statements.title: Step-Type Complexity Tradeoffs

assumptions_latex: The \(k\)-th bundle master problem has \(n\) primal variables, retains \(p_k\) cuts, and is solved to tolerance \(\tau_k\).
Its selected solver uses at most \(I(n,p_k,\tau_k)\) arithmetic operations.
For the uniform bound, \(p_k\le\bar p\), \(\tau_k\ge\tau>0\), \(I\) is nondecreasing in its size arguments, and \(I(n,p,\tau)\) is nonincreasing in \(\tau\).

notation.meaning: Number of cuts in master problem k
Arithmetic cost bound for the selected master solver

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: solver-parametric accounting avoids assuming a particular quadratic-programming algorithm
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solver-parametric arithmetic bound for repeated bundle master problems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If master solve \(k\) costs at most \(I(n,p_k,\tau_k)\) arithmetic operations, then total master work satisfies \[W_{\mathrm{mst}}\le\sum_{k=1}^{N_{\mathrm{mst}}}I(n,p_k,\tau_k).\] If \(p_k\le\bar p\), \(\tau_k\ge\tau>0\), \(I\) is nondecreasing in its size arguments, and \(I(n,p,\tau)\) is nonincreasing in \(\tau\), then \[W_{\mathrm{mst}}\le N_{\mathrm{mst}}I(n,\bar p,\tau).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Total master-solve work is bounded by the sum of solver costs, with a uniform bound available under explicit size and tolerance monotonicity assumptions.
knowledge_statements.title: Master-Solve Complexity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Newest-Cut-Only Memory Can Destroy Kelley Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of arbitrary fixed-memory deletion without an aggregate or other convergence-preserving cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Minimize \(f(x)=|x|\) over \([-1,1]\). A Kelley scheme that retains and minimizes only the newest exact supporting cut, initialized at \(x_0=1\), generates \(x_{2k}=1\) and \(x_{2k+1}=-1\). Hence \(f(x_k)=1\) for every \(k\), although \(\min_{[-1,1]}f=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Keeping only the newest cut makes Kelley’s method cycle on the absolute-value problem, so a memory cap alone does not preserve convergence.
assumptions_latex: At each iteration only the newest exact supporting cut is retained and minimized.
knowledge_statements.title: Newest-Cut-Only Memory Can Destroy Kelley Convergence

assumptions_latex: \(m_{\mathcal B}(y):=\max_{i\in\mathcal B}a_i(y)\) is a cutting-plane model satisfying \(a_i(y)\le f(y)\) for all \(i\in\mathcal B\) and \(y\in C\).
\(\mathcal B'\subseteq\mathcal B\) is obtained by deleting cuts.
\(x\in C\), \(f(x)<+\infty\), and both model infima are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m_{\mathcal B'}\le m_{\mathcal B}\le f\) on \(C\), and \(f(x)-\inf_Cm_{\mathcal B'}\ge f(x)-\inf_Cm_{\mathcal B}\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: monotonicity of maximum-affine models under cut deletion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower-bound and model-gap monotonicity under deletion of valid bundle cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m_{\mathcal B}(y):=\max_{i\in\mathcal B}a_i(y)\), where \(a_i(y)\le f(y)\) for every \(i\in\mathcal B\) and \(y\in C\). If \(\mathcal B'\subseteq\mathcal B\), then \[m_{\mathcal B'}(y)\le m_{\mathcal B}(y)\le f(y)\qquad\text{for every }y\in C.\] Whenever the model infima are finite, every incumbent \(x\in C\) with finite value satisfies \[f(x)-\inf_{y\in C}m_{\mathcal B'}(y)\ge f(x)-\inf_{y\in C}m_{\mathcal B}(y).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deleting valid cuts cannot raise the model lower bound and therefore cannot decrease the resulting model-gap upper bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Memory-Accuracy Tradeoffs

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Global Minorization Is Essential
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of incumbent-minus-model certification without a globally valid lower model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=\mathbb R\), \(f(y)=y^2\), \(x=1\), and \(m(y)=1+(y-1)^2\). Then \(L=\inf_y m(y)=1\) and \(f(x)-L=0\), while \(f(x)-f^*=1\). Thus a zero or small model gap need not certify optimality when \(m\le f\) fails on the optimization domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A model with the wrong global orientation can report zero gap at a nonoptimal incumbent.
assumptions_latex: The global-minorization condition \(m(y)\le f(y)\) on \(C\) is omitted.

notation.meaning: candidate model that is not a global minorant

knowledge_statements.title: Global Minorization Is Essential

assumptions_latex: \(C\) is nonempty and \(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) has finite optimum \(f^*:=\inf_{y\in C}f(y)\).
The model \(m:C\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{-\infty\}\) satisfies \(m(y)\le f(y)\) for every \(y\in C\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: valid global lower model yields a directly checkable primal-gap bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global model lower-bound certificate for convex minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f^*:=\inf_{y\in C}f(y)\in\mathbb{R}\), and let \(m(y)\le f(y)\) for every \(y\in C\), with \(L:=\inf_{y\in C}m(y)\in\mathbb{R}\). For every \(x\in C\) with \(f(x)<+\infty\), \[0\le f(x)-f^*\le f(x)-L=:G_m(x).\] Consequently, \(G_m(x)\le\epsilon\) is an \(\epsilon\)-optimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The incumbent value minus the finite global lower-model value is a computable upper bound on objective suboptimality.
knowledge_statements.title: Model-Gap Certificates

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Support-Function Aggregate Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp aggregate-cut suboptimality bound, with the bounded-radius seed bound as a norm estimate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty and convex, let \(f:C\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be convex with finite infimum \(f^*\), and let \(\bar a(y)=\bar a(x)+\langle\bar g,y-x\rangle\le f(y)\) on \(C\). If \(x\in C\), \(f(x)<+\infty\), and \(\sup_{y\in C}\langle\bar g,x-y\rangle<+\infty\), then \[f(x)-f^*\le f(x)-\bar a(x)+\sup_{y\in C}\langle\bar g,x-y\rangle.\] The seed estimate follows when \(\|y-x\|\le R\) on \(C\), because the supremum is at most \(R\|\bar g\|_*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Aggregate-cut discrepancy plus the support function of feasible displacements gives the sharp domain-dependent gap certificate; the radius–dual-norm bound is its corollary.
knowledge_statements.title: Support-Function Aggregate Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Touching Aggregate-Cut Optimality Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact constrained optimality certificate from a touching aggregate affine minorant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let \(\bar a(y)=\beta+\langle\bar g,y\rangle\le f(y)\) on \(C\). If \(x\in C\), \(\bar a(x)=f(x)<+\infty\), and \(-\bar g\in N_C(x)\), then \(x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in C}f(y)\). For \(C=\mathbb R^n\), the normal condition is equivalent to \(\bar g=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A touching valid aggregate cut whose slope is balanced by the feasible-set normal certifies global optimality.

notation.meaning: convex normal cone to C at x

knowledge_statements.title: Touching Aggregate-Cut Optimality Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Aggregate Slope Alone Is Insufficient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessity of aggregate-cut discrepancy or touching in addition to slope information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=[-1,1]\), \(f(y)=y^2\), and \(\bar a(y)=-1\). The cut \(\bar a\) is a convex aggregate of the tangent cuts at \(-1\) and \(1\), and its slope is \(\bar g=0\). At \(x=1\), however, \(f(x)-f^*=1\). Thus a vanishing aggregate slope alone does not certify incumbent optimality when the aggregate cut does not touch the objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A flat valid aggregate cut may lie strictly below the objective, so zero aggregate slope alone is not an optimality certificate.
assumptions_latex: The aggregate cut is valid but need not touch \(f\) at the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.title: Aggregate Slope Alone Is Insufficient

assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty and convex, and \(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) is convex with \(f^*:=\inf_{y\in C}f(y)\in\mathbb{R}\).
For the incumbent \(x\in C\), \(\|y-x\|\le R\) for every \(y\in C\), where \(\|\cdot\|_*\) is the dual norm.

notation.meaning: Radius of the feasible set about the incumbent

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: convex aggregation preserves cutting-plane validity and yields a bounded-domain gap estimate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounded-domain certificate from a convex aggregate of valid subgradient cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g_i\in\partial f(x_i)\) and \(a_i(y):=f(x_i)+\langle g_i,y-x_i\rangle\) for \(i=1,\ldots,p\). For weights \(\lambda_i\ge0\) with \(\sum_{i=1}^p\lambda_i=1\), define \(\bar a:=\sum_{i=1}^p\lambda_i a_i\) and \(\bar g:=\sum_{i=1}^p\lambda_i g_i\). If \(x\in C\) and \(\|y-x\|\le R\) for every \(y\in C\), then \[f(x)-f^*\le f(x)-\bar a(x)+R\|\bar g\|_*.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a bounded feasible set, the aggregate-cut discrepancy plus the radius times the dual norm of the aggregate slope bounds objective suboptimality.
knowledge_statements.title: Aggregate-Subgradient Certificates

knowledge_statements.statement_title: No Domain-Free Objective Bound from the Proximal Residual
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of residual-only objective certification without a radius, growth condition, or other error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each \(L>0\), let \(f_L(z)=|z|/L\) on \(\mathbb R\), set \(m_L=f_L\), \(y_L=L^2\), choose \(t>0\), and let \(x_L=y_L+t/L\). Then \(r_L:=(x_L-y_L)/t=1/L\in\partial m_L(y_L)\), and \(y_L\) solves
\[\min_z\left\{m_L(z)+\frac{|z-x_L|^2}{2t}\right\}.\]
Nevertheless, \(\|r_L\|=1/L\to0\), while
\[f_L(y_L)-\min_z f_L(z)=L\to\infty.\]
Thus no universal \(\psi(a)\to0\) can ensure \(f(y)-f^*\le\psi(\|r\|)\) from this residual alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact proximal residual can tend to zero across convex problems while the objective gap diverges.
assumptions_latex: The model equals the proper closed convex objective.
knowledge_statements.title: No Domain-Free Objective Bound from the Proximal Residual

assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, and \(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) is proper, closed, and convex, with \(f^*:=\inf_{z\in C}f(z)\in\mathbb{R}\).
\(m:C\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) is a proper closed convex bundle model satisfying \(m(z)\le f(z)\) for every \(z\in C\).
For \(t>0\), \(y\) solves \(\min_{z\in C}\{m(z)+(2t)^{-1}\|z-x\|_2^2\}\), the standard convex optimality condition holds at \(y\), and \(r:=(x-y)/t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(z\in C\), \(f(z)\ge f(y)-\delta+\langle r,z-y\rangle\), and \(f(y)-f^*\le\delta+R\|r\|_2\).

notation.meaning: Model discrepancy at the trial point
Feasible-set radius about the trial point

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: proximal master optimality plus model discrepancy yields an approximate subgradient certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constrained proximal-master residual certificate on a bounded feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y\) solve \[\min_{z\in C}\left\{m(z)+\frac{1}{2t}\|z-x\|_2^2\right\},\qquad t>0,\] under the standard convex optimality condition, and define \(r:=(x-y)/t\) and \(\delta:=f(y)-m(y)\ge0\). If \(m(z)\le f(z)\) and \(\|z-y\|_2\le R\) for every \(z\in C\), then \[f(z)\ge f(y)-\delta+\langle r,z-y\rangle\qquad\text{for every }z\in C,\] and \[f(y)-f^*\le\delta+R\|r\|_2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex constrained proximal master problem, the model discrepancy and proximal residual give a bounded-domain suboptimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.title: Proximal-Residual Certificates
Primal-Dual Master Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Computable certificate for an unconstrained proximal bundle master and its simplex dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(b_i=f(y_i)+\langle g_i,x^c-y_i\rangle\), where \(g_i\in\partial f(y_i)\), and let \(t>0\). For primal-feasible \((s,r)\), satisfying \(b_i+\langle g_i,s\rangle\le r\) for every \(i\), and dual-feasible \(\lambda\ge0\) with \(\sum_i\lambda_i=1\), define
\[P(s,r)=r+\frac{\|s\|^2}{2t},\qquad D(\lambda)=\sum_i\lambda_i b_i-\frac{t}{2}\left\|\sum_i\lambda_i g_i\right\|^2.\]
Weak duality gives \(P(s,r)-D(\lambda)\ge0\). Hence a gap not exceeding \(\varepsilon\) certifies \(\varepsilon\)-optimality for both master problems; a zero gap certifies primal-dual optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any feasible primal step and simplex multiplier give a nonnegative computable gap. A gap at most epsilon certifies epsilon-optimality; zero gap certifies optimality.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is convex and finite at the bundle points.

notation.meaning: value of cut i at the prox-center
simplex vector of dual cut weights

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Master-Gap Residual Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact decomposition of the feasible proximal-master primal-dual gap into complementarity and stationarity residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define \(\bar g:=\sum_i\lambda_i g_i\) and \(\sigma_i:=r-b_i-\langle g_i,s\rangle\ge0\). Then
\[P(s,r)-D(\lambda)=\sum_i\lambda_i\sigma_i+\frac{1}{2t}\|s+t\bar g\|^2.\]
Consequently, zero gap is equivalent to \(s=-t\bar g\) and \(\lambda_i\sigma_i=0\) for every \(i\). A gap at most \(\varepsilon\) implies \(\|s+t\bar g\|\le\sqrt{2t\varepsilon}\) and \(\sum_i\lambda_i\sigma_i\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The feasible master gap is the sum of weighted complementarity slack and a squared stationarity residual.
knowledge_statements.title: Master-Gap Residual Decomposition

knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Programming Master Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Epigraph interface for minimizing a polyhedral cutting-plane model over a polyhedral trust region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\le d\}\) be a nonempty polyhedron and let \(m(x)=\max_{i\in I}\{a_i+\langle g_i,x\rangle\}\). The polyhedral master problem \(\min_{x\in X}m(x)\) is represented by the linear program
\[\min_{x,r}\ r\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax\le d,\qquad a_i+\langle g_i,x\rangle\le r\quad(i\in I).\]
The solver interface therefore passes \((A,d)\), the cut rows \((g_i,a_i)\), and optional bounds, and returns a feasible pair \((x,r)\), status information, and cut multipliers. Whenever an optimum exists, its \(x\)-component solves the original master and \(r=m(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A maximum of affine cuts over a polyhedron becomes an LP by introducing one epigraph variable and one inequality per cut.
assumptions_latex: The displayed master attains a finite optimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The epigraph LP and \(\min_{x\in X}m(x)\) have the same optimal value and optimizing \(x\)-components.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a finite nonempty set \(I\), a nonempty closed polyhedron \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), a prox-center \(x^c\in\mathbb R^n\), a parameter \(t>0\), and the affine model \(m(x)=\max_{i\in I}\{a_i+\langle g_i,x\rangle\}\), the proximal master
\[\min_{x\in X}\left\{m(x)+\frac{1}{2t}\|x-x^c\|^2\right\}\]
has the equivalent quadratic-programming interface
\[\min_{x,r}\left\{r+\frac{1}{2t}\|x-x^c\|^2: x\in X,\ a_i+\langle g_i,x\rangle\le r\ \text{for every }i\in I\right\}.\]
This convex QP has a unique optimal trial point \(x^*\). Because the objective is strictly increasing in \(r\), its optimal epigraph variable is also unique and satisfies \(r^*=m(x^*)\); optimal constraint multipliers need not be unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proximal maximum-of-affine-cuts master over a nonempty closed polyhedron is represented by a convex epigraph QP. Its optimal trial point and epigraph value are unique, although its multipliers may not be.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Proximal Epigraph-QP KKT Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient exact optimality certificate for a proximal cutting-plane QP over an explicitly represented polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X=\{x:Ax\le d\}\) and consider
\[\min_{x,r}\left\{r+\frac1{2t}\|x-x^c\|^2:Ax\le d,\ a_i+\langle g_i,x\rangle-r\le0\quad(i\in I)\right\}.\]
A feasible pair \((x^*,r^*)\) is optimal if and only if there exist \(\mu\ge0\) and \(\lambda\ge0\) satisfying
\[\frac{x^*-x^c}{t}+A^{\mathsf T}\mu+\sum_i\lambda_i g_i=0,\qquad \sum_i\lambda_i=1,\]
\[\mu_j(Ax^*-d)_j=0\quad(j),\qquad \lambda_i(a_i+\langle g_i,x^*\rangle-r^*)=0\quad(i).\]
These conditions certify the unique primal pair, although the certifying multipliers may be nonunique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feasibility, nonnegative multipliers, stationarity, cut-multiplier normalization, and complementary slackness exactly certify the proximal epigraph-QP solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x^*,r^*)\text{ is optimal}\iff\exists(\mu,\lambda)\ge0\text{ satisfying the displayed KKT system}.\)
knowledge_statements.title: Proximal Epigraph-QP KKT Certificate
Projection-Subproblem Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection interface for a polyhedral model epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(m(x)=\max_{i\in I}\{a_i+\langle g_i,x\rangle\}\), define its polyhedral epigraph \(E=\{(x,r):a_i+\langle g_i,x\rangle\le r\ \text{for all }i\}\). Given \((x^c,\rho)\), Euclidean projection onto \(E\) is the subproblem
\[\min_{x,r}\ \frac12\|x-x^c\|^2+\frac12(r-\rho)^2\quad\text{subject to}\quad a_i+\langle g_i,x\rangle\le r\ (i\in I).\]
The interface accepts the reference point and cut rows and returns the unique projection \((x^+,r^+)\), multipliers, and residuals. The projection variational inequality is \(\langle (x^c,\rho)-(x^+,r^+),(x,r)-(x^+,r^+)\rangle\le0\) for every \((x,r)\in E\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection onto a cutting-plane epigraph is a strongly convex QP whose unique solution satisfies the standard projection variational inequality.
assumptions_latex: The epigraph \(E\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed QP has the unique solution \(P_E(x^c,\rho)=(x^+,r^+)\) satisfying the projection variational inequality.

source_refs.locator: 2.6 Convex Polyhedra p. 95; 2.8 Quadratic Programming Theory p. 113

source_witnesses.locator: 2.6 Convex Polyhedra p. 95; 2.8 Quadratic Programming Theory p. 113

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Epigraph-Projection KKT Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient multiplier certificate for projection onto a finite cutting-plane epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[E=\{(x,r):a_i+\langle g_i,x\rangle-r\le0\quad(i\in I)\}.\]
A feasible pair \((x^+,r^+)\in E\) equals \(P_E(x^c,\rho)\) if and only if there exists \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^I\) such that
\[x^+-x^c+\sum_i\lambda_i g_i=0,\qquad r^+-\rho-\sum_i\lambda_i=0,\]
\[\lambda_i\bigl(a_i+\langle g_i,x^+\rangle-r^+\bigr)=0\quad(i\in I).\]
Equivalently,
\[(x^c-x^+,\rho-r^+)=\sum_i\lambda_i(g_i,-1)\in N_E(x^+,r^+).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal feasibility, nonnegative multipliers, stationarity, and complementary slackness exactly certify projection onto the cutting-plane epigraph.
assumptions_latex: \(a_i\in\mathbb R\) and \(g_i\in\mathbb R^n\) for every \(i\in I\).
knowledge_statements.title: Epigraph-Projection KKT Certificate

children.title: Primal Master Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Solver interfaces exposing the primal master representation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Primal Proximal-Master Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact solver-facing primal interface for the unconstrained proximal finite-cut master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a finite nonempty set \(I\), cut data \((b_i,g_i)\), a prox-center \(x^c\), and \(t>0\), solve
\[\min_{s,r}\left\{r+\frac{1}{2t}\|s\|^2: b_i+\langle g_i,s\rangle\le r\quad(i\in I)\right\}.\]
The interface returns the unique optimal pair \((s^*,r^*)\), the trial point \(x^+=x^c+s^*\), the regularized master value \(p^*=r^*+\|s^*\|^2/(2t)\), primal feasibility residuals, and solver status. At the exact solution,
\[r^*=\max_{i\in I}\{b_i+\langle g_i,s^*\rangle\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The primal interface solves the unconstrained proximal epigraph master and returns its unique step, epigraph value, trial point, regularized objective value, residuals, and status.
assumptions_latex: \(b_i\in\mathbb R\) and \(g_i\in\mathbb R^n\) for every \(i\in I\).

notation.meaning: value of cut i at the prox-center

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Primal Proximal-Master Interface
Primal Master Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical primal interface for an unconstrained proximal bundle master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input a prox-center \(x^c\), parameter \(t>0\), and cuts \((b_i,g_i)\) expressed at \(x^c\). Solve
\[\min_{s,r}\ r+\frac{1}{2t}\|s\|^2\quad\text{subject to}\quad b_i+\langle g_i,s\rangle\le r\quad(i\in I).\]
Return \(x^+=x^c+s^*\), the model value \(r^*\), the predicted decrease \(\max_i b_i-r^*\), primal feasibility residuals, and termination status. The interface declares an \(\varepsilon\)-accurate solution only when its reported lower bound \(L\) satisfies \(r^*+\|s^*\|^2/(2t)-L\le\varepsilon\) together with the prescribed feasibility tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The primal interface solves the epigraph proximal master and returns the trial point, model prediction, residuals, status, and an accuracy gap.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned trial point is \(x^+=x^c+s^*\), with accuracy measured against a valid master lower bound.

notation.meaning: value of cut i at the prox-center
valid lower bound on the primal master optimum

children.title: Dual Master Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Solver interfaces exposing the dual master representation.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Master Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simplex-QP dual interface for an unconstrained proximal bundle master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input cut values \(b_i\), subgradients \(g_i\), and \(t>0\). Solve the concave quadratic program
\[\max_{\lambda}\ \sum_{i\in I}\lambda_i b_i-\frac{t}{2}\left\|\sum_{i\in I}\lambda_i g_i\right\|^2\quad\text{subject to}\quad \lambda_i\ge0,\quad\sum_{i\in I}\lambda_i=1.\]
Return \(\lambda^*\), the aggregate subgradient \(\bar g=\sum_i\lambda_i^*g_i\), the aggregate cut value \(\bar b=\sum_i\lambda_i^*b_i\), and the recovered step \(s^*=-t\bar g\). The interface also reports simplex feasibility, stationarity residuals, objective value, and solver status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dual interface optimizes cut weights on the simplex and returns aggregate cut data plus the primal step recovered from the aggregate subgradient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An optimal dual weight vector recovers the primal step through \(s^*=-t\sum_i\lambda_i^*g_i\).

notation.meaning: aggregate cut value at the prox-center

source_refs.locator: 2.8 Quadratic Programming Theory p. 113

source_witnesses.locator: 2.8 Quadratic Programming Theory p. 113

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Invariant Optimal Dual Outputs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniqueness of aggregate solver outputs despite possible nonuniqueness of optimal cut weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Lambda^*\) be the optimal set of
\[\max_{\lambda\in\Delta_I}\left\{\sum_i\lambda_i b_i-\frac t2\left\|\sum_i\lambda_i g_i\right\|^2\right\},\qquad t>0.\]
For all \(\lambda,\lambda'\in\Lambda^*\),
\[\sum_i\lambda_i g_i=\sum_i\lambda'_i g_i,\qquad \sum_i\lambda_i b_i=\sum_i\lambda'_i b_i.\]
Thus the aggregate subgradient, aggregate cut value, recovered step, and optimal value are invariant, although the individual weight vector may be nonunique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimal cut weights can be nonunique, but every optimal weight vector produces the same aggregate subgradient, aggregate cut value, recovered step, and objective value.
knowledge_statements.title: Invariant Optimal Dual Outputs

children.title: Primal–Dual Master Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Structural correspondence between primal and dual master views.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Master Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong duality and recovery relations for the unconstrained proximal master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For finite \(I\) and \(t>0\), consider
\[p^*=\min_s\left\{\max_i(b_i+\langle g_i,s\rangle)+\frac{\|s\|^2}{2t}\right\}.\]
Its simplex dual satisfies
\[p^*=\max_{\lambda\ge0,\,\sum_i\lambda_i=1}\left\{\sum_i\lambda_i b_i-\frac{t}{2}\left\|\sum_i\lambda_i g_i\right\|^2\right\}.\]
If \(\lambda^*\) is dual-optimal, then \(s^*=-t\sum_i\lambda_i^*g_i\) is the unique primal step. Moreover, \(\lambda_i^*>0\) implies \(b_i+\langle g_i,s^*\rangle=\max_j\{b_j+\langle g_j,s^*\rangle\}\). Conversely, primal and dual feasible points satisfying these recovery and complementarity relations are jointly optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proximal cutting-plane master equals its simplex dual; optimal dual weights aggregate active cuts and recover the unique primal step.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Strong duality holds, with step recovery and complementary support on active cuts.

source_refs.locator: 2.8 Quadratic Programming Theory p. 113

source_witnesses.locator: 2.8 Quadratic Programming Theory p. 113

children.title: Cut Selection Criteria
children.top_down_role: Criteria governing which cuts enter or remain influential in the bundle.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Zero Dual Weight Is Not Global Redundancy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits the inference obtainable from one master multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For cuts \(\ell_1(x)=0\) and \(\ell_2(x)=x-1\), center \(c=0\), and any \(t\in(0,1)\), the proximal master is uniquely minimized at \(x^*=0\), where an optimal multiplier assigns zero weight to \(\ell_2\). Nevertheless \(\ell_2(x)>\ell_1(x)\) for every \(x>1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut with zero current dual weight can become model-defining elsewhere and is not thereby globally redundant.
knowledge_statements.title: Zero Dual Weight Is Not Global Redundancy

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Support-Preserving Cut Selection at a Proximal Master Solution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact preservation obtained by retaining the support of one optimal simplex multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For
\[\min_x\left\{\max_{i\in I}(a_i+\langle g_i,x\rangle)+\frac1{2t}\|x-c\|^2\right\},\]
let \(x^*\) be the minimizer and let \(\lambda^*\in\Delta_I\) be an optimal cut-weight vector satisfying complementarity. If \(R\subseteq I\) contains \(\operatorname{supp}\lambda^*\), then the retained-cut master has the same unique minimizer \(x^*\) and the same optimal value. Cuts outside that support may still affect the model away from \(x^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Retaining the support of one optimal multiplier preserves the current proximal-master solution and value, but not necessarily the whole model.
assumptions_latex: \lambda^*\text{ is an optimal simplex multiplier satisfying complementarity}.

notation.meaning: indices with positive optimal cut weight

knowledge_statements.title: Support-Preserving Cut Selection at a Proximal Master Solution
Cut Selection Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic admissibility criterion for retaining informative bundle cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At iteration \(k\), let \(m_k(x)=\max_{i\in I_k}\ell_i(x)\), let \(x^c_k\) be the center, and let \(x^{k+1}\) be the master trial point. A retained index set \(R_k\subseteq I_k\) satisfies the active-and-aggregate selection criterion when
\[\{i:\ell_i(x^{k+1})\ge m_k(x^{k+1})-\delta_k\}\cup\{i:\lambda_i^k\ge\theta_k\}\subseteq R_k,\]
where \(\delta_k,\theta_k\ge0\), and either every positive-weight cut is retained or its aggregate cut \(\bar\ell_k=\sum_i\lambda_i^k\ell_i\) is retained. The newest oracle cut is also required to belong to \(R_k\). This criterion preserves current near-active information and the dual aggregate represented by the master solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Retain the newest cut, near-active cuts, and materially weighted dual cuts, or retain one aggregate cut representing all positive dual weights.
assumptions_latex: \(\lambda^k\) is a dual-feasible vector for the current master.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected bundle contains the newest cut, all prescribed near-active cuts, and the current dual aggregate information.

source_refs.locator: 3.4.2 Methods of Linear Approximation p. 87

children.title: Cut Deletion Policies
children.top_down_role: Policies governing removal of cuts from finite-memory bundles.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polyhedral Redundancy Test for a Candidate Cut
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Computable certificate for deletion without model loss on a polyhedral working region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(R\) be a finite nonempty retained index set, let \(\ell_i(x)=a_i^{\mathsf T}x+b_i\), and let \(X\) be a nonempty polyhedron. A candidate cut \(\ell_d\) is redundant relative to \(R\) on \(X\) exactly when
\[\sup_{x\in X,\,s}\{\ell_d(x)-s:s\ge\ell_j(x)\ \forall j\in R\}\le0.\]
A positive finite optimum has an optimizer witnessing model loss; if the supremum is \(+\infty\), some feasible point also gives positive loss.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Redundancy of one cut on a polyhedral region is certified by an LP; failure supplies a point where deletion lowers the model.

notation.meaning: epigraph variable for the retained model

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Redundancy Test for a Candidate Cut

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Regionally Exact Cut Deletion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact mathematical condition for deleting cuts without changing a finite cutting-plane model on a declared region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(I\) be finite, let \(D\subsetneq I\), and set \(R=I\setminus D\ne\varnothing\). For affine cuts \(\ell_i\) and a nonempty region \(X\), deletion of \(D\) is model-exact on \(X\) if and only if
\[\ell_i(x)\le \max_{j\in R}\ell_j(x)\qquad\forall i\in D,\ \forall x\in X.\]
Equivalently, \(\max_{i\in I}\ell_i(x)=\max_{j\in R}\ell_j(x)\) for every \(x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deleting cuts is exact on a region precisely when every deleted cut is dominated there by the retained model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: m_R=m_I\text{ on }X\iff \ell_i\le m_R\text{ on }X\ \forall i\in D.

notation.meaning: region on which exactness is required

knowledge_statements.title: Regionally Exact Cut Deletion

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pointwise Inactivity Does Not Certify Safe Deletion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between inactivity at one point and redundancy on a working region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(X=[-1,1]\), retained cut \(\ell_1(x)=0\), and candidate cut \(\ell_2(x)=x-\tfrac12\), one has \(\ell_2(0)<\ell_1(0)\), but \(\ell_2(1)>\ell_1(1)\). Thus strict inactivity at one point does not imply redundancy on a region.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut inactive at the current point can still be essential elsewhere in the working region.
knowledge_statements.title: Pointwise Inactivity Does Not Certify Safe Deletion
Cut Deletion Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe deletion by model dominance, with protected recent and aggregate cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given cuts \(\{\ell_i:i\in I_k\}\), a working region \(X_k\), and protected set \(P_k\), delete only indices in \(D_k\subseteq I_k\setminus P_k\). A deletion is model-exact on \(X_k\) when every deleted cut obeys
\[\ell_i(x)\le\max_{j\in I_k\setminus D_k}\ell_j(x)\qquad\text{for all }x\in X_k.\]
Choose \(D_k\) subject to this test and the memory limit; protect the newest oracle cut and any required aggregate cut. Replace the model by \(m_{k+1}(x)=\max_{j\in I_k\setminus D_k}\ell_j(x)\). If the dominance tests hold, then \(m_{k+1}=m_k\) throughout \(X_k\); otherwise deletion is inexact and its model loss must be recorded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Delete only unprotected cuts dominated by retained cuts on the working region. Such deletion leaves the model unchanged there; other deletion incurs measurable model loss.
assumptions_latex: \(X_k\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is the declared working region.
The protected set contains the newest and required aggregate cuts.

notation.meaning: region on which model fidelity is tested
