children.title: Memory–Fidelity Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Model-fidelity consequences of selection pressure and deletion pressure.

assumptions_latex: \(I\) is finite and \(R\subseteq I\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Bundle truncation gives \(m_R(x)\le m_I(x)\) for every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) and a no-larger proximal-master infimum over \(X\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotonic loss of cutting-plane fidelity under bundle truncation.

source_refs.locator: 3.4.2 Methods of Linear Approximation p. 87

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(I\) be finite, let \(R\subseteq I\) be nonempty, and define \(m_I(x)=\max_{i\in I}\ell_i(x)\) and \(m_R(x)=\max_{i\in R}\ell_i(x)\), where every \(\ell_i:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is affine. Then
\[m_R(x)\le m_I(x)\qquad\text{for every }x\in\mathbb R^n.\]
Consequently, for every nonempty set \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), prox-center \(x^c\in\mathbb R^n\), and parameter \(t>0\), whenever both infima are finite,
\[\inf_{x\in X}\left\{m_R(x)+\frac{\|x-x^c\|^2}{2t}\right\}\le\inf_{x\in X}\left\{m_I(x)+\frac{\|x-x^c\|^2}{2t}\right\}.\]
Thus reducing memory cannot raise the retained-cut model or its proximal-master infimum. The pointwise fidelity loss relative to the full model is \(m_I(x)-m_R(x)\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Discarding cuts never raises the cutting-plane model or the infimum of its proximal master. The nonnegative pointwise difference between the full and retained-cut models measures the resulting fidelity loss.
knowledge_statements.title: Memory–Fidelity Tradeoffs

source_witnesses.locator: 3.4.2 Methods of Linear Approximation p. 87

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Small Pointwise Loss at the Old Trial Does Not Control the New Master
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of a single-point fidelity measurement to bound reoptimized behavior.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X=[0,1]\), \(q\equiv0\), \(m_I(x)=\max\{0,1-2x\}\), and \(m_R(x)=1-2x\). At the full-master minimizer \(x_I=1/2\), \(m_I(x_I)-m_R(x_I)=0\). Nevertheless
\[\inf_Xm_I=0,\qquad \inf_Xm_R=-1,\]
and the retained master is minimized at \(x_R=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zero model loss at one old minimizer can coexist with a different retained-master value and minimizer.
knowledge_statements.title: Small Pointwise Loss at the Old Trial Does Not Control the New Master

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform Model-Loss Bound Transfers to Master Values
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative value stability under uniformly bounded truncation error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(m_R\le m_I\) on a nonempty set \(X\), and suppose
\[0\le m_I(x)-m_R(x)\le\delta\qquad\forall x\in X.\]
For any common regularizer \(q:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), if
\[v_I=\inf_{x\in X}\{m_I(x)+q(x)\},\qquad v_R=\inf_{x\in X}\{m_R(x)+q(x)\}\]
are finite, then \(0\le v_I-v_R\le\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniform truncation error of at most delta changes the regularized master value by at most delta.

notation.meaning: common master regularizer or indicator term

knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Model-Loss Bound Transfers to Master Values

children.title: Cut Aggregation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Memory regimes based on compressed retention of cut information.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex-Combination Cut Aggregation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compression of selected valid affine cuts into one normalized aggregate minorant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let J be nonempty, let \ell_i\le f be affine for i\in J, and choose \lambda_i\ge0 with \sum_{i\in J}\lambda_i=1. Define \bar\ell=\sum_{i\in J}\lambda_i\ell_i. Then \bar\ell(x)\le\max_{i\in J}\ell_i(x)\le f(x) for every x. Replacing the cuts in J by \bar\ell therefore preserves global lower-model validity but may weaken the maximum-of-cuts model. Exact preservation of a particular master value or stationarity requires master-optimal weights and the corresponding aggregate-mass transfer and is not implied by validity alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replace selected valid cuts by a normalized convex combination. The aggregate is still a valid lower cut, although it can weaken the model; master information is preserved only under additional optimal-weight conditions.
assumptions_latex: Each \(\ell_i\) is an affine global minorant of \(f\).
knowledge_statements.title: Convex-Combination Cut Aggregation
Cut Aggregation Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compression of selected affine minorants into one dual-weighted aggregate cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f\) be convex and let affine cuts satisfy \(\ell_i(x)\le f(x)\) for all \(x\). Choose a nonempty aggregation set \(J\) and weights \(\lambda_i\ge0\) with \(\sum_{i\in J}\lambda_i=1\), preferably the current master multipliers. Form
\[\bar\ell(x)=\sum_{i\in J}\lambda_i\ell_i(x).\]
Replace the cuts indexed by \(J\) with \(\bar\ell\), while retaining the newest cut and any required active cuts. Then \(\bar\ell(x)\le f(x)\) and \(\bar\ell(x)\le\max_{i\in J}\ell_i(x)\) for every \(x\). Thus aggregation preserves validity but may weaken the model; multiplier-based aggregation preserves the current dual combination exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replace several valid cuts by their convex combination. The aggregate remains a valid lower cut but can weaken the pointwise maximum model.
assumptions_latex: Each \(\ell_i\) is an affine global minorant of \(f\).
The aggregation weights form a simplex vector.

source_refs.locator: 3.4.2 Methods of Linear Approximation p. 87

source_witnesses.locator: 3.4.2 Methods of Linear Approximation p. 87

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A convex combination of valid minorants is indeed a valid minorant and lies below their pointwise maximum. However, the claim that multiplier-based aggregation preserves the current dual combination exactly requires additional conditions concerning the total multiplier mass on the aggregated subset and its representation in the reduced dual. The generic cited section does not support that algorithmic claim, so a bundle-aggregation source is required.

children.title: Bundle Resetting Regimes
children.top_down_role: Memory regimes based on partial or complete bundle reconstruction.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Valid Bundle Reset by Retained-Cut Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bundle reconstruction by retaining a nonempty selected collection of certified affine minorants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let B_k^+ be the finite bundle after any fresh cut has been added, let B_{k+1}\subseteq B_k^+ be nonempty, and define m_k^+(x)=\max_{\ell\in B_k^+}\ell(x) and m_{k+1}(x)=\max_{\ell\in B_{k+1}}\ell(x). If every \ell\in B_k^+ satisfies \ell\le f, then m_{k+1}(x)\le m_k^+(x)\le f(x) for every x. Thus a reset may discard certified cuts and rebuild the master from the retained collection, but it cannot claim preservation of the discarded model information without an additional invariant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reset by selecting a nonempty subset of the augmented valid bundle and rebuilding the master. The reset model remains a lower model but can be weaker than the pre-reset augmented model.
assumptions_latex: Every \(\ell\in B_k^+\) is an affine global minorant of \(f\).

notation.meaning: pre-reset bundle after adding any fresh cut
pre-reset augmented and post-reset maximum-of-cuts models

knowledge_statements.title: Valid Bundle Reset by Retained-Cut Selection
Bundle Resetting Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Controlled bundle restart retaining a fresh oracle cut and optional historical aggregate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At a reset iteration \(k\), obtain a fresh oracle pair \((f(y_k),g_k)\) with \(g_k\in\partial f(y_k)\), and define \(\ell_k(x)=f(y_k)+\langle g_k,x-y_k\rangle\). If historical dual weights are available, also form a valid aggregate cut \(\bar\ell_k\). Replace the bundle by either
\[B_{k+1}=\{\ell_k\}\qquad\text{or}\qquad B_{k+1}=\{\ell_k,\bar\ell_k\}.\]
Rebuild the master, recompute its primal-dual residuals, and continue only if the new master is feasible and numerically acceptable. Convexity guarantees every retained cut minorizes \(f\); the reset reduces memory but generally lowers the model relative to the pre-reset bundle.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restart with the newest oracle cut, optionally retaining one historical aggregate. Rebuild and validate the master before continuing; validity survives although fidelity may decrease.
assumptions_latex: Any retained aggregate is a convex combination of valid historical cuts.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reset bundle defines a valid lower model of \(f\), with reduced memory and possibly reduced fidelity.

source_refs.locator: 3.4.2 Methods of Linear Approximation p. 87

source_witnesses.locator: 3.4.2 Methods of Linear Approximation p. 87

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The retained fresh and aggregate cuts remain valid minorants, but the assertion that the reset model is lower than the pre-reset model is not justified unless the fresh cut is first included in a clearly defined pre-reset augmented bundle. The rebuild, acceptance, and optional-history policy also lacks support from the cited generic source. A bundle-resetting source and a precise pre-reset comparison set are required.

children.title: Reset-versus-Aggregation Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Operational boundaries separating compressed retention from bundle reconstruction.

assumptions_latex: \(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\) is proper convex on a nonempty closed convex set \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\).
The current bundle model is \(m(x)=\max_{i\in I}\{a_i+g_i^{\mathsf T}x\}\leq f(x)\), and an aggregate cut \(\bar a+\bar g^{\mathsf T}x\) is a convex combination of retained cuts.
The master problem has a proximal or trust-region stabilization centered at \(c\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Aggregation is admissible only while the aggregate cut is globally valid and preserves the master information required by the acceptance and stopping tests; otherwise a reset is required.
review_flags: No supplied locator directly states the aggregation-reset boundary or its numerical safeguards.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary for replacing bundle cuts by an aggregate versus discarding bundle memory.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(J\subseteq I\), let \(\lambda_i\geq0\) satisfy \(\sum_{i\in J}\lambda_i=1\), and define \(\bar g=\sum_{i\in J}\lambda_i g_i\) and \(\bar a=\sum_{i\in J}\lambda_i a_i\). Aggregation may replace the cuts in \(J\) when \(\bar a+\bar g^{\mathsf T}x\leq f(x)\) for every \(x\in C\), the resulting master remains feasible and bounded, and every quantity used in acceptance or termination remains reconstructible. A reset is required when cut validity cannot be certified, the center or stabilization geometry changes incompatibly, the master becomes numerically unreliable, or the retained information no longer supplies a certified lower model. Resetting removes suspect cuts and rebuilds the model from newly validated oracle records.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Aggregate only when validity, master well-posedness, and required certificates are preserved; reset when these properties cannot be certified.
knowledge_statements.title: Reset-versus-Aggregation Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the leaf, but the asserted reset requirements and certificate-preservation policy are algorithm-dependent and have no cited source. A bundle-method source directly addressing aggregation, resetting, and stabilization changes is required.

assumptions_latex: A linear master problem \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}z:A z=b,\ z\geq0\}\) has been solved with basis \(B\).
The next master changes only coefficients, bounds, or rows identified by the bundle update.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Basis reuse is valid as a warm start, but optimality may be declared only after feasibility and reduced-cost conditions are rechecked for the updated master.
review_flags: Locator supports linear and polyhedral master machinery but not bundle-specific reuse policy.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Warm-start validity for sequential linear cutting-plane masters.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 4. Pivoting Methods p. 225

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the updated master \(\min\{(c^{+})^{\mathsf T}z:A^{+}z=b^{+},\ z\geq0\}\), retain the old basis indices whenever the corresponding square matrix \(B^{+}\) is nonsingular. Compute the basic candidate \(z_{B}^{+}=(B^{+})^{-1}b^{+}\) and updated reduced costs \(r_{N}^{+}=c_{N}^{+}-(A_{N}^{+})^{\mathsf T}(B^{+})^{-\mathsf T}c_{B}^{+}\). The basis certifies optimality only if \(z_B^{+}\geq0\) and \(r_N^{+}\geq0\) under the minimization convention. If either test fails, the retained basis is merely an initial basis for primal, dual, or crossover pivots; singularity requires refactorization or basis replacement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reuse a nonsingular old basis as a warm start, then recompute feasibility and reduced costs before accepting it as optimal.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Master Basis Reuse

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 4. Pivoting Methods p. 225

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonsingularity Alone Does Not Validate a Reused Basis
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp distinction between algebraic basis reuse and an optimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A nonsingular reused basis need be neither primal feasible nor dual feasible for the updated master. For a one-variable standard-form problem with basis matrix \(B=[1]\), changing the right-hand side from \(b=1\) to \(b^+=-1\) leaves \(B\) nonsingular but gives \(z_B^+=-1<0\). Independently, an objective or nonbasic-column update can make an updated reduced cost negative. Thus nonsingularity certifies only that a basic candidate can be computed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An invertible old basis is only an algebraic warm start; updated primal and dual conditions must still be checked.
assumptions_latex: B\text{ is a square nonsingular retained basis}.
The updated master may change its right-hand side, objective, or nonbasic columns.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonsingularity Alone Does Not Validate a Reused Basis

assumptions_latex: The quadratic master is convex: \(\min_{z}\{\tfrac12 z^{\mathsf T}Hz+q^{\mathsf T}z:A z\leq b\}\) with \(H\succeq0\).
A previous solution and active set \((z,W)\) are available, and the updated master has compatible variables and constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The old active set is reusable as a working-set initialization; it certifies the updated solution only after the updated KKT conditions are satisfied.
review_flags: Locator supports convex quadratic programming theory but not bundle-specific active-set reuse.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Warm starts for sequential convex quadratic bundle masters.

source_refs.locator: 2.8 Quadratic Programming Theory p. 113

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For updated data \((H^{+},q^{+},A^{+},b^{+})\), retain each old index in \(W\) whose corresponding updated constraint exists, and use the resulting set as the initial equality-constrained working set. Reuse certifies an updated point \(z^{+}\) only if there is \(\lambda^{+}\geq0\) satisfying \(H^{+}z^{+}+q^{+}+(A^{+})^{\mathsf T}\lambda^{+}=0\), \(A^{+}z^{+}\leq b^{+}\), and \(\lambda_i^{+}((A_i^{+})^{\mathsf T}z^{+}-b_i^{+})=0\) for every constraint. Otherwise constraints with negative multipliers are eligible to leave and violated constraints to enter; ill-conditioned working-set systems must be refactorized or regularized.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Retain the prior active set as an initialization, but accept it only after all updated KKT conditions pass.
knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic-Master Active-Set Reuse

source_witnesses.locator: 2.8 Quadratic Programming Theory p. 113

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bordered Factorization Reuse for Quadratic Masters
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Factorization reuse when successive quadratic-master working sets differ by few constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let K_W=\begin{bmatrix}H&A_W^{\mathsf T}\\A_W&0\end{bmatrix} be nonsingular. If H is unchanged and W^+ differs from W by r constraint additions or deletions, a factorization of K_W may be transformed by bordered updates or downdates to solve the W^+ equality-constrained subproblem. For dense factors of order N, r transformations require O(rN^2) arithmetic rather than O(N^3) for fresh factorization. Updated factors must pass rank or inertia checks and residual tests; otherwise the system must be stably refactorized or regularized, with the resulting candidate verified against the unregularized updated KKT conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Update the old KKT factorization when few working constraints change, but refactorize whenever stability or residual checks fail.
assumptions_latex: H is unchanged and W^+ differs from W by r constraint additions or deletions.
Dense direct factors are used, and N denotes the KKT-system order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Stable bordered transformations reuse the old factorization in O(rN^2) work, subject to verification of the updated KKT system.
knowledge_statements.title: Bordered Factorization Reuse for Quadratic Masters

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Objective Translation Changes Max-Norm Scaled Gaps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparability boundary for the normalization \(\max\{1,|U|,|L|\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For certified bounds \(L\le f^*\le U\), set \(\gamma=(U-L)/\max\{1,|U|,|L|\}\). Adding a constant \(K\ge0\) to an instance with \((U,L)=(1,0)\) gives \((U_K,L_K)=(K+1,K)\). The absolute gap remains one, whereas \[\gamma_0=1,\qquad \gamma_K=\frac{1}{K+1}.\] Thus this normalization is not invariant under objective translation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding a constant to the objective can make the max-norm scaled gap arbitrarily small while leaving the absolute certified gap unchanged.
assumptions_latex: \(L\le f^*\le U\) are certified objective bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Scaled-gap values are comparable across runs only when the objective origin and normalization convention are fixed.

notation.meaning: upper-minus-lower gap divided by the max-norm scale

knowledge_statements.title: Objective Translation Changes Max-Norm Scaled Gaps

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Positive-Rescaling Invariance Under a Homogeneous Scale
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unit-change behavior on bound pairs whose declared normalization is positive and homogeneous along positive rays.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\subseteq\mathbb R^2\setminus\{(0,0)\}\) be closed under positive rescaling, let \(s:D\to(0,\infty)\), and define \(\gamma_s(U,L)=(U-L)/s(U,L)\). If \(s(aU,aL)=a\,s(U,L)\) whenever \((U,L)\in D\) and \(a>0\), then \[\gamma_s(aU,aL)=\gamma_s(U,L).\] Conversely, for a pair with \(U\ne L\), invariance of \(\gamma_s\) along its positive ray implies this homogeneity of \(s\) along that ray.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive homogeneous normalization preserves the scaled gap under positive changes of objective units; away from zero numerator, that homogeneity is also necessary along each ray.
assumptions_latex: \(D\subseteq\mathbb R^2\setminus\{(0,0)\}\) is closed under multiplication by positive scalars.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\gamma_s(aU,aL)=\gamma_s(U,L)\) for every admissible \((U,L)\) and \(a>0\); when \(U\ne L\), the converse holds along that positive ray.

notation.meaning: gap normalized by the declared scale s

knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Rescaling Invariance Under a Homogeneous Scale

assumptions_latex: At center \(c\in C\), the algorithm has an upper value \(U=f(c)\) and a certified lower bound \(L\leq f^*:=\inf_{x\in C}f(x)\).
A scale \(s(U,L)>0\) is fixed, for example \(s(U,L)=\max\{1,|U|,|L|\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The scaled gap \(\gamma=(U-L)/s(U,L)\) is nonnegative and yields the certificate \(f(c)-f^*\leq \gamma s(U,L)\).

notation.meaning: Certified upper and lower objective bounds

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports this normalization convention.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relative diagnostic based on certified primal and model bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(G=U-L\) and \(\gamma=G/s(U,L)\). Since \(L\leq f^*\leq U\), one has \(G\geq0\) and \(0\leq f(c)-f^*\leq G=\gamma s(U,L)\). Thus \(\gamma\leq\tau\) certifies \(f(c)-f^*\leq\tau s(U,L)\). The diagnostic is valid only when \(L\) remains a rigorous lower bound for the original problem and \(U\) is computed from a feasible point. A negative computed gap, a nonpositive scale, or a lower bound produced solely by an inexact or invalid model is a diagnostic failure rather than evidence of optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalize a certified upper-minus-lower bound; a small scaled gap bounds suboptimality only when both bounds and the scale are valid.
knowledge_statements.title: Scaled-Gap Diagnostics

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind fits the leaf and the bound follows from certified upper and lower bounds, but the selected scaling convention and its diagnostic interpretation have no cited source. A source specifying this normalization or a standard-field rationale is required.

assumptions_latex: Each oracle record \((x_i,f_i,g_i)\) is claimed to satisfy \(g_i\in\partial f(x_i)\) for a convex function \(f\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Model consistency requires interpolation at recorded points and global minorization; violations identify incompatible records or implementation error.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-oracle consistency checks for a convex cutting-plane model.

source_refs.locator: 3.4.2 Methods of Linear Approximation p. 87

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A finite exact-oracle record is model-consistent only if \(f_j\geq f_i+g_i^{\mathsf T}(x_j-x_i)\) for every pair \(i,j\). Under valid subgradient records, every cut satisfies \(f_i+g_i^{\mathsf T}(x-x_i)\leq f(x)\) for all \(x\) in the domain, hence \(m(x)\leq f(x)\), and the cut generated at \(x_i\) gives \(m(x_i)=f_i\). A pairwise inequality violation proves that the stored exact records cannot all arise from the asserted convex function. A failure of interpolation or minorization after otherwise valid records indicates an error in cut construction, scaling, indexing, or evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Check all cross-record subgradient inequalities, global model minorization, and interpolation at sampled points; any violation signals inconsistent data or construction.
knowledge_statements.title: Model-Consistency Diagnostics

source_witnesses.locator: 3.4.2 Methods of Linear Approximation p. 87

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Convex-Interpolation Equivalence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite consistency criterion for stored convex values and proposed subgradients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For finite data \(\{(x_i,f_i,g_i)\}_{i\in I}\), the following are equivalent:
\[(1)\quad \exists F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\text{ finite and convex with }F(x_i)=f_i\text{ and }g_i\in\partial F(x_i)\quad\forall i;\]
\[(2)\quad f_j\ge f_i+\langle g_i,x_j-x_i\rangle\quad\forall i,j.\]
When (2) holds,
\[F_0(x)=\max_{i\in I}\{f_i+\langle g_i,x-x_i\rangle\}\]
satisfies \(F_0(x_i)=f_i\) and \(g_i\in\partial F_0(x_i)\) for every \(i\). Thus a violated pairwise inequality is an exact inconsistency certificate, while satisfaction of all inequalities supplies an explicit consistent convex model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pairwise subgradient inequalities are necessary and sufficient for finite convex interpolation, with the maximum of stored affine cuts providing an explicit interpolant.
assumptions_latex: \(x_i,g_i\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(f_i\in\mathbb R\) for every \(i\in I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists F\text{ convex interpolating }(x_i,f_i,g_i)\iff f_j\ge f_i+\langle g_i,x_j-x_i\rangle\quad\forall i,j.\)
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Convex-Interpolation Equivalence

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Stored-Point Tests Do Not Certify a Global Oracle Inequality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-sampling limitation of pairwise inexact-oracle diagnostics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) satisfy \(f(y)=0\), and let the only stored record be \((x_1,\widetilde f_1,g_1,\varepsilon_1)=(0,0,1,0)\). Every pairwise stored-record comparison is the self-comparison \(0\le 0\). Nevertheless, the advertised global cut inequality would require \[0=f(y)\ge y\qquad\text{for every }y\in\mathbb R,\] which fails whenever \(y>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A false global oracle cut can pass every pairwise check on a finite stored set.
assumptions_latex: The stored set consists only of \((x_1,\widetilde f_1,g_1,\varepsilon_1)=(0,0,1,0)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Passing all stored-point pairwise tests does not imply the global inexact-oracle inequality.

notation.meaning: reported value, slope, and cut allowance at query i

knowledge_statements.title: Stored-Point Tests Do Not Certify a Global Oracle Inequality

assumptions_latex: At query \(x_i\), an inexact convex oracle returns \((\tilde f_i,g_i,\varepsilon_i)\) with \(\varepsilon_i\geq0\).
The intended guarantee is \(f(y)\geq\tilde f_i+g_i^{\mathsf T}(y-x_i)-\varepsilon_i\) for every \(y\in C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The adjusted cuts are mutually testable on sampled points; observed violations exceeding declared error allowances refute the oracle specification.
review_flags: No supplied locator fixes the intended inexact-oracle convention.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagnostics for an additive-error inexact first-order oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every stored pair \(i,j\), compute \(r_{ij}=\tilde f_i+g_i^{\mathsf T}(x_j-x_i)-\varepsilon_i-	ilde f_j\). If reported values are exact evaluations, oracle consistency requires \(r_{ij}\leq0\). If values additionally satisfy \(|\tilde f_j-f(x_j)|\leq\delta_j\), the necessary sampled-point test becomes \(r_{ij}\leq\delta_j\). The diagnostic must also verify \(\varepsilon_i\geq0\), finiteness of all returned quantities, and compliance with any prescribed error schedule. A residual beyond the declared allowance is evidence that at least one oracle record, error estimate, or stored query is incorrect; passing finitely many sampled tests does not establish the global oracle inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compare each adjusted cut with other sampled values and declared tolerances; excess residuals disprove the advertised oracle accuracy.
knowledge_statements.title: Oracle-Accuracy Diagnostics

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the diagnostic leaf, but the exact residual allowance depends on the chosen inexact-oracle convention. No source is supplied for the stated value-error and cut-error accounting, so the mathematical version cannot yet be accepted.

assumptions_latex: The exact master optimum is \(v^*=\inf_{x\in D}\Phi(x)\), where \(\Phi\) is a convex master objective on closed convex \(D\).
A solver returns feasible \(\hat x\in D\), a lower bound \(d\leq v^*\), and primal value \(p=\Phi(\hat x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The master solve is certified to absolute accuracy \(p-d\), and it meets tolerance \(\eta\) exactly when feasibility and \(p-d\leq\eta\) are verified.
review_flags: The locator supports convex quadratic dual bounds; solver-specific residual rules remain unspecified.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-dual accuracy certificate for a convex master problem.

source_refs.locator: 2.8 Quadratic Programming Theory p. 113

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Weak duality and feasibility give \(d\leq v^*\leq p\), hence \(0\leq p-v^*\leq p-d\). The returned master point is therefore \(\eta\)-optimal when \(\hat x\in D\), \(d\) is a rigorously valid dual or relaxation bound, and \(p-d\leq\eta\). A reported solver status alone is insufficient: the diagnostic must independently check primal feasibility to its stated tolerance, dual-bound validity, finiteness, and consistency of objective scaling. When only residual norms are available, they constitute a master-accuracy certificate only if a stated error bound converts those residuals into an objective-gap bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use feasible primal and valid dual bounds to certify master error; solver status or uncalibrated residuals alone do not suffice.
knowledge_statements.title: Master-Solver Accuracy Diagnostics

source_witnesses.locator: 2.8 Quadratic Programming Theory p. 113

children.title: Numerical Stopping Criteria
children.top_down_role: Numerically interpretable criteria used to support termination decisions.

assumptions_latex: A feasible center \(c\in C\) has upper value \(U=f(c)\), and the model-master computation supplies a certified lower bound \(L\leq f^*\).
Known allowances \(e_{m or}\geq0\) and \(e_{m ms}\geq0\) bound oracle and master-solver contributions not already included in \(L\).
User tolerances satisfy \(\tau_{m abs},\tau_{m rel}\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Termination certifies the displayed mixed absolute-relative bound only after model, oracle, and master-solver diagnostics have passed.
review_flags: No supplied locator directly states this composite numerical stopping rule.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composite termination certificate with explicit numerical error budgets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S=\max\{1,|U|,|L|\}\). Stop only if the center is feasible, all retained cuts satisfy their declared validity convention, the master lower bound is certified, and \[ U-L+e_{m or}+e_{m ms}\leq\tau_{m abs}+	au_{m rel}S. \] Under these conditions, \[ 0\leq f(c)-f^*\leq U-L+e_{m or}+e_{m ms}\leq\tau_{m abs}+	au_{m rel}S. \] If the error allowances are already incorporated into \(L\), they must not be added again. Failure of any feasibility, cut-integrity, oracle-accuracy, or master-accuracy diagnostic blocks certified termination even when the raw model gap is small.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stop only when a certified gap plus unaccounted numerical errors meets tolerance and every supporting diagnostic passes.
knowledge_statements.title: Numerical Stopping Criteria

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind fits numerical stopping criteria, but the composite error budget is convention-dependent and unsourced. In particular, whether oracle and master errors belong outside the bound or are already absorbed into the certified lower bound must be fixed by a cited convergence or implementation framework.

children.title: Premature-Termination Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Diagnostic boundaries where apparent numerical progress does not justify stopping.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Zero Reported Gap Without an Optimality Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit failures caused by an invalid lower bound or an infeasible reported incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R}x^2\), take \(\hat x=1\), \(\hat U=f(\hat x)=1\), and the invalid claimed lower bound \(\hat L=1\). Then \(\hat U-\hat L=0\), while \(f(\hat x)-f^*=1\). For \(\min\{x^2:x\geq1\}\), take the infeasible point \(\hat x=0\) and report \(\hat U=\hat L=0\). The reported gap is again zero, but \(\hat x\) is not an admissible incumbent and \(f^*=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero reported gap can accompany positive suboptimality when the lower bound is invalid or fail to certify any incumbent when the reported upper point is infeasible.
assumptions_latex: A stopping implementation accepts \((\hat U,\hat L)\) without independently certifying upper- and lower-bound validity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \hat U-\hat L=0\ \not\Rightarrow\ \text{certified optimality unless }\hat U\text{ is a feasible objective value and }\hat L\leq f^*.
knowledge_statements.title: Zero Reported Gap Without an Optimality Certificate

assumptions_latex: A stopping rule uses a computed upper value \(\hat U\), model bound \(\hat L\), and reported gap \(\hat G=\hat U-\hat L\).
The true optimum is \(f^*\), but feasibility, cut validity, oracle error, or master accuracy may be uncertified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A small computed gap does not certify near-optimality when any bound-defining invariant is absent or its unaccounted error is comparable to the tolerance.
review_flags: No supplied locator directly treats composite premature-termination boundaries.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions under which a numerically small model gap is not an optimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Premature termination is possible whenever \(\hat U<f(\hat c)\) because \(\hat c\) is infeasible or inaccurately evaluated, whenever \(\hat L>f^*\) because the model contains an invalid cut or the master lower bound is inexact, or whenever omitted oracle and solver errors exceed the stopping margin. In any such case, \(\hat G\leq	au\) does not imply \(f(\hat c)-f^*\leq	au\). The boundary is quantitative: if verified errors give \(f(\hat c)\leq\hat U+e_U\) and \(f^*\geq\hat L-e_L\), only \(\hat G+e_U+e_L\) bounds suboptimality. Termination before this corrected quantity meets tolerance is uncertified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tiny reported gap is unsafe if feasibility, lower-bound validity, or omitted errors are unverified; use the corrected gap instead.
knowledge_statements.title: Premature-Termination Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the leaf, and the corrected-gap algebra is coherent. However, no source supports the composite feasibility, cut-validity, oracle-error, and master-error boundary, so the reliability claim remains unsourced.

assumptions_latex: The objective \(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\) is convex on a convex set \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\).
A purported cut at \(x_i\in C\) is \(\ell_i(x)=\alpha_i+g_i^{\mathsf T}(x-x_i)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The cut is invalid precisely when it exceeds \(f\) somewhere in \(C\); including it can destroy the model lower-bound certificate.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact boundary between valid affine minorants and invalid cuts.

source_refs.locator: 3.4.2 Methods of Linear Approximation p. 87

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The affine function \(\ell_i\) is a valid supporting cut on \(C\) when \(\ell_i(x)\leq f(x)\) for every \(x\in C\); for an exact oracle this follows from \(\alpha_i=f(x_i)\) and \(g_i\in\partial f(x_i)\). It is invalid if there exists \(y\in C\) such that \(\ell_i(y)>f(y)\). If the bundle model is \(m(x)=\max_j\ell_j(x)\), one invalid cut can make \(m(y)>f(y)\), so the master value need not be a lower bound on \(f^*\). Consequently, gap tests using that master value cease to certify optimality until the cut is removed or corrected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut is invalid if it exceeds the objective anywhere; one such cut can invalidate the model lower bound and stopping certificate.
knowledge_statements.title: Invalid Supporting Cuts

source_witnesses.locator: 3.4.2 Methods of Linear Approximation p. 87

knowledge_statements.statement_title: A Single Wrong Slope Produces an Invalid Cut
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-dimensional witness that correct value interpolation at the anchor does not ensure cut validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=x^2\) on \(\mathbb R\), and consider \(\ell(x)=x\). Although \(\ell(0)=f(0)=0\), the slope \(1\notin\partial f(0)=\{0\}\), and \(\ell(x)>f(x)\) for every \(x\in(0,1)\). Thus a correctly anchored affine function can fail to be a supporting cut and can make a maximum-of-cuts model exceed \(f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For x squared, the line x has the correct value at zero but lies above the objective on (0,1), so correct anchoring alone does not ensure validity.
knowledge_statements.title: A Single Wrong Slope Produces an Invalid Cut

assumptions_latex: A finite record indexed by a finite set \(I\) contains triples \((x_i,f_i,g_i)\) asserted to be exact values and subgradients of one convex function.
All query points \(x_i\) lie in a convex set \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Violation of any pairwise subgradient inequality certifies that the oracle records cannot all be exact records of the asserted convex function.

notation.meaning: Query point, value, and claimed subgradient

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite pairwise certificate for inconsistency of exact convex oracle records.

source_refs.locator: 3.4.2 Methods of Linear Approximation p. 87

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each ordered pair \((i,j)\in I\times I\), define \(r_{ij}=f_i+g_i^{\mathsf T}(x_j-x_i)-f_j\). Exact convex-oracle consistency requires \(r_{ij}\leq0\) for all \(i,j\in I\), because the subgradient inequality at \(x_i\) must hold at \(x_j\). Hence any pair satisfying \(r_{ij}>0\) is a directly verifiable certificate that at least one stored value, slope, or query association is incorrect. Passing all pairwise inequalities is necessary for consistency and, for a finite dataset without additional smoothness requirements, the convex polyhedral function \(h(y)=\max_{i\in I}\{f_i+g_i^{\mathsf T}(y-x_i)\}\) interpolates the recorded values: \(h(x_j)=f_j\) for every \(j\in I\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compute every cross-record subgradient residual; any positive residual proves that the claimed exact convex oracle data are inconsistent, while satisfaction of all such inequalities yields a convex polyhedral interpolant of the finite records.
knowledge_statements.title: Inconsistent Oracle Records

source_witnesses.locator: 3.4.2 Methods of Linear Approximation p. 87

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Certified Correction and Uncontrolled-Error Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the method-independent distinction between cuts with certified overestimation allowances and oracle errors lacking such allowances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an oracle cut \(\ell_i\), define \(e_i=\sup_{x\in C}(\ell_i(x)-f(x))_+\). If a finite certified bound \(e_i\le\bar e_i\) is available, then \(\ell_i-\bar e_i\le f\) on \(C\), and \(\widehat m(x)=\max_i\{\ell_i(x)-\bar e_i\}\) is a valid lower model. If no certified finite bounds are available, neither \(\max_i\ell_i\) nor its master value is certified to lie below \(f\) or \(f^*\); computed model gaps therefore have no prescribed-accuracy interpretation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Known overestimation bounds convert approximate cuts into valid corrected minorants; without certified bounds, model lower bounds and gap-based accuracy claims are unavailable.
assumptions_latex: \(f:C\to\mathbb R\) is finite on a nonempty set \(C\).
Each \(\ell_i\) is an affine oracle cut whose global overestimation may be nonzero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Certified \(\bar e_i\) yield valid corrected cuts; absent such bounds, lower-bound and gap certificates are uncontrolled.
knowledge_statements.title: Certified Correction and Uncontrolled-Error Boundary

assumptions_latex: At iteration \(k\), the method uses an oracle cut \(\ell_k(x)=\tilde f_k+g_k^{\mathsf T}(x-x_k)\).
Its unknown global overestimation error is \(e_k=\sup_{x\in C}(\ell_k(x)-f(x))_+\), with no known usable upper bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Without controlled upper bounds on cut errors, model gaps and lower bounds cannot provide a prescribed-accuracy certificate, even when their computed values converge to zero.
review_flags: No supplied locator directly states the uncontrolled-error failure mechanism.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of certification when oracle errors lack enforceable bounds or decay.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m_k=\max_{i\u001c\leq k}\ell_i\). If known bounds \(e_i\leq\bar e_i\) exist, then \(m_k(x)-\max_{i\u001c\leq k}\bar e_i\leq f(x)\) supplies an error-corrected minorant. When no finite certified \(\bar e_i\) is available, the master value derived from \(m_k\) need not lie below \(f^*\), and a computed model gap can be arbitrarily smaller than the true suboptimality. Thus prescribed-accuracy termination requires bounded, summable, vanishing, or adaptively enforced oracle errors according to the convergence theory being used. Mere empirical stability of returned values or steps does not replace such control.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unknown, unbounded cut errors can make the model gap arbitrarily optimistic, so convergence or stopping accuracy cannot be certified.
knowledge_statements.title: Uncontrolled Oracle Errors

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the leaf, but the convergence-control alternatives and prescribed-accuracy conclusion require an inexact-oracle source. The statement also contains unsafe control characters in its index inequalities; these must be repaired after an authoritative error convention is selected.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Model-Agreement Identity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates global minorant validity from predictive fidelity at a proposed trial point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m\le f\), let \(x\) be the current point, and let a trial \(z\) have positive predicted decrease \(\Delta=f(x)-m(z)>0\). With model error \(e(z)=f(z)-m(z)\ge0\), the actual reduction satisfies \[f(x)-f(z)=\Delta-e(z),\qquad \frac{f(x)-f(z)}{\Delta}=1-\frac{e(z)}{\Delta}.\] Thus poor fidelity relative to this trial means that \(e(z)/\Delta\) is not small. If \(e(z)\ge\Delta\), the predicted descent produces no positive actual reduction despite validity of the model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a valid lower model, the shortfall between predicted and actual reduction is exactly the model error at the trial point; an error as large as the prediction eliminates actual descent.
assumptions_latex: \(m(x)\le f(x)\) for every point under consideration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x)-f(z)=\Delta-e(z)\); hence validity alone does not imply predictive accuracy.

notation.meaning: model error at the trial point

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Model-Agreement Identity

assumptions_latex: At iteration \(k\), the model is \(m_k(x)=\max_{i\in I_k}\{f(y_i)+g_i^{\mathsf T}(x-y_i)\}\), with \(g_i\in\partial f(y_i)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Model validity alone does not imply useful local accuracy; convergence arguments require an additional fidelity mechanism.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: supporting hyperplanes give global underestimation but not uniform local model accuracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes model validity from the local fidelity needed for reliable bundle steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Every stored cut is valid, so \(m_k(x)\le f(x)\) for all \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\). Poor model fidelity occurs along trial points \(z_k\) when the discrepancy \(f(z_k)-m_k(z_k)\) is not small relative to the predicted decrease \(f(x_k)-m_k(z_k)\); concretely, for some \(\eta>0\) and infinitely many \(k\), \[f(z_k)-m_k(z_k)\ge \eta\bigl(f(x_k)-m_k(z_k)\bigr)>0.\] Thus a globally valid polyhedral minorant may substantially overpredict improvement near \(x_k\), invalidating conclusions based only on model decrease.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Valid supporting cuts can still form a locally inaccurate model whose predicted decrease substantially exceeds the objective’s actual improvement.
knowledge_statements.title: Poor Model Fidelity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits the leaf, and the statement correctly distinguishes global minorant validity from local model fidelity. However, no source reference or inspectable locator supports the specific infinite-subsequence criterion or the asserted convergence requirement.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Static Boundary for Overaggressive Cut Deletion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes excessive deletion through the exact pointwise information lost from a valid maximum-of-cuts model, without asserting a method-specific convergence theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m(x)=\max_{i\in I}\ell_i(x)\le f(x)\), and retain only \(J\subset I\), giving \(\widetilde m(x)=\max_{i\in J}\ell_i(x)\). Then \(\widetilde m\le m\le f\), while the deletion loss \(D(x)=m(x)-\widetilde m(x)\) is nonnegative. Relative to a protected trial or localization set \(R\) and permitted loss \(\tau\ge0\), deletion is overaggressive when \(\sup_{x\in R}D(x)>\tau\). In particular, deleting every cut active at a reference point can destroy exact interpolation there even though global minorant validity is preserved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deleting valid cuts remains safe for minorant validity but is overaggressive when it lowers the model beyond the allowed tolerance on the region whose accuracy must be protected.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) is finite and nonempty, and every \(\ell_i\) is a global affine minorant of \(f\).
\(J\subset I\) is nonempty; \(R\) and \(\tau\) specify the locally required fidelity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\le D=m-\widetilde m\), and \(\sup_R D>\tau\) is a directly checkable excessive-deletion condition.
knowledge_statements.title: Static Boundary for Overaggressive Cut Deletion

assumptions_latex: Each retained affine cut is a global minorant of \(f\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Deletion is unsafe when it destroys the model-memory property required by the method’s convergence analysis.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: deleting valid cuts preserves underestimation but can erase essential aggregate or locality information
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Covers deletion that preserves validity but removes convergence-critical model memory.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m_k\) be the maximum of all active cuts and let \(\widetilde m_k\) be the maximum after deletion. Although \(\widetilde m_k\le m_k\le f\) remains valid, deletion is overaggressive if it removes every cut carrying the aggregate or locality information required at \(x_k\). A concrete failure signature is the existence of trial points \(z_k\) such that \[m_k(z_k)-\widetilde m_k(z_k)>0\] and this loss is comparable to, or larger than, \(f(x_k)-m_k(z_k)\). The reduced model may then repeatedly reconstruct discarded information without accumulating the approximation needed for convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cut deletion may preserve global underestimation while erasing aggregate or local information essential for progress and convergence.
knowledge_statements.title: Overaggressive Cut Deletion

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and local scope are appropriate, but the convergence-critical aggregate or locality information depends on the particular bundle method. An authoritative bundle-method source with a specific locator is required to support the deletion criterion and convergence consequence.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Scaled Rank and Residual Diagnostics for Cut Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Numerical diagnosis and stabilization of nearly dependent or badly scaled active cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let A be an active-cut matrix and let D_r,D_c be nonsingular diagonal row and column scalings. Analyze \widetilde A=D_rAD_c by rank-revealing QR or singular-value decomposition, with numerical rank r_\tau=\#\{i:\sigma_i(\widetilde A)>\tau\sigma_1(\widetilde A)\} for a stated relative threshold \tau. Scaling can reduce conditioning caused by units but cannot change exact rank. Dependency removal, regularization, or truncated solves may generate a stable candidate, but that candidate must be checked using feasibility and KKT residuals for the original unscaled, unregularized master.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Diagnose cut dependence after explicit scaling with a relative rank threshold, and verify stabilized candidates against the original master.
assumptions_latex: D_r and D_c are nonsingular diagonal scalings.
A relative numerical-rank threshold \tau is stated.
Any stabilized solve is used only to generate a candidate for the original master.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Scaled rank-revealing diagnostics distinguish scaling effects from dependence, while original-system checks prevent stabilization from being mistaken for a certificate.
knowledge_statements.title: Scaled Rank and Residual Diagnostics for Cut Systems

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nearly Parallel Cut-Normal Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parameterized cut system with diverging condition number despite exact nonsingularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \varepsilon>0, let A_\varepsilon=\begin{bmatrix}1&0\\1&\varepsilon\end{bmatrix}. Each A_\varepsilon is nonsingular, but its two row normals become parallel as \varepsilon\downarrow0 and \kappa_2(A_\varepsilon)\sim 2/\varepsilon. Thus arbitrarily small perturbations or residuals can be strongly amplified although exact rank is retained for every positive \varepsilon.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two distinct cut normals can remain exactly independent while their condition number diverges as they become parallel.

notation.meaning: active-cut matrix with nearly parallel rows

knowledge_statements.title: Nearly Parallel Cut-Normal Family

assumptions_latex: The master problem has a relevant constraint or linear-system matrix \(A_k\) assembled from the active cuts and master-problem constraints.
The master problem is solved in floating-point arithmetic, and conditioning is assessed relative to the scale of \(A_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A large scale-relative condition number signals sensitivity of computed master solutions and cut multipliers to perturbations and residual errors.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: nearly dependent or badly scaled active constraints can produce ill-conditioned master-problem linear algebra
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Numerical failure boundary for nearly dependent or badly scaled active-cut systems; the criterion is relative to matrix scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonsingular relevant matrix \(A_k\), the active cut system is ill-conditioned in the spectral norm when \(\kappa_2(A_k)=\sigma_{\max}(A_k)/\sigma_{\min}(A_k)\) is large; if \(A_k\) is rank deficient, set \(\kappa_2(A_k)=+\infty\). Equivalently in the nonsingular case, \(\sigma_{\min}(A_k)\) is small relative to \(\sigma_{\max}(A_k)\), not merely small in absolute units. Such conditioning can amplify perturbations and residual errors in linear systems used to compute primal steps or dual cut multipliers. Nearly dependent or badly scaled cuts may therefore cause unstable active-set identification, cancellation in predicted reductions, or inaccurate master solutions even though each cut is mathematically valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nearly dependent or badly scaled active-cut systems can make master solutions, multipliers, and predicted reductions sensitive to numerical error.
knowledge_statements.title: Ill-Conditioned Cut Systems

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Summable Proximal Parameters Can Stall Before the Minimizer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact one-dimensional model sequence demonstrating nonoptimal stagnation under persistently excessive stabilization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\tfrac12(x-1)^2\), \(x_0=0\), and at \(x_k\) minimize its exact affine support plus \((2t_k)^{-1}(x-x_k)^2\), taking \(t_k=2^{-k-2}\). The trial satisfies \(x_{k+1}=x_k+t_k(1-x_k)\). Since \(\sum_k t_k<\infty\), the iterates converge to a limit strictly below the unique minimizer \(1\), while every displacement tends to zero and \(|f'(x_k)|\) stays bounded away from zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a simple convex quadratic, summable proximal parameters produce decreasing, vanishing steps whose limit remains strictly short of the minimizer.
assumptions_latex: \(t_k=2^{-k-2}\), and every exact affine-model proximal trial is taken.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_k\to\bar x<1\) although \(x_k-x_{k-1}\to0\); hence vanishing steps need not imply stationarity.
knowledge_statements.title: Summable Proximal Parameters Can Stall Before the Minimizer

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Overstabilization Diagnostic
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the convention that smaller proximal parameter means stronger quadratic stabilization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(z_k\) minimizes \(m_k(x)+(2t_k)^{-1}\|x-x_k\|^2\). Then \((x_k-z_k)/t_k\in\partial m_k(z_k)\). If the relevant model subgradients have norm at most \(L\), then \(\|z_k-x_k\|\le t_kL\). Consequently, \(t_k\downarrow0\) forces trial displacements to vanish. This is overstabilization when the contraction persists while a valid nonstationarity measure, such as \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x_k))\), remains bounded away from zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An excessively strong proximal penalty forces small trials; it is a failure only when those small trials persist despite a nonvanishing stationarity measure.
assumptions_latex: The proximal master has a minimizer \(z_k\).
Relevant subgradients of \(m_k\) are bounded by \(L\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|z_k-x_k\|\le t_kL\); vanishing \(t_k\) together with persistent nonstationarity diagnoses overstabilization.
knowledge_statements.title: Overstabilization Diagnostic

assumptions_latex: A proximal bundle trial point minimizes \(m_k(x)+(2t_k)^{-1}\lVert x-x_k\rVert^2\).
The relevant model subgradients are bounded near \(x_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: As \(t_k\downarrow0\), trial displacements and obtainable decreases vanish, so excessive stabilization can cause stagnation away from optimality.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: a vanishing proximal parameter imposes an increasingly strong quadratic penalty
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the convention that smaller proximal parameter means stronger stabilization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Optimality of the proximal master problem gives \((x_k-z_k)/t_k\in\partial m_k(z_k)\). If \(\lVert g\rVert\le L\) for relevant \(g\in\partial m_k(z_k)\), then \[\lVert z_k-x_k\rVert\le t_kL.\] Hence \(t_k\downarrow0\) forces trial points toward \(x_k\), irrespective of whether \(0\in\partial f(x_k)\). Overstabilization occurs when this contraction is imposed persistently without a stationarity justification, making both the actual movement and the achievable model decrease tend to zero while the serious iterate can remain nonoptimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An excessively strong proximal penalty forces vanishing trial steps and can stall the serious iterate before stationarity.
knowledge_statements.title: Overstabilization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proximal-parameter convention is explicit, the displacement estimate is mathematically consistent, and failure_boundary fits the leaf. A source is still required for the stronger method-level claim that persistent contraction can leave the serious iterate nonoptimal and constitute overstabilization.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weak Proximal Localization Can Predict Ascent as Descent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-dimensional convex witness of a remote trial generated by an excessively large proximal parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=|x|\), take the serious point \(x=1\), and use its exact supporting cut \(m(y)=y\). The minimizer of \(m(y)+(2t)^{-1}(y-1)^2\) is \(z=1-t\). Its predicted decrease is \(f(1)-m(z)=t\), whereas its actual reduction is \(f(1)-f(z)=1-|1-t|\). For \(t>2\), the model predicts positive decrease \(t\) but the objective strictly increases.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the absolute-value objective, a sufficiently weak proximal penalty sends the trial past the minimizer and predicts descent even though the objective increases.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The trial \(z=1-t\) has predicted decrease \(t>0\) but actual reduction \(2-t<0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Weak Proximal Localization Can Predict Ascent as Descent

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Understabilization Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the convention that larger proximal parameter means weaker quadratic stabilization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the master \(m_k(x)+(2t_k)^{-1}\|x-x_k\|^2\), increasing \(t_k\) weakens localization. Let \(R_k\) be a region on which the permitted relative model error satisfies \(f(z)-m_k(z)\le\gamma\,[f(x_k)-m_k(z)]\) for some \(\gamma<1\). The master is understabilized when its trial leaves \(R_k\) and violates this agreement bound. At such a trial the valid lower model may predict descent while the actual reduction is nonpositive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stabilization is insufficient when the proximal master sends its trial outside the region where model error is smaller than predicted decrease, allowing predicted descent without actual descent.
assumptions_latex: \(m_k\le f\), and the proximal master has a trial point \(z_k\).
\(R_k\) and \(\gamma<1\) specify the required local-fidelity regime.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Leaving \(R_k\) with model error at least the predicted decrease is a quantitative understabilization failure.
knowledge_statements.title: Understabilization Boundary

assumptions_latex: A proximal bundle trial point minimizes \(m_k(x)+(2t_k)^{-1}\lVert x-x_k\rVert^2\).
The model is only a lower approximation of the convex objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Excessively large \(t_k\) permits remote, poorly predicted trials and can destroy the localization needed for reliable acceptance decisions.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: a large proximal parameter weakens localization of a lower cutting-plane model
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the convention that larger proximal parameter means weaker stabilization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Because the quadratic coefficient is \(1/(2t_k)\), increasing \(t_k\) weakens localization around \(x_k\). Understabilization occurs when \(t_k\) is sufficiently large that the master solution \(z_k\) leaves the region where accumulated cuts predict \(f\) accurately. The model may then report a large predicted decrease \(f(x_k)-m_k(z_k)\) while \(f(z_k)-m_k(z_k)\) is of comparable or greater magnitude. Such remote trials can be rejected repeatedly or can produce erratic serious steps; global minorant validity alone does not control this behavior.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weak proximal penalty permits remote trials where the cutting-plane model is inaccurate, causing rejection or erratic progress.
knowledge_statements.title: Understabilization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The statement correctly interprets large \(t_k\) as weak stabilization and fits the chapter boundary. The claimed relationship among remote trials, model fidelity, repeated rejection, and erratic serious steps is method dependent and has no cited support or inspectable locator.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Operational Boundary for Null-Step Proliferation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines pathological proliferation using observable rejection and progress quantities, without relying on an unspecified stationarity residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\) remain the serious point during consecutive trials \(z_k\), let \(\Delta_k=f(x)-m_k(z_k)>0\), and let \(\rho_k=(f(x)-f(z_k))/\Delta_k\). A null step has \(\rho_k<\eta\), leaves \(x\) unchanged, and updates the model. Infinitely many null steps are not intrinsically pathological if \(\Delta_k\to0\) or a valid stationarity test is approached. They constitute null-step proliferation when, for some \(\delta>0\), \(\Delta_k\ge\delta\) throughout an infinite rejection sequence while the updates never restore \(\rho_k\ge\eta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeated null steps become pathological when predicted progress stays bounded away from zero but model updates never produce acceptable agreement; rejection alone is not failure when prediction vanishes toward stationarity.
assumptions_latex: The method uses a fixed acceptance fraction \(\eta\in(0,1)\).
Every considered trial has positive predicted decrease.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An infinite sequence with \(\inf_k\Delta_k>0\) and \(\rho_k<\eta\) after every update is an observable null-step proliferation failure.
knowledge_statements.title: Operational Boundary for Null-Step Proliferation

assumptions_latex: A trial is a null step when the serious point is unchanged and a cut generated at the rejected trial is added.
The method uses a fixed positive acceptance fraction for actual versus predicted decrease.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Infinitely many null steps without vanishing stationarity residual constitute a failure of stabilization or model-improvement control.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: null steps should improve the model or drive a model-based stationarity measure to zero
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes pathological repeated rejection rather than ordinary finite model-refinement phases.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Null-step proliferation occurs when an infinite index set \(K\) satisfies \(x_{k+1}=x_k\) for every \(k\in K\), while the generated cuts fail to yield either a subsequent serious step or stationarity. A concrete failure criterion is \[\inf_{k\in K} r_k>0,\] where \(r_k\) is the method’s valid model-based stationarity residual. Repeated rejection alone is not failure: it becomes pathological when model refinement and parameter updates neither reduce \(r_k\) toward zero nor restore agreement between actual and predicted decrease.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeated null steps are pathological when they neither produce a serious step nor drive a valid stationarity residual to zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Null-Step Proliferation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record appropriately distinguishes pathological proliferation from ordinary null-step refinement, and failure_boundary is the correct role. However, \(r_k\) is only described as the method's valid residual, so the criterion and its convergence interpretation require a source tied to a specific bundle framework.

assumptions_latex: The master model is intended to satisfy \(m_k(x)\le f(x)\) on the feasible set \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A master value is a valid global lower bound only when every encoded cut is globally valid on \(X\) and the master is solved over the correct feasible set.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: minimizing a genuine global minorant over the true feasible set yields a lower bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies when a reported master optimum fails as a global lower-bound certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(L_k=\inf_{x\in X}m_k(x)\) and \(m_k(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in X\), then \(L_k\le f^*:=\inf_{x\in X}f(x)\). An invalid master lower bound is any reported \(\widehat L_k\) for which this implication lacks a certified premise, for example because an inexact oracle cut exceeds \(f\), the master uses an incorrect feasible region, or numerical error overstates its optimum. In such cases \(\widehat L_k>f^*\) is possible, so \(f(x_k)-\widehat L_k\) is not a valid optimality gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A master optimum certifies a lower bound only if all cuts are global minorants and the true feasible region is used.
knowledge_statements.title: Invalid Master Lower Bounds

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The lower-bound implication is correct and the failure-boundary role matches the certificate-failure container. No cited source supports the treatment of inexact cuts, feasible-region errors, or numerical overstatement of the master optimum; a specific cutting-plane or bundle reference is required.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Arbitrarily Small Localized Gap Far from Optimality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete separation between a localized model gap and global suboptimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let f(x)=|x| on \mathbb R, take x_k=1, and let 0<\varepsilon<1. The exact supporting cut \ell(x)=x is minimized over the trust region [1-\varepsilon,1+\varepsilon] at value 1-\varepsilon. Hence the displayed localized gap is f(x_k)-(1-\varepsilon)=\varepsilon, whereas f(x_k)-f^*=1. Thus the displayed gap tends to zero as \varepsilon\downarrow0 while global suboptimality remains one.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Shrinking a trust region can make a localized model gap arbitrarily small at a point whose global objective error stays fixed.
assumptions_latex: The master minimizes the exact supporting cut \ell(x)=x only over [1-\varepsilon,1+\varepsilon].

notation.meaning: trust-region radius and displayed localized gap

knowledge_statements.title: Arbitrarily Small Localized Gap Far from Optimality

assumptions_latex: \(x_k\in X\) is feasible and \(m_k\le f\) on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A small model gap certifies near-optimality only when the master value is a valid global lower bound computed to controlled accuracy.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: a model gap bounds suboptimality only through a certified global lower bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates a genuine global optimality gap from merely local or regularized model agreement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: When \(L_k:=\inf_{x\in X}m_k(x)\) is certified and \(m_k\le f\), one has \[0\le f(x_k)-f^*\le f(x_k)-L_k=\delta_k.\] A small displayed gap is misleading if its lower endpoint is instead a localized, proximal, trust-region, or inaccurately solved master value not known to satisfy \(L_k\le f^*\). It may also be misleading when objective and master errors are of the same order as \(\delta_k\). Then \(\delta_k\) measures internal model agreement, not necessarily global suboptimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A small displayed model gap need not imply near-optimality unless its lower endpoint is a certified global lower bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Misleading Small Model Gaps

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certified-gap inequality is correct, and the statement properly separates a global lower bound from localized or regularized master values. The distinctions among master variants and numerical errors need an authoritative source with a specific locator.

assumptions_latex: A computed incumbent value and lower bound have known absolute errors \(\varepsilon_U\) and \(\varepsilon_L\).
The exact certified values satisfy \(L_k\le f^*\le U_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Termination is justified only after accounting for all oracle, master-solve, and floating-point errors in the reported gap.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: numerical stopping must use an error-aware upper bound on the exact optimality gap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Error-aware boundary for gap-based stopping in finite-precision model methods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose computed values \(\widehat U_k\) and \(\widehat L_k\) obey \(U_k\le\widehat U_k+\varepsilon_U\) and \(L_k\ge\widehat L_k-\varepsilon_L\). Then a sufficient error-aware stopping test is \[\widehat U_k-\widehat L_k+\varepsilon_U+\varepsilon_L\le\tau,\] which implies \(U_k-L_k\le	au\). Premature numerical termination occurs when stopping uses only the displayed difference \(\widehat U_k-\widehat L_k\), or a residual below machine-resolvable scale, while omitted oracle, optimization, or rounding errors can exceed the requested tolerance. The reported certificate then does not establish the claimed accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stopping on a displayed gap is premature when unresolved oracle, solve, or rounding errors can exceed the requested tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Premature Numerical Termination

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The one-sided error assumptions imply the displayed sufficient stopping test, and failure_boundary is appropriate. The error model and the claims about oracle, solve, rounding, and machine-resolution failures have no supporting citation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Clarke Subgradient Without a Supporting Minorant
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elementary failure of convex supporting-plane logic for a nonconvex locally Lipschitz objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let f(x)=-|x| and y=0. Then \partial_C f(0)=[-1,1], so g=0 belongs to \partial_C f(0). The associated affine plane is f(0)+g(x-y)=0, but f(x)=-|x|<0 for every x\ne0. Hence Clarke subgradient membership does not make the plane a local or global minorant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the downward cusp, a valid Clarke subgradient generates an affine plane lying above the objective at every nearby nonzero point.
knowledge_statements.title: Clarke Subgradient Without a Supporting Minorant

assumptions_latex: The convex chapter relies on global affine minorants obtained from convex subgradients.
A nonconvex objective may have generalized subgradients that do not generate global supporting minorants.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Convex bundle guarantees do not transfer to nonconvex objectives without altered models, acceptance rules, and convergence notions.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: convex subgradient inequalities provide global minorants, whereas Clarke generalized subgradients of nonconvex functions generally do not
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Marks the loss of global supporting-plane logic outside convex optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For convex \(f\), \(g\in\partial f(y)\) implies \(f(x)\ge f(y)+g^{\mathsf T}(x-y)\) for every \(x\). This global minorant property underlies convex bundle lower bounds and gap certificates. For a nonconvex locally Lipschitz \(f\), membership \(g\in\partial_C f(y)\) does not imply this inequality globally, or locally for every \(x\). Consequently, directly reusing convex cutting-plane masters can yield models above the objective and invalid lower bounds. Nonconvex bundle methods therefore require distinct model axioms and typically certify stationarity rather than global optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonconvex generalized subgradients need not define supporting minorants, so convex bundle lower bounds and global guarantees no longer apply.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex Bundle Methods Boundary

assumptions_latex: The chapter concerns objective-model methods built from function values and subgradients.
Geometric cutting-plane methods instead maintain an explicit localization set containing candidate solutions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Results depending on objective minorants or proximal bundle gaps do not automatically apply to purely geometric localization schemes.

notation.meaning: geometric localization set at iteration k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates objective bundle models from center-based localization-set cutting-plane algorithms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A geometric cutting-plane method updates a localization region by \(P_{k+1}=P_k\cap H_k\), where the separating halfspace \(H_k\) is chosen to retain the solution set, and selects a center by a geometric rule such as volumetric, analytic, or ellipsoidal centering. This differs from minimizing a polyhedral objective minorant \(m_k\), possibly with proximal stabilization. Therefore bundle-specific quantities such as aggregate subgradients, serious and null steps, and proximal model gaps are not intrinsic to the geometric scheme. Complexity and termination claims must instead follow from localization geometry and valid separation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Geometric cutting-plane algorithms shrink solution-containing regions; their invariants and certificates differ from objective-model bundle methods.
knowledge_statements.title: Geometric Cutting-Plane Methods Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Marks assumptions lost when finite-dimensional bundle machinery is moved to function spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For convex \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), a cut may still have the form \(f(y)+\langle g,x-y\rangle\) with \(g\in X^*\). However, finite-dimensional conclusions do not transfer automatically: bounded sets need not be strongly compact, subdifferentials may be empty without continuity assumptions, quadratic stabilization may lack a canonical representation, and finite master solutions may not control convergence in the required topology. Thus an infinite-dimensional bundle method needs explicit choices of topology, duality pairing, prox geometry, oracle domain, and compactness or coercivity assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bundle methods in function spaces need explicit topology, duality, prox geometry, and compactness assumptions absent from finite-dimensional theory.
knowledge_statements.title: Infinite-Dimensional Bundle Methods Boundary
